# Phase 7L — Final Event Architecture Reconciliation and Freeze — AI Voice Agent Platform

Reconciliation artifact. It contains no application code, no SQL migration, no Alembic revision, no deployment manifest and no runtime configuration. It edits no frozen document.

### 1.2 What this document is, and what it is not

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| AUT-7L-01 | 7L is a reconciliation. It collects every handoff, conflict, erratum, owner decision, activation gate, obligation and residual risk that 7A–7K addressed to it, and gives each one exactly one disposition from the closed list of §3.2. |
| AUT-7L-02 | 7L redesigns nothing. Where frozen sources already decide a behaviour, 7L cites the deciding rule. Where they do not, 7L does not decide it: it records the open question for its owner (§27) and names the fail-closed state that holds meanwhile. |
| AUT-7L-03 | **A proposed amendment is not an applied amendment.** Every amendment packet of §18 carries `Source edit status: NOT APPLIED`. No frozen file was edited to produce this document (§29). A packet takes effect only when the owner of the target document applies it under that document's own change control, with the owner authorization the packet names. |
| AUT-7L-04 | **Three statements are kept apart everywhere:** *architecture reconciliation* (the frozen contracts, read together, assign one behaviour), *implementation readiness* (the migrations, functions, workloads and tests exist and pass) and *production activation* (an owner has authorized the capability on evidence). This document can establish only the first. It establishes the second and third for nothing. |
| AUT-7L-05 | A statement that a table, function, role, ACL user, key, workload or check "exists" is made only where it was read in the repository on 2026-10-13 (§2.4). Everything else is described as designed, required or future. |
| AUT-7L-06 | 7L is bound by 7A AUTH-01 … AUTH-05 and by the per-concern authority rule (7A §5; 7B §5.1): executed migrations govern physical schema; the owning Phase-6 document governs domain semantics; 7D–7K govern their own mechanisms. 7L governs only the consolidation. |

### 1.3 Provenance tags

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| [FROZEN] | Stated by an approved Phase 1–7K artifact or an executed migration. Cited, never changed here. |
| [OD] | Fixed by an owner decision recorded in a frozen document; cited by its original ID (§5). |
| [7L] | A consolidation rule of this document. It adds no behaviour to the event architecture. |
| [PROP] | Text proposed by 7L for a frozen document. It is not in force. |
| [OPEN] | Not decided by any frozen authority. Recorded for its owner in §27. |
| [CAND] / [MEAS] | As 7K defines them: an unmeasured candidate value; a value that must come from a measurement. |

**No measured value exists in this document.** No benchmark, load test, chaos test, restore drill, provider validation or migration was executed for it.

### 1.4 Scope

In scope: the consolidated handoff inventory; the disposition of every cross-phase conflict and erratum; the consolidated owner-decision register; the cross-phase compatibility matrix; the controlled amendment register and its packets; the master activation register; the consolidated implementation, migration, measurement and validation obligations; the residual-risk and legal-review registers; the outstanding owner decisions; the adversarial counterexample review; the freeze recommendation.

Out of scope, and not done here: any change to a route, error code, event, envelope, stream key, consumer group, retry budget, retention period, operator authority or residency rule; any SQL; any vendor choice; any acceptance of a risk on the owner's behalf; any legal conclusion; Phase 8.

## 3. Frozen-Source Precedence and Change-Control Policy

### 3.1 Precedence

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| GOV-7L-01 [FROZEN] | Authority is per semantic concern (7A AUTH-02 … AUTH-05; 7B AUTH-C-01 … AUTH-C-07; ADR-7A-15, ADR-7B-10). No closure artifact, 7L included, globally supersedes an owner document. |
| GOV-7L-02 [FROZEN] | An owner decision governs exactly its stated scope. Where an approval's numbered conditions are stricter than the option text, the conditions govern (7K §27.2; 7I §25; 7J §29.1). |
| GOV-7L-03 [7L] | Where a later frozen document narrows an earlier one without contradicting it (for example 7G RTY-10 narrowing 7F XAK-01; 7I ACC-06 narrowing 7D CLN-03), both are in force and the narrower behaviour is the behaviour. The earlier text is aligned by a packet; until then the later frozen rule already binds every implementation. |
| GOV-7L-04 [7L] | Where a later owner decision needs something an earlier frozen contract cannot express (CNF-7K-05, -08, -09, -10), **the later decision does not rewrite the earlier contract**. The fail-closed design of the later document is the behaviour in force, the capability stays closed, and the earlier contract changes only through a packet its owner applies. |
| GOV-7L-05 [7L] | 7L never resolves a conflict by choosing between two owners' semantics. Such a conflict is `OWNER DECISION REQUIRED` with the owner named. |

### 3.2 Disposition vocabulary

Exactly one disposition per record. The codes are used in the registers; the names are the binding vocabulary and are never substituted for one another.

| Code | Disposition | Means | Does **not** mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-ARF | `ALREADY RESOLVED BY FROZEN CONTRACT` | A frozen rule, cited, already assigns one behaviour; nothing further is owed | That anything was built |
| D-ROD | `RESOLVED BY APPROVED OWNER DECISION` | An approved owner decision, cited, settles the policy | That the frozen text it affects was edited, or that the capability is active |
| D-DOC | `DOCUMENTARY ALIGNMENT REQUIRED` | A frozen text is stale or imprecise; behaviour is already unambiguous from a governing rule; the owner aligns the wording | A behaviour change |
| D-CSA | `CONTROLLED SOURCE AMENDMENT REQUIRED` | A frozen contract must gain or change normative text before a capability can be built or activated | That 7L's proposed wording is in force |
| D-IMP | `IMPLEMENTATION DEFERRED — GATED` | The design is complete; nothing is built; a named gate keeps the capability closed | A design gap |
| D-MEA | `MEASUREMENT OR VALIDATION REQUIRED — GATED` | The exit condition needs executed evidence; a named gate keeps the dependent behaviour closed | A design contradiction |
| D-OWN | `OWNER DECISION REQUIRED` | No frozen authority settles it; an owner or domain owner must choose | That 7L chose |
| D-RSK | `ACCEPTED RESIDUAL RISK` | An owner decision, cited, explicitly accepts the residual | Acceptance inferred from a listing |
| D-BLK | `BLOCKED — UNRESOLVED DESIGN CONTRADICTION` | The frozen contracts, read together, cannot assign one behaviour and no fail-closed state exists | Unexecuted work |
| D-NA | `NOT APPLICABLE — WITH EVIDENCE` | The item needs no action, with the evidence cited | Ignored |

A record may also carry **secondary gates** (for example D-ROD with a packet and a closed gate). The primary disposition is the one that says who must act next.

### 3.3 Reconciliation record schema

Every record of §6 – §15 has the fields below. To keep one record on one row, fields whose value is the same for a whole disposition class are stated once here and repeated in a row only where that row differs.

| Field | Where it is given |
|---|---|
| Stable original source ID; source document and section | Row |
| Target owner | Row |
| Existing contract; conflict or missing requirement | Row (summarized; the source row is the full statement) |
| Approved decision authority | Row, where one exists |
| Proposed reconciled contract; exact amendment packet | Row → packet ID of §18 |
| Implementation dependency; activation gate | Row → §23 / §24 |
| Security and data-integrity implication | Row where material; otherwise the class default below |
| Validation evidence | Row → §25; class default below |
| Final disposition; remaining owner action | Row |

| Disposition class | Default security / integrity implication | Default validation evidence | Default remaining owner action |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-ARF | None beyond the cited rule | The cited frozen rule and its own tests | None |
| D-ROD | As the decision record states | The tests the decision's document names | Apply the linked packet, if any |
| D-DOC | None: wording only. An implementation that follows the stale wording is wrong, so the alignment is owed before the owning phase builds from that text | Review of the applied text against the packet | Apply the packet at the document's next governed revision |
| D-CSA | The capability is unsafe or unbuildable without it; the named gate is closed | The tests the packet names | Authorize and apply the packet; then implement |
| D-IMP | None while the gate is closed | The obligation's own tests | Build under the owning phase |
| D-MEA | None while the gate is closed | The executed benchmark, drill or validation | Execute; record; fix the value |
| D-OWN | The affected capability is closed until decided | — | Decide (§27) |
| D-RSK | As the accepting decision states | — | None; the risk stays visible in §26 |

**No record is marked complete from a citation alone.** A record is closed in 7L only as D-ARF, D-NA, or D-ROD without a packet. Every other record is open and has an owner.

### 3.4 Change-control policy for frozen sources

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| CHG-7L-01 | No Phase 1–7K document, migration `001` – `112`, Alembic revision, D0 source, runtime file or infrastructure file is edited by 7L. The only file created is this one (§29). |
| CHG-7L-02 | A frozen document changes only by its owner, through a governed revision that (a) cites the packet ID, (b) applies the packet text or records why it differs, (c) records the owner authorization, (d) re-records the document's hash. Until then the document is as frozen. |
| CHG-7L-03 | **Owner authorization is required** for every packet classified D-CSA and for every packet that adds a privilege, a principal, an operation kind, a state transition, a retention behaviour or a cross-region element. §18 marks each such packet `Owner approval: REQUIRED — NOT GIVEN`. The owner decisions already approved (OD-7K-04, OD-7K-05 and the others) approve the *policy*; none of them approves an edit to a frozen document or the activation of anything (7K §27.1). |
| CHG-7L-04 | A packet classified D-DOC needs the target document owner's approval only. |
| CHG-7L-05 | No new physical schema is created as "migration 113" by any Phase 7 document. Every schema need is a logical requirement on a future governed Phase-5 migration, whose DDL, names and number are that migration's (7F IO-7F-21; 7G IO-7G-01; 7H §17.3; 7I §23; 7J §31; 7K §29.1). |
| CHG-7L-06 | Withdrawn text is never consolidated. In particular the clause of ERR-7H-09 that `X-Platform-Signature-Previous` "stops being emitted up to 6 seconds before `previous_secret_expires_at`" is **withdrawn** by OD-7H-16 and is excluded from packet AP-7L-37 (7H HE-7L-7H-09). |

## 5. Owner-Decision Consolidation

### 5.1 Rules

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| ODR-7L-01 | The register reproduces each decision's approved option from its own decision record. 7L invents no approval date, choice or authority. Where a record gives a date, it is given; where it gives none, none is given. |
| ODR-7L-02 | No approved decision is reopened. A decision is shown as *narrowed* only where a later approved decision narrows it in its own record (OD-7K-02 by OD-7K-05; OD-7B-01 clarified by OD-7B-02; the "resolution bound" of OD-7I-24 … -25 superseded by OD-7I-26). |
| ODR-7L-03 | **Approval of a policy is not approval to activate it** (7K §27.1; 7I §24.3; 7J §32). Every decision's "Gate" column names what still keeps the capability closed. |
| ODR-7L-04 | Final status vocabulary: `BINDING` (approved; in force as policy); `BINDING — NARROWED` (in force as narrowed). No decision in Phase 7 is `OPEN`. The undecided matters are new records OD-7L-01 … -15 in §27. |

## 6. Phase 7A / 7B — Standards and Taxonomy Reconciliation

### 6.1 Mechanism classes A – I and their owners (7A §9, TAX-01, TAX-02)

Checked against 7B's catalogue and the later documents that own each class. No artifact of 7B–7K sits outside A–I, and none is classified twice.

| Class | Mechanism | Durable | Catalogue owner | Transport / mechanism owner | Preserved rule | Later refinement that does not change the class |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Transactional durable domain event | Yes | 7B §12 | 7D (outbox, relay); 7E (stream) | State and one outbox row in one transaction (7A PR-02; 7D PTX) | 7I ACC-13 position record beside the outbox (ERR-7I-13) |
| B | Conditional durable domain event | Yes, on the named branch | 7B §13 | 7D; 7E | Row written only on the named success branch | — |
| C | Worker-emitted durable domain event | Yes | 7B §14 | 7D; 7E | Written in the worker's own transaction; never a direct Redis publish | EV-079 producer is PRD-27 (OD-7B-02) |
| D | Direct Redis Stream signal | No | 7B §15 | 7D §32 (publisher); 7E §19 (4 SIGNAL pairs) | Never outboxed; never Billing-authoritative; never promoted silently | 7C SIGNAL envelope (OD-7C-06); 7G excludes SIGNAL from durable recovery |
| E | Celery task / command; APScheduler trigger | Job row durable; message not a fact | 7B §17 | 7D §33 – §35 (mandatory work); 7K §12, §14 (schedules) | A task is a command, not an event (ADR-7A-04); APScheduler is a timer only; mandatory work recovered from durable state (7A CEL-08) | 7K ADR-7K-09: ticks are not intent |
| F | Realtime WebSocket push | No | 7B §16 | The realtime contract (6A / 6D) | Raw WebSocket; best-effort; clients re-read REST after a gap; no Socket.IO server (7A WS-01) | 7K §2.3 follows 7A (CNF-7K-07) |
| G | Public outbound webhook | Delivery row durable | 7B §18 (19 topics) | 7H | Signed, at-least-once, dead-letter; separate from internal transport (ADR-7A-13) | 7H §8 state machine; 7I content guard |
| H | Provider callback (inbound) | Dedup row durable | 7B §19 | 7H §11 | Verify → dedup → fast ACK → process; ingress, not internal transport | OD-7H-08 processing input before the 2xx |
| I | Audit | Yes, immutable | 7B §20 | 7D §36; 7I §19 | Audit is not the event bus (ADR-7A-05); no consumer reads audit as a feed | OD-7D-02 same-transaction audit |

**Result.** The 7A architecture is preserved by every later document: transactional outbox for durable publication; Redis Streams as transport, never truth; Celery and APScheduler as separate mechanisms; public webhooks and provider callbacks as separate mechanisms; audit semantics; WebSocket non-durability; no distributed exactly-once guarantee (7A DEL-04; 7K INV-7K-04).

## 8. Phase 7D — Transactional Outbox Reconciliation

### 8.1 The publication boundary, as the combined contracts state it

| Step | Frozen rule | Later narrowing in force | Reconciled statement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Producing transaction | State and exactly one outbox row commit together (PTX-01 … PTX-04); Redis never gates a commit | 7F HCG-21: a publication fence in the producing transaction during a handler-obligation cutover | "Outbox publication" in owner documents means the row insert **inside** the transaction; "published after commit" describes relay publication (CNF-7F-09) |
| Claim | Only through `audit.fn_claim_outbox_events`; `SKIP LOCKED`; lease 300 s; batch 50 | 7I INV-20: executable by the relay principal alone (IR-01 … IR-03; not installed, §2.4) | One behaviour; the grant change is D-CSA (ERR-7I part of AP-7L-38) |
| Publish | Outside any transaction; `CONFIRMED` only by the 7E mechanism (TPT-02; ADR-7D-19) | 7F HCG-26, -27: publication admission and quiescence before a cutover boundary (CNF-7F-13) | Normal operation unchanged; the admission is a relay-runtime addition for cutovers only (AP-7L-34) |
| Mark published | Compare-and-swap in a short transaction | 7I ACC-13: the confirmed position is recorded beside the outbox in the same transaction by a superseding function (ERR-7I-13) | Position is transport position only; never an identity or a publish input |
| Ambiguous outcome | `UNKNOWN` is never `CONFIRMED`; every doubt resolves toward a duplicate, never a loss (ADR-7D-06; AMB-01 … -04) | — | Preserved; duplicates absorbed by domain-owned guards (7F) |
| Crash recovery | CRS-01 … CRS-10: lease expiry and reclaim; republication with the same `event_id` | 7K OBX-7K-10 … -12 | Preserved |
| Cleanup | `PUBLISHED` after 7 days; `FAILED` retained until a 7G disposition (CLN-02 … -04) | 7G §48 interlock (CNF-7G-01); 7I ACC-06: also every owed group accounted (ERR-7I-10) | The narrowest predicate is the behaviour: 7 days **and** every owed group has an accounting row or a case **and** no undispositioned `FAILED` |

### 9.3 Generation transition: one lifecycle across 7E, 7F, 7G, 7I and 7K

7E LCY-07 states five steps. Later frozen documents add steps without removing any. 7K §9.8 is the combined order (CNF-7K-03 = CNF-7F-14). 7L confirms the combination is consistent and identifies the one step that no frozen identity can execute.

| LCY-07 step | Added by | Combined requirement | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Provision keys and groups at `0` | 7F TK-1 … TK-6; 7I ACC-15 | Also: per-key handler-contract intervals for every active type; the group registration record; consumers admit the key **before** any relay may publish to it | Consistent; D-IMP (IO-7F-37; IO-7K-15) |
| 2 Deploy relays for `g<n+1>` | 7F TKO-05, -06 | The relay-enable gate is closed until the admission proof exists | Consistent |
| 3 Deployment gate: no relay on `g<n>` | 7K GEN: three-layer fence, including an ACL fence for old producers | Consistent; depends on CNF-7K-08 (c) (per-generation key patterns) | D-CSA (AP-7L-06) |

### 10.3 Per-stream append order versus claimed per-aggregate processing order

This is the one place where an earlier frozen sentence, taken literally, would make a consumer wrong. The reconciled position is stated once so that no downstream phase builds from the 7B sentence:

|---|---|
| ORD-7L-01 [FROZEN: 7E ORD-7E-01, -06, -09; 7F ORD-7F-01 … -08] | The only ordering the platform provides is append order within one physical stream key. Two events of one aggregate can arrive in either order, and a republished duplicate of an older event can arrive after a newer one. No consumer may depend on arrival order, including within one aggregate. |
| ORD-7L-02 [7L] | Until AP-7L-25 is applied, 7B IO-7B-08 and CR-04 are read as ORD-7L-01. An implementation that relies on per-aggregate order is non-conformant whatever the 7B sentence says, because 7F froze its design against ORD-7E-09 and 7E recorded the conflict (ORD-7E-10). |

| Recovery-case gate before the handler | RTY-01, RTY-02: a mandatory point read before D-09; `PARKED`, `REPLAYING`, `RECONCILIATION_PENDING` never run the handler |

| Billing deferred acknowledgement | BIL-01 … BIL-07: a Billing reconciliation entry stays pending until Billing's terminal decision (T-14) |

| A stopped replay changes no case | A plan's state (`STOPPED`, `CANCELLED`, `PAUSED`) is a state of the plan; no case transitions because an operation stopped (7G §42.3; 7K MRA-7K-17 (1)) |

## 13. Phase 7I — Security and Compliance Reconciliation

This is a high-scrutiny workstream. The governing distinction, repeated from 7I §24.3 and §29.4: **a documented policy is not an implemented control.** §2.4 shows that the installed grants are still the pre-7I grants. Every protection described below is designed; none is installed.

### 13.1 Designed controls and their installed state

| Area | Designed by 7I | Installed today (§2.4) | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|

### 13.5 OD-7I-30, OD-7I-31 and the `FROM_T0` limitation, stated accurately

| ID | Statement |
|---|---|
| SEC-7L-01 [FROZEN: INV-32; OD-7I-30] | The content access guard is designed for the **content-bearing event stores**: webhook deliveries, replay material, callback processing inputs, the sealed vault and the outbox payload paths of the CAG-05 inventory. It is not a guard on recordings, transcripts, documents or memories (CAG-17 (d)). |
| SEC-7L-02 [FROZEN: RR-12] | The guard is not atomic with an external handoff. A send that began inside the handoff margin can complete after the deadline by at most that handoff's timeout. This is disclosed under OD-7I-30 condition 9 and is not closed by any later document. |
| SEC-7L-03 [FROZEN: INV-33; OD-7I-31; RR-11] | For a `FROM_T0` organization, identity and association history from before the index existed is unknown and cannot be reconstructed. A missing historical edge is never read as "no earlier association". `FROM_T0` is never promoted to `FROM_ORIGIN`. The per-organization acceptance is a precondition of certification and is an input to no hold, deadline, decision or guard. **It is not proof of complete historical attribution and not evidence of compliance.** |
| SEC-7L-04 [7L] | A subject identity that predates the verified index-history epoch is therefore handled by classification as uncertain (HLD-25), never by assumption. The production rule is index-first, so that organizations are born `FROM_ORIGIN` (AB-7I-16). |
| SEC-7L-05 [7L] | No statement in this document, in a packet of §18 or in a contract template derived from them may describe the platform or a tenant as compliant with any law, certified, or approved by any regulator. 7I asserts none (7I §17.3, §29.4), and 7L asserts none. |

They are closed at design level; their implementation is gated by AB-7I-01, -05, -12, -13, -14. The items 7I *did* hand on are evaluated below against the installed schema.

It is not a Phase 7 design contradiction. It is **not** rated Minor by 7L and is **not** accepted by 7L: it lets the credential alter tenant business rows without the tenant's audit trail | **D-OWN** (OD-7L-10 a). Owners: 5B, 5D – 5J, 6M. Carried P1-class item against the Phase 5 / 6M administrator model; the independent reviewer rates it. 7L's recommendation: narrow before the 6M credential is used in production |
| (b) | `organization.organizations`: `INSERT, UPDATE` to `app_api`, `app_worker`; membership rows writable under `app_api` | RR-01; ARA-12 | Covered by RR-01 (a stolen runtime credential acts within that role's grants). **HE-7L-7I-11 — owning-context holds, sealing and index completeness.** Owed by each of the 5C – 5G owning contexts before any data-subject erasure runs there: (1) each owner-context erasure function takes the hold gate in share mode and calls the effective-hold function in its transaction, and is registered as an erasure step (HLD-14; the frozen `081_5F4` functions contain no hold check today); (2) that context's own sealing of an uncertain row past its limit (SEAL-13: "not designed in this document"); (3) the completed and classified index inventory (IR-50). **Disposition: D-CSA per context** (a governed design per context). **Concrete blocker: AB-7I-14 stays closed. No data-subject erasure is executed in any context.**

**HE-7L-7I-12 — owning-context access-time retention guard.** Not designed in 7I and not claimed (CAG-17 (d)): an access-time retention guard for recordings, transcripts, documents and memories equivalent to 7I §14.7b, and the reconciliation of their table grants with it. Also carried: RR-11, RR-12, CNF-7I-29, CNF-7I-30, and the frozen `LEGAL_HOLD` suppression reason of 4I §8.6, which 7I maps to no registry hold of its own.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| SEC-7L-06 [FROZEN minimum] | Until a governed design per context exists, or the owner records that a context's existing controls suffice: (a) no document, contract, product surface or report may state that owning-context content is inaccessible after its retention deadline, or that a hold or a seal restricts ordinary access to it; (b) the event-store protections of 7I are not to be described as protections of the owning domains; (c) recording and transcript access continues to rest only on the frozen RBAC of 6D and 6L (`call:read`, `transcript:access_content` and the rest), which is unchanged. |
| SEC-7L-07 [OD-7L-11; approved 2026-10-13] | **Gate AG-7L-01 is binding.** An owning context serves no production read of recordings, transcripts, `summary_text`, Knowledge documents or Conversation Memory until its access-time retention guard is governed, implemented and tested; expired content is denied at read time whether or not a purge has run. The earlier wording of this row, which proposed the gate and described it as not in force, is superseded. The full rule set is OCG-7L-01 … -10 (§33.4). |

**Disposition of HE-7L-7I-12: D-OWN** (OD-7L-11), with the concrete blockers AB-7I-14 (erasure) and SEC-7L-06 (no claim). It is not marked closed and is not rated Minor.

## 14. Phase 7J — Observability and SLO Reconciliation

### 14.1 What is preserved

| Subject | Frozen position |
|---|---|
| Telemetry is never authoritative state and never a control | PRN-01; SECM-01; 7K INV-7K-20. Passing a telemetry gate never opens a durability or security gate (7J §32) |
| No tenant or entity identifier as a metric label | LBL-01; 7I RED-07 |
| Trace propagation | Derived from `event_id` (TRC-01); **no envelope, entry or header field is added** (HE-7L-7J-10) |
| Error-budget governance | Rolling 28 days = exactly 672 consecutive UTC hours; a window with any unmeasured hour gives **no valid verdict** and moves no budget (OD-7J-02, -11) |
| Candidate objectives | Every numeric objective of 7J §11.2 is `PROPOSED / REQUIRES BENCHMARK`; none is binding until the owner approves it on measurement evidence (OD-7J-01; 7K SLO-7K-01) |
| Sampling and retention | 25% baseline plus the fault set (OD-7J-06); raw metrics 30 days, SLO aggregates 13 months, traces 14 days, alert history 13 months, incident records 2 years (OD-7J-03) |
| Erasure and telemetry | Telemetry always expires; required evidence is preserved separately; a failed preservation is recorded as a loss (OD-7J-08 … -10) |
| No CSAT label derived from sentiment | [FROZEN] 6L DEC-6L-01 = Option C: no CSAT in V1; 6L §38 classifies it as a producer gap. Checked: the string "CSAT" occurs in no Phase 7 document, and 7J contains no sentiment-derived metric, label or objective. The sentiment fields that 7B and 7C bind in payloads are not a CSAT source, and no packet of §18 makes them one |

### 14.4 The lifecycle-evidence lifetime `Λ` and the measurement parameters

`Λ` is the finite lifetime of organization status-transition evidence (ERR-7J-15), which SLI-11 needs to decide whether a delivery was eligible. 7J approved a candidate minimum; 7K analysed it; nobody has measured it.

| Parameter | Meaning | Status after 7K | Relation to `Λ` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `L` | Routine-fold lookback | [CAND] one hour (OAC-7K-02); correctness does not depend on it | None directly |
| `P_rf`, `P_cf`, `D_cf` | Routine fold period; completeness fold period and duration | [CAND] 15 s; one hour **if** BM-7K-12 shows the load acceptable, otherwise daily (OAC-7K-06) | `D_reg ≤ P_cf` plus any observer outage enters `D_settle` |
| `T_fold` | Oldest unregistered age threshold | [CAND] 15 minutes (OAC-7K-08) | None directly |
| `G`; settle delay | Grace before finalization; delay before a delivery is settled | [CAND] one hour; settle delay ≤ `G` | Settle delay enters `D_settle` |
| `T_final_lag` | Permitted finalization-watermark lag | Must be ≥ `P_cf + B_max + G + D_cf,max + margin`; [CAND] `P_cf` + 2 hours (OAC-7K-07) | None directly |
| `T_uncertain` | Threshold on `uncertain` deliveries | Informational only; any non-zero count raises a ticket-severity notice (OAC-7K-11) | — |
| `m` | Safety margin against a source's guaranteed life | `m ≥ D_cf,max` plus cleanup timing slack; [CAND] 24 hours (OAC-7K-04) | — |
| `R_min` | Source retention per stream | [FROZEN] 7 days for the two outbox-based streams; 30 days for the delivery-based streams (OAC-7K-03) | — |
| `T_unsettled` | Unsettled-window age threshold | [CAND] 30 days, set well below `Λ` (OAC-7K-17) | Must stay below `Λ` |
| `Λ` | Lifecycle-evidence lifetime | [CAND] 45 days as a **minimum** (OD-7J-15) | **Adequate for a delivery exactly when `D_settle = A_fanout + D_reg + B + settle delay < Λ`** (OAC-7K-13) |

| ID | Finding or rule |
|---|---|
| LAM-7L-01 [FROZEN: OAC-7K-14] | 45 days is adequate for the normal path, for design outages and for a restore. It is **not** adequate for recovery deliveries: a fan-out performed by an R2 replay of a parked case, by an R3 backfill or after a long consumer outage can create a first delivery more than 45 days after its event, and replay material alone lives up to 90 days (OD-7I-09). |
| LAM-7L-02 [FROZEN: OAC-7K-15; 7J AOA-27 (g)] | For those deliveries the frozen response is fail-closed: settled `uncertain`, basis `EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE`; the window is `NOT_ESTABLISHED`; no verdict; no budget movement. Nothing is assumed `ACTIVE`. |
| LAM-7L-03 [7L] | **The 45-day value is a candidate minimum under OD-7J-15. It is not proof of sufficient retention for every late replay, and 7L does not treat it as one.** |
| LAM-7L-04 [OPEN: OD-7L-05] | The final finite value of `Λ`, with its erasure, backup, restore and authorized-preservation treatment, is the owner's to approve, because a larger value lengthens the retention of lifecycle provenance (class `PID`). OD-7J-15 condition 2 requires 7K's validation first (T-7K-39; BM-7K-12), which has not been executed. 7K recommends neither 45 days nor "at least 90 days plus `P_cf` and margin" as final (OAC-7K-16). **7L therefore records no value.** |
| LAM-7L-05 [FROZEN: AG-7J-14] | Until OD-7L-05 is decided and IR-7J-48 is built and verified, **AG-7J-14 is closed**: SLI-11 is not reported in any form, M-290 for it is not emitted, and no objective on it (SLO-D1) can be approved. |
| LAM-7L-06 [7L; boundary on the future decision] | Whatever value is chosen must satisfy all of: finite (no indefinite retention; OD-7J-15); at or above the validated minimum; `T_unsettled < Λ`; removal only by the Organization context's guarded maintenance function under the organization row's share lock, taken first and with `SKIP LOCKED`, so that 7H ADM-04's lock order holds (ERR-7J-15); `covered_from` only moves forward; erasure, backup and restore treatment as 7I states for `PID`-class evidence. These are restatements of frozen conditions, not new policy. |

Findings for the owner before any objective is approved (HE-7L-7K-07), carried verbatim in substance: OAC-7K-11 (SLI-11 will often have no verdict: almost every suspension or reactivation of an organization that is actively receiving deliveries produces at least one `uncertain` delivery, which keeps the window without a verdict for up to 28 days); OAC-7K-12 (every database incarnation change, a lossless promotion included, leaves every accounted indicator without a verdict for 28 days); SLO-7K-03 (whether 99% of rows can be published within 2 s under `appendfsync everysec` is open); SLO-7K-05 (every publication objective is missed for `T_recap` after a single event-transport node failure). **D-OWN after measurement** (OD-7L-06).

## 15. Phase 7K — Failure Recovery and Regional Reconciliation

### 15.1 What is preserved

The twenty-two invariants INV-7K-01 … -22 of 7K §4 are frozen restatements of earlier rules; 7L relies on them unchanged. In particular: modular monolith, no new service or broker (INV-7K-01); PostgreSQL authoritative, Redis never (INV-7K-02); a committed outbox row is never lost (INV-7K-03); at-least-once, no exactly-once claim (INV-7K-04); `XADD` then same-connection `WAITAOF 1 1` (INV-7K-05); dedicated regional cluster, `noeviction`, one replica per primary (INV-7K-06); no acknowledgement without durable evidence (INV-7K-08); EV-079 only through the shared finalization, never synthesized (INV-7K-12); no bus on the voice hot path (INV-7K-13); no residency downgrade and no silent cross-region routing (INV-7K-15); no cross-region event bus (INV-7K-16); every irreversible erasure journaled, a recovered database quarantined (INV-7K-17); no numeric objective binding until measured and approved (INV-7K-21).

### 15.2 7K conflicts CNF-7K-01 … -11

| CNF-7K-05 | Billing origin check | D-ROD (OD-7K-04) + **D-CSA** | 7F, 7G, 7I | AP-7L-01 … -03 | **AG-7K-10** |

**None of the eleven is D-BLK.** For each of CNF-7K-05, -08, -09 and -10, the 7K design is complete, the frozen contracts as they stand assign exactly one behaviour, and that behaviour is the fail-closed branch: the Billing check stays off (SEC-7K-19), no key is deleted and no generation change is started (GEN-7K-11, SUP-7K-09), no recovered content is stored and the stack is not reopened (MRA-7K-06, -10, -13), no journal prefix or key is copied across regions (REG-7K-16). The capability is absent, not undefined.

### 15.3 The five controlled reconciliations

Each record follows the schema of §3.3 in full.

Relation to 6K: the check is one added statement inside the Billing consumer's owner transaction. It changes no tenant-visible contract, so **no 6K amendment is required for it**. The 6K amendment that Billing's EV-079 handler needs is the separate, earlier AP-7L-28.

| (a) Clearance | 7I JRN-13 step 5 | A restore-only *recovery privacy clearance* written by the restore reconciler for every restored `PUBLISHED` outbox row and every case restored in `OPEN_RETRY` or `HOLD` without material; verdict `CLEAR`, `BARRED` (with reason) or `HELD_RESTRICTED`; computed once per event; the row's record and every such case's record carry the same verdict | Not be writable by any other principal; not be stored only inside the database being restored in a way a second restore could replay as valid (the record names its incarnation; MRA-7K-06) | AP-7L-10 |
| (b) Refusal | 7I ACC-05, CAG-05 (7), HLD-10; 7G DSR-12 | A `PUBLISHED` row is captured only if its clearance is `CLEAR`, unconsumed and for the running incarnation, in one transaction under the organization's hold gate in exclusive mode with a current-timeline re-check; a non-`CLEAR` row is never captured and never republished; a consumed clearance means the row is never read again | **Add any waiting clause, or any clock of the restore.** ACC-03, ACC-16 and ACC-17 apply unchanged | AP-7L-11 |
| (c) Obligation, first form | 7G T-08, RPM-01, RSM-04; 7I JRN-25 | A restore-scoped entry into `RECONCILIATION_PENDING`, class `V`, no material, for an obligation with no admissible source: **the same case** where one exists; the first and only case of the identity where none does | Create a second case (7G PID-01); resolve a case (7G DAU-02); weaken 7I JRN-27 (the restore-only functions keep refusing once the database is activated; the post-activation path is a **separate** guarded ledger function) | AP-7L-12 |
| (c) Obligation, second form | 7G T-07 | A restore-scoped park-with-capture for a case whose source is **still eligible** when `T_obl` has passed since the capture time | Be used outside its incident and actor; let any state of a replay plan enter the condition; let any plan move the time | AP-7L-13 |
| (d) Verification | 7I JRN-26 | Count and equality assertions over clearances and cases; any difference keeps the environment quarantined | — | AP-7L-14 |

The ten categories that prevent `CLEAR` (7K MRA-7K-04), all preserved:

| # | Situation | Verdict | Frozen treatment preserved |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Subject erasure, completed or pending, reaching the attribution reference | `BARRED`, `SUBJECT_ERASURE` | 7I JRN-25 first principle; ERA-08; JRN-15 (b) |
| 2 | Organization erasure | `BARRED`, `ORGANIZATION_ERASURE` | 7I ERA-17 |
| 3 | A journaled time-based erasure names the case or row | `BARRED`, `TIMED_ERASURE` | 7I JRN-24; JRN-25 rows 6, 7, 10 |
| 4 | The row or case is sealed | `BARRED`, `SEALED` | 7I SEAL-02, SEAL-07 |
| 5 | A legal hold reaches the candidate | Alone: `CLEAR`. With any of 1 – 4, 6, 7: `BARRED`, `HELD_RESTRICTED` | A hold preserves; it does not authorize ordinary use past a deadline and never turns into a deletion (7I CAG-04, SEAL-14, HLD-03) |
| 6 | Attribution cannot be resolved | `BARRED`, `ATTRIBUTION_UNPROVEN` | 7I HLD-18: never classified as unrelated by default |
| 7 | Content deadline passed, or cannot be computed | `BARRED`, `DEADLINE_PASSED` | 7I CAG-01, CAG-09, CAG-13 |
| 8 | Restored row in an earlier lifecycle state than its journaled evidence | Decided after the 7I JRN-25 treatment | 7I JRN-25 |
| 9 | Journal records missing or contradicting the restored row | **No verdict is written** | 7I JRN-16: the stack stays quarantined; the supersession never starts |
| 10 | The journal copy cannot be proved complete (recovery kind F) | No verdict is written | 7I JRN-16; 7K REG-7K-20, -21 |

Rules that the packets must leave exactly as frozen, stated so that the reviewer can test them:

| ID | Rule | Frozen source |
|---|---|---|
| RST-7L-01 | **One clock.** The age of an unaccounted pair is database `now()` minus the earliest `recorded_at` of the row's positions, or the row's `published_at` where it has none. Positions recorded before the restore count as they stand. The time spent in quarantine is part of the age. No activation time, capture time or republication time enters the classification or the deadline | 7I ACC-17; 7K MRA-7K-16 (1) |
| RST-7L-02 | **A replay status never suspends the ACC-17 deadline.** An R4 that is `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, slow, stuck, unpublished or unavailable suspends nothing | 7K MRA-7K-16 (2) |
| RST-7L-03 | **A stopped replay plan never reclassifies a still-lawful capture as missing.** The class of a pair follows the eligibility of its source, never the state of an operation. `DRAFT` … `COMPLETED` are states of a plan; none changes a class | 7K MRA-7K-17 (1) |
| RST-7L-04 | **Successor plans never restart the operational replay deadline.** It is fixed at the capture; a successor plan is the unprocessed remainder of its predecessor, a new governed operation with its own approval; at most one publishes in the region at a time | 7K MRA-7K-16 (8); MRA-7K-17 (2), (3) |
| RST-7L-05 | **One permitted capture per source.** A consumed clearance means the row was captured once; its stored source, and never the row again, is what the restore's R4 publishes | 7K MRA-7K-06, -08, -15 |
| RST-7L-06 | **No superseded-stream content is read**, by any recovery step, whatever the verdict. No case receives bytes from a stream | 7K MRA-7K-05, -07 |
| RST-7L-07 | **No tombstone and no deletion of a `PUBLISHED` row.** The row "is transport", is "not altered" and ages out by its frozen lifecycle; the barrier is the refusal of the capture functions, not the absence of the bytes | 7I RET-01, CAG-02; 7K MRA-7K-10 (1), (2) |
| RST-7L-08 | **Source loss** leaves an explicit, unresolved, owner-visible case: class RM-4 (the same case moves) or RM-5 (the first and only case is opened); never `RESOLVED` by the restore | 7K MRA-7K-14; 7G DAU-02 |
| RST-7L-09 | **Billing deferred acknowledgement is unaffected.** A Billing case in `RECONCILIATION_PENDING` after a restore is released only by T-14; the money gate of OD-7K-03 stays closed until Billing's reconciliation | 7G BIL-04; 7K DRS-7K-17, -18 |
| RST-7L-10 | **Restore quarantine has no override.** Rows 9 and 10 write no verdict; the environment stays quarantined | 7I JRN-16; INV-18 |

**Naming delegated to 7L.** CNF-7K-09 leaves two internal reason codes for 7L to name. 7L proposes, as part of AP-7L-12 and AP-7L-13 and with the same approval status as those packets: `RESTORE_SOURCE_INADMISSIBLE` for the reason "the source may not be read, or does not exist, after a restore" (reasons 4 – 7 of MRA-7K-04 and a missing source), and `RESTORE_REPLAY_DEADLINE` for the restore-scoped park-with-capture of T-07. Both are internal ledger values; neither is a public error code, a state or a transition; each is distinct from the frozen `RESTORE_RECONCILIATION` parking reason of ERR-7I-15, which 7I uses for a case restored in `HOLD` with crash-loop material. `PRIVACY_MATERIAL_ERASED`, which reasons 1 – 3 use, is already frozen. The names are [PROP]: the 7G owner may substitute others when applying the packet, provided the two meanings stay distinct.

### 16.1 Proof that the combined contracts do not contradict each other

The proof is by exhaustive pairing of the rules that act on the same object. For each object, the rules are listed with what each requires; a contradiction would be two rules that require incompatible outcomes for the same state.

| Object | Rules acting on it | Why they compose |
|---|---|---|
| An outbox row after publication | 7D CLN-03 (deletable after 7 days); 7G §48 (not while an undispositioned `FAILED` exists); 7I ACC-06 (not until every owed group is accounted or has a case); 7I RET-01 ("not altered"); 7K MRA-7K-10 (no tombstone) | Each later rule only removes rows from the deletable set. The deletable set is the intersection, which is well defined. No rule deletes early or alters a row |
| A stream entry | 7E TRM-02, -03 (trim only at the watermark, never while a registered group is missing); 7G PAT-09 (never deleted individually); 7I RDS-10 (`XDEL` denied); 7K MRA-7K-07 (a superseded entry is never read) | An entry leaves only by safe trim or by destruction of a fenced, superseded or retired key. No rule reads a superseded entry and no rule deletes a live one |
| `XACK` for one (group, entry) | 7F XAK-05 (after the owner commit); 7G RTY-10 (after the case is resolved); 7G BIL-04 (Billing: after T-14); 7I GWY-08, -10 (after evidence and the accounting commit) | A strict sequence of preconditions; each is a conjunct. The earliest instant at which all hold is unique |
| A recovery case for one identity | 7G PID-01 (at most one); 7G state machine T-01 … T-18; 7I ERA-13 (no transition by erasure from `OPEN_RETRY` / `HOLD`); 7K CNF-7K-09 (c) (restore-scoped entries, same case) | The packets add triggers and actors to existing edges or one new edge into an existing state; none creates a second case; none adds an edge out of `RESOLVED` |
| The obligation deadline of a pair | 7I ACC-17 (one PostgreSQL clock); 7K MRA-7K-16 (no restore clock) | One clock, one definition. The packets forbid a second |
| A stream key's existence | 7E LCY-07 (retire after drain); 7G TPG-05 (not while a non-terminal operation references it); 7I RDS-10 (nobody may delete it); 7K GEN-7K-11, SUP-7K-09 | As frozen, the conjunction is "never deleted". That is a missing capability, not a contradiction: the state "key still present" is always safe. AP-7L-04 supplies the missing authority |
| A journal record's durability | 7I JRN-06, -07 (durable in the origin region before the erasure commits); OD-7K-05 (the copy is asynchronous and takes no part) | The copy is outside the write-ahead protocol, so it cannot conflict with it |
| A shard's capability | 7E CAP-01 … -09; 7K RED-7K-36 (start flag) | The start flag makes 7E's own condition CAP-04 (8) false until admission. 7K uses the frozen check as written |
| Tenant scope of one handler transaction | 7C TEN-C02 … -05; 7F TEN-7F-02; 7I TCX-05, INV-02; CNF-7F-08 (6C wording) | All frozen Phase 7 rules agree. The 6C sentence is documentary and equal by schema |
| The EV-079 occurrence time | 7B OCC-01 … -07; 7C §22; 7K VOX-7K-19; 7J CNF-7J-18 | One source of the time. Telemetry counts a late insert as a correction and does not redefine the time |
| A webhook request's signature set | 6J §21 (frozen scheme); 7H SIG-06, -07, -18; OD-7H-16, -17; ERR-7H-09 (revised) | The withdrawn early-cutoff clause was the only inconsistent statement; it is excluded (CHG-7L-06) |

**Three places where the frozen contracts, as written, do not yet assign a behaviour to a capability, each with a closed gate and a safe state:** the final status function of Campaign qualification (OD-7L-01; CON-05 does not run); the source of the recording cleanup key (OD-7L-02; CON-08 does not run); the plugin asynchronous result path (OD-7L-03; no ingress exists). None is a contradiction between two frozen rules about the same state, and none affects a capability that can be active.

(3) A zone failure pauses durable publication for the recapability interval; no committed event is lost, and the "under 5 minutes, no loss" target of §10.1 does not hold for publication latency as stated (7E HPR-02; 7K TOP-7K-07). (4) The second-region database replica, object replication and weekly snapshot of §11.1, §11.3 and §12 are **not** provisioned for a stack that hosts an `INDIA_ENTERPRISE` organization: every copy, backup, persistence file, object, key, telemetry store and the erasure journal stay in the contracted region, and destruction of that region is unrecoverable (OD-7K-01). For other stacks they exist only with a recorded residency-policy and contract authorization (OD-7K-02). (5) A restore, a point-in-time recovery and a promotion each produce a quarantined database that is activated only after erasure-journal reconciliation; the drill includes it (7I ERR-7I-12). (6) The regional targets of §12 are unvalidated; for a cross-region recovery no recovery-point or recovery-time objective is claimed after permanent loss of the origin region's erasure journal (OD-7K-05). ## 20. Versioning, Generation and Compatibility Consistency Checks

Four version axes exist and are never conflated: the internal durable `event_version` (7C); the topology generation `g<n>` (7E); the handler-contract generation per group (7F); the webhook topic version AX-E / AX-F (AVS; 7H §15). 7A VER-08 forbids describing AX-D as the axis of internal durable events.

| ID | Check | Sources compared | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| VER-7L-01 | Only a BREAKING change creates `event_version` N + 1; a closed-enum addition is BREAKING; a new PII or sensitive field is never COMPATIBLE | 7C §27 – §30 (MX-08, MX-16); OD-7C-01 | Preserved. No later document adds a field to a V1 payload or to the envelope |
| VER-7L-02 | A consumer validates the original version before idempotency and before any upcast; identity is the original `event_id` | 7C §32, §37; 7F VER-7F-01 … -08 | Consistent |
| VER-7L-03 | An unsupported version is held, never acknowledged; after `compat_hold_max_age` (24 hours) it is parked with exact material | 7C §33; 7F §24; 7G IMP-02, IMP-03 | Consistent |
| VER-7L-04 | The relay is schema-agnostic and never gates on the manifest | 7D MAN-04, MAN-05, ADR-7D-10 | Consistent |
| VER-7L-05 | Topology generation: no in-place re-partitioning; `P_f` never changes inside a generation; consumers read both generations until retirement | 7E LCY-05, LCY-07; 7F RDL two-generation reads, TKO-01 … -10 | Consistent; the retirement step lacks an authorized actor (§9.3; CNF-7K-08) |
| VER-7L-06 | Handler-contract generation: a worker reads only when capable of all of `H_active(g)`; a change is a closed-group cutover behind a publication fence; onboarding and a cutover are mutually exclusive per group | 7F HCG-01 … -31; 7H §16.3 | Consistent |
| VER-7L-07 | A recovery case survives a topology cutover: its material is in the ledger and never depends on a key (7G TPG-05); its canonical origin provenance is never overwritten by a replay or a later cutover (7F HCG-29; 7G PRV) | 7G §36, §37; 7F HCG-28 … -31 | Consistent after AP-7L-35 for sources captured before a later cutover |
| VER-7L-08 | Webhook body and headers are immutable across attempts and replays; a successor topic `X.vN` cannot be made subscribable before the receiver dedup question is settled | 7H HTP-04 … -06, VER-7H-06a; 6J §21.2 | Consistent; **successor behaviour open** (OD-7L-04; AB-7H-07 closed) |

## 21. Billing, Voice and Financial-Integrity Consistency Checks

### 21.1 The EV-079 path, end to end

| Step | Frozen rule | Installed? | Blocking item |
|---|---|---|---|
| Per-turn checkpoint accumulation of five metrics | 7B ACC-01 … -06; IO-7B-15 | No (`012_5C` has no accumulator) | Governed Phase-5 migration |
| Persisted service-end time for every way a call can end | 7B OCC-01 … -07; 7K VOX-7K-20; IO-7K-06 | No (`completed_at` is nullable; no rule names the value for a reaper-forced end) | AP-7L-27 |
| Finalization guard: at most one EV-079 per finalization generation | 7B IDN-10, IDN-11; IO-7B-16 | No | Governed Phase-5 migration |
| Shared finalization: claim guard → finalize usage → one EV-079 outbox row → commit | OD-7B-02; FIN-1 … FIN-4 | No | Phase 9 |
| Corrupt or missing state: no guard claim, no usage, no outbox row; durable `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` marker | 7K VOX-7K-16, -17; IO-7K-05 | No | Governed Phase-5 migration |
| Publication, transport, delivery | §8, §9 | No | AG-7K-01, -02 |
| Billing ingestion: horizon gate → (origin pre-guard, when active) → guard `uq_ue_idempotency` → usage rows → completion record | 7F §28.7; 7K §22.3 | No | AP-7L-28; AG-7K-03, -10 |
| Beyond the 90-day horizon, or origin-unverifiable: held, unacknowledged, until Billing's T-14 decision | 7F RET-7F-09; 7G §35; 7K SEC-7K-20 | No | 7F IO-7F-34; IO-7G-23 |

**Result.** The contracts are mutually consistent and assign one behaviour at every step. **Voice usage is not billable today**, and CON-06's `conversation.completed` handler stays `GOVERNED MIGRATION REQUIRED` (7F §35.2).

### 21.3 IO-7B-18 — reconciliation of abnormal or corrupt Voice state

7B hands this to 7L: "Reconcile conversations whose durable usage state is missing or corrupt. No charges are synthesized; Billing receives nothing for such a conversation until reconciliation resolves it." 7K's exit condition for HE-7L-7K-08 is "Reconciliation procedure defined by the Voice and Billing owners". 7L therefore fixes the frame the frozen rules already determine and leaves the business procedure to its owners.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| VRC-7L-01 [FROZEN: VOX-7K-16] | **Entry.** A conversation enters reconciliation only by the durable marker `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` with a coded reason on its finalization record, set by the shared finalization operation when the durable totals or the persisted service-end time are missing or fail validation. The marker is the work list. Until the marker exists physically (IO-7K-05), the recovery finalizer W2 is not activatable. |
| VRC-7L-02 [FROZEN: VOX-7K-17] | **Validation is total.** Every durable state is valid or corrupt; there is no branch in which a worker repairs a value. Minimum predicates: a service-end time is present, not earlier than the conversation's start and not later than the database clock; every total is non-negative; the turn counter agrees with the committed turns. |
| VRC-7L-03 [FROZEN: OD-7B-02; OCC-05; VOX-7K-18, -19] | **What reconciliation may never do.** Synthesize usage; supply a total, a time or a flag from an operator; default the occurrence time to a recovery actor's clock; emit a different event; write `usage_events`; send Billing anything for the conversation while the marker stands. |
| VRC-7L-04 [FROZEN: VOX-7K-18] | **Exit.** Leaving `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` is a Voice-owner action with a recorded reference: the Voice owner repairs or confirms the durable state through its own governed path and clears the marker; the same shared finalization is then invoked and produces the one EV-079, or returns `CORRUPT_STATE` again. |
| VRC-7L-05 [FROZEN: 7F RET-7F-09; VOX-7K-24] | **Interaction with Billing's horizon.** An EV-079 whose service-end time is older than Billing's 90-day evidence horizon is held by the Billing consumer for Billing-owned reconciliation and is never applied by the normal handler. A conversation unfinalized or marked for more than `T_fin_critical` ([CAND] 7 days) is escalated to the Voice and Billing owners. |
| VRC-7L-06 [7L] | **Audit.** Each exit is one audited owner action naming the conversation, the reason code, what was repaired or confirmed, the evidence used and the actor. This restates 7D OD-7D-02 for the owner path; it adds no mechanism. |
| VRC-7L-07 [OPEN] | **Left to the Voice and Billing owners, and not decided here:** (a) which durable evidence is admissible to repair a missing service-end time or total (for example provider call records); (b) whether, and under whose authority, a conversation may be closed as never billable; (c) the governed path and its permission; (d) any time limit for the owners' decision. Item (b) is a financial write-off policy and is the owner's. |
| VRC-7L-08 [FROZEN: RR-7K-04] | **No deadline forces resolution.** A corrupt conversation is never billed until an owner repairs it. An alert or a named owner is not a bound. This residual is pending acceptance (§26.1). |

Disposition of IO-7B-18: the frame is D-ARF; the procedure is **D-OWN** for the Voice and Billing owners (VRC-7L-07); activation is gated by AG-7K-06 and AG-7J-04.

### 22.1 The sixteen cross-checks

Each row states the frozen rule that carries the property, what the installed schema does today, and the gate. "Design holds" means the frozen contracts, read together, give the property. It never means the property is enforced in a running system.

| # | Property | Frozen rules | Design holds? | Enforced today? | Gate |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tenant context cannot be supplied by an untrusted event payload | 7A ADR-7A-11, TEN-02; 7C TEN-C02 … -05; 7F TEN-7F-02; 7I INV-02; `trg_outbox_tenant_check` (`077_5J1`) | Yes | Partly: the outbox tenant trigger exists; no consumer exists | AB-7I-01, -11 |
| 2 | Cross-tenant access is rejected | 7I §6, INV-04, INV-06; forced RLS on the tenant-owned relations; guarded cross-tenant functions return identifiers and state only | Yes | Partly: frozen RLS exists; the Phase 7 stores do not | AB-7I-01 |
| 3 | Domain-owned principals cannot silently inherit platform-admin authority | 7I CTX-01 … -14 (nine context principals, no role membership); INV-03 (no pipeline component connects as `app_platform_admin`); INV-21, INV-28 | Yes | **No.** One shared `app_worker`; the administrator still holds wide DML (§2.4) | AB-7I-01, -11 |
| 4 | `SECURITY DEFINER` and SQL function permissions are correctly represented | 7I INV-04, INV-20; PRV rules; a later `CREATE OR REPLACE` is read, not the first body (`crm.fn_merge_contacts` is `097_5D5`'s) | Yes, as designed | **No.** The three outbox functions are executable by `app_worker` and `app_platform_admin`; `fn_integrations_anonymize_org` by the administrator | AB-7I-01 |
| 5 | Redis gateway authorization cannot be bypassed by a replay worker | 7I INV-19; GWY-01 … -13; 7G ADR-7G-13 (R2 uses an internal path and never republishes to the shared stream; no stream write by R2 or R3); the repair publisher holds `XADD` only and passes publication admission | Yes | No transport exists | AB-7I-02, -03, -10 |
| 6 | Sensitive event content is not exposed by telemetry | 7I INV-07, RED-01 … -07; 7J LBL-01, TRC-09, LOG rules; OBP-04 payload-free observer | Yes | D0 redaction only | AG-7J-01, -02, -06 |
| 7 | Signed webhooks use the approved version and key policy | 6J §21; 7A WH-07 … -12; 7H SIG-01 … -18; OD-7H-12, -16, -17 | Yes | No dispatcher exists | AB-7H-02 |
| 8 | Unsafe egress and endpoint changes are blocked | 7H §14.4, DST-04 … -11, ELK-01 … -06; 7I INV-15, INV-21, EGR-01 … -07 | Yes | **No.** The administrator can still write `webhook_endpoints` | AB-7H-02; AB-7I-01, -06 |
| 9 | Erasure-journal completeness is mandatory on restoration | 7I INV-18, JRN-13, JRN-16; 7K REG-7K-20, -21 | Yes; no override | No journal exists | AB-7I-05; AG-7K-08 |
| 10 | Lawful trim and data retention are not confused | 7A §32.3; 7I §14.1; 7K INV-7K-19; RED-7K-39 (a removal is lawful by evidence of its execution-time state) | Yes | — | AG-7K-02, -09 |
| 11 | No subject's erased data is reconstructed from an old Redis stream | 7K MRA-7K-05, -07 (no superseded entry is read); 7I ERA-S2 (an entry leaves by safe trim; later fan-out reads tombstoned owner state); CNF-7K-09 | Yes, fail-closed: with CNF-7K-09 unadopted the stack is not reopened | — | AG-7K-08 |
| 12 | Legal holds do not authorize unrestricted reads | 7I INV-32: a hold changes how long content is preserved and through which restricted path it can be inspected; it never restores ordinary access; MRA-7K-04 row 5 (`HELD_RESTRICTED`) | Yes, **for the event stores** | No | AB-7I-14, -15 |
| 13 | Recording and transcript access respects approved RBAC | 6D, 6L (`call:read`, `transcript:access_content`); 7I INV-07 (no transcript, utterance or recording content in any event, body, log, metric or trace) | Yes for the event plane. **Owning-context access-time guards are not designed** (HE-7L-7I-12); `summary_text` under `call:read` is unreconciled (CNF-7I-09) | Frozen RBAC only | SEC-7L-06; OD-7L-11 |

**Reading.** All sixteen properties hold at design level. **None is fully enforced today**, and seven (rows 3, 4, 8, 14, 16 directly; 9 and 11 by absence of the mechanism) depend on controls that §2.4 shows are not installed. Each has a closed gate. This is the expected state after an architecture phase and is not a finding against the architecture; it would be a finding against any statement that the event infrastructure is production-ready.

### 22.2 Residency

| Profile / class | Frozen position | Copy outside the region | Regional-disaster objective |
|---|---|---|---|
| `INDIA_ENTERPRISE`; class E stack | Everything in the contracted region: copies, backups, Redis persistence files, objects, keys, telemetry stores, the journal (OD-7K-01 condition 1). Outbound webhook and plugin egress only by the tenant-directed permission and the enterprise lock (OD-7I-04) | **None.** A class E stack never falls back to class S | **None claimed.** Destruction of the region is unrecoverable (RR-7K-03, accepted) |
| `STANDARD`; class S stack | Region-local event transport; no cross-region event bus | A database, object and journal-prefix copy **only** with a recorded residency-policy and contract authorization (OD-7K-02 condition 1; REG-7K-17) | **None guaranteed.** Partial regional failure may be recoverable; permanent loss of the origin journal is not (RR-7K-09, accepted) |
| `REGIONAL` | Future; no topology designed | — | — |

No compliance certificate, India regulatory approval, statutory deadline, effective date or contractual sufficiency is asserted. Every legal question is in §26.3 and is unanswered.

## 23. Final Activation-Dependency Graph

### 23.1 The four statuses

They are never collapsed into one `PASS`.

| Status | Means | Who can set it | State after 7L |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DESIGN APPROVED` | The capability's design is in a document that passed its independent freeze gate | The independent review of that document | Set for 7A–7K (§2.3), except where a design question is open (§27) |
| `CONTRACT RECONCILIATION COMPLETE` | Every packet of §18 that the capability depends on has been authorized and applied to its target | The target documents' owners | **Set for nothing.** 0 of 41 packets are applied |
| `IMPLEMENTATION VERIFIED` | The migrations, functions, workloads and configuration exist and the gate's named tests, benchmarks and validations have passed with recorded evidence | The implementing phase and its reviewer | **Set for nothing.** Nothing is built (§2.4) |
| `PRODUCTION ACTIVATION AUTHORIZED` | An owner has authorized the capability for production on that evidence | The platform owner | **Set for nothing** |

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| ACT-7L-01 | A gate is closed until every condition in its own "until" clause is met by **executed** evidence (7K §29.2). A document, 7L included, opens no gate. |
| ACT-7L-02 | Gates compose by conjunction. A capability is activatable only when every gate that names it is open: the frozen gates of 7F §35, 7G §56, 7H §17.5, 7I §24, 7J §32 and 7K §29.2 all apply together, and no later gate replaces an earlier one (7J §32; 7K §29.2). |
| ACT-7L-03 | A gate that stays closed after the architecture freeze is acceptable only with a named owner, an exact exit condition and a fail-closed operating state. §23.3 gives all three for every gate. |
| ACT-7L-04 | **An unimplemented migration is never called an existing database control.** Every "Dependent migrations" entry below is a logical requirement on a future governed Phase-5 migration (CHG-7L-05). |
| ACT-7L-05 | Partial activations that the frozen documents prohibit stay prohibited: webhook fan-out without dispatch, or dispatch on the unfenced frozen functions (7H §17.5); a durable consumer before the recovery ledger exists (7G MIG-02); a durable consumer without its group's generation-1 handler-contract record (7F HCG-07). |

**Note on AG-7K-08.** As frozen, it gates "any stack serving production". It is therefore the widest gate in Phase 7: nothing serves production before the restore path, the supersession authority and the restore privacy clearance are consolidated, implemented and drilled. 7L does not narrow it.

### 23.4 Dependency order

The order below is the conjunction of the gate conditions. It is a statement of what depends on what, not a schedule.

1. **Owner authorization of the packets** (OD-7L-15) and the open decisions that a packet waits for (OD-7L-01, -02, -09).
2. **Governed Phase-5 migrations** (§24.2): roles and grants; outbox ACLs and the position record; recovery ledger; handler-contract record; completion and accounting records; transition functions; delivery schema extensions; journal state, hold registry, subject index, sealing, access guard; observer functions and accounting relations; Voice accumulators, guard and marker.
3. **Event-transport cluster** with the start configuration, ACL parity and the V-1 … V-3 validations (AG-7K-02) → **relay** (AG-7K-01) → **gateway and consumers** (AG-7K-03) → **recovery** (AG-7K-04).
4. **External delivery** (capabilities 5, 6) and the **owner-phase consumers** (CON-01 … CON-11), each behind its own row.
5. **Privacy operations** (capability 7), which must be open before the first retention deadline of any content-bearing row (AB-7H-05; AB-7I-05, -15).
6. **Restore path** (capability 8), which AG-7K-08 makes a precondition of serving production at all.
7. **Observability accounting** (capability 11) can follow go-live: until it is open the accounted indicators are simply not reported.
8. **Optional or later:** topology-generation change (4); class S cross-region recovery (9); Billing origin check (10).

## 25. Consolidated Measurement and Validation Obligations

### 25.1 Execution-state vocabulary

`EXECUTED / VERIFIED`; `SPECIFIED / NOT EXECUTED`; `INCONCLUSIVE`; `BLOCKED`; `NOT APPLICABLE`.

**State of every measurement, benchmark, test, drill and provider validation in Phase 7: `SPECIFIED / NOT EXECUTED`.** No row below is `EXECUTED / VERIFIED`. No throughput, latency, capacity, recovery-time or failure-recovery result exists, and none is described as verified anywhere in this document. The environment for all of them is one that does not exist yet: a deployed event plane on the actual managed PostgreSQL 18, object store, key service and Redis 7.2+ builds.

### 25.2 Benchmarks BM-7K-01 … -14

Results that feed an objective are delivered to the owner; approval is the owner's (SLO-7K-08).

| RSK-7L-02 | A risk that affects financial correctness, tenant isolation, erasure or mandatory work carries a **safe operating boundary**: the closed gate or frozen control that holds whether or not the risk is ever accepted. It is never deferred to implementation without one. |

### 29.3 Adversarial counterexamples

For each: the authoritative rule, the single expected behaviour, and the gate at which it is validated. **"Basis" is `REASONED` for all twenty-five: every one rests on architectural reasoning over frozen text. None was executed, and none is a `PASS`.** "Deterministic" asks whether the combined frozen contracts assign exactly one behaviour.

The owner reconciler's state scan finds the work and runs it; a late reconciler only adds duplicates. The audit row is not at risk: it committed with the transaction. A durable event is not at risk: its outbox row committed with the transaction | T-7K-33; AG-7K-06 | Yes |
| 2 | Relay publication becomes `UNKNOWN` | 7E WAO-02 … -05; 7D AMB-01 … -04, ADR-7D-06 | Never `CONFIRMED`; the row is not marked published; after lease expiry it is republished with the same `event_id`; a duplicate is absorbed by the consumer's guard | T-7K-09, -17; AG-7K-01 | Yes |
| 3 | A Redis entry survives without a confirmed publication | 7E ACC-02; 7F ADR-7F-01; 7I ACC-13; 7K RED-7K-39 | A group may read and process it. The later republication is a duplicate (`ALREADY_COMMITTED`). The position record is written only when the row is marked published; the completion record then accounts the pair. The entry is not in the demanded durable set | T-7K-07, -11; AG-7K-02, -03 | Yes |

In operation it is an integrity anomaly: a position-keyed `TRANSPORT_INTEGRITY` case; the identity is recovered from the position record and the outbox row; ACC-16 classes the pair `GONE` and ACC-05 opens the obligation case | 7E IO-7E-12; T-7K-10, -11, -42; AG-7K-02 | Yes |

## 30. P0 / P1 / Minor Freeze-Gate Findings

### 30.1 Severity reading used

P0 and P1 are as the Phase 7L assignment defines them. The clause "without an explicit safe boundary" is read as qualifying the P1 list: an unresolved owner decision, a missing contract or an implementation-blocking ambiguity is P1 when the affected capability could be built or activated in an unsafe or undefined state, and is not P1 when the capability is closed by a named gate with a fail-closed state. An unexecuted benchmark is not a P1 while its feature stays gated. **If the reviewer reads "unresolved material owner decision" as P1 regardless of a safe boundary, the candidates are OD-7L-01, -02, -03, -10, -11 and -15, and the status of §32 would then be `BLOCKED ON OWNER DECISION`.** That reading is stated so that it can be applied without re-deriving it.

| **P1** | **0** | No substantive contradiction between two frozen rules about the same state (§16.1). Every missing contract (CNF-7K-05, -08, -09, -10; CNF-7F-02 … -07, -13, -14; CNF-7G-02, -05, -06, -09) has a complete packet or a named open decision, and a closed gate with a fail-closed state (§23.3). At first submission: fifteen owner decisions; thirty-two residual-risk acceptances; forty-one packets, none applied. **After the first remediation (§33.12):** OD-7L-01 … -22 approved; one new deferrable question (OD-7L-23); thirty-two risks still unaccepted, each with a proposed disposition; forty-eight packets, none approved for application and none applied; every activation gate closed; every measurement unexecuted; the legal and contract register unreviewed.

This document does not declare Phase 7L, or Phase 7, approved or frozen. That is the act of the independent final freeze-gate review and of the owner. The first submission's status was superseded by the review outcome; the current status line is in §33.14.

### 33.3 FG-7L-01 — Financial authenticity gate

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| FAG-7L-01 [OD-7L-16] | **CON-06 MUST NOT apply a billable financial effect in production unless server-authoritative origin verification is active and its own activation evidence is complete.** This holds for every event type CON-06 consumes: `call.ended`, `conversation.completed` (EV-079), `document.indexed`, `campaign.contact.call_attempted`, `workflow.execution.completed`. |
| FAG-7L-02 [OD-7L-16] | **Gate AG-7L-02.** Production activation of the logical group `cg.billing.usage-ingestion` requires, in addition to every gate that already names it: (a) IO-7K-08 implemented; (b) AP-7L-01, -02, -03 and -42 authorized and applied (stage 3 of OD-7L-15); (c) BM-7K-09 executed and accepted; (d) T-7K-31 (a) … (j) and T-7L-01 passed; (e) a security test of the origin function's ACL, definer rights and digest; (f) the owner's explicit activation approval. AG-7K-10's conditions are a subset of these. |
| FAG-7L-03 [7L] | **How this reconciles with frozen 7K without editing it.** 7K SEC-7K-19 says: "Until AG-7K-10 holds, CON-06 runs as frozen and 7I RR-03 stays covered by detective controls only", and AG-7K-10 gates "the origin check in production". Both were written under OD-7K-04, whose record says the decision blocks "production activation of the check only". OD-7L-16 is a later owner decision on the question 7K left open: whether CON-06 may run in production without the check. Under GOV-7L-02 it governs exactly that scope. It contradicts no 7K rule about the check's design (SEC-7K-10 … -18, -20 … -24 are untouched); it withdraws one permission, the first clause of SEC-7K-19. **The frozen 7K text is not edited; it is aligned by AP-7L-42 when its owner applies it. Until then the binding effect comes from OD-7L-16 as recorded here and from AG-7L-02.** |
| FAG-7L-04 [7L] | **Enforcement, using mechanisms that are already frozen.** (1) *Admission.* No durable worker issues its first `XREADGROUP` without its group's generation-1 handler-contract record (7F HCG-07; IO-7F-31: "there is no bootstrap mode"). The generation-1 record of `cg.billing.usage-ingestion` is provisioned only by the governed step that records AG-7L-02's evidence. Until it exists no Billing worker is admitted, so no entry is read and no effect is applied. (2) *No switch.* The origin pre-guard of AP-7L-01 is unconditional in every build of the CON-06 handler: no configuration value, environment variable, feature flag, build option or operator action disables or skips it. A build-conformance check rejects a CON-06 handler that reaches the guard statement on any path that has not passed the pre-guard. (3) *Fail closed.* If the origin function is absent, errors, or refuses the caller, the result is the frozen "Unavailable" row of 7K §22.3: no effect, dependency gate open, entry pending. |
| FAG-7L-05 [7L] | **What is not enforced by the above, stated.** A recorded gate enforces nothing. (1) and (2) are enforced by the frozen admission mechanism and by a build check; they do not exist until 7F IO-7F-31 and the handler are built. Before then nothing can run at all (§2.4), which is the safe state. |
| FAG-7L-06 [FROZEN, preserved] | Unchanged: OD-7K-04; the guard `uq_ue_idempotency` and the horizon gate (7F §28.7; SEC-7K-17); the Billing deferred acknowledgement (7G BIL-01 … -07, as extended by AP-7L-02); the gateway evidence rule (7I GWY-08, as extended by AP-7L-03); the distinction between `ORIGIN_MISMATCH` (a position-keyed integrity case for the entry) and `ORIGIN_ABSENT` (duplicate, or `ORIGIN_UNVERIFIABLE` held for Billing); the 7-day outbox cleanup under the accounting interlock; reconciliation of a legitimate delayed event through a captured source or Billing's T-14 decision; no new refund or payment-settlement authority; every `WAITAOF 1 1` transport rule. |
| FAG-7L-07 [7L] | **Consequence for transport retention, disclosed.** Groups are created at `0` before relay activation (7E BST-01), and a group that is not consuming pins the trim watermark of the families it subscribes to (7E TRM-02; RR-7K-02). If the event plane is activated while AG-7L-02 is closed, entries for the Billing group accumulate on the `voice`, `knowledge`, `campaign` and `workflow` family keys, and no usage is ingested or lost: the entries are retained and the outbox rows stay under the accounting interlock (7I ACC-06). The pacing of 7K §13 applies. In practice AG-7L-02 is a go-live prerequisite of any deployment that produces billable events at volume. 7L sets no deadline and discards nothing. |
| FAG-7L-08 [OD-7L-16] | **Not offered:** a monitoring-only mode; an interim acceptance of RR-03 for the financial effect; a per-type exemption; a bypass for replay, backfill or R2. R2 "still runs the whole pipeline, including this check" (SEC-7K-17). |
| FAG-7L-09 [7L] | Non-production environments are outside OD-7L-16's wording ("in production"). They may exercise CON-06 without the gate's evidence; they still carry the unconditional pre-guard of FAG-7L-04 (2), because the build is the same. |

**Regression T-7L-01 — a forged entry arrives before the authentic one.** Specified; **not executed**. Owner: Billing. Gate: AG-7L-02.

| Case | Setup | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| (a) | Authoritative outbox row present. A forged entry with the same `event_id` and different payload bytes is appended first; the genuine entry second | Forged: `ORIGIN_MISMATCH`; a `TRANSPORT_INTEGRITY` case on (group, key, entry ID); no usage row; acknowledged only after that case commits. Genuine: `ORIGIN_MATCH`; exactly one set of usage rows. No case on (group, `event_id`) |
| (b) | As (a), forged `organization_id` | As (a); no row in any organization but the authoritative one |
| (c) | As (a), forged `event_type` | As (a) |
| (d) | Row already cleaned up; the event was never processed; forged entry first | Neither is applied. One class `V` case, `RECONCILIATION_PENDING`, `ORIGIN_UNVERIFIABLE`; the second arrival is a differing variant on the same case; **no `XACK` for either** until Billing's T-14 decision |
| (e) | Row cleaned up; a captured source exists | The entry whose digest matches the captured source is `ORIGIN_MATCH`; the other is held as (d) |
| (f) | A forged entry with a **new** `event_id` that has no outbox row and no usage evidence | `ORIGIN_ABSENT`, not a duplicate: held; nothing applied |
| (g) | Origin function unavailable while the forged entry is delivered | No effect; dependency gate open; entry pending |
| (h) | The same sequence driven through R2 replay | As (a) – (f): the check runs in replay |
| (i) | A CON-06 build with the pre-guard removed or made conditional | Rejected by the build-conformance check; never admitted |
| (j) | A Billing worker started with no generation-1 handler-contract record | Not admitted; no `XREADGROUP` issued |

### 33.4 FG-7L-02 — Owning-context retention guard

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| OCG-7L-01 [OD-7L-11] | **AG-7L-01 is binding.** No owning context serves production traffic that reads content of the kinds below until its access-time retention guard is designed under governance, implemented and tested. SEC-7L-07's "[PROP]" status is withdrawn; SEC-7L-06 remains in force until AG-7L-01 opens for a context. |
| OCG-7L-02 [OD-7L-11] | **Access-time eligibility is a precondition of every ordinary content read.** A read of owning-context content returns the content only while the database clock is before that content's authoritative retention deadline. From that instant no tenant read, worker read, export, search hit, embedding lookup, download link or diagnostic obtains it, **whether or not any purge, sealing or deletion has run**. |
| OCG-7L-03 [OD-7L-11] | **A scheduled purge and an alert are not access controls.** The purge removes bytes; the guard denies reads. Neither substitutes for the other, and no document may cite a purge schedule, a backlog alert or a named owner as the control. |
| OCG-7L-04 [7L] | **Scope: four content families.** (1) Voice recordings: object bytes and any presigned access to them. (2) Voice transcripts and transcript segments, **and `conversations.summary_text`**. (3) Knowledge documents, document versions and derived chunks. (4) Conversation Memory entries. The classified index inventory of 7I IR-50 is the list of relations; a relation outside it holding such content is a defect. |
| OCG-7L-05 [7L] | **The deadline is the owning context's own.** It is fixed by that context's retention contract (its `RetentionProfile` and the frozen retention rules of its Phase 4 – 6 documents), computed inside the database by a function that the read path, the purge predicate and any sealing all call. 7L defines no deadline and changes no retention period. A missing or inconsistent input denies. |
| OCG-7L-06 [OD-7L-11] | **Held or sealed content keeps its restricted path.** A legal hold or a seal changes how long content is preserved; it never restores ordinary access after the deadline. Content preserved past its deadline is reachable only through the existing authorized restricted pathways: the purpose-bound, durable, releasable break-glass grant for sensitive voice content (`107_5B5`; 6M §9), and the dual-controlled inspection of held or sealed material (7I OD-7I-30). No new pathway is created. |
| OCG-7L-07 [OD-7L-11] | **`summary_text` is sensitive content.** It is returned only to a caller holding `transcript:access_content`. To a caller with `call:read` alone the field is absent or `null`. The only exception is a separately approved, demonstrably safe redacted projection, which does not exist and is not designed. |
| OCG-7L-08 [7L] | **Per-context deliverables**, each a governed design owned by its context: (a) the deadline function; (b) a guarded read function per content relation, with the guard inside it; (c) grants such that no login role holds `SELECT` on a content column or object reference except through that function; (d) object-store access issued only by the guarded path, with no presigned URL outliving the deadline; (e) the hold and seal binding of 7I HLD-14 and SEAL-13; (f) regression tests: a stopped purge worker with content past its deadline is unreadable on every path; a held row is unreadable ordinarily and readable through the restricted path; a derived artefact (chunk, embedding, summary) is covered; a replica read is covered. |
| OCG-7L-09 [7L] | **The two retention contracts stay distinct.** 7I §14.7b governs the content-bearing event stores. OCG-7L-01 … -08 govern the owning contexts. An event-store control is never cited as protecting an owning-context row, and the converse. |
| OCG-7L-10 [7L] | **Not atomic with a handoff.** As for the event stores (RR-12), a response that began before the deadline can complete after it by at most its timeout. This is stated, not hidden; it is added to the residual register as part of RR-12's class and needs its own acceptance (§33.9). |

Owners: Voice (5C / 6D) for families 1 and 2; Knowledge (5F / 6F) for 3; Memory (5G) for 4. Dependencies: 7I IR-49 … -53; OD-7L-02 for recording objects. Packet: AP-7L-43.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| PRM-7L-01 | **7L revokes nothing and grants nothing.** Every correction below is a future governed Phase-5 migration with its own number, authored and approved under the Phase-5 change process. Migrations `001` – `112` are not edited. |
| PRM-7L-02 [OD-7L-10] | **Gate AG-7L-03.** No runtime database role is authorized for production until every corrective migration that names it has been **executed** and its catalogue assertions pass on the executed schema. A statement that a future migration will fix a permission authorizes nothing. |
| PRM-7L-03 [OD-7L-10] | Broad privileges are not accepted as a permanent risk. Until AG-7L-03 opens, RR-01 and the items below stay open and the affected credentials are not used in production. |
