The table gives these at requirement level; the migration author completes them. |
| PRM-7L-05 | **No new security privilege is created by this section.** Where a correction needs a new principal (the relay role, the context principals, the maintenance principal), that principal was already decided by an approved 7I owner decision, cited in the row. Its exact grant list is stage-3 material under OD-7L-15 and needs its security review before the migration is authored. |
| PRM-7L-06 | Four kinds of item are kept apart in the "Kind" column: **P5** an existing Phase 5 security defect (the installed catalogue is wider than any frozen contract needs); **6M** a divergence from the frozen 6M contract; **P7** a new Phase-7-specific worker privilege; **FUT** a future governed migration for something no migration defines. |

**The 6M divergence, verified.** Frozen 6M §9 item 2 states that `app_platform_admin`'s "direct table grants are minimal: `SELECT` only on `organization.organizations`, `billing.refunds`, `billing.payment_attempts`, `billing.quota_configs`; full DML on `billing.invoices` …; **zero** grant on `voice.recordings`, `voice.transcript_segments` …, `voice.conversations`, `voice.turns`, `voice.transcripts`". The installed migrations agree for the relations 6M names (`105_5B4` L377; `106_5H3` L257, L459 – L460; `107_5B5` L857 – L861). They do **not** agree with "minimal" elsewhere: the schema-wide grants of `025_5D` L20 (`crm`), `033_5E` L14 (`campaign`), `044_5F` L14 (`knowledge`), `046_5G` L14 (`memory`) and `074_5J` L23 (`analytics`) have no later `REVOKE` for that role in any of those schemas; `046_5G` L12 – L13 (`workflow`, `prompt`) and `058_5H` L4 (`billing`) are narrowed only for the named relations of `100_5G1` and `109_5B7`; `018_5C` L10 (`voice`) is narrowed only for the five relations above and `voice.agents` insert. Combined with `BYPASSRLS` (`001_5B` L44), the credential can therefore write tenant rows that 6M says it reaches only through `SECURITY DEFINER` functions.

### 33.7 Voice and Billing reconciliation contract

VRC-7L-01 … -06 and -08 stand. **VRC-7L-07 is superseded:** its four open items are decided by OD-7L-17 … -22.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| VBR-7L-01 [OD-7L-17] | For a conversation whose call ended abnormally (process crash, or an end forced by the stale-session reaper), the service-end time is the timestamp of the **last validated, durably committed per-turn checkpoint that proves the supported service interval**. |
| VBR-7L-02 [OD-7L-17] | That checkpoint qualifies only if the Voice contract (the 6D amendment, AP-7L-27 (iii)) defines it so that (a) it establishes the accounting cutoff and (b) it corresponds to the committed usage totals of the same transaction. **A generic last-turn timestamp is not sufficient by itself.** Until the amendment defines such a checkpoint, and the accumulator migration (G-02) persists it, every abnormally ended conversation is `CORRUPT_STATE`. |
| VBR-7L-03 [OD-7L-17] | Never a source of a service-end time: the recovery worker's clock; the scheduler tick; Redis state; a log entry; an estimated duration; the relay or delivery time; and, by itself, the telephony provider's call-end time, where that interval is not supported by durable platform usage evidence. |
| VBR-7L-04 [OD-7L-18] | **Admissible repair evidence, and only this:** (1) authenticated, committed platform records (turn records, accounting checkpoints, durable usage evidence); (2) verified provider call records from an authorized telephony adapter, with authenticated origin and reliable correlation to the conversation. |
| VBR-7L-05 [OD-7L-18] | Provider evidence may corroborate call identity, call duration and start and end times. **It never creates AI usage totals, token counts, tool usage or any other platform-consumption record.** Not evidence: an operator-supplied value, an estimate, a frontend value, the hot-tier cache, an untrusted provider payload, an application log. |
| VBR-7L-06 [OD-7L-18] | A repair verifies tenant identity, call identity, source provenance, timestamp validity, accounting consistency and the existing finalization state. If the evidence cannot establish an exact supported value, the state stays unrepaired and unbilled. No repair mutates a finalized or paid invoice. |
| VBR-7L-07 [OD-7L-19] | **Dual control.** A Voice-authorized principal verifies the durable evidence and proposes or records the repair. A **different** Billing-authorized principal approves any correction that affects billable usage or a financial quantity. Platform administrators, event operators and unrestricted service credentials cannot perform or bypass either step. |
| VBR-7L-08 [OD-7L-19] | After authorization only the shared finalization operation (7B FIN-1 … FIN-4) and Billing's own accounting mechanisms apply the result. Nobody changes a finalized invoice directly; nobody fabricates EV-079. Any new function, privilege or workflow transition is specified by AP-7L-45 and **does not exist and is unavailable** until implemented and validated. |
| VBR-7L-09 [OD-7L-20] | **Non-billable disposition.** A conversation whose durable accounting state is irreparable may be closed as non-billable only by an explicit Billing-authorized decision with independent review, documented evidence, a reason code and the audit record of VBR-7L-12. Never by elapsed time, by repeated reconciliation failure or by a scheduled worker. |
| VBR-7L-10 [OD-7L-20] | The disposition (1) preserves the conversation and its reconciliation evidence under the approved retention rules; (2) prevents any unsupported charge and any invented usage; (3) is durable, idempotent and auditable; (4) keeps irreparable conversations, and any supportable loss exposure, in financial reporting; (5) is mutually exclusive with finalization for the same finalization generation, so that no EV-079 can commit afterwards and no second disposition can; (6) keeps Voice state reconciliation and Billing financial authority separate. |
| VBR-7L-11 [OD-7L-20] | **Terminology and limit.** It is an operational disposition of **unbilled** service. It is not an accounting write-off of an existing receivable and is never described as one. A receivable write-off, refund, credit or general-ledger posting needs its own accounting evidence and the approved Billing permissions. No monetary loss amount is fabricated. **The frozen contracts do not define this terminal disposition** (7K VOX-7K-18 leaves `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` only through repair and finalization), so it is specified by AP-7L-45 and stays disabled until approved, implemented and tested. |
| VBR-7L-12 [OD-7L-21] | **Audit.** Every authorized repair, financial-impacting correction and non-billable disposition commits its state transition and its audit record in one PostgreSQL transaction (OD-7D-02). The record contains: organization ID and conversation / call ID; operation ID; reason code and operation type; references to supporting evidence, without embedding sensitive content; previous durable accounting state; resulting state; Voice proposer identity and independent Billing approver identity; authorization and decision timestamps; financial classification where applicable; event / finalization correlation identifiers and the idempotency identity. It is immutable under application and administrator permissions (the frozen audit relation: `072_5J`). If it cannot be persisted, the action fails atomically. An asynchronous or best-effort audit is not a substitute. |
| VBR-7L-13 [OD-7L-22] | **The 90-day horizon decides nothing.** It never authorizes billing, a write-off, a non-billable disposition, an invoice modification or the deletion of unresolved reconciliation evidence. A conversation repaired after its service-end time is more than 90 days old emits EV-079 only when every frozen validation, generation and idempotency condition holds, with its **original** service-end time; CON-06 holds it for Billing-owned reconciliation (7F RET-7F-09; 7G §35) and applies no ordinary billable effect. Any financial disposition needs its Billing authorization, evidence and audit; a late adjustment uses the frozen Billing adjustment mechanism; finalized and paid invoices are immutable. A seven-day escalation is a [CAND] operational target (7K VOX-7K-24), never a financial trigger. |
| VBR-7L-14 [7L] | **Gate AG-7L-04.** The Voice repair, accounting-correction and non-billable-disposition workflows are disabled until: AP-7L-27 and AP-7L-45 are complete, approved (stage 3) and applied; the migrations for the checkpoint, the guard, the marker and the disposition record exist; the two authorities and their functions exist with no administrator or event-operations path; and regression T-7L-02 passes. AG-7K-06 and AG-7J-04 apply in addition. |

**Regression T-7L-02** (specified; not executed; owners Voice and Billing): (a) a stale conversation with no qualifying checkpoint → `CORRUPT_STATE`, no EV-079, no usage; (b) a reaper-forced end writes no service-end time from its own clock; (c) a repair attempted with an operator-typed value is refused; (d) provider evidence alone cannot set a token or usage total; (e) proposer and approver being the same person is refused; (f) an administrator or event-operations credential cannot call the repair or disposition function; (g) a non-billable disposition followed by a finalization attempt for the same generation produces no EV-079; (h) a second disposition is a no-op; (i) the audit insert is made to fail and the transition rolls back; (j) a repair after 90 days emits EV-079 with the original service-end time and CON-06 holds it; (k) a scheduled worker cannot create a disposition.

**AP-7L-23 — 7E FMD-09 (b)** (authority OD-7L-09; stage S3). A **replacement** node is a membership change and keeps its explicit per-instance authorization. A missing, failed or inconclusive proof refuses the admission; no operator and no automation may clear the flag without it. **AP-7L-32 — 6H and 4D** (authority OD-7L-01; stage S2). 6H §24.3 (L1370): the clause "`WHERE id = ... **AP-7L-46 — 3F §16.3** (authority OD-7L-13; stage S2). Replacement of the per-key-space eviction table for the shared hot-tier cluster: ⟦The shared hot-tier cluster uses `maxmemory-policy volatile-lru` on every node. Every cache and session key that may be evicted carries a TTL, enforced at the write wrapper; a write of such a key without a TTL is refused. Broker, queue, lock and every correctness-critical key carries no TTL and is therefore never evicted. An active Voice session's state is either held under a key class that is not evictable or is recoverable without loss from PostgreSQL. When no volatile key remains, writes fail with `OOM`; callers treat that as a retryable dependency failure and apply backpressure. Each key space has a named owner, a memory limit, eviction monitoring and a recovery responsibility. Eviction never excuses the loss of durable work or authoritative state: such state is in PostgreSQL. The dedicated event-transport cluster is unaffected and stays `noeviction` (7E).⟧ Gate **AG-7L-05**: TTL discipline, memory-pressure behaviour and workload isolation validated before the shared cluster carries production traffic. **Approval NOT GIVEN. NOT APPLIED.**

**Governance.** §34 is narrow. §1 – §33 stand except where §34.14 lists a row as changed in place. **Where §34 and an earlier section differ, §34 governs.** No approval in this section is inferred. OD-7L-23 … -29 were put to the platform owner on 2026-10-14 as options with a recommendation. Each was then approved in writing with conditions, and every condition is mapped to a rule below (§34.2). This remediation authors no migration, executes none and edits no frozen document. Every function, trigger, grant, record and check named in §34 is **designed** (AUT-7L-05). None exists.

**Citation correction made in this remediation (FND-7L-09, Minor).** §33 cited the administrator principles of frozen 6M as "6M §4". 6M §4 is *Non-Goals*. The principles are **6M §9** ("Architecture Principles & Invariants"): item 1, cross-tenant mutation only through `SECURITY DEFINER`; item 2, minimal direct grants; item 3, `session_user` trust; item 4, refund settlement by `app_billing_reconciler` only; item 5, purpose-bound break-glass. The occurrences in §33 are corrected in place (§34.14). The substance of each citation is unchanged.

**How the seven were obtained, stated so it is not mistaken for inference.** OD-7L-23 was opened by the review. OD-7L-24 … -29 arose from this remediation's source reading, which found choices that no frozen source settles: the frozen 6M administrator invoice capability (OD-7L-24); producer behaviour under a prolonged Billing stall (OD-7L-25); the clock of the checkpoint (OD-7L-26); whether the Billing admission rule extends to every registered group (OD-7L-27); the CON-09 count predicate (OD-7L-28); and whether domain-owner wording may follow the freeze (OD-7L-29). Each was asked before the affected rules were finalized.

### 34.3 FG-7L-R2-01 — Financial record immutability and administrator privilege

#### 34.3.1 Root cause, verified in the executed migrations

| # | Installed fact | Source | Consequence |
|---:|---|---|---|
| F-1 | `billing.fn_invoice_immutability()` acts only `IF OLD.status IN ('PAID','VOID')`, and then only on `subtotal_amount`, `total_credits_amount`, `total_tax_amount`, `total_due_amount`, `billing_period_id`, `currency`. It never compares `NEW.status` with `OLD.status` | `054_5H` L50 – L63 | `UPDATE … SET status = 'DRAFT'` on a `PAID` row changes no guarded column, so it passes. The row is then `DRAFT`, and the next `UPDATE` of any total is not guarded at all |
| F-2 | The trigger is `BEFORE UPDATE` only. There is no `INSERT` or `DELETE` guard on `billing.invoices` | `054_5H` L63 | A direct `INSERT` can create a row already `OPEN` or `PAID` (the `CHECK`s demand only a number and a timestamp); `DELETE` is restricted only by foreign keys |
| F-3 | `invoice_lines` and `tax_lines` have no trigger at all. `UPDATE`, `DELETE` are revoked from `app_api` and `app_worker` only | `054_5H` L93 – L96, L120 – L123 | The administrator may update or delete any line of a finalized or paid invoice. `app_worker` may `INSERT` a line into an `OPEN` or `PAID` invoice, which contradicts 5H INV-BILL-02 ("no lines may be added") |
| F-4 | `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on `invoices`, `invoice_lines`, `tax_lines` to `app_platform_admin`, repeated schema-wide by `058_5H` L4. No later migration revokes it for these three relations or for `billing_accounts` (`048_5H` L39). `106_5H3` and `109_5B7` revoke it for eleven other `billing` relations only | `054_5H` L71, L96, L123; `058_5H` L4; `106_5H3` L257, L459 – L460; `109_5B7` L163 – L164, L276, L612 – L614, L1023 – L1024 | Together with `BYPASSRLS` (`001_5B` L44), the administrator can perform F-1 to F-3 in any tenant |
| F-5 | `EXECUTE` on `fn_finalize_invoice`, `fn_mark_invoice_paid`, `fn_void_invoice`, `fn_update_payment_status`, `fn_allocate_invoice_number`, `fn_create_late_usage_billing_adjustment`, `fn_process_payment_webhook_receipt`, `fn_apply_successful_payment_webhook_receipt` is granted to `app_worker` **and** `app_platform_admin`. None checks `session_user`. None writes an audit row. `fn_mark_invoice_paid` takes `p_payment_amount` and `p_currency` from its caller | `052_5H` L99; `057_5H` L27, L47, L66, L116; `102_5H2` L1537 – L1538, L1720 – L1721, L2039 – L2041 | The administrator can mark an invoice paid for an arbitrary amount without provider evidence. It can also allocate invoice numbers outside finalization, which burns the gapless sequence (INV-BILL-11). No 6M route uses any of these functions (searched: no occurrence in 6M, the authorization matrix or the final API reconciliation) |
| F-6 | `app_worker` holds `SELECT, INSERT` on `invoices` and no `UPDATE`. Frozen 6K §26.2 step 7 is "`UPDATE invoices SET subtotal_amount, total_credits_amount, total_tax_amount, total_due_amount` (computed, never client-set)". No function in `001` – `112` writes those columns | `054_5H` L69 – L70; 6K §26.2 | **The frozen generation pipeline cannot execute step 7 under the installed grants.** Only the administrator (or the migration principal) can. The administrator's DML is therefore not merely unused by routes: it is the only installed path for a legitimate `DRAFT` edit, and removing it without a replacement would break invoice generation |
| F-7 | Frozen 6K §39.3 states that after `OPEN` or `PAID` the totals and every line are "guaranteed structurally by `fn_invoice_immutability`". The trigger does not cover `OPEN` and does not cover lines | 6K §39.3; `054_5H` L52 | The frozen guarantee is not what the installed trigger enforces. It holds today only because no login role other than the administrator can update an invoice |
| F-8 | 6M §9 item 2 calls the administrator's invoice DML a "pre-existing 6K support capability". 6M §27 and §57 record `billing.billing_accounts` / `billing.invoices` raw CRUD as an "ADR-5H-006 residual … for a future pass". 5H ADR-5H-006: "`app_platform_admin` retains full access for operational corrections" | 6M §9, §27, §57; 5H ADR-5H-006 | The capability is frozen and approved. Withdrawing it is a change to an approved capability: hence OD-7L-24 |

**Root cause.** The installed protection is a column comparison on two terminal states, not a lifecycle. It does not check transitions, it does not cover `OPEN`, `INSERT`, `DELETE` or child rows, and it relies on a grant boundary that the most privileged runtime role is on the wrong side of. The administrator's escape hatch then became the only installed writer for a legitimate `DRAFT` step (F-6), which made the defect easy to keep and hard to remove.

#### 34.3.2 The frozen lifecycle that the corrective contract enforces

From 5H §16.1 ("`DRAFT` → `OPEN` → `PAID` | `VOID`"), the three frozen functions of `057_5H` and 6K §26.2. Nothing is added.

| From | To | Frozen operation | Columns it sets | Frozen precondition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | `DRAFT` | Invoice generation, step 2 (6K §26.2) | Every column, at `INSERT` | — |
| `DRAFT` | `DRAFT` | Steps 3 – 7: lines and tax lines inserted; totals computed | Lines and tax lines (`INSERT`); the four totals | Totals "computed, never client-set" (INV-6K-01, 5H INV-BILL-03) |
| `DRAFT` | `OPEN` | `fn_finalize_invoice` (step 8) | `status`, `invoice_number`, `issue_date`, `updated_at` | `status = 'DRAFT'` under `FOR UPDATE` |
| `OPEN` | `PAID` | `fn_mark_invoice_paid`, called by the settlement function `fn_apply_successful_payment_webhook_receipt` (`102_5H2`) | `status`, `paid_at`, `amount_paid_amount`, `amount_paid_currency`, `updated_at` | `status = 'OPEN'` under `FOR UPDATE` |
| `DRAFT` or `OPEN` | `VOID` | `fn_void_invoice` | `status`, `voided_at`, `void_reason`, `updated_at` | `status IN ('DRAFT','OPEN')` under `FOR UPDATE`. **`DRAFT → VOID` cannot commit as installed** (F-9 below) |

**F-9, found while checking this table.** `chk_inv_number_open` (`054_5H` L45) requires `invoice_number IS NOT NULL` for `VOID`, and a `DRAFT` never has a number (it is allocated at `OPEN`). So `fn_void_invoice` on a `DRAFT` fails the constraint, although 5H §16.1, the function's own precondition and 6K §26.5 ("a `DRAFT` invoice that is later `VOID`ed before ever reaching `OPEN`") all intend the edge. Under AUT-7L-06 the executed schema governs: **as installed, a `DRAFT` cannot be voided.** The consequence fails closed. Such a `DRAFT` has no number, cannot be paid (`fn_create_payment_attempt` requires `OPEN`, `102_5H2`) and is never finalized unless the generation worker finalizes it. Whether to relax the constraint for a never-numbered void, or to drop the edge, is a Billing-owner correction. It is recorded as **FND-7L-10** and as a compatibility item of CM-11. The lifecycle guard below permits the edge, so it neither adds nor removes the restriction; the constraint decides.

**The authoritative finalization boundary is `DRAFT → OPEN`.** From `OPEN` on, totals, lines, tax lines and pricing snapshots are immutable (6K §39.3, DEC-6K-04); `PAID` and `VOID` are terminal (5H INV-BILL-02; 6K INV-6K-06). No frozen source defines a transition out of `PAID` or `VOID`, or from `OPEN` back to `DRAFT`, and none is created here.

#### 34.3.3 Corrective contract

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| FIL-7L-01 [OD-7L-24] | **Scope.** `billing.invoices`, `billing.invoice_lines`, `billing.tax_lines`; administrator privileges on `billing.billing_accounts`; the eight functions of F-5. Everything is a future governed Phase-5 migration, **CM-11**, authored under the Phase-5 change process (PRM-7L-01). |
| FIL-7L-02 [7L] | **Two independent controls.** (1) *Who*: after CM-11 no login role holds `UPDATE` or `DELETE` on the three relations, and only the frozen writer (`app_worker`) holds `INSERT`. (2) *What*: a lifecycle guard trigger on each relation decides whether a row change is valid **whoever executes it**, including the table owner, a `SECURITY DEFINER` function and a `BYPASSRLS` session. Either control alone is insufficient: (1) does not bind the definer functions; (2) does not stop a privileged principal from making a valid but unauthorized change. |
| FIL-7L-03 [7L] | **Guard function properties.** `billing.fn_invoice_lifecycle_guard()` (on `invoices`) and `billing.fn_invoice_child_guard()` (on `invoice_lines`, `tax_lines`) are `SECURITY DEFINER`, owned by the migration principal, `SET search_path = billing, pg_catalog`, with `EXECUTE` revoked from `PUBLIC`. They read the parent row without depending on the caller's RLS context, so a `BYPASSRLS` session and a tenant session get the same verdict. A failed check raises, so the statement and its transaction roll back. |
| FIL-7L-04 [7L] | **Triggers.** `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE … FOR EACH ROW` on each of the three relations, and `BEFORE TRUNCATE … FOR EACH STATEMENT` raising unconditionally (`TRUNCATE` fires no row trigger). The installed `trg_inv_immutability` stays and is superseded in effect: the new guard is strictly stronger. The installed body of `054_5H` is not edited. |
| FIL-7L-05 [OD-7L-24] | **Insert.** A new invoice row must have `status = 'DRAFT'`, `invoice_number`, `issue_date`, `paid_at`, `voided_at`, `void_reason`, `e_invoice_ref` all `NULL`, and `amount_paid_amount = 0`. Its `organization_id` must equal the `organization_id` of its `billing_account_id`, of its `billing_period_id` (if set), of its `subscription_id` (if set) and of its `related_invoice_id` (if set). Every `*_currency` column must equal `currency`, and `currency` must equal the billing account's currency (5H INV-BILL-01). |
| FIL-7L-06 [OD-7L-24] | **Identity columns never change.** `id`, `organization_id`, `billing_account_id`, `billing_period_id`, `subscription_id`, `invoice_kind`, `currency`, every `*_currency` column, `related_invoice_id`, `created_at`, in every state. |
| FIL-7L-07 [OD-7L-24] | **Permitted transitions, exactly those of §34.3.2.** Every other `(OLD.status, NEW.status)` pair is refused: in particular `PAID → DRAFT`, `PAID → OPEN`, `PAID → VOID`, `VOID → *` and `OPEN → DRAFT`. **Any `UPDATE` of a row whose `OLD.status` is `PAID` or `VOID` is refused**, including an update that changes nothing but `updated_at`. |
| FIL-7L-08 [OD-7L-24] | **Columns per transition.** `DRAFT → DRAFT`: only the four totals and `updated_at`. `DRAFT → OPEN`: only `status`, `invoice_number` (non-null), `issue_date`, `updated_at`. `OPEN → PAID`: only `status`, `paid_at`, `amount_paid_amount`, `amount_paid_currency` (equal to `currency`), `updated_at`. `DRAFT → VOID` and `OPEN → VOID`: only `status`, `voided_at`, `void_reason` (non-blank), `updated_at`. `OPEN → OPEN`: nothing (refused if any column differs). Everything else the trigger compares with `IS DISTINCT FROM`, so `NULL` changes are caught. |
| FIL-7L-09 [OD-7L-24] | **Financial consistency at the boundary.** `DRAFT → OPEN` is refused unless `total_due_amount = subtotal_amount − total_credits_amount + total_tax_amount` (5H INV-BILL-03) and `total_due_amount ≥ 0` (INV-BILL-04). |
| FIL-7L-10 [OD-7L-24] | **Pricing snapshots.** `place_of_supply`, `tax_profile_snapshot`, `tax_rule_versions_applied`, `due_date`, `notes` and `e_invoice_ref` are written at `INSERT` and never updated. On a line, `unit_price_source`, `included_quantity_source`, `commercial_pricing_agreement_version_id` and every amount are written at `INSERT` (as `102_5H2` already states) and never updated. 5H ODD-5H-09 keeps `e_invoice_ref` reserved, with no V1 writer; a future IRN integration needs its own amendment. |
| FIL-7L-11 [OD-7L-24] | **Child rows are append-only, and only into a `DRAFT` parent.** On `invoice_lines` and `tax_lines`: `UPDATE` and `DELETE` are refused in every state. `INSERT` reads the parent invoice `FOR SHARE` and is refused unless the parent is `DRAFT`, `NEW.organization_id` equals the parent's, and every currency equals the parent's `currency`. On `tax_lines`, a non-null `invoice_line_id` must name a line of the same invoice and organization. |
| FIL-7L-12 [OD-7L-24] | **No deletion, ever.** `DELETE` and `TRUNCATE` on the three relations are refused for every principal. A `DRAFT` that must not proceed is voided (`DRAFT → VOID`), as 5H §16.1 provides, once F-9 is resolved by Billing; until then it stays an unnumbered, unpayable `DRAFT`, which bills nothing. Any future retention-driven removal of financial records is a separate governed change with its own legal review (LR register, §26.3). |
| FIL-7L-13 [7L] | **Concurrency.** `fn_finalize_invoice`, `fn_mark_invoice_paid` and `fn_void_invoice` already lock the invoice `FOR UPDATE`. A child insert takes `FOR SHARE` on the same row, which conflicts with `FOR UPDATE`. Two orders are possible, and both are safe. (a) The insert locks first: finalization waits until it commits, then includes the new line through FIL-7L-14 (b). (b) Finalization locks first: the insert waits until finalization commits, then sees `OPEN` and is refused. No line can join an invoice after the totals that finalization verifies. |
| FIL-7L-14 [OD-7L-24; 6K §26.2] | **The legitimate `DRAFT` edit (closes F-6).** (a) `billing.fn_recompute_draft_invoice_totals(p_organization_id, p_invoice_id)`, `SECURITY DEFINER`, `EXECUTE` to `app_worker` only. It locks the invoice `FOR UPDATE`, requires `DRAFT` and a matching organization, computes the four totals **only** from the invoice's own lines and tax lines read in the same transaction, writes them, and writes an audit row (FIL-7L-17). It takes no amount argument. (b) The superseding body of `fn_finalize_invoice` calls the same computation under its own lock before the `DRAFT → OPEN` update, so the finalized totals always equal the lines present at the boundary. **The computation is 6K's "steps 3 – 7" aggregation, whose exact line-type mapping (which of `BASE_FEE`, `USAGE`, `OVERAGE`, `CREDIT`, `DISCOUNT`, `TAX`, `ADJUSTMENT` feed `subtotal_amount` and `total_credits_amount`, and how `tax_lines` feed `total_tax_amount`) no frozen source states.** It is Billing-owner wording item **BIL-W-01**, required before (a) and (b) are authored. FIL-7L-09 holds whatever the mapping is. Until BIL-W-01 exists, invoice generation has no installed step 7 in any case (F-6), so nothing that works today stops working. |
| FIL-7L-15 [OD-7L-24] | **Administrator table privileges.** Revoke `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `TRUNCATE`, `REFERENCES`, `TRIGGER` on `invoices`, `invoice_lines`, `tax_lines`, `billing_accounts` from `app_platform_admin`. Its `SELECT` stays only until CM-12 (OD-7L-23) moves cross-tenant reads to guarded functions; **no 6M route reads these relations**, so CM-12 grants no replacement for them (GAD-7L-03). |
| FIL-7L-16 [OD-7L-24] | **Administrator function privileges.** Revoke `EXECUTE` from `app_platform_admin` on the eight functions of F-5. The administrator keeps `EXECUTE` only on the guarded, audited 6M wrappers that already exist: `fn_platform_create_billing_adjustment`, `fn_platform_apply_credit`, `fn_platform_reserve_refund` (`106_5H3`, `107_5B5`, `109_5B7`). Refund settlement stays with `app_billing_reconciler` (6M §9 item 4). |
| FIL-7L-17 [OD-7L-24; OD-7D-02] | **Audit atomic with every invoice lifecycle mutation.** The superseding bodies of `fn_finalize_invoice`, `fn_void_invoice`, `fn_mark_invoice_paid` and the new `fn_recompute_draft_invoice_totals` each call `audit.fn_insert_audit_event` in their own transaction. The audit row records organization, invoice, previous and resulting status, the changed totals where applicable, and the `session_user` (6M §9 item 3). 6K §26.2 step 9 already requires this for finalization. A failed audit insert rolls the mutation back. Signatures are unchanged, so callers are unaffected. |
| FIL-7L-18 [OD-7L-24] | **Preserved legitimate paths.** Invoice generation (`app_worker`: `INSERT` of `DRAFT` invoices and of lines into `DRAFT` invoices; FIL-7L-14; `fn_finalize_invoice`); payment settlement (`fn_process_payment_webhook_receipt`, `fn_apply_successful_payment_webhook_receipt`, which calls `fn_mark_invoice_paid` with the server-derived amount, all `app_worker`); voiding (`fn_void_invoice`, `app_worker`); late usage (`fn_create_late_usage_billing_adjustment`, `app_worker`); refunds (6M §19 saga); credits and adjustments (the 6M wrappers). |
| FIL-7L-19 [OD-7L-24; 6K DEC-6K-04] | **Corrections never edit history.** A finalized or paid invoice is corrected only by the frozen adjustment mechanisms: a `billing_adjustments` row created by `fn_create_late_usage_billing_adjustment` or `fn_platform_create_billing_adjustment`, applied to a later invoice. A credit is applied through the frozen credit functions. The original invoice row and its lines remain byte-identical. |
| FIL-7L-20 [OD-7L-10] | **Raw functions without a trusted caller.** Revoke `EXECUTE` on `fn_allocate_invoice_number` from `app_worker` as well: it is called only inside `fn_finalize_invoice`, which runs as the owner, and a direct call burns the gapless sequence (INV-BILL-11). Revoke `EXECUTE` on `fn_mark_invoice_paid` from `app_worker`: its only frozen caller is the settlement function, which also runs as the owner, and a direct call accepts an arbitrary amount. **Compatibility condition:** the CM-11 author confirms, against 6K §29 – §30, that no frozen 6K path calls either function directly as `app_worker`. Any such path is re-pointed to the settlement or finalization function before the revoke. |
| FIL-7L-21 [7L] | **Tenant authorization inside the functions.** Every lifecycle function requires that the invoice's stored `organization_id` equals `p_organization_id`. When a tenant context is set on the session, it must also equal `organization.current_tenant_id()`. A mismatch raises the frozen "not found" error, so a cross-tenant probe learns nothing. |
| FIL-7L-22 [7L] | **What no grant, attribute or ownership bypasses.** Row triggers fire for `BYPASSRLS` sessions, for the table owner and inside `SECURITY DEFINER` functions. Two things can still bypass the triggers, and both are excluded from every runtime principal: (1) disabling the trigger (`ALTER TABLE … DISABLE TRIGGER`), which needs ownership, held only by the migration principal (7I PRV-15: DDL only, never a runtime connection; D0 refuses it); (2) `session_replication_role = replica`, which needs superuser or a granted `SET` privilege on that parameter. CM-11's assertion block checks: no runtime role owns these relations; no runtime role is superuser; no runtime role holds `SET` on `session_replication_role` (`pg_parameter_acl`); no runtime role holds `TRUNCATE` or `TRIGGER`. The residual, a governed migration that replaces the guard, is change control, not a runtime path (RR-7L-F1, §34.9). |
| FIL-7L-23 [7L] | **Nothing a document asserts counts as enforced.** Until CM-11 is executed and its assertions pass, F-1 … F-6 are real, AG-7L-03 keeps the administrator credential out of production, and no production Billing invoice generation is authorized (it cannot run step 7 in any case, F-6). |
| FIL-7L-24 [OD-7L-24] | **Billing accounts.** Only the administrator's `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE` on `billing.billing_accounts` are withdrawn. 6M DEC-6M-02 already excludes a manual administrator account override in V1. The tenant and worker grants of `048_5H` L37 are 6K's and are not changed by this remediation. |

"S" `SELECT`, "I" `INSERT`, "X" `EXECUTE`; "—" none. CM-12 (OD-7L-23, §34.4) later removes the administrator's remaining direct `SELECT`s; it adds nothing on these objects, because no 6M route reads them.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `billing.invoices` | S | S, I (guarded by FIL-7L-05) | S | S (until CM-12) | — |
| `billing.invoice_lines` | S | S, I (guarded by FIL-7L-11) | S | S (until CM-12) | — |
| `billing.tax_lines` | S | S, I (guarded by FIL-7L-11) | S | S (until CM-12) | — |
| `billing.billing_accounts` | as `048_5H` | as `048_5H` | S | S (until CM-12) | — |
| `fn_recompute_draft_invoice_totals` (new) | — | X | — | — | — |
| `fn_finalize_invoice`, `fn_void_invoice` | — | X | — | — | — |
| `fn_mark_invoice_paid`, `fn_allocate_invoice_number` | — | — | — | — | — |
| `fn_update_payment_status`, `fn_process_payment_webhook_receipt`, `fn_apply_successful_payment_webhook_receipt`, `fn_create_late_usage_billing_adjustment` | — | X | — | — | — |
| `fn_platform_create_billing_adjustment`, `fn_platform_apply_credit`, `fn_platform_reserve_refund` | as installed | as installed | — | X | — |

`PUBLIC` holds nothing on any object above. The assertion block of CM-11 checks this table exactly with `has_table_privilege` / `has_function_privilege` for every cell.

**AP-7L-44 (revised) — 5B role catalogue; 6M §9, §27, §57** (authority OD-7L-10, OD-7L-23, OD-7L-24; stage S3). Replaces the documentary sentence of §33.8.3.

### 34.4 OD-7L-23 — Guarded administration, then revoke `BYPASSRLS`

**Status: APPROVED (option A, 2026-10-14), with the conditions of §34.2.** It does **not** block the Phase 7 design freeze: no event-pipeline component may connect as `app_platform_admin` (7I INV-03; D0 refuses it), and every Phase 7 control is independent of the attribute. It blocks only production use of the administrator credential, which AG-7L-03 and AG-7L-08 keep closed.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| GAD-7L-01 [OD-7L-23] | **Target.** `app_platform_admin` is `NOBYPASSRLS`, holds no table privilege on any tenant-owned relation, and reaches tenant data only through purpose-validated, audited `SECURITY DEFINER` functions or guarded views, each scoped to one explicitly named organization. Mutations already follow this pattern (6M §9 item 1); OD-7L-23 extends it to reads. |
| GAD-7L-02 [7L; verified in 6M §25] | **Affected routes: the 20 that 6M §25 marks "Role grant only" (they read with the role's own grants and, for tenant tables, its `BYPASSRLS`).** Organizations list and detail (`organization.organizations`); quota-override listing (`billing.quota_overrides`, `billing.capacity_quota_overrides` through the `rls_*_platform_admin` policies, 6M §66 – §67); break-glass listing (`break_glass_grants`); payment attempts (`billing.payment_attempts`); plans list and detail; commercial pricing agreements list and detail; tax categories; tax rules; financial analytics and provider health (6L projections); audit events (`audit.audit_events`); failed and dead-letter webhook deliveries (`webhooks.webhook_deliveries`, metadata columns, ERR-7I-02); workflow execution diagnostic; user, session and API-key safe views (`identity.v_platform_safe_*`). **These relations, at these columns, are the interim direct-`SELECT` list** that CM-01 and CM-07 keep until CM-12. Every other administrator route already calls a `fn_platform_*` function. |
| GAD-7L-03 [OD-7L-23] | **Replacement, by relation class.** (a) *Tenant-owned relations*: one read function per route, returning exactly the fields of the frozen 6M response, filtered by `organization_id = p_organization_id` inside the function. (b) *Platform-wide catalogues* (`plans`, `plan_versions`, `plan_prices`, `tax_categories`, `tax_rules`): a direct `SELECT` grant is kept **only if** the compatibility assessment confirms that the relation has no row-level security and holds no tenant row; otherwise class (a). (c) *Views* (`identity.v_platform_safe_*`, analytics projections): kept only if they are owned by a role that does not bypass row-level security, or are `security_invoker`, and their underlying relations are readable without `BYPASSRLS`; otherwise class (a). Relations no 6M route reads (the invoice family, `billing_accounts`, every `crm`, `campaign`, `knowledge`, `memory`, `workflow`, `prompt` relation other than the workflow diagnostic) get **no** replacement: the administrator loses access. |
| GAD-7L-04 [OD-7L-23] | **Checks inside every class (a) function**, in this order, each failing closed with the frozen 6M error contract: (a) `organization.is_platform_admin()` (6M §17); (b) a purpose code from the closed vocabulary that the 6M amendment defines per function (**GAD-W-01**, 6M owner); a free-text reason is not a purpose; (c) `session_user = 'app_platform_admin'` and the `p_admin_user_id` trust check of the 6M §65 wrappers, never a session GUC alone (6M §9 item 3); (d) `p_organization_id` is an explicit argument that must name an existing organization; no organization is taken from a session setting, a header or a payload, and a function that lists across organizations exists only where 6M §25 already lists across organizations (organizations list, audit events, failed and dead-letter webhooks), with the same filters and limits. |
| GAD-7L-05 [OD-7L-23] | **Definer hygiene.** Owned by the migration principal (no new owner role); `SET search_path = pg_catalog, <its schema>`; every relation schema-qualified; `EXECUTE` revoked from `PUBLIC` and granted to `app_platform_admin` alone; no dynamic SQL built from an argument; `STABLE` where it only reads. |
| GAD-7L-06 [OD-7L-23] | **Audit.** Every class (a) call writes `audit.fn_insert_audit_event` in its own transaction: administrator identity, purpose code, organization, route, and count of rows returned. Rows are not echoed into the audit record. A failed audit insert fails the read. Catalogue reads of class (b) are not tenant data and need no audit row. |
| GAD-7L-07 [OD-7L-23] | **Sensitive content is not widened.** Recording, transcript, conversation and turn relations stay at zero grant; access stays the break-glass functions of `107_5B5` (6M §9 item 5; OCG-7L-06). No GAD function returns `summary_text` or any content column (OCG-7L-07). |
| GAD-7L-08 [OD-7L-23] | **Per-route validation before re-pointing.** Each of the 20 routes is exercised against its replacement with the frozen request, response, permission and error contract unchanged (no tenant-visible change; 6M is not redesigned). |
| GAD-7L-09 [OD-7L-23] | **The 22 function-backed routes (20 mutation routes and the two break-glass content-access routes; 42 routes in 6M §25 in all) are re-verified with the attribute removed**, in a staging copy: each `fn_platform_*` is `SECURITY DEFINER` and should not depend on the caller's `BYPASSRLS`, but this is proved by test, not assumed. |
| GAD-7L-10 [OD-7L-23] | **Revocation order, enforced by gate.** (1) CM-01, CM-07, CM-11 executed; (2) CM-12 creates the class (a) functions and any class (b) / (c) grants; (3) every route re-pointed and GAD-7L-08 passed; (4) CM-12 revokes the interim direct `SELECT`s; (5) GAD-7L-09 and T-7L-04 pass on a staging copy whose administrator role is `NOBYPASSRLS`; (6) a governed migration executes `ALTER ROLE app_platform_admin NOBYPASSRLS`; (7) the catalogue assertion `rolbypassrls = false` passes. A failed step stops the sequence with the credential still out of production. |
| GAD-7L-11 [OD-7L-23] | **Until GAD-7L-10 (7) holds**, the administrator credential is not used in production (AG-7L-03; AG-7L-08). |
| GAD-7L-12 [OD-7L-23] | **No workaround principal.** No new role with `BYPASSRLS`, superuser, `CREATEROLE`, ownership of tenant relations or membership in another role is created for administration, support or migration of these routes. The migration principal remains DDL-only (7I PRV-15). |
| GAD-7L-13 [7L] | **Event pipeline unchanged.** 7I INV-03, PRV-14 and CNF-7I-01 stand. Nothing in §34.4 grants the administrator anything in the event pipeline. |
| GAD-7L-14 [7L] | **What remains after GAD-7L-10.** A stolen administrator credential can call the guarded functions, within their purpose, organization scope and audit. That residual is carried as part of RR-01 (§34.9); it is not accepted here. |

**CM-12 (new).** Guarded administrative read surface and `BYPASSRLS` revocation. Kind: P5; 6M. Authority: OD-7L-23. Scope: GAD-7L-03 … -06, -10 steps (2), (4), (6), (7). Owner: 5B with 6M. Depends on: CM-01, CM-07, CM-11; GAD-W-01; AP-7L-44 (revised) approved (stage S3). Compatibility assessment: all 42 routes of 6M §25 (GAD-7L-08, -09). Security regression: T-7L-04. Gate: AG-7L-08.

**Regression T-7L-04 — guarded administration** (specified; not executed; owners 5B, 6M):

| Case | Action | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| (a) | Each class (a) function with a valid purpose, organization X | Exactly X's rows, only the 6M response fields; one audit row |
| (b) | Same call naming organization Y | Only Y's rows; no X row |
| (c) | No purpose, an unknown purpose, or free text | Refused; audit of the refusal per 6M |
| (d) | Called with a forged `app.is_platform_admin` setting under `app_api` | `42501` |
| (e) | `p_organization_id` omitted or `NULL`, or organization taken from a session setting | Refused; no rows |
| (f) | After step (4): direct `SELECT` by the administrator on each formerly granted tenant relation | `42501` |
| (g) | After step (6): all 42 routes of 6M §25 | All pass with unchanged responses |
| (h) | After step (6): a direct `SELECT` on any tenant relation with RLS, under any tenant context or none | Zero rows or `42501`; never another tenant's row |
| (i) | Audit insert made to fail | The read returns nothing |
| (j) | Catalogue: `rolbypassrls` for every login role | `false` for every runtime role and for the administrator; `true` only for the migration principal |

### 34.5 FG-7L-R2-03 — Initial publication admission and sustained Billing backlog

#### 34.5.1 Why a binding rule is needed

Frozen 7E creates every registered durable group at position `0` on every physical key of its streams before relay activation (BST-01), and gates the relay only on the groups **existing** (BST-02; IO-7E-13). The trim watermark is computed over every present group (TRM-02); a registered but missing group stops trimming entirely (TRM-03). A group is never deleted because it is idle (RET-02), and an offline group pins "until it returns" (7K RTN-7K-08). Before AG-7L-02, no Billing worker can even be admitted (FAG-7L-04 (1)). So an event plane activated before CON-06 is admitted accumulates every entry of LS-D-VOX, LS-D-KNW, LS-D-CPN and LS-D-WFL in Redis for as long as Billing is absent, with no frozen exit. FAG-7L-07 disclosed this; nothing forbade it. The same arithmetic holds for **every** registered durable group: an unadmitted CON-05, CON-08 or CON-09 pins its streams exactly as Billing does. OD-7L-27 makes the rule general.

#### 34.5.2 Stream → owed-group matrix (verified against 7E §29.1 – §29.3, 7B §22 and 7F §28 / §35.2)

7E §29.3 is the authoritative stream view. It lists 11 durable groups, 18 (group, stream) subscriptions and one SIGNAL group. The example list in the decision panel was checked against it. LS-D-VOX has **six** owed groups, CON-10 among them. LS-D-CRM, LS-D-CPN and LS-D-BIL also depend on CON-10.

| Logical stream | Owed durable groups (7E §29.3) | Handler-contract and consumer prerequisites, per group (7F §35, 7L §23.3) | Capability status today | Production-admission prerequisite (SPA-7L-05) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LS-D-IDN | CON-01 `cg.identity.session-denylist` | §35.1 common; IO-7F-11 | Not built | CON-01 admitted |
| LS-D-ORG | CON-02 `cg.compliance.default-policy-seeding` | §35.1; IO-7F-12 | Not built | CON-02 admitted |
| LS-D-CMP | CON-03 `cg.compliance.active-policy-pointer` | §35.1; AP-7L-31 applied; IO-7F-13 | Not built; packet complete, not applied | CON-03 admitted |
| LS-D-VOX | CON-04 `cg.crm.call-history`; CON-05 `cg.campaign.record-call-outcome`; CON-06 `cg.billing.usage-ingestion`; CON-07 `cg.analytics.projections`; CON-08 `cg.voice.recording-object-cleanup`; CON-10 `cg.integrations.webhook-engine` | CON-04: IO-7F-14, -33, -35. CON-05: AP-7L-32; IO-7F-15. CON-06: AG-7L-02; AP-7L-27, -28 for EV-079; IO-7F-16, -33 … -35. CON-07: IO-7F-17, -33, -35. CON-08: AP-7L-27 (vii); IO-7F-18. CON-10: IO-7F-20, -21 (= MR-7H-01); AB-7H-01; **and AB-7H-02, because fan-out without dispatch is a prohibited partial activation (ACT-7L-05; 7H §17.5)** | None built; CON-06 behind AG-7L-02; CON-08 behind AP-7L-27 (vii); CON-10 behind the whole external-delivery capability (§23.2 row 5) | All six admitted |
| LS-D-AGT | none | — | — | Infrastructure prerequisites only (SPA-7L-04) |
| LS-D-KNW | CON-06; CON-09 `cg.knowledge.document-count` | CON-06 as above. CON-09: AP-7L-33 (now complete, §34.6.4); IO-7F-19 | Not built | CON-06 and CON-09 admitted |
| LS-D-CRM | CON-07; CON-10 | As above | Not built | Both admitted |
| LS-D-CPN | CON-06; CON-10; CON-11 `cg.campaign.import-worker` | CON-11: AP-7L-32; IO-7F-22 | Not built | All three admitted |
| LS-D-WFL | CON-06 | As above | Not built | CON-06 admitted |
| LS-D-INT | none | — | — | Infrastructure prerequisites only |
| LS-D-BIL | CON-10 | As above | Not built | CON-10 admitted |
| LS-S-VOX (SIGNAL) | `sg.analytics.signal-projections` (best effort) | IO-7F-23; IO-7C-11 | Not built | **Not subject to SPA**: OD-7L-27 covers durable groups; the SIGNAL group pins nothing durable and blocks no durable stream (§23.3) |

**Consequence, stated so that it is not discovered later.** Every call produces LS-D-VOX entries. So production voice traffic needs CON-04, -05, -06, -07, -08 and CON-10 admitted, and CON-10 needs external webhook dispatch (capability 5). Billing (AG-7L-02), recording cleanup (AP-7L-27 (vii)), campaign outcome (AP-7L-32) and the webhook engine are therefore all on the critical path of the first production call. This follows from frozen 7E plus OD-7L-27. It creates no new dependency between contexts: it only stops the platform from going live into a state that frozen 7K already treats as an incident (RTN-7K-09). It is carried as an availability and schedule risk, RR-7L-S1 (§34.9), not as a safety risk.

#### 34.5.3 Stream publication admission (OD-7L-27)

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| SPA-7L-01 [OD-7L-27] | **Admission record.** For each (region, topology generation, logical durable stream) there is one durable admission record in PostgreSQL with state `CLOSED` or `OPEN`. It starts `CLOSED`. Its only transition is `CLOSED → OPEN`, made by the governed provisioning step of SPA-7L-09. Physical form: governed migration requirement **G-13**. |
| SPA-7L-02 [OD-7L-27] | **Meaning.** While a stream's record is `CLOSED`, no outbox row whose type routes to that stream is published in production (SPA-7L-10), and no producing capability whose types route to it is enabled for production traffic (SPA-7L-11). |
| SPA-7L-03 [OD-7L-27 (1)] | **The owed-group set comes from PostgreSQL, not from Redis.** It is the governed group registry (7E §29 and any governed later registration; the same registry from which 7J generates its expected-source registry, RR-7J-10) materialized in PostgreSQL by G-13 as rows (logical stream, logical group, consumer, owning context). What Redis currently shows is checked against it, never used instead of it: a group present in Redis but absent from the registry is an anomaly that refuses admission (7E TRM-04); a registry group absent from Redis refuses admission. |
| SPA-7L-04 [7L] | **Infrastructure prerequisites for every stream**, including streams with no owed group: AG-7K-01, AG-7K-02, AB-7I-01, AB-7I-02 and the frozen IO-7E-13 relay gate. |
| SPA-7L-05 [OD-7L-27 (2)] | **A group is admitted for a stream** only when all of these hold, each read from the state that enforces it: (a) the Redis group exists on every physical key of the stream for the generation, created at `0` (BST-01), verified with `XINFO GROUPS`; (b) its generation-1 handler-contract record exists and is `OPEN` with the content of 7F HCG-07 (IO-7F-31); (c) the deployed handler build passed the 7F build checks (REG-7F-02, SHD-08) and its conformance tests (IO-7F-07 … -10 for that consumer) are recorded as passed for that build identity; (d) at least one worker of that build has completed admission (HCG-02, HCG-03, HCG-04) under the group's own context principal (7I CTX-01, CTX-08) and is registered in the handler-contract record; (e) every gate that names the group is open: 7F §35.1 and its §35.2 row, 7G MIG-02 (the recovery ledger), AB-7I-10, AB-7I-11, AG-7K-03, and for CON-06 AG-7L-02. |
| SPA-7L-06 [OD-7L-27 (3)] | **Disabled is not admitted.** A handler that is disabled by an unresolved owner decision, a closed security gate, a missing implementation or an unapproved contract fails SPA-7L-05 (e) by construction. No flag, waiver or manual entry marks it admitted. |
| SPA-7L-07 [OD-7L-27 (4)] | **Per stream, no global block.** Each stream's record opens on its own owed set. A stream whose owed groups are all admitted opens even while another stream stays `CLOSED`. LS-D-AGT and LS-D-INT open on SPA-7L-04 alone. |
| SPA-7L-08 [OD-7L-27 (5)] | **Frozen transport rules untouched.** Groups are created at `0`, never `$`; no owed group is omitted, deferred or created later to let a stream open; routing (7E §18), generations (LCY-07) and safe trimming (TRM-02 … -05) are unchanged; no entry is acknowledged, trimmed or dropped to satisfy or bypass admission. |
| SPA-7L-09 [OD-7L-27 (6)] | **The provisioning step that opens a record** is a governed operation of the stream-lifecycle authority (AP-7L-04; 7I matrix 6). It re-reads, in one run, every item of SPA-7L-03 … -05 from PostgreSQL, from Redis (`XINFO GROUPS`, read-only) and from the handler-contract store. It writes the record `OPEN` together with an immutable evidence row: the owed set, each group's record generation, build identity, admitted worker identities, gate evidence references, operator and time. A document, an operator assertion or a monitoring alert is not an input. |
| SPA-7L-10 [OD-7L-27 (6)] | **Database enforcement at the relay.** The superseding claim function that CM-03 already requires (`audit.fn_claim_outbox_events` with the `session_user` check, IR-01) claims a row only if the admission record of the stream its type routes to is `OPEN` for the relay's region and generation. A row of a `CLOSED` stream is not claimed: it stays `PENDING`, its `attempt_count` does not grow, and nothing is deferred or failed (as 7K BPR-7K-04 RED). This is a database fact, not a relay configuration value. |
| SPA-7L-11 [OD-7L-27 (6), (9)] | **Deployment admission for producers.** The deployment pipeline enables, for production traffic, a producing capability only if every stream that its event types route to has an `OPEN` record. The pipeline reads the record; it does not accept an operator override. The capabilities and their streams are listed in G-13's routing rows (7E §18 type → stream). If a capability is nonetheless enabled by hand, SPA-7L-10 still keeps Redis empty of that stream's entries; the rows then accumulate in the outbox, which frozen 7D tolerates and frozen 7K alerts on (outbox oldest eligible age), and the deployment-conformance check reports the violation. |
| SPA-7L-12 [OD-7L-27 (7)] | **Monotone.** An `OPEN` record never returns to `CLOSED` because an admitted consumer becomes unavailable. A later outage of an admitted consumer is handled by frozen 7K (backlog monitoring, `pressure(g)`, tiers, RTN-7K-08 / -09, recovery) and, for Billing, by BIA-7L-05 … -18. Closing a record is only part of a governed decommissioning or generation retirement (LCY-07), never a pressure response. |
| SPA-7L-13 [OD-7L-27 (8)] | **OD-7L-16 is not weakened.** For any stream that CON-06 subscribes to, SPA-7L-05 (e) includes AG-7L-02. An admitted Billing group is one whose origin verification is active. |
| SPA-7L-14 [OD-7L-27 (9)] | **No obligation is removed to let a producer go live.** A consumer that is not implemented or not authorized keeps its stream `CLOSED`. Removing or re-routing an owed type is a governed 7B / 7E registry change with its own owner decision (7E RET-01), never an admission shortcut. |
| SPA-7L-15 [OD-7L-27 (10); 7D PTX-04] | **No transport-health dependency inside a business transaction.** The admission record is read by the provisioning step, by the claim function and by the deployment pipeline. It is never read by a producing transaction. Producing transactions commit their state and outbox row unconditionally, as frozen (PTX-01 … -04). |
| SPA-7L-16 [7L] | **Relation to generation changes.** A later topology generation already requires that "consumers admit the key **before** any relay may publish to it" (7F TK-1 … TK-6; §9.3 step 1). SPA applies the same principle to the first generation `g1`, under the same record. A generation change creates the record of `g<n+1>` `CLOSED` and opens it by the same step. |

#### 34.5.4 Billing ingestion admission and backlog (FG-7L-R2-03; OD-7L-25)

**Phases kept apart.** (P1) *Initial activation*: SPA governs; Billing is either admitted or its streams are closed. (P2) *Temporary outage after activation*: frozen 7K governs; nothing changes for producers. (P3) *Prolonged outage*: OD-7L-25 adds one producer-side measure, batch deferral. (P4) *Recovery and catch-up*: frozen 7K exit rules, with deferred batches released at a bounded rate.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| BIA-7L-01 [7L] | **Billing admission evidence** (P1). For the four Billing streams, SPA-7L-05 holds for CON-06 only when, in addition: AG-7L-02 is open (FAG-7L-02 (a) … (f)); the origin function is present and executable by the Billing context principal only (`has_function_privilege` on the executed catalogue); and the CON-06 build carries the unconditional pre-guard (FAG-7L-04 (2)). |
| BIA-7L-02 [7L] | **Ingestion state** of the Billing group, per region: `ADMITTED` (consuming, no condition below), `LAGGING`, `STALLED`, `SATURATED`. It is computed by the observer (7J; read-only `XINFO GROUPS`, `XPENDING` summary, the dependency-gate state of 7K §22.3, outbox statistics) and written to a PostgreSQL state record with the evidence it was computed from (**G-14**). It is a measurement, not a gate decision: the consequences of BIA-7L-10 follow from it deterministically. |
| BIA-7L-03 [7L] | **Signals**, each measured per Billing key and reduced by maximum: `age_b` = oldest pending age of `cg.billing.usage-ingestion`, or, where nothing is pending, age of the oldest entry after its last-delivered ID (undelivered backlog); `lag_b` = the group's lag in entries; `gate_b` = the origin-verification dependency gate is open (the "Unavailable" row of 7K §22.3); `adm_b` = number of admitted Billing workers; `res_b` = share of the outbox reserve of 7K §16.1 occupied by rows of types routed to the four Billing streams and not yet accounted for Billing. |
| BIA-7L-04 [7L] | **States.** `LAGGING`: `pressure(cg.billing.usage-ingestion)` raised (7K BPR-7K-09) or `age_b > A_lag(billing)` (BPR-7K-08). `STALLED`: `adm_b = 0` for at least `T_stall`, or `gate_b` open for at least `T_stall`, or `age_b` rising while `lag_b` does not fall for `T_stall`. `SATURATED`: `STALLED` **and** any of `age_b ≥ A_bil,t2`, `res_b ≥ ρ_t2`, or the region in frozen tier 2 on a shard that carries a Billing key. Entry and exit use the frozen hysteresis: a state is left only after its trigger has been clear for `T_clear` (7K §13.4). Values: `T_stall` [CAND] 15 minutes; `A_bil,t2` [CAND] 6 hours (= `A_pin,warn`, 7K RTN-7K-09); `ρ_t2` [CAND] 0.5; all [MEAS] by BM-7K-02 and BM-7K-05, and recorded in the parameter registry (§25.6). **These candidates are not binding until measured and approved under the 7K parameter rules.** |
| BIA-7L-05 [FROZEN; 7K] | **P2: `LAGGING` and `STALLED` change nothing for producers.** Frozen 7K applies: alerts, scaling (ASC-7K-03), R2 / R3 pause for the group (BPR-7K-10), pacing by memory zone (BPR-7K-03, -04), the 7I ACC-17 obligation deadline and its class `V` cases after `T_obl` (BPR-7K-08; never suspended), RTN-7K-09 escalation at `A_pin,warn` and `A_pin,max`. |
| BIA-7L-06 [FAG-7L-04 (3)] | **Origin function unavailable after activation.** The frozen "Unavailable" row of 7K §22.3: no effect, dependency gate open, entry pending. It feeds `gate_b`. No unverified effect is applied to drain the backlog (FAG-7L-08). |
| BIA-7L-07 [7L] | **Explicit degraded-state response.** On every transition into `STALLED` or `SATURATED`: an incident is opened with its named cause (RTN-7K-08); the state record carries the cause; the platform status for the region shows Billing ingestion degraded; and, at `SATURATED`, BIA-7L-10 applies. The response is driven by the state record, not by the alert. |
| BIA-7L-08 [7L] | **Region-wide consequence, disclosed.** While Billing pins its four streams, the memory of the shards that carry them grows. When a shard reaches AMBER or RED, frozen pacing slows or pauses relay claims on that shard for **every** family it carries (BPR-7K-06). That is frozen behaviour and RR-7K-02; 7L does not hide it and does not override it. Families on other shards are unaffected. |
| BIA-7L-09 [7L] | **Unrelated work is not stopped.** No rule of §34.5.4 stops a capability whose events route only to streams that Billing does not subscribe to (LS-D-IDN, -ORG, -CMP, -AGT, -CRM, -INT, -BIL), beyond what frozen memory pacing does to a shared shard (BIA-7L-08). |
| BIA-7L-10 [OD-7L-25] | **P3: batch deferral at `SATURATED`.** While the Billing state of a region is `SATURATED`, the owning contexts do not admit *new* batch or scheduled billable work in that region. The job classes are: (a) outbound campaign dialing work, a new dialing batch of a running campaign and the start of dialing of a newly started campaign (types reaching LS-D-CPN and LS-D-VOX); (b) knowledge ingestion jobs not yet claimed (LS-D-KNW, `document.indexed`); (c) scheduled and standalone workflow executions whose completion is billable (LS-D-WFL, `workflow.execution.completed`). |
| BIA-7L-11 [OD-7L-25] | **Where the check is made.** At the job-admission step of each class: the claim or start step that moves a job from its queued state to its running state. That step reads the region's Billing state record. If it is `SATURATED`, the job is not admitted and stays in its queued state. The check is a separate statement before, and outside, any business transaction that produces outbox rows (BIA-7L-15). |
| BIA-7L-12 [OD-7L-25] | **Deferred work stays in its existing authoritative state.** Campaign dialing: the contacts stay in their queued campaign-contact state and the campaign stays in its current status (as frozen tier 2 already keeps "new campaign preparation … in their queued status"). Knowledge ingestion: the document stays `PENDING`. Workflow: the execution stays in the queued representation that 6I defines for a due execution. **Where no verified durable queued representation exists for a class, new work of that class is refused or deferred safely before any execution obligation is created** (OD-7L-29 condition 5): a standalone, API-initiated billable workflow execution is refused with the existing retryable error class of its 6I route; a scheduled billable workflow is **not production-activated** until the Workflow owner supplies either a verified queued representation or a verified durable refusal record (OD-7L-29 item (5); AG-7L-07). No new state is invented here. Nothing deferred is cancelled, silently dropped, marked completed, re-ordered within an organization or lost. |
| BIA-7L-13 [FROZEN; OD-7L-25] | **Frozen tier 2 and tier 3 stay as they are.** Tier 2 already queues new campaign preparation and import jobs and pauses relay claims under RED; BIA-7L-10 adds a Billing-specific trigger for the three classes, and nothing in tier 2 is relaxed. |
| BIA-7L-14 [OD-7L-25] | **Calls and interactive work.** Calls already in progress finish. New inbound calls and interactive operations continue **only within approved resource headroom and frozen admission rules**: the concurrency and quota controls of 6D and 6K (`CONCURRENT_CALLS` capacity, quota overrides), the frozen 7K tiers and the frozen 6D / 6H admission contracts. BIA-7L-10 does not authorize unlimited interactive or inbound billable work, and it does not loosen any of those limits. |
| BIA-7L-15 [OD-7L-25; 7D PTX-04] | **Admission checks are outside the committed business transaction.** No producing transaction reads the Billing state record or any transport state. A job that was admitted runs its business transactions unconditionally, and each commits its state and outbox row together. |
| BIA-7L-16 [7L] | **Tenant fairness of the release.** When `SATURATED` clears, deferred jobs are admitted again under their frozen per-organization and regional concurrency bounds (BPR-7K-16) and in their frozen order within an organization. The release is never all at once: the per-organization bound limits how fast any one organization's backlog re-enters. |
| BIA-7L-17 [FROZEN; OD-7L-25] | **At the frozen tier-3 boundary** (a dependency down: PostgreSQL, the event transport, the hot tier, the key service, the journal, the secret manager or the egress path), the frozen tier-3 response applies: retryable failure of API mutations that need the dependency, retryable server errors on callback receipts, gate-specific pauses. OD-7L-25 neither replaces it nor adds to it. |
| BIA-7L-18 [7L] | **P4: recovery and catch-up.** The Billing group drains in append order through the verified handler: origin check, guard, deferred acknowledgement and delayed-event reconciliation unchanged (FAG-7L-06). Entries older than the 90-day horizon are held for Billing (7F RET-7F-09; SEC-7K-20). Cases opened after `T_obl` are resolved through 7G, not by the catch-up. Catch-up exit is frozen OBX-7K-17 and BPR-7K-17. The state returns to `ADMITTED` only after its triggers have been clear for `T_clear`. |
| BIA-7L-19 [OD-7L-25] | **Never, under any state:** discarding a committed event; removing, recreating or resetting an owed group; skipping or falsifying an acknowledgement; trimming an undelivered or pending entry; admitting an unverified Billing consumer to drain Redis; deleting or reclassifying outbox rows; converting mandatory work into best-effort work (7K BPR-7K-01; RTN-7K-10). |
| BIA-7L-20 [OD-7L-16] | **OD-7L-25 does not override OD-7L-16.** No billable financial effect is applied in production while AG-7L-02 is closed, in any state. |
| BIA-7L-21 [7L] | **Regional interruption.** After a regional outage or a restore (7K §20, §21): the Billing group is re-admitted only through HCG-04 revalidation of its record and with origin verification available; restored-database work is subject to the money gate (OD-7K-03; 7K §21.8); the stream's admission record is unchanged (SPA-7L-12); the backlog is caught up under BIA-7L-18; batch deferral applies while the state is `SATURATED`. |
| BIA-7L-22 [7L] | **Billing amounts stay server-authoritative.** Nothing in §34.5 computes, estimates, pre-aggregates or carries a monetary value; usage reaches Billing only through CON-06 (6K). |

**Staging procedure (the exception the review allowed).** An "initial production publication before Billing admission" is permitted only under a bounded staging procedure that a later owner decision approves on evidence. It must meet all of these conditions. It runs in a stack with no tenant traffic. Its producers are platform-owned synthetic organizations, so the entry count on each Billing stream is bounded by construction and stated in advance. It ends before tenant admission, either with SPA-7L-05 met for every owed group or with the whole event-transport cluster re-provisioned. It is never ended by deleting keys or groups, which no frozen identity may do (§9.3 step 5). No billable effect is applied to any organization. **No such procedure is designed or approved; until one is, SPA-7L-10 and SPA-7L-11 admit no exception.**

#### 34.5.5 Reconciliation with frozen 7K

| 7K element | Effect of §34.5 |
|---|---|
| BPR-7K-01, -02 (backpressure moves work toward PostgreSQL; producers never gated) | Preserved. SPA-7L-10 leaves rows `PENDING` in PostgreSQL. BIA-7L-11 acts at job admission, which is not a producing transaction. **7K BPR-7K-02's list of producer-facing waits gains one entry by AP-7L-51: "the batch-job admission of OD-7L-25"** |
| §13.4 tiers | Tier 2 gains the Billing `SATURATED` trigger for three job classes (AP-7L-51). Tiers 0, 1 and 3 are unchanged |
| §16.1 outbox reserve | `res_b` is measured against it; `ρ_t2` sits below the reserve so that deferral starts before the reserve is consumed |
| §17.4 case volume | Unchanged: an outage longer than `T_obl` still opens class `V` cases; batch deferral reduces `λ_g` for the Billing group during a prolonged outage and so reduces the case volume, without changing the rule |
| RTN-7K-08 … -11 | Unchanged. SPA prevents the "never onboarded" pin at go-live; it does not change the exits for a later pin |
| BPR-7K-16 bulk producers | Its bounds also govern the release (BIA-7L-16) |
| OBX-7K-17, BPR-7K-17 exits | Govern P4 |

#### 34.5.6 Regression T-7L-05 — stream admission and Billing backlog

Specified; **not executed**. Owners: Platform; Billing; Campaign; Knowledge; Workflow. Gates: AG-7L-06, AG-7L-07.

| Case | Setup | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| (a) | Billable producer enabled before Billing admission: LS-D-VOX record `CLOSED`, a call committed | Outbox row `PENDING`, never claimed (SPA-7L-10); no entry in Redis; the deployment pipeline refuses to enable the call capability (SPA-7L-11); the call transaction committed normally (SPA-7L-15) |
| (b) | CON-06 handler without a generation-1 record | Not admitted (HCG-07); SPA-7L-05 (b) fails; record stays `CLOSED` |
| (c) | Origin function absent or not executable by the Billing principal | BIA-7L-01 fails; record stays `CLOSED`. After activation: entries pending, no effect, `gate_b` raised (BIA-7L-06) |
| (d) | A Redis group present that is not in the registry; a registry group missing in Redis | Admission refused in both cases (SPA-7L-03) |
| (e) | CON-08 disabled because AP-7L-27 (vii) is not applied | LS-D-VOX stays `CLOSED` (SPA-7L-06); LS-D-IDN opens on CON-01 alone (SPA-7L-07) |
| (f) | Billing group admitted, then lagging for less than `T_stall` | State `LAGGING`; no producer effect (BIA-7L-05) |
| (g) | Billing workers stopped beyond `T_stall`, then `age_b ≥ A_bil,t2` | `STALLED`, then `SATURATED`; incident opened; new campaign dialing batch, unclaimed ingestion job and scheduled workflow run stay queued; a call in progress finishes; a new inbound call is admitted only within `CONCURRENT_CALLS` capacity |
| (h) | Redis memory pressure: a Billing shard AMBER, then RED | Frozen pacing; on RED no claims on that shard; families on other shards publish; nothing trimmed |
| (i) | Outbox growth to `res_b ≥ ρ_t2` with the Billing group stalled | `SATURATED`; deferral as (g); no outbox row deleted or reclassified |
| (j) | Billing consumer recovers | Drain in append order through the origin check; held entries beyond the horizon go to Billing; state returns to `ADMITTED` after `T_clear`; deferred jobs re-admitted under per-organization bounds, in their frozen order |
| (k) | Nonbillable workloads during (g) | CRM, identity, organization, compliance, integrations configuration continue; their streams publish unless they share a RED shard (BIA-7L-08, -09) |
| (l) | Regional interruption with a Billing backlog, then restore | Re-admission through HCG-04; money gate applies to restored work; admission records unchanged; catch-up as (j) |
| (m) | An operator sets the Billing state record to `ADMITTED` by hand while workers are stopped | The observer recomputes it on its next cycle from Redis and gate state; the hand-written value does not survive; the write itself is refused, because the record is writable by the observer principal only (G-14) |
| (n) | A producing transaction during `SATURATED` | Commits normally; no read of the state record inside it (statement log of the test) |
| (o) | An attempt to open a record by a direct `UPDATE` | Refused: only the provisioning function writes the record, under the stream-lifecycle principal (G-13) |
| (p) | A previously admitted CON-04 down for a day | Record stays `OPEN` (SPA-7L-12); 7K pin escalation applies |

### 34.6 FG-7L-R2-02 — Amendment-packet completeness, by category

#### 34.6.1 Categories and rules

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| PKC-7L-01 [7L] | **Category A — mandatory V1 architecture contract.** A capability that V1 production needs, or a correctness, privacy or financial guarantee that V1 production relies on. Its contract must be implementation-deterministic before the Phase 7 design freeze: every state, transition, authority, transaction and failure path stated. Physical names (columns, function names, migration numbers) may be left to the governed migration where a frozen rule already does so (7B ACC-06). |
| PKC-7L-02 [7L] | **Category B — later or optional capability with an already-authorized deferral.** The frozen architecture or an approved owner decision already names a closed gate for it, and V1 runs safely without it. Its text may stay incomplete, provided the deferral authority, the prohibited V1 behaviour and the fail-closed gate are stated. |
| PKC-7L-03 [7L] | **Category C — needs an owner or domain-owner decision.** The architecture is resolved, but a domain fact that no frozen source states is needed (AUT-7L-02: 7L does not invent it). Each such item is owned, gated and, where it may be deferred, deferred by the owner's decision OD-7L-29. |
| PKC-7L-04 [7L] | **A packet is not "complete" because nothing is implemented yet.** A packet whose text still has a bracketed gap in a category A item is incomplete. Where §34.6 removes a gap, the replacement text is given here in full. |
| PKC-7L-05 [7L] | **A deferred registered consumer still pins its stream.** Deferring a durable consumer is safe only while its streams publish nothing in production. That is now enforced by SPA (OD-7L-27). A packet whose consumer is on a V1 stream is therefore category A for that stream's go-live, whatever its domain priority. This is why AP-7L-27 (vii) (CON-08) and AP-7L-33 (CON-09) are category A. |
