#### 34.6.3 AP-7L-27 (iii) — the per-turn service checkpoint (OD-7L-17, OD-7L-26)

| # | Field | Content |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Target and rule | 6D §12 (runtime and worker roles) and §12.4 (EV-079), as AP-7L-27 (ii), (iii); 7B ACC-01, OCC-01 … -07; 7K VOX-7K-16 … -20 |
| 2 | Existing contract | 7B ACC-01: the five metrics accumulate durably in the per-turn checkpoint transaction. OCC-03: the recovery path reuses "the authoritative persisted service-end timestamp". 7K VOX-7K-20: the 6D amendment must name that value for every way a call ends, or the finalization returns `CORRUPT_STATE`. OD-7L-17: the last validated, durably committed per-turn checkpoint whose service-end semantics the contract proves. Installed: no accumulator, no guard, no marker, no checkpoint (`012_5C`; §2.4) |
| 3 | Replacement text (6D) | ⟦**Per-turn service checkpoint.** When the live conversation runtime completes a turn, one PostgreSQL transaction (the *checkpoint transaction*) does exactly this, through the guarded checkpoint function: (1) lock the conversation's accounting row `FOR UPDATE`; (2) verify that the conversation is not finalized and that the turn is the next one (CKP-7L-04); (3) add the turn's validated usage to the five durable cumulative totals; (4) **after** the totals are written, read `clock_timestamp()` and store `checkpoint_at = GREATEST(clock_timestamp(), previous checkpoint_at)`; (5) record the checkpoint row (organization, conversation, turn sequence, finalization generation, cumulative totals, `checkpoint_at`); (6) commit. `checkpoint_at` is the **accounting cutoff**: the totals of the same row account for service up to it and for nothing after it. It is not the telephony provider's disconnect instant. **The service-end time of a conversation whose call ended abnormally** (process death, or an end forced by the stale-session reaper) is the `checkpoint_at` of its last checkpoint row, and its usage is that row's totals. For a call that ends normally it is the value persisted at call end, as before. If no checkpoint row exists, or the last one fails validation, the finalization returns `CORRUPT_STATE`.⟧ |
| 4 | Identities and authority | Writer: the live conversation runtime, under the Voice context's database principal, through the guarded checkpoint function only (no direct `INSERT` or `UPDATE` on the accumulator or checkpoint relation for any login role). Reader: the shared finalization operation (FIN-1 … FIN-4), invoked by the normal finalizer and by W2 under the Voice reconciler principal (VOX-7K-13). No other context, no administrator, no event operator |
| 5 | Authoritative durable state | The cumulative accumulator and the checkpoint rows (G-02). `checkpoint_at`, totals and turn sequence are written together and never updated |
| 6 | Transitions | Per conversation: `ACCUMULATING` (checkpoints may be added) → `FINALIZED` (guard claimed; no further checkpoint accepted) or → `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` (VOX-7K-16). A checkpoint is refused once the guard is claimed |
| 7 | Transaction and locks | One transaction per turn; the conversation accounting row lock serializes checkpoints of one conversation; the finalization operation takes the same lock before FIN-1, so a checkpoint and the finalization are strictly ordered |
| 8 | Idempotency and concurrency | (organization, conversation, turn sequence) is unique; a retried checkpoint of a committed turn is a no-op that returns the stored row; an out-of-sequence turn is refused; two concurrent checkpoints of one conversation serialize on the lock. `checkpoint_at` is non-decreasing by construction (`GREATEST`), even if the database clock steps back |
| 9 | Security and tenant checks | The function sets nothing from a payload: organization and conversation come from the call session row under the tenant context set transaction-locally (7I TCX-05); every total increment is non-negative; the turn must belong to the conversation and organization |
| 10 | Failure and rollback | Any failed check raises: totals, checkpoint and turn commit together or not at all. A runtime that cannot checkpoint does not bill that turn (VOX-7K-06: under-billing at most the turns in flight, never over-billing) |
| 11 | Migration / API | G-02 (accumulator, guard, marker), extended by the checkpoint row and the guarded checkpoint function. No route changes |
| 12 | Regression oracle | T-7L-06 (§34.7) |
| 13 | Activation gate | AG-7K-06; AG-7J-04; AG-7L-04 for repair paths |
| 14 | Further owner decision | None: OD-7L-26 decided the clock. Physical names are migration choices (7B ACC-06) |

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| CKP-7L-01 [OD-7L-26] | The service checkpoint's timestamp source is PostgreSQL `clock_timestamp()`, read inside the checkpoint transaction. |
| CKP-7L-02 [OD-7L-26] | The checkpoint is written in the same transaction that commits the turn's validated usage; timestamp and cumulative totals commit atomically. |
| CKP-7L-03 [OD-7L-26] | The timestamp is read **after** the turn's usage is written in that transaction. (`clock_timestamp()` is volatile and returns the time of the call, not the transaction start; `now()` / `DEFAULT NOW()` would return the transaction start and is not used.) |
| CKP-7L-04 [OD-7L-26] | The row is bound to organization, conversation, turn sequence and finalization generation; the turn sequence must be the next one. |
| CKP-7L-05 [OD-7L-26] | `checkpoint_at` never precedes the previous accepted checkpoint of the conversation. |
| CKP-7L-06 [OD-7L-26] | Ordering is by the conversation accounting row lock (as FIL-7L-13 does for invoices), so concurrent writers cannot interleave. |
| CKP-7L-07 [OD-7L-26] | Invalid evidence (negative increment, wrong organization, finalized conversation, out-of-sequence turn) rolls the whole transaction back. |
| CKP-7L-08 [OD-7L-26] | No runtime, client, provider or application clock value is accepted as, or substituted for, `checkpoint_at`; the function has no timestamp parameter. |
| CKP-7L-09 [OD-7L-26; 7K VOX-7K-19] | No estimated, synthetic or recovery-worker value is ever a service-end time. W1 and W2 have no parameter through which a time could enter. |
| CKP-7L-10 [OD-7L-26] | No billable time beyond the interval the checkpoint proves: EV-079's totals are the last checkpoint's totals; post-checkpoint service is not billed. |
| CKP-7L-11 [OD-7L-26] | `checkpoint_at` is the supported accounting cutoff. It may be later than the end of the counted service by the checkpoint latency; it never precedes usage it covers. It is not the provider's disconnect instant, and the provider's call-end time is not substituted for it (OD-7L-18 limits on provider evidence). |
| CKP-7L-12 [OD-7L-17; OD-7L-26] | No checkpoint, or a checkpoint failing VOX-7K-17 validation → `CORRUPT_STATE`, the `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` marker, no EV-079, no usage. |
| CKP-7L-13 [7L] | Preserved: the shared atomic finalizer (FIN-1 … FIN-4); EV-079's occurrence-time semantics (OCC-01 … -07; its `occurred_at` is the service-end time defined above); OD-7L-17 … -22; the 90-day horizon (7F RET-7F-09; VBR-7L-13). |

**What remains unproven, stated.** The checkpoint proves which service the totals cover and when the accounting stopped. It does not prove that the provider stopped carrying the call at that instant, and nothing in V1 bills the difference. That difference is under-billing only (RR-7L-C1, §34.9).

#### 34.6.4 AP-7L-27 (vii) — recording cleanup intent and versioned-object deletion (OD-7L-02)

*Superseded by §35 (third remediation): the deletion protocol, state machine, evidence and adapter admission are §35.4 – §35.7; the 6D text is the revised AP-7L-27 (vii) of §35.8. The fields below stand only where §35 does not replace them.*

| # | Field | Content |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Target and rule | 6D §16.3a; 7F §28.9 (CON-08); 3F §11.3 |
| 2 | Existing contract | 6D §16.3a hands the object key in `_internal_cleanup_ref` (L786, L793), which OD-7L-02 forbids. 3F §11.3: S3 with **versioning enabled** on the primary bucket, **cross-region replication** to a secondary bucket, and a lifecycle transition of recordings to a cold storage class after 90 days. OD-7K-01 / -02: no second-region copy for an `INDIA_ENTERPRISE` stack; elsewhere only with recorded authorization |
| 3 | Replacement text (6D §16.3a) | §33.8.2 item (vii) text stands, with the bracket replaced by: ⟦**Absent, for the S3-compatible versioned adapter**, means all of the following, verified after the deletions and recorded as evidence on the intent: (a) for every bucket that may hold a copy of the object — the primary bucket and every replication destination recorded for the stack at the time the recording was stored — a version listing of the exact key returns no object version and no delete marker; (b) every version was deleted by an explicit version-specific delete, never by a plain delete (which on a versioned bucket only adds a delete marker); (c) every delete marker for the key was itself deleted by version; (d) no version is under an object-lock retention or legal-hold setting, and if one is, the intent stays open and a privacy incident is raised; it is never closed on the remaining versions. Replication does not propagate version-specific deletes, so each destination bucket is deleted and verified on its own. The cold-storage class is a storage class of the same object versions and is covered by (a) – (c). **A storage adapter that cannot enumerate and delete every version and delete marker of a key in every bucket that may hold it is not admitted for recordings.**⟧ |
| 4 | Identities and authority | Intent written by the Voice delete transaction (the 6D recording-deletion route or the governed erasure operation) under the Voice principal. Executor: CON-08 under the Voice context principal, reading the object reference from the intent, never from a payload. Storage credentials: a cleanup identity with list-versions and delete-version rights on the recording prefix only, held by the CON-08 workload alone |
| 5 | Durable state | The cleanup intent (organization, recording, object reference, bucket set, state, attempts, evidence) in a Voice-owned relation (G-15); `voice.recordings.status`, `deleted_at` (`014_5C`) |
| 6 | Transitions | Intent `PENDING` → `DELETING` → `VERIFIED_ABSENT` (closed) ; `PENDING` / `DELETING` → `BLOCKED_HOLD` while a hold or unexpired retention duty applies → back to `PENDING` on release; `DELETING` → `INCIDENT` when a locked version is found (stays open) |
| 7 | Transaction and locks | The intent is created in the delete transaction (with the `recording.deleted` outbox row). Each attempt: lock the intent row; check holds (the organization hold gate, 7I HLD); record attempt start; commit; then storage calls; then one transaction records the evidence and the new state. No database transaction is held across storage I/O (7A PR-06) |
| 8 | Idempotency and concurrency | Deleting an absent version is success; the intent row lock admits one attempt at a time; a redelivered `recording.deleted` finds the intent and does not create a second one |
| 9 | Security and tenant checks | The object reference must begin with the organization's own prefix `org/{organization_id}/recordings/` (5C §16 path convention; `chk_rec_storage_ref_path` in `014_5C` enforces only `org/%`, so the organization part is checked by the function). Because 5C clears `storage_ref` when a recording is deleted, the intent's copy of the reference is the only one left, which is why OD-7L-02 makes it Voice-owned and durable; a reference outside it raises an incident and deletes nothing; no presigned URL is issued for a recording whose intent exists; the access guard (AG-7L-01) already denies reads once deletion is requested |
| 10 | Failure and rollback | A failed storage call leaves the intent open and is retried on the frozen budget (7G); a missing bucket in the recorded set is an incident, not a success; evidence is written only after verification |

Documents that are `PENDING`, `PROCESSING`, `FAILED`, `ARCHIVED` or `DELETED`, and any document with `deleted_at` set whatever its status, are not counted. The value is recomputed by the Knowledge consumer of `document.indexed` and `document.deleted` (CON-09) and by nothing else; no route accepts it and no client supplies it.⟧ |
| 4 | Identities and authority | CON-09 under the Knowledge context principal (7I CTX-01); its write goes through the Knowledge recount function of 7I ERR-7I-17 / IR-44 ("recompute without a value argument") |

| 7 | Transaction and locks | One `READ COMMITTED` transaction: tenant context from the validated envelope; `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the knowledge-base row; then the `COUNT(*)` with the predicate, taken after the lock, so its snapshot is later than any commit the lock waited for (7F §28.10 row "Concurrency-race protection"); `UPDATE` of `document_count`; completion record (7I CEV); commit; then `XACK` |
| 8 | Idempotency and concurrency | Recount, not increment (IC-4; 7F OC-5): a duplicate, a retry, a delayed `document.indexed` for an older version and a reversed order all produce the current count. Two concurrent recounts serialize on the row lock |
| 9 | Security and tenant checks | Organization from the validated envelope; the knowledge base is located by the document named by the event (`knowledge.documents` row) within that organization, and the payload's `knowledge_base_id` must equal it. If the document row is not found, the payload `knowledge_base_id` is used only after verifying under the tenant context that the knowledge base exists in that organization; otherwise the entry is classified as a handler failure (7G), not acknowledged as applied. Because the effect is a recount of authoritative rows in the same organization, a wrong identifier can at worst recount another knowledge base of the same tenant correctly; it can never inflate a count or cross a tenant |
| 10 | Failure and rollback | Any failure rolls back the recount; the entry is retried under 7G; nothing is acknowledged before the commit |
| 11 | Migration / API | The recount function and its grant (IR-44; G-08). No route change. **6F gains no field and loses none** |
| 12 | Regression oracle | T-7L-08 (§34.7) |

| 14 | Further owner decision | None: OD-7L-28 |

#### 34.6.11 AP-7L-45 — Voice accounting repair, correction and non-billable disposition (architecture contract)

| # | Field | Content |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Target | 6D (reconciliation states and Voice repair proposal) and 6K (Billing approval and non-billable disposition); 7K VOX-7K-16 … -18; VBR-7L-01 … -14 |
| 2 | Existing contract | `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` is left only by an owner repair and re-finalization (VOX-7K-18). No terminal non-billable state exists. No repair authority exists. OD-7L-17 … -22 decide the policy |
| 3 | Replacement text | ⟦A conversation marked `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` has one reconciliation case. **Repair**: a Voice-authorized principal records a repair proposal citing admissible evidence (VBR-7L-04, -05) and the corrected durable accounting state; a different, Billing-authorized principal approves or rejects it. On approval, one transaction applies the corrected state to the accumulator, clears the marker, writes the audit record and invokes the shared finalization (FIN-1 … FIN-4), which writes EV-079 with the original service-end time. **Non-billable disposition**: a Billing-authorized principal, with an independent reviewer, records the disposition with evidence and reason code; one transaction claims the conversation's finalization guard for the current finalization generation with outcome `NON_BILLABLE`, closes the case and writes the audit record; no EV-079 is written then or later for that generation. Neither operation changes an invoice. A repair that cannot establish an exact supported value is rejected and the marker stays.⟧ |
| 4 | Identities and authority | Voice repair proposer (Voice-authorized human principal through a Voice route); Billing approver and Billing disposer (Billing-authorized human principals through Billing routes), distinct persons; an independent reviewer for the disposition. Database: the Voice and Billing context functions, executable only by the API role behind those routes after an API action proof (7I pattern ERR-7I-19). **Not**: `app_platform_admin`, event-operations roles, `app_worker`, any scheduler |
| 5 | Durable state | The marker and reason (G-02); the reconciliation case; the proposal; the approval or rejection; the disposition; the audit record (VBR-7L-12) |
| 6 | Transitions | Case `OPEN` → `PROPOSED` → `APPROVED` → `REPAIRED` (EV-079 written) ; `PROPOSED` → `REJECTED` → `OPEN` ; `OPEN` → `DISPOSED_NON_BILLABLE` (terminal). `REPAIRED` and `DISPOSED_NON_BILLABLE` are mutually exclusive through the finalization guard (VBR-7L-10 (5)) |
| 7 | Transaction and locks | Each transition one transaction that locks the case and the conversation accounting row, in that order, and commits the audit record with it |
| 8 | Idempotency and concurrency | One case per conversation and finalization generation; an approval or disposition carries an idempotency key; a second disposition is a no-op; a finalization racing a disposition is decided by the guard (exactly one wins) |
| 9 | Security and tenant checks | Proposer ≠ approver ≠ reviewer, checked in the function from authenticated identities, not arguments alone; organization from the conversation row; the evidence references must belong to the same organization and conversation |
| 10 | Failure and rollback | Audit insert failure rolls back the transition (VBR-7L-12); invalid evidence rejects the proposal; nothing is applied partially |
| 11 | Migration / API | G-16 (case, proposal, approval, disposition, functions, permissions); 6D and 6K route additions by controlled amendment, with no change to existing routes |
| 12 | Regression oracle | T-7L-02 (§33.7) |
| 13 | Activation gate | AG-7L-04; AG-7K-06; AG-7J-04 |
| 14 | Further owner decision | Physical names of states, functions and permissions: OD-7L-29 item (6). The policy is fully decided (OD-7L-17 … -22) |

### 34.7 New regression specifications

All **specified; not executed.**

**T-7L-06 — service checkpoint (owner Voice; gates AG-7K-06, AG-7L-04).** (a) Two turns checkpointed: totals equal the sum, `checkpoint_at` non-decreasing, both bound to organization, conversation, turn and generation. (b) The test sets the database clock back between turns: the second `checkpoint_at` equals the first (`GREATEST`). (c) A checkpoint call that supplies a timestamp: impossible (no parameter); a client value in the payload is ignored. (d) A negative increment, a wrong organization, an out-of-sequence turn: rollback; no totals change. (e) Process killed after the turn's usage write and before commit: nothing of that turn is persisted. (f) Abnormal end after three checkpoints: W2 finalization emits EV-079 with the third `checkpoint_at` as `occurred_at` and the third totals. (g) Abnormal end with no checkpoint: `CORRUPT_STATE`, marker, no EV-079. (h) A checkpoint attempted after the guard is claimed: refused. (i) Two concurrent checkpoint calls for one conversation: serialized; one per turn sequence. (j) The reaper's forced end writes an end time from its own clock: that value is never read by the finalization (statement-level assertion). (k) A conversation whose last checkpoint is more than 90 days old when repaired: EV-079 carries that `checkpoint_at`; CON-06 holds it (VBR-7L-13).

**T-7L-07 — recording cleanup (owner Voice; gate CON-08). Replaced by §35.9.** (a) Versioned bucket with three versions and a delete marker, replicated to one destination: completion only after every version and marker is deleted by version in both buckets and both listings are empty. (b) A plain delete only: the listing shows versions; the intent stays open. (c) A version under object-lock retention: intent `INCIDENT`, never closed. (d) A legal hold on the organization: `BLOCKED_HOLD`; nothing deleted; released → resumes. (e) An object reference outside the organization's prefix: incident; nothing deleted. (f) Redelivered `recording.deleted`: no second intent. (g) Storage error mid-way: intent open; retried; completion recorded once. (h) A presigned URL request after the intent exists: refused. (i) An unadmitted adapter: no recording is stored through it.

**T-7L-08 — CON-09 (owner Knowledge; gates CON-09, AG-7L-06).** (a) Documents READY ×3, PENDING, PROCESSING, FAILED, ARCHIVED, DELETED, one READY with `deleted_at` set: count = 3. (b) `document.indexed` delivered twice and out of order with `document.deleted`: count equals the authoritative state after each commit. (c) A re-index producing a second `document.indexed` for the same document: count unchanged. (d) Payload `knowledge_base_id` differs from the document's: not applied, failure recorded. (e) Envelope organization A, knowledge base of organization B: no row visible; nothing written in B. (f) Two concurrent recounts: serialized; final count correct. (g) A document moved READY → ARCHIVED without an event, then any later event on that knowledge base: the recount excludes it (DCN-7L-08). (h) No route accepts `document_count`.

### 35.2 Root cause, before and after

**Before (§34.6.4).** The intent became `VERIFIED_ABSENT` when, after version-specific deletes, the version listing of the key was empty in the primary bucket and in every replication destination *recorded for the stack at the time the recording was stored*. That is one observation at one instant. It proves nothing about three things:

1. **A replication still in flight.** AWS documents that "for temporary failures, such as if a bucket or Region is unavailable, replication status doesn't transition to `FAILED`, but remains `PENDING`. After the resource is back online, Amazon S3 resumes replicating those objects." A version that was still `PENDING` when the listings were taken can therefore be written to a destination after the verification. AWS also does **not** document what happens to a `PENDING` replication when the source version is deleted first. It only advises: "Before deleting an object from a source bucket that has replication enabled, check the object's replication status to make sure that the object has been replicated."
2. **Destinations added later.** Live replication does not copy existing objects to a destination added later, but **S3 Batch Replication** does. It can also replicate replicas and previously replicated objects. A destination set frozen "at the time the recording was stored" misses both.
3. **Writes in place.** A Batch Copy, a re-upload or a copy out of an archive class creates a new version of the same key.

**After (§35).** `VERIFIED_ABSENT` is reachable only after a proof with four parts:
1. A **fence**: no ordinary write, replication-configuration change or batch job can touch the key.
2. **Replication quiescence**: every known version, in every bucket of the replication closure, has a terminal replication status, or is a replica that no rule re-replicates, and no batch job is open.
3. **Deletion**: every version and every delete marker is deleted by version ID in every closure bucket.
4. **Final verification**: the evidence shows that no documented provider mechanism can recreate a version, because no source version of the key remains anywhere in the closure and the fence still holds.

An empty listing is never sufficient by itself. Where any element cannot be proven, the intent stays non-terminal and escalates (§35.5).

### 35.3 Provider semantics relied on (AWS S3; read 2026-10-14)

Only documented behaviour is used. The protocol relies on nothing that the provider leaves undocumented.

| # | Documented behaviour (Amazon S3 User Guide / API Reference) | Use in §35 |
|---:|---|---|
| S-1 | A source object version reports `x-amz-replication-status` `PENDING`, `COMPLETED` or `FAILED` (on `HeadObject` / `GetObject` with a version ID) **if it is eligible for replication**. A replica reports `REPLICA`. A version not eligible for any rule returns no status header | Per-version quiescence (RDQ-7L-10) |
| S-2 | With several destinations the source status is `COMPLETED` only when replication succeeded to **all** destinations; it stays `PENDING` until all complete; it is `FAILED` if one or more failed | One status per source version covers all its destinations |
| S-3 | Temporary failures keep `PENDING`, and replication resumes later. `FAILED` cannot be retried by live replication: "you must upload the object again, or you must use S3 Batch Replication" | `PENDING` is never treated as quiescent; `FAILED` is quiescent only while the batch fence holds |
| S-4 | A `DELETE` with a version ID deletes that version in the bucket where it is issued and **is not replicated** to destinations. A `DELETE` without a version ID adds a delete marker, which some configurations replicate | Every closure bucket is deleted separately, by version ID; no unversioned delete is issued |
| S-5 | Live replication does not replicate replicas created by another rule, does not re-replicate objects already replicated to a former destination, and does not replicate objects that existed before a rule was added; **Batch Replication** does all three | Batch jobs are fenced and checked (RDQ-7L-08, -12) |
| S-6 | Batch Replication cannot re-replicate a version deleted by version ID from the destination; a Batch **Copy** in place creates new source versions that then replicate | Batch Copy is fenced like Batch Replication |
| S-7 | Objects in archive classes (Glacier Flexible Retrieval, Deep Archive, Intelligent-Tiering archive tiers) are not replicated until restored and copied to another class; the copy is a new version | Restore-and-copy is a write, fenced by RDQ-7L-05 |
| S-8 | S3 Lifecycle does not expire or transition a version while its replication status is `PENDING` or `FAILED` | Lifecycle cannot race the quiescence wait |
| S-9 | S3 Batch Operations `ListJobs` returns current jobs and jobs ended recently, with statuses `Active`, `Cancelled`, `Cancelling`, `Complete`, `Completing`, `Failed`, `Failing`, `New`, `Paused`, `Pausing`, `Preparing`, `Ready`, `Suspended`; `DescribeJob` returns a job's operation and manifest | Batch-job evidence (E-8) |
| S-10 | Strong read-after-write consistency for object `PUT`, `DELETE`, `LIST` and `HEAD`. **Bucket configurations are eventually consistent** | Final listings are meaningful; configuration snapshots are compared over time, not trusted at one instant (RDQ-7L-07) |
| S-11 | A presigned URL is usable repeatedly until its expiry, expires earlier when its signing credential expires or is revoked, and **a download begun before expiry continues past it** | Residual of issued capabilities (RDQ-7L-25; RR-7L-R1) |
| S-12 | Object Lock retention prevents deletion of a locked version for its period; retention information is replicated to replicas | Lock → `INCIDENT` (RDQ-7L-19) |
| S-13 | S3 Inventory reports list object versions with their replication status | Post-completion sentinel (RDQ-7L-27) |

### 35.4 Replication-safe deletion contract

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| RDQ-7L-01 [OD-7L-02] | **Three conditions, kept apart.** *Logically denied*: no ordinary path serves the recording. This holds from the commit of the intent. *Physically deleted*: every version recorded in the intent's inventory has been deleted by version ID in every closure bucket. *Verified permanently absent* (`VERIFIED_ABSENT`): §35.6 E-1 … E-18 hold together. No status, report, tenant response or audit text names a weaker condition by a stronger name. An inaccessible object is never reported as deleted, and a deleted one never as permanently absent before E-1 … E-18. |
| RDQ-7L-02 [OD-7L-02] | **Object identity.** The intent holds: organization; recording ID; the exact key, taken from the row in the delete transaction (5C §5.8: `org/{organization_id}/recordings/{year}/{month}/{call_id}.{ext}`); the primary bucket; the checksum recorded on the row (`checksum_sha256`, `014_5C`); the stack identifier. The key must begin with `org/{organization_id}/recordings/` for the intent's organization; otherwise the intent goes to `INCIDENT` (`KEY_OUT_OF_PREFIX`) and nothing is deleted. Listings are by exact key: a prefix listing is filtered to `Key` equal to the recorded key, so a neighbouring key is never deleted and never mistaken for absence. |
| RDQ-7L-03 [7L] | **Replication closure.** The set of buckets that may hold a version of the key. It is the transitive closure, starting at the primary bucket, of every replication destination, and also of every other copy target (a backup vault, a cross-account copy). Each destination contributes for **any** period between the recording's earliest version and the closure computation, according to the destination-history record (G-17), not according to today's configuration alone. A destination's own replication rules for the recording prefix are followed in turn. |
| RDQ-7L-04 [7L] | **Destination history.** The replication configuration of every recording bucket changes only by a governed stack-configuration operation, which writes the destination-history record (G-17): bucket, rule identifiers, destinations, prefix filters, delete-marker setting, replica-modification-sync setting, effective-from and effective-to. Provider-side enforcement: only the governed provisioning identity holds `s3:PutReplicationConfiguration` and `s3:DeleteReplicationConfiguration` on recording buckets (bucket policy deny for every other principal). **Revised for FG-7L-R5-03:** that identity holds no standing change permission; each change uses a change session bound to a committed change record (§35.4f ACF-7L-03). At closure computation, the executor reads the current configuration of every closure bucket (`GetBucketReplication`) and compares it with G-17. **A difference is `INCIDENT` (`CONFIG_UNRECORDED`), never a silent update.** |
| RDQ-7L-05 [OD-7L-02] | **Write fence.** From the intent's commit, no ordinary path writes the key: the row is `DELETED`, which is terminal (6D §16.3; 7F CON-08 "the row is never re-stored"); no upload URL or recorder write is issued for a recording that is not `IN_PROGRESS`; an object key is never reused (7F §28.9 obligation). Copy-in-place, restore-and-copy from an archive class, and Batch Copy are writes and are covered by RDQ-7L-08. No cleanup session and no closure-verifier identity holds a `PutObject`, copy, replication or job-creation right, and the role and bucket policies deny them explicitly (TSA-7L-04, -06, -08). |
| RDQ-7L-06 [7L] | **Configuration fence.** From `FENCED` until the intent is terminal, the governed stack-configuration operation of RDQ-7L-04 cannot change the replication configuration of a closure bucket. The operation takes, exclusively, a per-bucket configuration lock in PostgreSQL that the intent holds in share mode across these states (a lock *record*, not a session lock, so that no transaction spans provider I/O). |
| RDQ-7L-07 [7L; S-10] | **Configuration snapshot.** At `QUIESCING` entry and again at `VERIFYING`, the executor reads `GetBucketReplication` for every closure bucket and stores a digest of each. Equal digests, with G-17 showing no governed change in between, are evidence E-4. Because bucket configuration is eventually consistent, the first snapshot is taken only once the last G-17 change of that bucket is older than the propagation allowance `T_cfg` ([CAND] 15 minutes, the figure AWS itself gives for a versioning change; [MEAS] on the provider). |
| RDQ-7L-08 [7L; S-5, S-6, S-16, S-17] | **Batch fence.** Only the governed provisioning identity can create or resume a Batch Operations job (`s3:CreateJob`, `s3:UpdateJobStatus`, with the `iam:PassRole` it needs) that can reach a closure bucket. The provider enforces this in every account that could host such a job, by SCP and by the closure buckets' own policies (§35.4b BQA-7L-04). The per-bucket lock alone does not enforce it. A governed batch operation (Batch Replication, Batch Copy, restore-and-copy) that covers the recording prefix of a bucket takes the same per-bucket lock exclusively. It therefore cannot start while an intent on that bucket is between `FENCED` and its terminal state, and an intent cannot pass `QUIESCING` while such a job is open. |
| RDQ-7L-09 [7L; S-25, S-26] | **Version inventory (revised for FG-7L-R5-01).** In `QUIESCING`, for every closure bucket: one complete, paginated, exact-key `ListObjectVersions` run classifies every entry as class V (a `Version` element) or class M (a `DeleteMarker` element) (§35.4d OC-7L-01). For each class V entry, `HeadObject` with its version ID records `x-amz-replication-status`, storage class, size, checksum and Object Lock retention / legal-hold state (OC-7L-02). For each class M entry the listing entry is the evidence; no `HeadObject` metadata is required, and a `405` is handled as OC-7L-03 states. The inventory, with each entry's class, is stored on the intent (G-15). A version whose checksum or size contradicts the row's `checksum_sha256` is still deleted: every entry of the exact key is in scope, whatever its content or class. |
| RDQ-7L-10 [7L; S-1 … S-3] | **Quiescence predicate, per entry.** For class M, quiescence is defined by OC-7L-05 (m1), (m2); the clauses below define it for class V. A class V version is quiescent when it is: (a) a source version with status `COMPLETED`; (b) a source version with status `FAILED`, while the batch fence of RDQ-7L-08 is held; (c) a source version with no status header, in a bucket whose recorded configuration (G-17) shows that no rule made it eligible during its lifetime; or (d) a replica (`REPLICA`), in a bucket where no rule re-replicates it (S-5) and replica modification sync is off. **`PENDING` is never quiescent.** A status that contradicts G-17 (for example a source version with no status in a bucket whose rule covers it) is `INCIDENT` (`STATUS_UNEXPLAINED`). |
| RDQ-7L-11 [7L] | **No deletion before quiescence.** No version is deleted in any closure bucket until every version of the key in every closure bucket is quiescent. Per class (OC-7L-06): a class V deletion needs Q_V(key); a class M deletion needs Q_V(key), Q_M(key) and every class V entry of its bucket `RESOLVED_DELETED`. This is the rule that closes the counterexample: the provider documents no outcome for deleting a `PENDING` source version, so the protocol never creates that state. |
| RDQ-7L-12 [7L; S-9, S-14, S-15] | **Batch-job evidence, account-complete (revised for FG-7L-R4-02).** In `QUIESCING`, and again in `VERIFYING`, the protocol of §35.4b runs. In every (account, Region) of the job-discovery set (BQA-7L-02, -03), `ListJobs` is called with every non-terminal status (`Active`, `Cancelling`, `Completing`, `Failing`, `New`, `Paused`, `Pausing`, `Preparing`, `Ready`, `Suspended`) and paginated by `NextToken` to the end. `DescribeJob` is called for each job returned. The intent passes only if no covering job (BQA-7L-06) exists anywhere in that set, and only if the creation fence (BQA-7L-04) and the authorization-surface digests (BQA-7L-07) hold. A job whose scope cannot be determined counts as covering. **A listing in the source account is never treated as a global inventory (S-14).** An incomplete proof is never a pass (BQA-7L-11). |
| RDQ-7L-13 [OD-7L-02; 7I HLD-03, -10, -11, -14, -15] | **Hold gate before every provider deletion (replaced for FG-7L-R4-01).** There is no batch authorization and no lease; the former `T_auth` is withdrawn. Each version-specific delete is admitted only by its own **issue record**. That record is committed by a transaction that takes the organization's hold gate in share mode and evaluates the effective-hold function for the row that holds the storage reference, as §35.4a HLC-7L-02 specifies. The provider admits the request only before the record's deadline (HLC-7L-04). **The erasure of that version linearizes at the issue commit** (HLC-7L-03). A hold that commits earlier prevents it. A hold that commits later does not preserve that one version, and the outcome is recorded against the hold (HLC-7L-08). Every version not yet issued is preserved. Frozen 7I HLD-03 states only two orders, and this third interval needs the controlled wording of AP-7L-53. Until AP-7L-53 is applied, AG-7L-09 stays closed. The intent is registered as an erasure step (7I ERA-05; HLD-14). |
| RDQ-7L-14 [S-4] | **Version-specific deletion, every closure bucket.** Every inventoried version and every delete marker is deleted by `DeleteObject` with its version ID, bucket by bucket: the primary first, then each destination; within a bucket, every class V entry before any class M entry (OC-7L-06). Each delete has its own issue record (HLC-7L-02) and its own per-operation session (TSA-7L-03). **No unversioned delete is issued.** It would add a delete marker and remove nothing. The provider refuses one in any case (TSA-7L-04, -06). |
| RDQ-7L-15 [7L] | **Deletion acknowledgement is not proof.** A delete response is recorded, but a version counts as physically deleted only when an exact-key listing of that bucket, taken after `not_after + T_skew`, no longer shows it (§35.4e OPT-7L-03 T-1 (a), T-2). A delete that returns an error, times out or is ambiguous is resolved only by the evidence of OPT-7L-03; an ambiguous one with the version still listed is `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN` and is never resolved by elapsed time (OPT-7L-04). It is retried only through a new issue record, which checks the hold gate again. |
| RDQ-7L-16 [7L; S-10] | **Final verification.** In `VERIFYING`, after every delete: complete, paginated exact-key listings of every closure bucket (OC-7L-01) return no class V and no class M entry; the configuration snapshot equals the one taken at `QUIESCING` (RDQ-7L-07); RDQ-7L-12 holds again; the authorization-change reconciliation of §35.4f covers the whole interval (ACF-7L-05, -06); the fence locks are still held; the capability horizon has passed (RDQ-7L-25); for a CDN in the delivery path, its evidence holds (RDQ-7L-26). If a version or marker is found, the intent returns to `QUIESCING` with a new inventory, and the appearance is recorded. A third return to `QUIESCING` ([CAND] 3) is `INCIDENT` (`UNEXPLAINED_REAPPEARANCE`). Returns are counted from the intent's commit, or from the latest closure of an `UNEXPLAINED_REAPPEARANCE` occurrence of the intent, whichever is later (revised for FG-7L-R7-01; §35.4h IRE-7L-09). |
| RDQ-7L-17 [7L] | **Why E-1 … E-18 prove permanent absence on S3.** Every documented way to create a version of the key is excluded: the write fence (RDQ-7L-05) excludes a client or worker `PUT` and every copy; the batch fence and evidence (RDQ-7L-08, -12), which are account-complete and fenced by the provider (§35.4b), exclude Batch Replication and Batch Copy in any account that could reach the key; quiescence before deletion (RDQ-7L-11) excludes live replication that is still in flight (S-3); version-specific deletes are not replicated (S-4), so no deletion itself causes a copy; FAILED versions can be retried only by a fenced batch job (S-3); and after deletion **no source version of the key exists in any closure bucket**, so no replication of any kind has a source to copy from (S-5, S-6). The configuration fence and snapshot (RDQ-7L-06, -07) keep the closure exactly the one inventoried. |
| RDQ-7L-18 [OD-7L-02; 7I] | **Legal holds.** A held recording is not deleted. Its versions stay in the closure buckets and are reachable only through the restricted pathways (OCG-7L-06: the purpose-bound break-glass functions of `107_5B5`; the dual-controlled inspection of OD-7I-30). Logical denial of ordinary access continues. While held, the versions are checked for presence (HLC-7L-13). On release, an intent in `BLOCKED_HOLD` resumes at `QUIESCING` with a new inventory (HLC-7L-11); one in `INCIDENT` stays there (ICM-7L-10). Which versions were deleted before a hold, and why, is recorded per version (HLC-7L-08). |
| RDQ-7L-19 [S-12] | **Object Lock.** A version under Object Lock retention or legal hold cannot be deleted for its period. The intent goes to `INCIDENT` (`OBJECT_LOCKED`, Class 1) and stays open. The other entries are deleted only by containment issues under ICM-7L-03 and F (revised for FG-7L-R6-01). It is never closed on the remaining versions. No identity holds `s3:BypassGovernanceRetention` for recording buckets. RAD-7L-05 excludes Object Lock defaults on recording buckets at admission, so this path means a configuration defect. |
| RDQ-7L-20 [S-7, S-8] | **Lifecycle and storage classes.** A version in an archive class is deleted by version ID like any other. Lifecycle cannot transition or expire a `PENDING` or `FAILED` version (S-8). A lifecycle expiration of a noncurrent version during the protocol only removes a version earlier; it shows in the next listing. No lifecycle rule may add a delete marker that a recording rule replicates (RAD-7L-04). |
| RDQ-7L-21 [7I ERA-01] | **Evidence is kept, content is not.** The intent keeps the key (class `SEC`, 7I CLS-08, encrypted at rest under the Voice context, readable only by the cleanup executor), version IDs, checksums, statuses, digests and timestamps. These remain proof of processing (7I ERA-01, -02). No byte of the recording is copied for evidence. |
| RDQ-7L-22 [7F EXT-01] | **Crash safety.** Every state change is one committed PostgreSQL transaction. No transaction spans provider I/O. Provider reads are repeatable and deletes are idempotent. An executor that crashes, at any point, resumes in the recorded state and repeats that state's step from its beginning: a new inventory in `QUIESCING`, re-listing before re-deleting in `DELETING`, the whole verification in `VERIFYING`. A crash after a delete and before its record is harmless when the next listing no longer shows the version (OPT-7L-03 T-2). A crash after an issue commit leaves an open operation. That operation is never sent again after its deadline, and no second credential is minted for it. It is resolved only by OPT-7L-03 evidence; a crash after a send may leave it `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN` (HLC-7L-09; §35.4e fault sequence 9). |
| RDQ-7L-23 [7L; S-18 … S-22] | **Credentials and tenant scope (replaced for FG-7L-R4-03 by §35.4c).** The cleanup executor runs under the Voice context principal in PostgreSQL and **holds no standing storage permission**. Each object-level action uses a session minted for that one operation by a separate storage-authority broker: an exact-key listing, the inspection of one version, or the deletion of one version. The broker takes its binding from the committed Voice intent, never from the caller (TSA-7L-02). The session is bound **by the provider** to the intent's organization prefix (a session tag read by the role policy and by the bucket policy), to the exact bucket, key and version, and to an admission deadline (TSA-7L-03 … -06). Account-scoped reads use a separate, read-only closure-verifier identity with no object access: replication configuration, policies, job discovery (TSA-7L-08). Neither identity holds `PutObject`, copy, `PutReplicationConfiguration`, `CreateJob`, unversioned `DeleteObject` or `BypassGovernanceRetention`. The former statement, that "a bucket policy cannot list a condition per tenant", was wrong: a policy variable over a session tag does exactly that (S-19). RDQ-7L-02's check in the executor remains, as a second and independent check. |
| RDQ-7L-24 [OD-7K-01, -02, -05] | **Residency.** For a class E stack (any stack that has hosted an `INDIA_ENTERPRISE` organization), every closure bucket must be in the contracted region (7K REG-7K-18 conformance record). A registered, admitted closure bucket outside it is a residency incident: the intent goes to `INCIDENT` (`RESIDENCY_VIOLATION`, Class 1). Deletion there, and in every other closure bucket, continues **only** as containment issues under ICM-7L-03 and the fresh-evidence predicate F, because deletion reduces exposure and is not a new transfer (revised for FG-7L-R6-01). A copy in a bucket that G-17 does not register is `CONFIG_UNRECORDED` or `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` (Class 2), and nothing is deleted until a resolution registers that bucket (§35.4g, situation 3). For a class S stack, a cross-region destination is permitted only for the recovery region `R_r`, with the authorization record of REG-7K-17; any other destination is the same incident. Nothing here changes any journal policy (OD-7K-05) or authorizes any copy. **Revised for FG-7L-R7-01.** A bucket for which a `RESIDENCY_VIOLATION` occurrence of this intent was closed as *contained* (§35.4h) stays in the closure history and is inventoried at every later pass, but does not raise the reason again while it holds no entry of the key and no rule recorded in G-17 can write the key there. A new entry there, or such a rule, opens a new occurrence (IRC-7L-03). The violation itself stays recorded as a residency incident. |
| RDQ-7L-25 [6A §29; 6D §16.2b; S-11] | **Issued capabilities.** From the intent's commit no new presigned URL is issued: 6D issues one only for `STORED`, and AG-7L-01 denies it. Each issued URL is audited with its lifetime (`RECORDING_ACCESS_GRANTED`, `expires_in_seconds = 900`; 6D §16.2b). A URL cannot be revoked one by one (S-11). It stops working at the earlier of its expiry and the deletion of its version in its bucket (S-10). A transfer begun before either continues to its end (S-11). The **capability horizon** is the latest `issued_at + expires_in_seconds` among the recording's grants, and `VERIFIED_ABSENT` requires the database clock to be past it. |
| RDQ-7L-26 [3F §13.1, row "Call recordings (S3)"] | **CDN.** 3F §13.1 says that recordings are served "via signed CDN URLs". If a CDN is in the delivery path, the adapter is admitted only if recordings are not cached at the edge (verified at admission, RAD-7L-06), or if a path invalidation is issued in `DELETING` and its provider-reported completion is recorded before `VERIFYING` (E-11). A CDN that can do neither makes the adapter **NOT ADMITTED** for recordings. |
| RDQ-7L-27 [7L; S-13; 7I ERA-22] | **Sentinel after completion.** After `VERIFIED_ABSENT`, the next two S3 Inventory reports ([CAND] 2) of every closure bucket that cover the recording prefix are checked for the key. The 7I ERA-22 orphan reconciliation also runs. Any later appearance is a privacy incident, and its privacy-incident record is written. The sentinel's transaction records its result and a challenge record and makes `VERIFIED_ABSENT → REOPENED`. It opens no reason by itself, because a report entry is not an exact-key listing (§35.4k PCI-7L-03). In `REOPENED`, the exact-key listings decide: a write after the commit opens its reason (`REOPENED → INCIDENT`); otherwise the intent runs the protocol again (`REOPENED → QUIESCING`). The earlier verification is recorded as challenged, and then as falsified if a listing confirms the entry, by immutable records; it is never overwritten (PCI-7L-05, -06; revised for FG-7L-R9-01). |
| RDQ-7L-28 [7I RTN-7K-07; HLD-18] | **Deadlines are not extended.** The intent carries the deadline of the erasure step or retention rule that created it; 7L sets none. Replication lag, a quiescence wait, a hold-free incident or a retry never moves it. The approaching deadline is raised `T_dl,warn` before; a missed deadline is a privacy incident, recorded as the record-only `DEADLINE_MISSED`, which changes no state and grants no permission (ICM-7L-02, -08; revised for FG-7L-R6-01). A recording still present after its deadline without a hold is **unauthorized retention**. It is reported as such and is not described as bounded, resolved or deleted (7I HLD-18 pattern). Where no frozen deadline applies (a tenant deletion through the 6D route), `T_q,warn` ([CAND] 1 hour in `QUIESCING`) and `T_q,max` ([CAND] 24 hours) are alerts and escalation ages, not bounds. |
| RDQ-7L-29 [7L] | **Restore.** The intent's creation is an erasure step (RDQ-7L-13), so it is journaled (7I JRN-02). A database restored to a point before the intent is quarantined and reconciled against the journal before it serves (7I ERR-7I-12; 7K §21). The reconciliation re-creates the intent and keeps the recording `DELETED`, so a restore neither republishes nor ordinarily serves an erased recording. Object storage is not restored from database backups, and no backup copy of a recording object exists outside the closure (RAD-7L-03). |
| RDQ-7L-30 [7F EXT-02, EXT-03] | **The stream entry does not wait for replication.** OD-7L-02's intent is a durable local work-intent created in the producing transaction, so CON-08 follows 7F EXT-02. Its handler verifies, under the envelope's tenant context, that the recording row is `DELETED` and that its intent exists. It records completion, commits and acknowledges. The remaining external work belongs to the intent's executor (EXT-03) and is not re-driven by the event. This keeps a long quiescence wait from pinning LS-D-VOX (7E TRM-02). AP-7L-52 aligns the 7F CON-08 card and 7I ACC-08 with it. |

#### 35.4a Legal-hold concurrency for external deletion (FG-7L-R4-01)

**Root cause.** Frozen 7I HLD-03 is exact for an erasure inside PostgreSQL: "A hold placed concurrently therefore either commits before the erasure reads and prevents it, or waits for the erasure to commit and finds the data already gone. There is no third order." In that case the decision and the destruction are one commit. An object-storage delete is not part of any PostgreSQL transaction. The last instant at which the database can decide always precedes the instant at which the provider destroys the version. A hold that commits between the two is a **third order**, which no lock can remove, because frozen HLD-10 forbids holding the gate across a wait for another process. RDQ-7L-13 made the interval larger, with a five-minute lease over a batch, and gave it no rule. The correction:

1. shrinks the interval to one version and a short deadline that the **provider** enforces;
2. makes the hold win over every version whose deletion was not yet decided;
3. records each version that the interval affects;
4. states the interval in frozen-7I terms as a controlled amendment (AP-7L-53). Until that amendment is applied, the capability stays gated.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| HLC-7L-01 [7L; 7I HLD-02, -10, -11] | **Authoritative state.** Whether a hold applies is decided only by the hold registry, the gate and the effective-hold function's verdict (7I HLD-02, -10, -11). Whether a version may be deleted is decided only by its **deletion operation** record in the intent (G-15). The record holds: intent; bucket; exact key; version ID; attempt number; state; `issued_at`; `not_after`; the verdict reference (the empty hold list that HLD-11 returned, with the evaluation's identifier); the journal reference; the broker claim; the provider request identifiers; the outcome. The provider is authoritative for **what exists** (listings), never for **why** it was deleted. |
| HLC-7L-02 [7L; 7I HLD-10, -15; ERA-05; INV-23] | **The issue transaction, in this exact order.** One `READ COMMITTED` transaction of a guarded Voice function, with no provider I/O. (1) Take the organization's hold gate `FOR SHARE`, as the first lock (HLD-10). (2) Take the recording row `FOR SHARE`. That row holds the storage reference, so the object is attributed through it (HLD-16). (3) Take the intent row `FOR UPDATE`. Check that the intent is `DELETING`, or `INCIDENT` with containment permitted by ICM-7L-03 (revised for FG-7L-R6-01), that the fresh-evidence predicate F of ICM-7L-04 holds for the entry, that the version is in the current inventory, and that no operation is open for that (bucket, key, version): a partial unique index over the open states enforces this. The index's predicate names states only, not times: `ISSUED`, `CLAIMED`, `SEND_STARTED`, `RESPONDED_OK`, `REFUSED` and `AMBIGUOUS`. An operation leaves those states only through the resolution function, which runs after `not_after + T_skew`, so the index excludes exactly the operations under which the provider can no longer admit a request. `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN` is not in the predicate (§35.4e OPT-7L-01, -04). (4) Call the effective-hold function for the recording row. It locks the index heads it reads, to commit (HLD-11 reading discipline). (5) **Held:** create no operation; record the version `SKIPPED_HELD` on the erasure step (ERA-05); move the intent to `BLOCKED_HOLD`, or, if it is `INCIDENT`, leave it there (ICM-7L-10); commit. (6) **Not held:** insert one operation `ISSUED`, with `issued_at` read by `clock_timestamp()` in a statement after step (4) and `not_after` = `issued_at` + `T_issue` ([CAND] 60 s); append the issue to the independent journal before commit, as HLD-09 does for a placement; if the journal cannot confirm, raise, and nothing is issued; write the audit row `RECORDING_VERSION_DELETE_ISSUED` in the same transaction; commit. **One operation covers exactly one version in one bucket.** The lock order (gate → recording row → intent row → operation row → index heads) follows HLD-15. Placement, release and decisions lock none of the Voice rows, so no cycle exists. `issued_at` and `not_after` bound the provider's admission; they are never used to order a deletion against a hold. |
| HLC-7L-03 [7L; 7I HLD-03, -10] | **Linearization point: the commit of the issue transaction.** The share gate conflicts with the exclusive gate taken by every placement, release, rejection, merge and decision (HLD-10). So each of those commits either before the issue transaction takes the gate or after it commits. In the first case, the verdict of step (4) sees the commit: in `READ COMMITTED`, a statement that follows a lock wait sees every row committed before it began (HLD-10). Attribution changes are ordered by the head locks in the same way (HLD-11, -16). No hold can commit between the verdict and the issue commit. **Why this is consistent with the frozen semantics.** The first order of HLD-03 holds verbatim: a hold committed before the issue prevents it. The second order holds with "commit" read as the issue commit, the point after which the erasure of that version has been decided. What frozen HLD-03 does not say is that the version may still be readable at the provider for a bounded interval after a later hold has committed. That interval is HLC-7L-05, and AP-7L-53 states it. |
| HLC-7L-04 [7L; S-18, S-20, S-22] | **Provider-call admission.** No delete reaches the provider without an issued operation. The worker holds no standing permission (TSA-7L-01). It obtains a session from the broker, which mints one only for an operation it reads as `ISSUED` and committed (TSA-7L-02). The session policy allows `s3:DeleteObjectVersion` on exactly that bucket, key and version, and only while `aws:CurrentTime` is before `not_after` (TSA-7L-03). **After `not_after`, the provider refuses the request**, whatever the worker's clock says and however long the worker paused. An operation exists only after the gate check, and a credential exists only after the operation. So a delete never runs on an authorization that a later hold could have revoked, except for the interval of HLC-7L-05. |
| HLC-7L-05 [7L; S-20, S-24, S-37] | **The in-flight interval *W* of one operation** (revised for FG-7L-R5-02), from its issue commit to its terminality evidence (§35.4e OPT-7L-03). A hold that commits inside *W* does not preserve that operation's version. Bounds: (a) **enforced by the provider**: no request is admitted after `not_after`, with a clock difference between the database and AWS of at most `T_skew` ([CAND] 5 s; monitored; [MEAS]); (b) **not bounded**: when an admitted request takes effect is documented nowhere (S-24, S-37). *W* ends at `not_after + T_skew` only for an operation with T-0 or T-1 evidence. For an ambiguous one it ends only with T-2 or T-3 evidence, which may never come. The former `T_settle` bound is withdrawn; nothing, including the preservation check (HLC-7L-13), shortens *W*. *W* still contains at most one version, and only a version whose deletion was decided under the gate before the hold. It is not a lease, and nothing else can be deleted in it. |
| HLC-7L-06 [7L; 7I HLD-10, -12] | **What hold placement inspects: nothing new.** The frozen placement functions are unchanged. They never wait for provider I/O. They never fail, and never wait, because a deletion is in flight: HLD-12 forbids a hold that is refused or left pending. Correctness comes from the gate (HLC-7L-03). There is nothing to revoke. An operation not yet issued does not exist: there is no lease and no batch authorization. An issued request cannot be proven to be revocable before it reaches the provider, so no revocation is claimed. The race record is written by the executor (HLC-7L-08). |
| HLC-7L-07 [7L; S-10, S-24, S-37] | **Outcome and resolution (replaced for FG-7L-R5-02 by §35.4e).** Each send is an attempt record (OPT-7L-02); the provider response is recorded as `RESPONDED_OK` (2xx), `REFUSED` (a definitive refusal of OPT-7L-03 T-1 (b)) or `AMBIGUOUS` (a timeout or reset after a connection was established, any 5xx, or a crash after `SEND_STARTED`). The SDK's automatic retries are off; a new attempt is allowed only after an attempt that provably sent nothing. **No operation is resolved before `not_after + T_skew`, and none by elapsed time.** Then only the evidence of OPT-7L-03 decides: T-0 → `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT`; T-1 (a) or T-2 → `RESOLVED_DELETED`; T-1 (b) or T-3 → `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED`. An ambiguous operation whose version is still listed is `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN` (OPT-7L-04) and is **never** `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED` by a listing that shows the version. A response is never resolution by itself (RDQ-7L-15). A version that is not deleted is deleted only through a new issue record, which checks the hold gate again. |
| HLC-7L-08 [7L; 7I HLD-04, ERA-05] | **Which operation wins, and the race record.** A hold that commits before the issue commit wins: no operation exists. An operation whose issue committed before the hold wins for its one version, and for nothing else. Resolution is a short transaction under the share gate. It evaluates the effective-hold function again for the recording row. If a hold now applies: (a) for `RESOLVED_DELETED`, record `DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD`, linking the operation, its journal position, the issue commit and each hold now applying, with a tenant-scoped audit row `RECORDING_VERSION_DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD`. The erasure step records the version as erased before the hold (HLD-04). It is never recorded `SKIPPED_HELD` and never reported as preserved. (b) For `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED`, the version is held: `SKIPPED_HELD`; the intent moves to `BLOCKED_HOLD`, or stays `INCIDENT` (ICM-7L-10). (c) **For an operation still without terminality evidence** (`OUTCOME_UNPROVEN`, or before `not_after + T_skew` without a definitive response), the version is `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED`, never `SKIPPED_HELD`, and §35.4e OPT-7L-06 governs its exits. The hold's own records are not written by Voice; they are read through the function only. |
| HLC-7L-09 [7F EXT-01; RDQ-7L-22] | **Crash and restart.** (a) A crash before the issue commit leaves nothing. (b) A crash after the commit and before the request leaves an open operation. The broker's claim is single-use (TSA-7L-02), so a restarted worker cannot obtain a second credential for that operation, and the provider refuses the old one after `not_after`. Without `SEND_STARTED` the operation resolves `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT` after `not_after + T_skew` (OPT-7L-03 T-0, worker-record basis); any further attempt is a new issue under the gate. (c) A crash after `SEND_STARTED`, with or without provider success, leaves the attempt `AMBIGUOUS`: a later listing without the version resolves it `RESOLVED_DELETED` (T-2), with HLC-7L-08 applied; a listing with the version leaves it `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN` (OPT-7L-04). |
| HLC-7L-10 [7L] | **Concurrent deletion workers.** The issue and resolution transactions both lock the intent row `FOR UPDATE`. At most one operation per (bucket, key, version) is open (partial unique index), and the broker claims each operation once. Two workers can never hold credentials for the same version at the same time. A duplicate request inside one window affects only that one, already-decided version. A version-specific delete is idempotent in effect, and the listing decides. |
| HLC-7L-11 [7I HLD-05, -11; DSH-07] | **Hold release, then retry.** A release, a rejection or a determination commits under the exclusive gate, and removes only its own entry from the verdict (HLD-11). An intent in `BLOCKED_HOLD` resumes at `QUIESCING` with a new inventory (RDQ-7L-18); an intent in `INCIDENT` stays there, and containment may resume only under ICM-7L-03 (ICM-7L-10). Each remaining version needs a new issue record. Any other hold still in force blocks it. |
| HLC-7L-12 [7I HLD-11, -16, -17] | **A recording newly attributed to a held subject.** The verdict of step (4) reads the subject index under its head locks, held to commit. An attribution edge committed before the issue is seen, and the version is held. An attribution writer that arrives during the issue transaction waits on the head lock until the issue commits. The version's deletion has then been decided before the coverage existed: HLC-7L-08 (a) records it, with reason `DELETED_BEFORE_COVERAGE` and the edge's provenance. Every version not yet issued is held. An `UNVERIFIED` relation or an unreadable key version is never "no match" (HLD-19, -20): no issue is made, and a decision record opens (HLD-18). |
| HLC-7L-13 [7L; 7I HLD-06] | **Preservation check while held.** On entering `BLOCKED_HOLD`, on recording a held entry in `INCIDENT` (ICM-7L-10), and every `T_pres` ([CAND] 24 h) after that, exact-key listings of every closure bucket confirm that each held entry, of either class, is present. A held entry that is absent, with no operation whose issue preceded the hold **and whose own data event shows the deletion** (§35.4e OPT-7L-05, -06), is `INCIDENT` (`HOLD_PRESERVATION_BREACH`): a privacy and legal incident, never closed by elapsed time. A version that is `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED` is re-reported at each check. An absent held entry whose `HOLD_PRESERVATION_BREACH` occurrence has been closed (§35.4h) is re-reported at each check as a **recorded breach**, never as preserved and never as a new occurrence; an absence of any other held entry opens one (revised for FG-7L-R7-01). The check **detects**; it prevents nothing. The audit reconciliation of TSA-7L-10 is the second detector. |
| HLC-7L-14 [7L] | **Authorization expiry.** No authorization lease exists to expire. The only expiry is an operation's `not_after`. After it the worker sends nothing, and an operation with no delivered attempt resolves `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT` (OPT-7L-03 T-0). If it does send, the provider refuses (S-20), and the operation becomes `REFUSED`, then `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED` (T-1 (b)). Any new attempt is a new issue under the gate, which sees every hold committed meanwhile. |
| HLC-7L-15 [7L; 7I §19] | **Mandatory audit.** Each of these writes an audit row in the transaction that records it: the issue, the broker claim, the provider response, the resolution, `DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD` / `DELETED_BEFORE_COVERAGE`, `SKIPPED_HELD` and `HOLD_PRESERVATION_BREACH`. Each storage action of a session is also in the provider's audit trail under its `SourceIdentity`, and is reconciled (TSA-7L-09, -10). |
| HLC-7L-16 [7L] | **Fail-closed outcomes; no override.** If the journal is unavailable, no issue is made. If the broker is unavailable, the operation expires unsent and resolves `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT` (T-0). If the effective-hold function fails, or the index is `UNVERIFIED`, no issue is made. If a listing cannot be read, the operation stays unresolved. Past `T_q,max` it is `INCIDENT` (`OPERATION_UNRESOLVED`). No path, operator or role deletes a version without an issue record. No operator override exists, and no operator, role or function can set an operation's outcome (OPT-7L-09). |
| HLC-7L-17 [7I HLD-03, -04, -14] | **What frozen 7I can and cannot express.** HLD-03's dichotomy is exact for erasure inside the database. HLD-04 ("steps already completed are not reversed") does not define when an external delete is complete. For an object version, HLC-7L-03 and -05 give a third order: per version, recorded, decided before the hold, and bounded in **admission** by the provider. Its **effect** is not bounded (S-37; §35.4e), so a version with an ambiguous operation is neither erased nor preserved, for the hold, until terminality evidence exists (OPT-7L-06). Frozen 7I does not state it. **AP-7L-53 gives the exact wording.** It is not approved and not applied. Until it is applied, no recording version is deleted in production (AG-7L-09). AB-7I-14 continues to block every data-subject erasure. The logical denial of RDQ-7L-01 is unaffected. 7L does not edit 7I. |

#### 35.4b Account-complete batch quiescence (FG-7L-R4-02)

**Root cause.** `ListJobs` is scoped to the account named in `x-amz-account-id`, and to one Region's endpoint (S-14, S-15). A job can run in another account and act on a closure bucket, if that bucket's policy admits the job's role (S-16). RDQ-7L-12 called one account's listing proof that no job anywhere could recreate a version. Two things make the proof complete. (1) **Discovery**: every account and Region that could host a job reaching the key. (2) A **provider-enforced fence**: it makes every other account incapable of reaching the key, whether or not the platform knows the account.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| BQA-7L-01 [7L; G-17] | **Closure account record (part of G-17, with history).** For each closure bucket *b*, the record holds: AWS account ID; Region; bucket ARN; owner; Object Ownership `BucketOwnerEnforced` (ACLs disabled); versioning. It also holds the **authorization surface**: the bucket policy; every access point and Multi-Region Access Point, with its policy; and the allowlist *P(b)* of principals permitted to read object versions of the recording prefix, write it, replicate into or out of it, or generate inventories or manifests over it. For each principal the record holds its role ARN, account, trust policy, permission policies and function: recorder upload identity, playback signer, live replication role, governed batch role, deletion role (TSA-7L-04), closure verifier (TSA-7L-08). It records the SCPs in force over each account; the job operations permitted (none on a recording prefix, except a governed Batch Replication by the governed batch role); the discovery role per account; the governed manifest bucket. Each element has effective-from and effective-to. |
| BQA-7L-02 [7L; RDQ-7L-03] | **The job-discovery account set *J*.** Every account that, at any time from the recording's earliest version to now (G-17 history), owned a closure bucket or held a principal in *P(b)* of a closure bucket. Current and historical destination accounts are both included. **An account or bucket removed from the configuration stays in *J*** for every intent whose recording existed while it was in the closure. |
| BQA-7L-03 [S-15] | **Regions.** For each account *a* in *J*, the Region set *R(a)* is every Region enabled for *a*. It is narrower only where an SCP over *a*, recorded in the authorization surface, denies `s3:CreateJob` outside a listed set; then it is that set. The reason: a copy job runs in the destination's Region. So a copy *from* a closure bucket can be created in the Region of any bucket the job writes to. |
| BQA-7L-04 [S-16, S-17] | **Creation fence, enforced by the provider.** All of these hold. (i) Each account in *J* is a member account of the platform's AWS Organization. It is not the management account, which SCPs do not restrict. (ii) An SCP denies `s3:CreateJob`, `s3:UpdateJobStatus`, and `iam:PassRole` of any role in *P(b)*, to every principal except the governed provisioning principal. That principal performs the governed operation of RDQ-7L-08, which takes the per-bucket lock first. (iii) Each closure bucket's policy explicitly denies every object action on the recording prefix to every principal not in *P(b)*. So a job created in an account outside the organization, or by an unknown principal, or with a role not in *P(b)*, cannot read or write the key. **This clause makes the proof independent of discovering such accounts.** (iv) No service-linked role is in *P(b)*, because SCPs do not restrict service-linked roles. (v) No role in *P(b)* other than the governed batch role trusts `batchoperations.s3.amazonaws.com`. Each clause is evidenced by a digest of the policy concerned. If one cannot be established, the bucket set is **NOT ADMITTED** (RAD-7L-10). For an existing intent, the intent goes to `INCIDENT` (`BATCH_PROOF_INCOMPLETE`). |
| BQA-7L-05 [S-14] | **Enumeration.** For each (*a*, *r*) in *J* × *R(a)*, the closure verifier assumes *a*'s discovery role. It calls `ListJobs` in *r*, with `jobStatuses` set to the ten non-terminal statuses and `maxResults` 1,000. It follows `NextToken` until a response carries none, and records each page's request identifier and count. An enumeration that ends in `InvalidNextTokenException`, a 5xx, exhausted throttling, `AccessDenied` or a missing page is **incomplete**. It is restarted from the first page. Pages from different runs are never merged. Then `DescribeJob` is called for each job returned. A `DescribeJob` that is denied or fails leaves the job's scope **unknown**. |
| BQA-7L-06 [S-15, S-16] | **Covering job.** A job covers the key when two things hold. First, its operation is anything other than `S3PutObjectTagging` or `S3DeleteObjectTagging`: copy, replication, restore, Lambda invocation, Object Lock changes and any operation added later all count. Second, its manifest or manifest generator can include the key in a closure bucket. The verifier reads a manifest only in the governed manifest bucket, and evaluates a generator on its `SourceBucket` and filters. A manifest elsewhere, an unreadable or undecryptable manifest, or an unknown scope **counts as covering**. A covering job keeps the intent in `QUIESCING`, and `T_q,max` applies (RDQ-7L-28). |
| BQA-7L-07 [S-10, S-14, S-36; RDQ-7L-07] | **From the first check to the last (revised for FG-7L-R5-03).** Pass 1 runs at `QUIESCING`, after `FENCED`. Pass 2 runs at `VERIFYING`. Between them, the provider fence (BQA-7L-04) excludes creation by anyone except a change session, and the per-bucket lock excludes change sessions (RDQ-7L-08; ACF-7L-03). **Continuity between and before the passes is proven only by §35.4f** (ACF-7L-05, -06): the change-event and data-access reconciliations over the interval *I*. The authorization-surface digests are still taken at both passes, with `T_cfg` respected for propagation, and must be equal; a difference is `INCIDENT` (`AUTHZ_CHANGED`). **Equal digests are necessary and never sufficient** (ACF-7L-07): a change made and reverted between the passes leaves them equal. Pass 2 lists, besides the ten non-terminal statuses, `Complete`, `Failed` and `Cancelled`, and keeps every job whose creation time is at or after the intent's commit, whatever its status; the `CreateJob` management events of *J* × *R(a)* over *I* are reconciled as well (ACF-7L-05), because a job created and ended between the passes is invisible to a non-terminal listing, and `ListJobs` keeps ended jobs only for a period that its own page states inconsistently (S-14). A covering job found in pass 2 sends the intent back to `QUIESCING` with a new inventory. If it was created after the intent's commit by anything other than a change session under a change record, that is a fence breach: `INCIDENT` (`BATCH_PROOF_INCOMPLETE`). |
| BQA-7L-08 [7L] | **Changes in relationships during cleanup.** An account that leaves the organization, moves to an organizational unit without the SCP, is closed, or loses its discovery role makes the proof incomplete: `INCIDENT` (`BATCH_PROOF_INCOMPLETE`). *J* never shrinks for an open intent. |
| BQA-7L-09 [RDQ-7L-16, -27; TSA-7L-10] | **A delayed copy after an empty listing.** Three detectors: the final listings of RDQ-7L-16, taken after pass 2; the sentinel of RDQ-7L-27; and the audit reconciliation (TSA-7L-10) of every object-write data event on the key in every closure bucket. Any write to the key after the intent's commit is `INCIDENT` (`UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`). After `VERIFIED_ABSENT`, a write shown by its data event opens that reason through `VERIFIED_ABSENT → REOPENED → INCIDENT` in one transaction (§35.4k PCI-7L-02); an entry found only by the sentinel makes `VERIFIED_ABSENT → REOPENED`, and the listing decides (PCI-7L-03) (revised for FG-7L-R9-01). |
| BQA-7L-10 [7L] | **Not claimed.** AWS documents no global job inventory, and §35 does not assume one. The proof covers *J* × *R(a)* as recorded. It covers any other account only through BQA-7L-04 (iii). That is why the bucket-side deny is a condition of admission, not a recommendation. |
| BQA-7L-11 [7L] | **Fail-closed list.** Each of these keeps the intent non-terminal (`QUIESCING`), or sends it to `INCIDENT` (`BATCH_PROOF_INCOMPLETE`; `QUIESCENCE_UNPROVABLE` past `T_q,max`): a missing account; an unavailable discovery identity; an unknown manifest scope; incomplete pagination; a Region that cannot be queried; a creation fence that cannot be enforced; management-account membership. **No `VERIFIED_ABSENT` rests on an incomplete cross-account proof.** |

#### 35.4c Tenant-scoped storage authority (FG-7L-R4-03)

**Root cause.** RDQ-7L-23 gave one long-lived cleanup identity version listing and deletion over `org/` in every closure bucket. The tenant check was in the executor. A stolen credential, or a fault in the executor, could therefore delete another organization's recordings, and nothing at the storage boundary would refuse it. The correction removes every standing object permission. Each object action uses a session bound **by the provider** to one organization's prefix and one exact object.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| TSA-7L-01 [7L] | **No standing object permission.** The cleanup worker's own AWS identity can call the broker and nothing else in S3. Object actions use per-operation sessions only (TSA-7L-03). Account-scoped reads use the closure verifier (TSA-7L-08). Provisioning uses the governed provisioning identity, which the worker cannot assume. |
| TSA-7L-02 [7L; RDQ-7L-30; 7C] | **The storage-authority broker.** A separate workload with its own PostgreSQL principal. That principal can call exactly one guarded function: the claim of an operation by its identifier. The function returns the binding **from the committed intent and operation**: organization, bucket, exact key, version (for a deletion), operation kind, `not_after`. It marks the operation claimed, and a second claim is refused. It refuses an operation that is not `ISSUED`, or whose `not_after` has passed. An inspection binding (exact-key listing and per-version reads) also needs an operation record, created by the executor for one (bucket, key). It is written without the hold gate, because it deletes nothing. It is issued only for an intent in a state whose row of the §35.5 action table permits inspection operations that need an object session: `QUIESCING`, `DELETING`, `VERIFYING`, `BLOCKED_HOLD`, `INCIDENT` and `REOPENED` (revised for the seventh review, FND-7L-12: the list omitted `INCIDENT` and `REOPENED`; the checks of `PENDING` and `FENCED` read only the database and G-17). The broker takes nothing from the caller except the operation identifier. It validates that the key matches the 5C §5.8 pattern for that organization exactly, and that the organization identifier is a canonical UUID. Otherwise it refuses, and the intent goes to `INCIDENT` (`KEY_OUT_OF_PREFIX`). The broker principal holds no table privilege and cannot create an intent or an operation. |
| TSA-7L-03 [S-18, S-20, S-21, S-22] | **The session.** The broker calls `AssumeRole` on the deletion role of the bucket's own account, with: session tag `organization_id` = the binding's organization; `SourceIdentity` = the operation identifier; no transitive tags; `DurationSeconds` 900 (the minimum); and an inline session policy. **Deletion:** `s3:DeleteObjectVersion` on `arn:aws:s3:::<bucket>/<exact key>` with `StringEquals s3:VersionId = <version>` [VERIFY, S-22] and `DateLessThan aws:CurrentTime = <not_after>`. **Inspection:** `s3:ListBucketVersions` on the bucket with `StringEquals s3:prefix = <exact key>`; `s3:GetObjectVersion`, `s3:GetObjectRetention`, `s3:GetObjectLegalHold` on the exact key ARN; `aws:CurrentTime` before the inspection deadline (`T_insp`, [CAND] 300 s). Nothing else. |
| TSA-7L-04 [S-19] | **Role permission policy (the tenant boundary on the identity).** Illustrative; PV-R2 validates the exact syntax. `{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":"s3:ListBucketVersions","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::<bucket>","Condition":{"StringLike":{"s3:prefix":"org/${aws:PrincipalTag/organization_id}/recordings/*"}}},{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:GetObjectVersion","s3:GetObjectRetention","s3:GetObjectLegalHold","s3:DeleteObjectVersion"],"Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::<bucket>/org/${aws:PrincipalTag/organization_id}/recordings/*"},{"Effect":"Deny","Action":["s3:Put*","s3:Replicate*","s3:InitiateReplication","s3:RestoreObject","s3:Create*","s3:Update*","s3:Bypass*","s3:DeleteObject","s3:DeleteBucket*","iam:*","sts:*","organizations:*"],"Resource":"*"}]}`. A session without the tag matches no resource (S-19), so it is refused. Unversioned `s3:DeleteObject` is explicitly denied, so the provider itself enforces RDQ-7L-14. |
| TSA-7L-05 [S-18, S-19, S-21] | **Trust policy of the deletion role.** It allows `sts:AssumeRole`, `sts:TagSession` and `sts:SetSourceIdentity` to the broker's role ARN only, under these conditions: tag keys limited to `organization_id`; `organization_id` present; `SourceIdentity` present; no transitive tag keys; the broker's network boundary, a VPC endpoint condition [VERIFY, PV-R2]. A separate deny refuses `sts:TagSession` when the tag value contains a literal `*` (`${*}`), a literal `?` (`${?}`) or `/`. This stops a tag value from widening the resource pattern into which it is substituted. |
| TSA-7L-06 [S-19] | **Bucket policy (the tenant boundary on the resource; an equivalent provider-side deny).** It denies `s3:DeleteObjectVersion` on the recording prefix to every principal except the deletion role (`ArnNotEquals aws:PrincipalArn`). It denies the deletion role every object action whose `NotResource` is `arn:aws:s3:::<bucket>/org/${aws:PrincipalTag/organization_id}/recordings/*`, and `s3:ListBucketVersions` whose `s3:prefix` is not like `org/${aws:PrincipalTag/organization_id}/recordings/*`. If the tag is absent, the `NotResource` matches every resource and the deny applies: it fails closed. It denies `s3:DeleteObject` without a version on the recording prefix to every principal. Together with BQA-7L-04 (iii), it denies every object action to principals not in *P(b)*. So a role policy that was wrongly widened still cannot delete across tenants. |
| TSA-7L-07 [7L] | **Cross-account destinations.** Each account that holds a closure bucket has its own deletion role, with TSA-7L-04 and -05, and its own bucket policy, with TSA-7L-06. The broker assumes that role directly, without role chaining. The tag and the session policy are set for that bucket. A session minted for one account's bucket is valid in no other account. |
| TSA-7L-08 [7L] | **Account-scoped operations: a separate identity.** The closure verifier is a read-only identity per account.
