It holds `s3:GetReplicationConfiguration`, `s3:GetBucketPolicy`, `s3:GetBucketVersioning`, `s3:GetBucketOwnershipControls`, `s3:GetBucketObjectLockConfiguration`, access-point policy reads, `s3:ListJobs` and `s3:DescribeJob`, IAM role and policy reads for *P(b)*, and organization policy reads through a delegated administrator. It can read objects only in the governed manifest bucket. It holds no write, no delete and no job creation, and it reads no recording object. The governed provisioning identity is a third identity: it alone changes configuration (RDQ-7L-04, -08). It is never available to the cleanup worker. Revised for FG-7L-R5-03: it holds no standing change permission, and acts only through change sessions bound to committed change records (ACF-7L-03). The closure verifier also holds `cloudtrail:LookupEvents` and read access to the organization trail's log-archive objects and digest files, for ACF-7L-05. |
| TSA-7L-09 [S-21] | **Auditable credential use.** CloudTrail management events record each `AssumeRole`, with its tags and `SourceIdentity`. CloudTrail data events are enabled on every closure bucket, for every object action on the recording prefix. Each event carries the operation identifier as `SourceIdentity`. |
| TSA-7L-10 [7L] | **Reconciliation.** Every data event by a deletion role must map to a claimed operation, with an equal bucket, key and version and an event time not after `not_after + T_skew`. Every object-write data event on the key after the intent's commit is reported, and after `VERIFIED_ABSENT` so is every successful data event on the key after the final listing (§35.4k PCI-7L-08; revised for FG-7L-R9-01). An unmatched event is `INCIDENT` (`UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`); after `VERIFIED_ABSENT` it opens through PCI-7L-02. An event attributed by an committed IRR of this intent whose class matches (§35.4h IRE-7L-06) counts as matched for this intent only (revised for FG-7L-R7-01). For `VERIFIED_ABSENT`, the trail must be delivered through the last operation plus `T_ct` ([CAND] 15 min; [MEAS]) (E-18). A gap in delivery keeps the intent in `VERIFYING`. |
| TSA-7L-11 [S-18, S-20] | **Expiry and revocation.** The admission deadline is `aws:CurrentTime` (TSA-7L-03). STS expiry, at 900 s, is the backstop. In an incident, every session of a deletion role is revoked by a `DateLessThan aws:TokenIssueTime` deny on the role. That deny is eventually consistent, and nothing claims that it stops a request already admitted (S-24). |
| TSA-7L-12 [RDQ-7L-02, -30] | **Tenant provenance.** The organization in every binding is the intent's. The intent's organization was set in the delete transaction from the recording row, under the tenant context taken from the validated envelope (RDQ-7L-30). It never comes from a request parameter, a payload or the caller of the broker. The broker refuses a key outside that organization's prefix. The provider refuses it independently (TSA-7L-04, -06). |
| TSA-7L-13 [7L] | **A stolen credential versus a compromised workload.** *A stolen per-operation session* reaches one version, or one key for inspection, until its deadline. That version's deletion was already decided. *A stolen worker credential* (AWS or PostgreSQL) can claim only issued operations. It can create issues only for intents that exist, through the guarded function, which checks the hold gate. It cannot reach another organization's object except through such an intent. *A stolen broker credential used off its network boundary* is refused by the trust policy [VERIFY, PV-R2]. *A fully compromised broker workload* (code execution inside its boundary) can mint sessions for any organization's prefix in admitted buckets. That is not prevented. It is detected by TSA-7L-10 and stated as RR-7L-R5. |
| TSA-7L-14 [7L] | **Fail closed.** If the provider cannot narrow a bucket's authority as TSA-7L-03 … -07 require, the bucket is **NOT ADMITTED** (RAD-7L-11). This covers: no session policies; no session tags or tag variables in `Resource`; no `aws:CurrentTime`; no version condition; no bucket policy; no audit of data events. An intent that meets such a bucket goes to `INCIDENT` (`STORAGE_AUTHORITY_UNNARROWABLE`), and nothing is deleted there. A broad credential is never used as a fallback. |

#### 35.4d Object classes: data-bearing versions and delete markers (FG-7L-R5-01)

**Root cause.** RDQ-7L-09 asked for `HeadObject` metadata of every inventoried version, and E-6 for the replication status and Object Lock state of every version. A delete marker has none of these. AWS documents that a `HeadObject` or `GetObject` naming a marker's version ID returns `405 Method Not Allowed`, with `x-amz-delete-marker: true` and `Last-Modified` (S-25, S-26), and no page read documents a replication status for a marker (S-28). So, for any key that has a marker, the inventory could not be completed and the quiescence predicate was not defined. The inventory also had no pagination rule, although `ListObjectVersions` is paginated (S-26). The correction gives each class its own evidence path, defines quiescence for both, and leaves every other safeguard unchanged. (Classes V and M are object classes. They are unrelated to the stack classes E and S of OD-7K-05.)

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| OC-7L-01 [S-26] | **The class comes from the listing only.** The inventory of a closure bucket is one exact-key `ListObjectVersions` run (`prefix` = the exact key), paginated with `NextKeyMarker` and `NextVersionIdMarker` until `IsTruncated` is false, and filtered to `Key` equal to the exact key. A run that ends in an error, exhausted throttling or a missing page is incomplete. It is restarted from the first page, and pages of different runs are never merged (the BQA-7L-05 pattern). Each `Version` entry is **class V**, a data-bearing version. Each `DeleteMarker` entry is **class M**, a delete marker. The class is read from the element, never inferred from an HTTP status or from a missing header. It is recorded per (bucket, version ID): the same version ID in two buckets is classified in each. |
| OC-7L-02 [S-1, S-12, S-25] | **Class V evidence.** For each class V entry, the inspection session (TSA-7L-03) calls `HeadObject` with the version ID and records: `x-amz-replication-status`, or its absence; the storage class (no header means S3 Standard, S-25); `Content-Length`; the checksum (`x-amz-checksum-mode: ENABLED`); and the Object Lock mode, retain-until date and legal-hold status (`GetObjectRetention`, `GetObjectLegalHold`). Responses: a `200` is recorded. A `405` contradicts the listing: the key is listed again, and if the entry is still a `Version` the intent goes to `INCIDENT` (`CLASS_CONTRADICTION`). A `404` or a `403` can mean that the version is gone (S-25: `403` when the caller lacks `s3:ListBucket`, which the inspection session does not hold): the key is listed again. If the entry has gone, OC-7L-09 applies. If it is still listed, its evidence is incomplete, and past `T_q,max` the intent is `INCIDENT` (`QUIESCENCE_UNPROVABLE`). A `5xx` is retried within `T_insp`. |
| OC-7L-03 [S-25, S-26, S-28, S-30] | **Class M evidence.** For each class M entry, the evidence is the listing entry itself: version ID, `IsLatest`, `LastModified`, `Owner`, and the listing's request identifier. No `HeadObject`, `GetObjectRetention` or `GetObjectLegalHold` is required or issued. A marker has no data, no ACL, no documented replication status and no WORM protection (S-30). **Nothing is fabricated for it, a replication status least of all.** If a `HeadObject` is issued for a class M entry (a diagnostic, or T-7L-12 (d)), the only consistent response is the documented one: `405` **and** `x-amz-delete-marker: true`. A `405` without that header is not evidence of a marker (HEAD errors are generic, S-25); the key is listed again, and the listing decides. A `200` for a class M entry is `INCIDENT` (`CLASS_CONTRADICTION`). |
| OC-7L-04 [S-28, S-31; G-17] | **Where a marker came from (audit, not quiescence).** On an admitted stack no principal can make an unversioned delete on the recording prefix (TSA-7L-04, -06), and no rule replicates a marker (RAD-7L-04). A marker is therefore either `LIFECYCLE`, or `UNEXPLAINED`. It is `LIFECYCLE` when a lifecycle expiration rule recorded in G-17 covered the key at the marker's `LastModified`, and a class V version was current in that bucket just before it (S-31; frozen 3F §11.3, 4G §18.6 and 4I §25.14 put recordings under lifecycle rules). An `UNEXPLAINED` marker shows that a write fence failed at some time, specifically the bucket policy's deny of unversioned deletes, which is part of the storage authority (TSA-7L-06). The intent goes to `INCIDENT` (`MARKER_UNEXPLAINED`, **Class 2**). **No further entry is deleted in any closure bucket** until a dual-controlled resolution with Security's approval (ICR-7L-01 … -05) returns it to `QUIESCING`, as TSA-7L-14 requires ("nothing is deleted there"). The round-5 instruction that it "still deletes" is withdrawn (FG-7L-R6-01). The finding goes to Security. If the marker's `LastModified` is after the intent's commit, it is also a write after the commit (BQA-7L-09). **Revised for FG-7L-R7-01:** a third origin, `INCIDENT_RECONCILED`, applies to a marker whose creating event is attributed by an committed IRR of this intent with a matching class (§35.4h IRE-7L-06), closed together with a `MARKER_UNEXPLAINED` occurrence. Such a marker is then inventoried and deleted like any class M entry (OC-7L-06). No other path gives a marker that origin. |
| OC-7L-05 [S-1 … S-3, S-28, S-29] | **Quiescence, per class (completes RDQ-7L-10).** For an entry *e* in bucket *b*: if *e* is class V, Q(*e*) is RDQ-7L-10 (a) – (d), unchanged, and `PENDING` is never quiescent. If *e* is class M, Q(*e*) holds when **(m1)** every replication rule of *b* that G-17 records as covering the key at any time from *e*'s `LastModified` until now is a current-schema rule (with a `Filter` element) whose `DeleteMarkerReplication` is `Disabled`, or is a tag-based rule (where marker replication is not supported, S-28), **and (m2)** the batch fence of RDQ-7L-08 holds (Batch Replication can replicate a marker, S-29). Otherwise Q(*e*) is **not provable**: a marker has no replication status, so no observation can show that its replication is finished. That is `INCIDENT` (`MARKER_REPLICATION_UNPROVABLE`, Class 1, scope class V only: containment may delete class V entries under ICM-7L-03 and F, and issues no class M deletion), and also a configuration defect under RAD-7L-04. Define Q_V(key) as Q over every class V entry of every closure bucket, and Q_M(key) as Q over every class M entry. Over an empty set each is true. An entry whose evidence is incomplete (OC-7L-02) is not quiescent. |
| OC-7L-06 [RDQ-7L-11, -14] | **What each predicate admits.** A class V deletion is issued only when Q_V(key) holds and RDQ-7L-12 holds. A class M deletion is issued only when Q_V(key) and Q_M(key) hold and every class V entry of the key **in the same bucket** is `RESOLVED_DELETED`. So a marker never stops content from being deleted, and content is always deleted before the markers above it. The order matters: deleting the current marker first would make the newest remaining class V version current again, and readable by key without a version ID. |
| OC-7L-07 [S-4, S-27, S-30; HLC-7L-02] | **Deleting a marker.** A class M entry is deleted exactly like a class V version. It has its own issue record under the hold gate: HLC-7L-02 does not depend on the class, because it evaluates the hold for the recording row, so the markers of a held recording are held too. No hold policy changes. It has its own per-operation session with `s3:DeleteObjectVersion` on that version (TSA-7L-03) and a `DeleteObject` with the marker's version ID. The documented success is `204` with `x-amz-delete-marker: true` (S-27). A `204` without that header, for a class M entry, is recorded as `CLASS_CONTRADICTION`, and the listing decides. The deletion is not replicated (S-4). Object Lock never applies to a marker (S-30), so `OBJECT_LOCKED` never arises for class M. A refusal is resolved under §35.4e like any other; a marker whose deletion is still refused past `T_q,max` is `INCIDENT` (`DELETE_REFUSED`). |
| OC-7L-08 | **Both classes keep every safeguard.** See the table below. |
| OC-7L-09 [RDQ-7L-16; BQA-7L-09; TSA-7L-10] | **Entries that appear or disappear.** An entry in a later listing that is not in the inventory sends the intent back to `QUIESCING` with a new inventory (RDQ-7L-16). In `INCIDENT` it does not: it triggers a new containment pass (ICM-7L-06 (iv)), or it opens the reason the entry reveals (revised for the seventh review, FND-7L-13). In `REOPENED`, PCI-7L-03 decides: the reason the entry reveals opens (`REOPENED → INCIDENT`), or the intent goes to `QUIESCING` (revised for FG-7L-R9-01). A class M entry whose `LastModified` is after the intent's commit is `LIFECYCLE` only under OC-7L-04's two conditions. Otherwise it is a write after the commit: `INCIDENT` (`UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`). An inventoried entry that disappears without a claimed operation is attributed to a G-17 lifecycle rule that can remove it [VERIFY, PV-R3 (m)], or else is `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`. While a hold applies, the disappearance of an entry of either class is judged by HLC-7L-13. |

| Safeguard | Class V | Class M |
|---|---|---|
| Exact key and tenant prefix (RDQ-7L-02; TSA-7L-02, -04 … -06) | Required | Required; same resource ARN, same session tag |
| Closure inventory (RDQ-7L-03, -09; OC-7L-01) | `Version` entry, then `HeadObject` | `DeleteMarker` entry; no `HeadObject` |
| Legal hold and retention (HLC-7L-02, -08, -13; RDQ-7L-18, -19, -28) | Hold gate; Object Lock → `OBJECT_LOCKED` (S-12) | Hold gate; Object Lock does not apply (S-30); the same deadlines |
| Version-specific deletion (RDQ-7L-14) | Yes | Yes, after every class V entry of its bucket |
| Issue record (HLC-7L-02) | One per version | One per marker |
| Provider restriction (TSA-7L-03 … -07) | `s3:DeleteObjectVersion` on that version [VERIFY, S-22] | Same |
| Audit (HLC-7L-15; TSA-7L-09, -10) | Data event `DeleteObject` with the version ID | Same; `x-amz-delete-marker: true` recorded |
| Final absence (RDQ-7L-16; E-12) | No `Version` entry | No `DeleteMarker` entry |
| Crash and retry (§35.4e) | Evidence of OPT-7L-03 | Same |

#### 35.4e Ambiguous provider outcomes and terminality (FG-7L-R5-02)

**Root cause.** S-24 records that AWS does not say how long an accepted request may take to take effect. HLC-7L-07 nevertheless resolved an ambiguous operation by a listing taken after `not_after + T_skew + T_settle`. A version that is still listed then proves only that the request has not taken effect *yet*. It does not prove that it never will. `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED` was reachable without evidence. A hold that committed afterwards could then record the version as `SKIPPED_HELD`, that is, preserved, while the earlier request could still delete it. **`T_settle` is withdrawn as a decision point.** AWS documents neither an upper bound on completion nor any cancellation of an accepted request (S-37). §35 therefore takes outcome B of the review wherever no proof exists: the operation stays unresolved, its intent stays non-terminal, and nothing is inferred from elapsed time. Outcome A applies only to the four kinds of evidence in OPT-7L-03.

| # | Notion | Meaning in §35 | Established by |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Request admission deadline | `not_after`: the last instant at which the provider admits a request under the operation's session | `aws:CurrentTime` in the session policy (S-20), within `T_skew` |
| 2 | Credential expiration | STS expiry (900 s), never earlier than `not_after`; a backstop only | STS (TSA-7L-11) |
| 3 | Request acceptance | The provider has received and authorized a request | Not observable by the client, except through 4 or 8 |
| 4 | Provider response | An HTTP response received and recorded by the worker | The attempt record (OPT-7L-02) |
| 5 | Confirmed physical deletion | The version is absent from a strongly consistent, complete exact-key listing | `ListObjectVersions` (S-10; OC-7L-01) |
| 6 | Confirmed refusal or cancellation | The provider reported that it did not perform the request. **Cancellation of an accepted request is not documented and is never claimed** | A definitive refusal (4), or the provider's record of it (8) |
| 7 | Ambiguous outcome | A request may have reached the provider, and no definitive result is held | The attempt record |
| 8 | Provider-backed terminality evidence | T-0 … T-3 | OPT-7L-03 |
| 9 | Incident and reconciliation | What happens while 8 is missing, and what detects a late effect | OPT-7L-05 … -09 |

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| OPT-7L-01 [S-20, S-24, S-37] | **What the deadline does, and what it does not do.** The provider refuses every request that arrives after `not_after` (within `T_skew`). That says nothing about a request admitted before `not_after`, which may take effect at any later time. No rule infers non-deletion from the deadline, from credential expiry, from a revocation (TSA-7L-11) or from elapsed time. **An IAM admission deadline does not cancel an accepted request.** |
| OPT-7L-02 [7F EXT-01] | **Attempt records; at most one possibly delivered request.** Each send under an operation is an *attempt*. It is committed as `SEND_STARTED` before the worker opens the connection. The SDK's automatic retries are disabled. An attempt whose transport failed before a connection was established (name resolution, TCP connect or TLS handshake) provably delivered nothing. It is recorded `NOT_DELIVERED`, and the worker may make one more attempt before `not_after`. An attempt that established a connection may have delivered the request. After it, no further attempt is made under that operation, whatever the result. One operation therefore has at most one request that can have reached the provider. That rests on worker discipline; a second request under the same session is detected (OPT-7L-08). |
| OPT-7L-03 [S-10, S-20, S-27, S-30] | **Terminality evidence: the only exits from a non-terminal operation.** **T-0, no credential or no delivered attempt.** (i) The operation was never claimed before `not_after`: the broker refuses a later claim (TSA-7L-02), and any session would carry `aws:CurrentTime` before `not_after`, so no request can ever be admitted. (ii) After `not_after + T_skew`, the operation was claimed but has no attempt, or only `NOT_DELIVERED` attempts (worker-record basis; a credential used by anyone else is caught by OPT-7L-08). → `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT`. **T-1, a definitive response received.** (a) A `204` (with `x-amz-delete-marker: true` for class M), and a later complete exact-key listing without the version → `RESOLVED_DELETED`. A `204` followed by a listing that still shows the version is `INCIDENT` (`PROVIDER_CONTRADICTION`). (b) A refusal from the closed list `403 AccessDenied`, `400 InvalidArgument`, `404 NoSuchBucket` → after `not_after + T_skew`, with a listing that shows the version, `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED`. This relies on the API contract that an error response reports a request that S3 did not perform (S-30 shows it for a locked version); PV-R3 (e) reproduces it. **T-2, confirmed absence.** After `not_after + T_skew`, a complete exact-key listing does not show the version → `RESOLVED_DELETED`, whatever the response was. Nothing that arrives later can act on the data of that version: a version-specific delete of an absent version removes nothing, and only a delete without a version ID creates a marker (S-27), which the provider refuses (TSA-7L-04, -06). **T-3, the provider's record of a refusal.** A CloudTrail data event for the operation's one possibly delivered request (same `SourceIdentity`, bucket, key and version) whose `errorCode` is in the T-1 (b) list → after `not_after + T_skew`, `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED`. A data event without an error, while the listing still shows the version, is `PROVIDER_CONTRADICTION`. [VERIFY, PV-R3 (e): that S3 data events record a refused `DeleteObject` with its `errorCode` and `SourceIdentity`.] **Until PV-R3 (e) passes, T-3 is not available.** **Not evidence:** elapsed time; any number of listings that still show the version; credential expiry or revocation; a `5xx`; the absence of a CloudTrail event (S-36); an operator's statement; a benchmark. |
| OPT-7L-04 | **`OUTCOME_UNPROVEN`.** An operation with an ambiguous attempt that, at `not_after + T_skew`, has no T-1, T-2 or T-3 evidence while its version is listed enters `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN`. It is **non-terminal**. It is never turned into `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED` by time, retries, listings or assertion. It leaves only by T-2 or T-3. It no longer counts as open in HLC-7L-02 (3)'s index, because the provider admits nothing under it any more (OPT-7L-01). A **successor operation** for the same version can therefore be issued, under the hold gate. When any operation of the version reaches T-2, every `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN` operation of that version resolves `RESOLVED_DELETED`, each with its own attribution (OPT-7L-05). |
| OPT-7L-05 [TSA-7L-09, -10] | **Attribution of an absence.** `THIS_OPERATION`, when a data event under the operation's `SourceIdentity` shows the deletion; `OTHER_OPERATION`, when another operation's event does; `LIFECYCLE`, when a G-17 lifecycle rule can remove the version and no operation's event shows it; `PENDING_ATTRIBUTION`, until trail delivery is proven through `not_after + T_skew + T_ct`; then `UNATTRIBUTED`, which is `INCIDENT` (`UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`). The data event's `eventTime` is recorded as the time of the request [VERIFY, PV-R3 (e)]; when the deletion *took effect* is not known. |
| OPT-7L-06 [7I HLD-03, -04; HLC-7L-08, -13] | **A hold while an operation is unproven.** Consider a hold *H* that commits after the issue of operation *P*, while *P* has no terminality evidence and its version *v* is listed. No successor is issued, because the gate sees *H*. *v* is recorded `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED` (*v*, *H*, *P*), **never `SKIPPED_HELD`**. A tenant-scoped audit row `RECORDING_VERSION_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED` is written, Privacy is notified, and the record is readable with the hold's evidence; Voice writes no hold record (HLC-7L-08). The intent is `BLOCKED_HOLD` (or stays `INCIDENT`, ICM-7L-10), and every preservation check re-reports *v*. Exits: T-3 → *P* is `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED`, and *v* becomes `SKIPPED_HELD`, preserved from then on. T-2 with attribution `THIS_OPERATION` → `DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD`, marked **late effect**: the deletion was decided and admitted before *H* committed, and took effect after. T-2 with any other attribution → `HOLD_PRESERVATION_BREACH`, and `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` where that applies. **Prevention and detection, kept apart.** The hold *prevents* the deletion of every entry not issued before it, and of every entry whose operations all ended in T-0, T-1 (b) or T-3. For an entry with an unproven operation, nothing prevents a late effect. It is *detected* (by the data event and the preservation check) and recorded, and the entry is never reported as preserved. This is RR-7L-R4 (b). |
| OPT-7L-07 | **Prompt successor.** For a version that is not held, a successor operation is issued as soon as its predecessor enters `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN`. This shortens the only interval in which OPT-7L-06 can arise. It moves no deadline. |
| OPT-7L-08 [TSA-7L-10, -13] | **Reconciliation of credential use.** A second deletion data event under one `SourceIdentity`, or any data event under an operation recorded `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT`, is `INCIDENT` (`UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`): a credential was used outside the attempt records. The operation is classified again from that event. |
| OPT-7L-09 [RDQ-7L-28; HLC-7L-16] | **Escalation, deadlines and no manual resolution.** An operation `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN` for longer than `T_unp,warn` ([CAND] 1 hour) raises an operational alert. Past `T_q,max`, with its version still listed and no successor able to delete it, the intent is `INCIDENT` (`OPERATION_UNRESOLVED`). RDQ-7L-28's deadline does not move. Past it, a listed version that is not held is **unauthorized retention**, and a held version with an unproven operation stays `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED`. No function, role or operator can set an operation's outcome. The resolution function accepts only OPT-7L-03 evidence (listing request identifiers and data-event identifiers), which it re-reads itself, through the inspection session and the closure verifier. |

**Mandatory fault sequences.** Each row gives the authoritative outcome evidence and the only permitted transitions. "Listing" means a complete exact-key listing taken after `not_after + T_skew`.

| # | Sequence | Authoritative outcome evidence | Permitted transitions | Never permitted |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delete rejected before admission | (1a) The broker refused the claim, because `not_after` had passed: T-0 (i). (1b) `403 AccessDenied` received (the session policy, the bucket policy or Object Lock): T-1 (b) | (1a) `ISSUED` → `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT`. (1b) `SEND_STARTED` → `REFUSED` → `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED`; a new issue under the gate | Treating a refusal as deletion |
| 2 | Delete returns definitive success | `204` and a listing without the version: T-1 (a); the data event later gives the attribution `THIS_OPERATION` | `RESPONDED_OK` → `RESOLVED_DELETED` | `RESOLVED_DELETED` before the listing; a `204` with the version still listed is `PROVIDER_CONTRADICTION` |
| 3 | Delete times out before reaching AWS | The transport failed before a connection was established: the attempt is `NOT_DELIVERED`. One more attempt is allowed before `not_after`; otherwise T-0 (ii) | → another attempt, or `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT` | Calling a timeout *after* a connection was established "before AWS" |
| 4 | Delete reaches AWS but the response is lost | None at first. Then a listing without the version (T-2), or a refusal event (T-3) | `AMBIGUOUS` → `RESOLVED_DELETED` (T-2), or `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED` (T-3), or `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN` with the version listed; then a successor (OPT-7L-07) | `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED` because the version is still listed |
| 5 | Delete accepted; an applicable hold then commits | The issue is before *H* in journal order (HLC-7L-03). The outcome comes from T-1, T-2 or T-3 | Success known (T-1 (a), T-2 with `THIS_OPERATION`) → `DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD`. No evidence yet → `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED`; then OPT-7L-06's exits | `SKIPPED_HELD`, or "preserved", while the outcome is unproven |
| 6 | Ambiguous; the listings keep showing the version | No terminality evidence | `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN`, without limit. If not held: a successor, whose own outcome decides the version. If held: `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED`, re-reported. Past `T_q,max` without a deletable successor: `INCIDENT` (`OPERATION_UNRESOLVED`) | Any conversion by elapsed time |
| 7 | Ambiguous; the version later disappears | T-2, with the attribution of OPT-7L-05 | `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN` → `RESOLVED_DELETED` (`THIS_OPERATION`, a late effect; `OTHER_OPERATION`; `LIFECYCLE`; or `UNATTRIBUTED` → `INCIDENT`). If held: OPT-7L-06 | Recording an unattributed disappearance as a deletion by the platform |
| 8 | Authorization expires before a request is issued | No attempt before `not_after`: T-0 (ii). A late send is refused by the provider (S-20): T-1 (b) | `CLAIMED` → `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT`; or `REFUSED` → `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED`; a new issue under the gate | Re-using the expired session; minting a second session for the same operation |
| 9 | Worker crashes between issue, send and response | (9a) After the issue, before the claim: T-0 (i). (9b) After the claim, before `SEND_STARTED`: T-0 (ii). (9c) After `SEND_STARTED`, before a response: ambiguous. (9d) After a response, before it is recorded: the response is lost, so ambiguous | (9a), (9b) → `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT`. (9c), (9d) → as sequence 4 | A second claim (refused, TSA-7L-02); a send after restart under the old operation |
| 10 | An operator tries to resolve an ambiguous operation manually | None: an operator is not a source of evidence | None. No grant or function writes an outcome (OPT-7L-09; HLC-7L-16). The attempt is logged; the operator may add a note to an incident | Any change of operation state; any change of the deadline |
| 11 | An unresolved operation outlives the privacy-deletion deadline | T-0 … T-3 only | `DEADLINE_MISSED` (RDQ-7L-28). A listed version that is not held is reported as unauthorized retention. A held one stays `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED`. Successors continue | Reporting the version as deleted, bounded or resolved; extending the deadline |

#### 35.4f Authorization-change fence (FG-7L-R5-03)

**Root cause.** BQA-7L-07 compared authorization digests at the two job passes. Equal digests show only that the surface was the same at two instants. A principal able to change it can widen it, use the widening (a batch copy of the recording to an unregistered bucket, for example), and restore it between the two instants. The two snapshots then agree. **Snapshots stay as a necessary check, never as evidence of continuity.** Continuity rests, for each component, on three things: **prevention by the provider** where AWS can enforce it; a **change record that the changing principal cannot suppress**; and a **reconciliation of every access to the key**. Where the provider cannot prevent a change, that is recorded as a deficiency and the adapter stays NOT ADMITTED (ACF-7L-09).

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| ACF-7L-01 [RDQ-7L-03; BQA-7L-02, -03] | **Interval and surface.** The continuity interval *I* of an intent runs from `T_cfg` before the recording's earliest version to the last listing of `VERIFYING`, with audit delivery proven to its end plus `T_ct`. It covers the whole lifetime, not only the cleanup, because a copy taken to an unregistered target at any time defeats "permanently absent". The surface is every component of the table below, in every account of *J* and Region of *R(a)*, in `us-east-1` for IAM and STS events (S-36), and in the Regions where Organizations and Multi-Region Access Point control-plane events are recorded [VERIFY, PV-R3 (i)]. |
| ACF-7L-02 [S-32, S-34] | **Change prohibition in member accounts.** An SCP denies every change action of the table to every principal of every account of *J*, **the member account's root user included** (S-32), except a change session (ACF-7L-03). The bucket-owner root's standing right to change its bucket policy is restrained by that SCP, one of the two mechanisms AWS names for it (S-34 [VERIFY]). No delegated administrator for Organizations policy management exists, or the same SCP restrains it (S-32 applies SCPs to delegated administrators). `organizations:LeaveOrganization` is denied to member accounts. The management account cannot be restrained this way (ACF-7L-09). |
| ACF-7L-03 [RDQ-7L-04, -06, -08; S-19, S-20] | **Change sessions under change records (revises the governed provisioning identity of RDQ-7L-04, -08 and TSA-7L-08).** The governed provisioning identity holds no standing change permission over the surface. Each governed change is a **change record** committed in PostgreSQL. It takes, exclusively, the per-bucket configuration lock of every closure bucket it touches and a per-account surface lock of every account whose IAM, access-point or Batch Operations surface it touches. Every intent holds both locks in share mode from `FENCED` until it is terminal (RDQ-7L-06). So no change record commits while an intent on that bucket or account is open, and no intent reaches `FENCED` while a change record is open. A separate **change broker** mints a session only for a committed change record, with: session tag `change_record` = its identifier; `SourceIdentity` = the identifier; an inline policy naming only the record's actions and resources; `aws:CurrentTime` before the record's `not_after`. The SCP exemption of ACF-7L-02 is conditioned on that tag (S-19). An admitted change can take effect later (S-37), so `FENCED` also requires the record's change events to be reconciled (ACF-7L-05) and `T_cfg` to have passed since its `not_after + T_skew`. **Liveness.** Intents may be open on a bucket almost continuously, so the exclusive lock alone could block a security change, such as revoking a compromised role, indefinitely. A change record that Security marks *urgent* may therefore commit while intents hold share locks. Its commit sends every such intent that is not in `INCIDENT` back to `QUIESCING`. An intent in `INCIDENT` stays there: its latest containment pass is invalidated, and a new pass is triggered (ICM-7L-06 (iii)). §35.5 permits `INCIDENT → QUIESCING` only through ICR-7L-05 (revised for the seventh review, FND-7L-13). In `QUIESCING` the snapshots, the inventory and both job passes are repeated after the change's `not_after + T_skew + T_cfg`. Its events match the record, so they are not `AUTHZ_CHANGED`; its G-17 rows enter *P(b)* and the closure from their effective time. No deadline moves. Every other change record waits, and an alert is raised after `T_chg,warn` ([CAND] 24 hours). |
| ACF-7L-04 | **The component table.** See below. Each row answers the ten questions of the review. |
| ACF-7L-05 [S-35, S-36] | **Change-event reconciliation (continuous; evidence E-17).** A monitor, running under the closure verifier's read-only identity, reads the organization trail and, for each account and Region, CloudTrail Event history, which is immutable for 90 days and not affected by trail configuration (S-36). Over *I*: (a) every **successful** write event on the surface must map to a change record, with equal resources and an event time inside the record's session window. An unmatched event, or any successful event while the intent holds its share locks, is `INCIDENT` (`AUTHZ_CHANGED`), **even if a later event restores the earlier state**. An event attributed by a committed IRR of this intent of class `CHANGE_REVERTED_UNUSED` or `CHANGE_ADOPTED` counts as matched for this intent only; a restoring event alone never does (revised for FG-7L-R7-01; §35.4h IRE-7L-06). The event stays a raw row of every run, and is counted as matched through `matched_by_irr` (CRX-7L-01, -09). (b) **Denied** attempts (`errorCode` `AccessDenied`) are reported to Security and recorded on the intent; they show the fence working and do not stop the intent. (c) Every `AssumeRoot` event (S-35) and every Organizations write event is treated as (a). (d) Trail continuity: no `StopLogging`, `DeleteTrail`, `UpdateTrail` or `PutEventSelectors` event; digest files present and valid, without a gap, for every account and Region of *I* (S-36); delivery proven through the end of *I*. A gap keeps the intent in `VERIFYING`, and past `T_q,max` it is `INCIDENT` (`AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE`). (e) For the part of *I* within the last 90 days, Event history agrees with the trail on the surface's management write events; a disagreement is `AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE`. A real-time rule on the same events raises the incident without waiting for the pass. |
| ACF-7L-06 [TSA-7L-09, -10] | **Data-access reconciliation over *I*.** Every data event on the exact key, in every closure bucket, must be by a principal of *P(b)* as G-17 records it at the event's time, acting in a function that G-17 records for it, for example: the recorder (writes while the row is `IN_PROGRESS`); reads through the playback signer's URLs (until the capability horizon, RDQ-7L-25); live replication; the governed batch role under a change record; inspection and deletion sessions under claimed operations. Any other read, copy or write, a `GetObject` or `CopyObject` source read by a batch-job role outside a change record in particular, is `INCIDENT` (`UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`), unless a committed IRR of this intent attributes it with a matching class: `REFUSED_NO_EFFECT`, `PLATFORM_OPERATION`, `WRITE_CONTAINED` or `DELETION_ATTRIBUTED`. A successful read (`READ_EXPOSURE`) never matches (revised for FG-7L-R7-01; §35.4h IRE-7L-06). The raw row is kept in every run, and the match is recorded through `matched_by_irr` (CRX-7L-09). The copy of the adversarial example is caught here, at the source key, **whatever its unregistered target**. A covering job created during *I*, in any status, is also found by its `CreateJob` event and by pass 2 (BQA-7L-07). CloudTrail data events and logs are retained for at least the recording's lifetime plus the cleanup plus `T_ct` (RAD-7L-12). |
| ACF-7L-07 [BQA-7L-07; RDQ-7L-07] | **Snapshots.** The authorization-surface digests at `QUIESCING` and at `VERIFYING` are still taken. They must be equal to each other and to the G-17 state. A difference is `AUTHZ_CHANGED`. **Equality is necessary and never sufficient.** |
| ACF-7L-08 [S-10] | **Propagation.** Bucket configuration is eventually consistent (S-10). IAM propagation was not read in this session [VERIFY, PV-R3]. A change event inside *I* is an incident whether or not it had propagated. `T_cfg` ([CAND] 15 min; [MEAS]) is the wait between the last change record and the first snapshot. It is never proof. |
| ACF-7L-09 [S-32, S-33, S-35, S-36, S-37] | **What cannot be fenced (deficiency DEF-7L-R5-03).** (i) **The management account.** SCPs do not affect its users and roles (S-32), RCPs do not affect its resources (S-33), and it can obtain a root session in a member account that removes a bucket policy (S-35 [VERIFY]). It can therefore detach or edit an SCP or RCP, disable the policy type (which detaches every SCP, S-32), move or remove an account, or change the organization trail, and then restore all of it. AWS documents no mechanism that refuses these actions. (ii) **The completeness of CloudTrail itself.** Delivery timing is not guaranteed, and no page read guarantees that every API call produces an event (S-36, S-37). A missing event cannot be told from no event. The snapshots (ACF-7L-07) and the data-access reconciliation (ACF-7L-06) are the backstops, and neither catches a change that is reverted and whose use leaves no delivered event. (iii) **A fully compromised change broker**, like RR-7L-R5 (a). Under (i) – (iii), continuity is **detected, not prevented**. These are recorded as **RR-7L-R6**. RAD-7L-14 keeps every recording bucket set **NOT ADMITTED** until the owner gives RR-7L-R6 an individual disposition under OD-7L-12. 7L makes and proposes no such disposition. |
| ACF-7L-10 | **Fail closed.** If any row of the table cannot be established as stated (no SCP; an exemption not bound to the tag; a Multi-Region Access Point containing a closure bucket; a bucket policy that delegates access control to access points; a trail without data events, global events or integrity validation; Event history not readable by the verifier), the bucket set is NOT ADMITTED. For an existing intent, the outcome is `INCIDENT` (`AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE`), and there is no `VERIFIED_ABSENT`. |

**The mandatory adversarial example, traced.**

| Step | Event | What the fence does | Evidence and state |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | The cleanup records digest *D* at `QUIESCING` | Snapshot 1 (ACF-7L-07) | Recorded; proves nothing about later instants |
| 2 | An infrastructure principal relaxes a bucket policy, or removes a restrictive SCP | (2a) A member-account principal, the member root included: the SCP refuses `PutBucketPolicy` (S-32); the attempt is a denied event. (2b) The management account detaches the SCP, or removes the bucket policy through `AssumeRoot`: AWS does not refuse it (ACF-7L-09) | (2a) A Security report; nothing changes; the intent continues. (2b) `DetachPolicy`, `AssumeRoot` or `DeleteBucketPolicy` is an unmatched change event during the intent's locks: `INCIDENT` (`AUTHZ_CHANGED`) at once, through the real-time rule |
| 3 | A batch-copy actor gains temporary access to the recording | The read of the source key is a data event by a principal outside its function; the job's `CreateJob` event is unmatched | `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` (ACF-7L-06); `BATCH_PROOF_INCOMPLETE` (BQA-7L-07) |
| 4 | The policy is restored to *D* | The restoring event is itself unmatched | Recorded. It closes nothing |

If every event of steps 2 – 4 were missing (ACF-7L-09 (ii)), the earlier verification is recorded as falsified (`REOPENED`, RDQ-7L-27), not overwritten | This residual is RR-7L-R6 (ii); it is stated, not closed |

#### 35.4g Incident classification, containment and resolution (FG-7L-R6-01; OD-7L-30, -31)

**Root cause.** Round-3 and round-5 prose (RDQ-7L-19, -24; OC-7L-04, -05; T-7L-07 (a′), (i), (r); T-7L-12 (b), (f2), (g2), (i); adversarial check 28) told the executor to keep deleting after the intent entered `INCIDENT`, "because deletion reduces exposure". The state machine of §35.5, which is the authoritative contract, gave `INCIDENT` no deletion action and one exit: `QUIESCING`, "after a recorded resolution by the Voice and privacy owners". The issue function accepted only `DELETING` (HLC-7L-02 (3)). No mechanism to record that resolution existed. An implementation therefore had to choose between two readings, and either reading broke a rule: deleting from `INCIDENT` broke the state machine, and halting broke frozen 7K RTN-7K-07 and 7I JRN-29 ("neither suspends nor extends the obligation") once `DEADLINE_MISSED` had sent the intent to `INCIDENT`. Neither reading said which incidents leave the deletion preconditions intact. One of the "continue" cases was also unsafe: an unexplained delete marker shows that the bucket policy's deny of unversioned deletes (TSA-7L-06) did not hold, and TSA-7L-14 already said "nothing is deleted there".

**Counterexamples, before and after.**

| # | Sequence | Before (round 5) | After (§35.4g) |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | An unexplained marker is found in `QUIESCING`; the executor goes to `INCIDENT` (`MARKER_UNEXPLAINED`) | OC-7L-04: "still deletes in every closure bucket". §35.5: no deletion action exists in `INCIDENT`; HLC-7L-02 refuses any state but `DELETING`. Two implementations behave differently | Class 2. The issue function refuses every issue (ICM-7L-03). Inspection, op resolution and preservation checks continue. The intent leaves only through ICR-7L-01 … -06, with Security's approval |
| 2 | A class E closure bucket is out of region; `INCIDENT` (`RESIDENCY_VIOLATION`) | RDQ-7L-24 deletes there; §35.5 forbids it | Class 1. Containment issues are explicitly authorized by §35.5 and ICM-7L-03, each under the fresh-evidence predicate (ICM-7L-04) and the hold gate. No copy is made, and the deadline is unchanged |
| 3 | The deadline passes during a long `PENDING` wait; `DEADLINE_MISSED` | The intent went to `INCIDENT`; a halt-reading suspended erasure, against RTN-7K-07 | `DEADLINE_MISSED` is a record-only incident record (ICM-7L-02): it changes no state and grants no permission. The intent stays `QUIESCING`; unauthorized retention is reported |
| 4 | `INCIDENT` (`OPERATION_UNRESOLVED`), then a Class 2 reason (`AUTHZ_CHANGED`) opens | Undefined | Containment stops at once: a Class 2 reason in the open set refuses every issue (ICM-7L-03 (1)). Already-open operations still resolve by OPT-7L-03 evidence; none is converted |
| 5 | `INCIDENT`; an owner "approves" in a ticket, and someone edits the state | Undefined | The state changes only through the ICR-7L-05 function, with two or three verified operator action proofs bound to the current incident fingerprint. A ticket or a direct write changes nothing |

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| ICM-7L-01 [OD-7L-30] | **One incident set per intent (revised for FG-7L-R7-02).** An intent in `INCIDENT` carries a set of *open incident reasons*. Each reason is an **opening occurrence**: an immutable row with the reason code, the subject it concerns, its occurrence number, the evidence that raised it (listing, data-event or finding identifiers) and `opened_at` (§35.4i IRC-7L-01). The row is never updated: it does not record its resolution. An occurrence is closed by a separate, immutable **closure** row that the execution of a request inserts (IRC-7L-05). The open set is the occurrences without a closure (IRC-7L-04). An occurrence and the transition into `INCIDENT` commit in one transaction; from `VERIFIED_ABSENT`, that transaction passes through `REOPENED` (§35.4k PCI-7L-02; revised for FG-7L-R9-01). A further occurrence opens in its own transaction; the intent stays `INCIDENT`. The **class** of a reason is a fixed property of its code (the matrix below), held in a constant table that no runtime principal can write. The class is never decided by a person or at incident time. |
| ICM-7L-02 [OD-7L-30; 7K RTN-7K-07; 7I JRN-29] | **Three classes.** *Class 1, containment permitted*: the cause leaves every deletion precondition provable. *Class 2, halt required*: the cause makes a mandatory precondition unavailable or invalid. *Record-only*: `DEADLINE_MISSED`. It is written as a privacy-incident record (RTN-7K-07; LR-09) and an unauthorized-retention report where the entry is not held. It changes no intent state, grants no permission, removes none, and is never "resolved". |
| ICM-7L-03 [OD-7L-30] | **Containment, by construction.** In `INCIDENT`, the issue function (HLC-7L-02) admits a per-entry deletion issue only when **all** of these hold, each read by the function itself in the issue transaction: (1) every open reason is Class 1; (2) a **containment pass** has completed after the latest reason opened (ICM-7L-06); (3) the entry is in that pass's inventory and is not excluded by the scope column of the matrix; (4) the fresh-evidence predicate of ICM-7L-04 holds for the entry; (5) the hold gate and the effective-hold verdict say "not held" (HLC-7L-02, unchanged); (6) the class order of OC-7L-06 holds. Otherwise no issue is made. If the failure is itself a halting cause, its Class 2 reason opens. Nothing else in `INCIDENT` creates a deletion operation. |
| ICM-7L-04 [OD-7L-30, condition: fresh verification for every operation] | **The fresh-evidence predicate F, for every version-specific deletion issue, in `DELETING` and in `INCIDENT` alike.** "Fresh" means obtained after the latest event that could invalidate it, and, for per-entry provider reads, no older than `T_fresh` ([CAND] 15 minutes) at the issue commit. (f1) *Identity:* the recording row is `DELETED`; the intent's organization equals the row's; the key passes RDQ-7L-02; the (bucket, key, version, class) is in the current pass's inventory and in an exact-key listing taken by an inspection operation within `T_fresh`. (f2) *Tenant-scoped storage authority:* the RAD-7L-11 catalogue check of the bucket's deletion role and bucket policy, taken in the current pass, equals G-17; no open Class 2 reason. (f3) *Closure:* the closure of the current pass was computed from G-17 with no `CONFIG_UNRECORDED`; the bucket is in it. (f4) *Quiescence and batch fences:* for class V, a `HeadObject` within `T_fresh` shows a status that RDQ-7L-10 calls quiescent; for class M, OC-7L-05 (m1), (m2); the current pass's batch evidence (RDQ-7L-12) is complete; no `CreateJob` event for *J* × *R(a)* is recorded after it; the fence locks are held (RDQ-7L-06, -08; ACF-7L-03). (f5) *Hold and order:* HLC-7L-02's share gate, verdict and journal append, in the issue transaction itself. (f6) *Authorization continuity:* the ACF-7L-05 monitor's proven-delivery watermark is within `T_ct` of the issue, with no unmatched event since the recording's earliest version; an event attributed by an committed IRR of this intent with a matching class counts as matched (§35.4h IRE-7L-06; revised for FG-7L-R7-01). The watermark lags delivery, so this evidence is current only to the watermark; the real-time rule narrows the gap and the rest is RR-7L-R6 (ii). (f7) *Audit:* the issue's audit row and journal entry commit in the issue transaction (HLC-7L-02, -15). (f8) *Privacy and residency:* the bucket's residency classification against the conformance record is recorded (E-14). For a bucket in violation, deletion is permitted, because it makes no copy and no transfer (RDQ-7L-24). The deadline record is intact and unchanged. Each item is stored on the issue record with its source identifier. |
| ICM-7L-05 [OD-7L-30] | **What a missed deadline or an unresolved operation does not do.** Neither widens F, waives a precondition or makes any issue admissible that would otherwise be refused. An `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN` operation stays unproven (OPT-7L-04). A successor for its version is admitted only by ICM-7L-03 and F, exactly as for any entry. An ambiguous earlier outcome is never treated as cancelled or resolved without OPT-7L-03 evidence. |
| ICM-7L-06 [OD-7L-30] | **The containment pass.** Run by the executor in `INCIDENT` when every open reason is Class 1. It repeats `QUIESCING`'s work without leaving `INCIDENT`: closure from G-17 and the configuration snapshot (RDQ-7L-03, -07); the complete classified inventory (OC-7L-01 … -03); quiescence (RDQ-7L-10; OC-7L-05); both job passes' discovery (BQA-7L-05) and the creation-fence evidence (BQA-7L-04); the storage-authority catalogue check (RAD-7L-11); the ACF-7L-05, -06 reconciliation to its watermark. It is recorded under a pass number by compare-and-swap on the intent row. A reason that opens later invalidates it (ICM-7L-03 (2)). A pass that finds a halting cause opens that Class 2 reason instead. **Triggers (revised for FG-7L-R7-02).** A pass starts only when every open occurrence is Class 1 and one of these happens: (i) an occurrence opens; (ii) a hold on the recording is released while the intent is `INCIDENT` (ICM-7L-10); (iii) an urgent change record commits on a bucket or account of the intent's closure (ACF-7L-03); (iv) an inspection finds an entry that is not in the latest pass's inventory (OC-7L-09). Each of (iii) and (iv) also invalidates the latest pass. No pass runs on a timer. Per-entry freshness under F is met by inspection operations, not by passes. Retries and successors within the scope of the latest pass need no new pass. The pass number is a fingerprint component (§35.4i RQL-7L-02), so it changes only on these triggers. |
| ICM-7L-07 [OD-7L-30] | **Containment is not completion.** No transition from `INCIDENT` reaches `VERIFYING` or `VERIFIED_ABSENT`. An intent whose every entry was deleted by containment stays `INCIDENT` until ICR-7L-05 moves it to `QUIESCING`. Only the ordinary path (`QUIESCING` → `DELETING` → `VERIFYING`), with E-1 … E-18 complete, reaches `VERIFIED_ABSENT`. |
| ICM-7L-08 [OD-7L-30; RDQ-7L-28] | **Deadlines.** The intent's deadline is the erasure step's or the retention rule's, set when the intent was created; no incident, containment pass, resolution or hold changes it. Past it, every listed entry that is not held is reported as unauthorized retention until it is absent. The `DEADLINE_MISSED` record is kept for the life of the intent's evidence (7I RET-29 pattern). |
| ICM-7L-09 [OD-7L-30, -31] | **No bypass.** No operator, role, function or flag deletes, issues, claims, resolves an operation or changes an intent's state outside the functions named here. There is no emergency path, no single-operator path and no override of a hold, the tenant scope, the closure or the fences. |
| ICM-7L-10 [7I HLD-03, -10 … -13] | **Holds in `INCIDENT`.** A hold is not an incident reason. In `INCIDENT` every issue still takes the gate, so a held entry is recorded `SKIPPED_HELD` (or `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED`, OPT-7L-06) and the intent stays `INCIDENT`. The preservation check (HLC-7L-13) runs for every held entry in `INCIDENT` exactly as in `BLOCKED_HOLD`. A release (HLC-7L-11) changes nothing else: containment may resume only through ICM-7L-03 and F. |

**Incident-classification matrix (ICM-7L-02).** *Sec* = Security's approval is also required to resolve it (ICR-7L-03). "Scope" is what ICM-7L-03 (3) still excludes under a Class 1 reason.

| Reason | Raised by | Class | Sec | Containment scope | Why this class |
|---|---|---|:---:|---|---|
| `OBJECT_LOCKED` | RDQ-7L-19 | 1 | — | Every entry except the locked ones | The other entries' preconditions are untouched; a locked version is refused by the provider anyway (S-30) |
| `DELETE_REFUSED` | OC-7L-07 | 1 | — | All entries; the refused one only through a new issue | A refusal deletes nothing (T-1 (b)); it does not invalidate F for other entries |
| `OPERATION_UNRESOLVED` | OPT-7L-09; HLC-7L-16 | 1 | — | All entries; a successor only under ICM-7L-05 | The unproven operation stays unproven; nothing is inferred from it |
| `RESIDENCY_VIOLATION` (a registered, admitted closure bucket outside the permitted Regions: for class E any other Region; for class S any Region other than `R_o`, or `R_r` without REG-7K-17's record) | RDQ-7L-24; E-14 | 1 | — | All entries | The bucket's storage authority is admitted (TSA-7L-07, RAD-7L-11); deletion makes no copy and no transfer |
| `MARKER_REPLICATION_UNPROVABLE` | OC-7L-05 | 1 | — | Class V entries only; **no class M issue** | Q_V is provable; Q_M is not |
| `KEY_OUT_OF_PREFIX` | RDQ-7L-02; TSA-7L-02 | 2 | Sec | — | Tenant attribution is not established |
| `CONFIG_UNRECORDED` (includes an unregistered destination) | RDQ-7L-04 | 2 | Sec | — | The closure is not complete, so RDQ-7L-11 cannot hold |
| `STATUS_UNEXPLAINED` | RDQ-7L-10 | 2 | — | — | Replication state not provable |
| `QUIESCENCE_UNPROVABLE` | RDQ-7L-28; BQA-7L-11; OC-7L-02 | 2 | — | — | Replication state not provable |
| `UNEXPLAINED_REAPPEARANCE` | RDQ-7L-16 | 2 | Sec | — | An unknown mechanism recreates versions |
| `ADAPTER_INCAPABLE` | RAD-7L-08 | 2 | — | — | No admitted provider capability |
| `HOLD_PRESERVATION_BREACH` | HLC-7L-13; OPT-7L-06 | 2 | Sec | — | A held entry vanished; investigation and legal handling first |
| `BATCH_PROOF_INCOMPLETE` | BQA-7L-04, -07, -08, -11 | 2 | Sec | — | The batch fence is not proven |
| `AUTHZ_CHANGED` | BQA-7L-07; ACF-7L-05, -07 | 2 | Sec | — | Broken authorization fence |
| `AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE` | ACF-7L-05, -10 | 2 | Sec | — | Continuity not proven |
| `STORAGE_AUTHORITY_UNNARROWABLE` | TSA-7L-14 | 2 | Sec | — | Provider-side deletion authorization not valid |
| `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` (includes an unauthorized write after the intent and a copy to an unregistered target) | TSA-7L-10; ACF-7L-06; OC-7L-09; OPT-7L-05, -08 | 2 | Sec | — | A write or credential path outside the fence exists |
| `MARKER_UNEXPLAINED` | OC-7L-04 | 2 | Sec | — | On an admitted stack its required proof cannot be established: the TSA-7L-06 deny that should have prevented it is part of the storage authority (TSA-7L-14) |
| `CLASS_CONTRADICTION` | OC-7L-02, -03, -07 | 2 | — | — | Identity and class of an entry not established |
| `PROVIDER_CONTRADICTION` | OPT-7L-03 | 2 | Sec | — | The provider behaved outside its documentation; F's provider reads cannot be trusted |
| `DEADLINE_MISSED` | RDQ-7L-28; ICM-7L-08 | Record-only | — | Changes nothing | Frozen RTN-7K-07, JRN-29: neither suspends nor extends the obligation |

**The ten situations of the review.** "Resolution" means ICR-7L-01 … -06. Every row keeps the original deadline (ICM-7L-08) and needs AP-7L-54 for its resolution path; no row needs any other amendment (§35.8).

| # | Situation | Intent state | Reason (class) | Further physical deletion | Authorized actor | Approvals | Hold-gate check | Transition | Allowed per-entry issue | Replication and storage-authority prerequisites | Audit evidence | Crash and restart |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Unexplained delete marker | `INCIDENT` | `MARKER_UNEXPLAINED` (2) | No | Executor: inspection, operation resolution, preservation checks only | To resolve: Voice request, Privacy and Security approvals | No issue, so none | Any non-terminal → `INCIDENT`; `INCIDENT` → `QUIESCING` only by resolution | None | Resolution evidence: the creator's attribution, and a fresh RAD-7L-11 catalogue check showing TSA-7L-06 effective | Reason row; audit `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_OPENED`; Security notice | Restart in `INCIDENT`; nothing issued |
| 2 | Unauthorized regional copy in a registered closure bucket | `INCIDENT` | `RESIDENCY_VIOLATION` (1) | Yes, by containment | Executor | None to contain; to resolve: Voice request, Privacy approval | Every issue (ICM-7L-03 (5)) | `INCIDENT` stays; → `QUIESCING` by resolution | Every entry, under F | F (f2) through (f4) for that bucket's account; its own deletion role (TSA-7L-07) | Residency incident record; E-14 failure; issue records with F's sources | Restart in `INCIDENT`; a new containment pass before any issue |
| 3 | Unregistered destination (a rule or a copy outside G-17), in or out of region | `INCIDENT` | `CONFIG_UNRECORDED` or `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` (2), plus `RESIDENCY_VIOLATION` where its Region is known | No, in any bucket | Executor: inspection only | Voice request, Privacy and Security approvals; the evidence includes the change record that registers and admits the destination, or removes it (G-17; RAD-7L-03, -11) | None | → `QUIESCING` by resolution; the new closure includes it | None | The closure is incomplete until G-17 registers it | Reason rows; ACF-7L-06 event identifiers | As 1 |
| 4 | Unexpected data-bearing version | (a) Any version written before the intent's commit by a principal in its G-17 function is **not** an incident: it is in scope (RDQ-7L-09). (b) Otherwise `INCIDENT` | (b) `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` (2) | (a) Yes, as any entry. (b) No | Executor | (b) Voice, Privacy, Security | (a) Every issue | (b) As row 1 | (a) Under F | (a) F | Inventory; data event of the write | As row 1 |

Class 1: Voice, Privacy to resolve | Every issue | Class 2: as row 1. **Dual-controlled resolution contract (OD-7L-31; AP-7L-54).** Its form follows frozen 7I OEA-03 … -09 and OPA-04, -07, -08, -10, -11 and -13. It adds no emergency or single-operator path.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| ICR-7L-01 [OD-7L-31, condition 1] | **Request.** A human holding `recording.cleanup.incident.request`, a grant for the Voice-owner function, submits through the tooling one request per intent. It names the intent and every open Class 1 and Class 2 reason it resolves, with each reason's required evidence references (ICR-7L-02), a reason code and ticket (OPA-06), and the **incident fingerprint** (ICR-7L-04). It carries an operator action proof (OEA-04 form; purpose label `RECORDING_INCIDENT_RESOLVE_REQUEST`). A partial unique index allows one open request per intent. **Revised for FG-7L-R7-02:** the request's states, the index predicate over the open states and every transition are those of §35.4i (RQL-7L-01 … -08). A request that becomes terminal frees the slot in the same transaction. |
| ICR-7L-02 [OD-7L-31, condition 5] | **Evidence per reason (replaced for FG-7L-R7-01).** Each actionable reason has a closed evidence profile: the resolution-evidence matrix of §35.4h, which covers all 20 actionable reasons of ICM-7L-02 and, for each, gives the technical condition, the closing condition (restored, contained or proven safe), the evidence kinds with their producing subsystem and immutable reference (IEV-01 … -16), whether the cause can stay unresolved, the Voice, Privacy and Security responsibilities, validity, revalidation at execution, the fail-closed outcome and the regression oracle. Evidence is verified when the request is made and again at execution (IRE-7L-04, -05). Human attestation is recorded and is never sufficient (IRE-7L-01). A reason whose closing condition cannot be proven is not resolvable (IRE-7L-10). The round-6 text gave evidence for some reasons only, and for `KEY_OUT_OF_PREFIX` cited "the governed Voice correction" of a recording's key; **no such correction exists** in any frozen source or in 7L, and that reference is withdrawn. Evidence is referenced, never copied: no recording byte and no object key appears in the request (RDQ-7L-21). |
| ICR-7L-03 [OD-7L-31, conditions 2, 3, 4] | **Approval.** A different authenticated human holding `recording.cleanup.incident.approve` under a grant for the **Privacy** function approves or rejects the request. When any reason is marked *Sec*, a third human holding the same capability under a grant for the **Security** function must also approve. Identities are compared on the human (OPA-07): one person with two roles or two sessions counts once, and no one approves a request they made. Each decision carries an operator action proof (`RECORDING_INCIDENT_RESOLVE_APPROVE` or `_REJECT`), is bound to the request identifier and the fingerprint (OPA-08), and is unique per (request, fingerprint, approver) (OPA-13). A rejection ends the request; the reasons stay open. **Revised for FG-7L-R7-01 and -02:** the Security approver is also required when the request cites an IRR or an `INCIDENT_REGISTERED` row, whatever the reason (IRE-7L-08). Each approval carries its function's attestation (IEV-11, IEV-12), recorded and never sufficient alone (IRE-7L-01). Decisions are immutable rows, one per human and, for approvals, one per function (RQL-7L-04). The intermediate state `PENDING_REQUIRED_APPROVALS` and the terminal `REJECTED` are RQL-7L-04's. |
| ICR-7L-04 [OD-7L-31, condition 8] | **Staleness.** The incident fingerprint is a digest over: the intent identifier and state; the identifiers and `opened_at` of every open reason; the latest containment pass number; the latest monitor finding identifier for the intent; the number of the intent's operations and of its open operations; and the latest hold verdict reference. Any material change (a new reason, a new pass, a new finding, a new operation or resolution, a hold change) changes it. A request or approval with a different fingerprint is refused as `STALE`, and so is one older than 24 hours (OPA-11). **Revised for FG-7L-R7-02:** the exact components and encoding are RQL-7L-02 (every component above is kept). A change moves the open request to the terminal state `STALE` in the transaction that makes the change (RQL-7L-06), and every request function also recomputes the fingerprint and checks it (RQL-7L-07). A request is `EXPIRED` from `requested_at` + 24 h (RQL-7L-08). `STALE` and `EXPIRED` are terminal states that free the slot. They are not refusals that leave the request open. |
| ICR-7L-05 [OD-7L-31, conditions 5, 6] | **Execution.** A guarded function of the cleanup executor whose only argument is the request identifier (OEA-05 pattern). In one transaction it: locks the intent row `FOR UPDATE`; requires state `INCIDENT` and an equal fingerprint; re-verifies every proof and the two (or three) distinct human identities; re-checks every capability grant, its function, its scope (Region; the intent's organization) and MFA freshness (OPA-10); re-verifies the evidence references; requires that the request covers every open Class 1 and Class 2 reason; inserts one immutable closure row per covered occurrence, and the IRRs, **without updating any opening row** (IRC-7L-05); sets the request `EXECUTED` and the intent to `QUIESCING`; writes the provenance and audit rows. The organization comes from the intent, never from an argument. **Revised for FG-7L-R7-02:** the exact steps, the lock order, the hold evaluation, the confirmations and each refusal's outcome are RQL-7L-09 … -11. A second execution finds the request `EXECUTED` and returns its stored outcome. A revoked grant makes the request `STALE` (`APPROVAL_INVALIDATED`); an expired request becomes `EXPIRED`. |
| ICR-7L-06 [OD-7L-31, "permitted resolution"] | **The only effect: `INCIDENT → QUIESCING`.** In `QUIESCING` everything reruns: the closure from G-17 and the configuration snapshot; the classified inventory of every closure bucket; quiescence; the account-complete batch evidence; the storage-authority and IAM / SCP catalogue checks; residency (E-14); the ACF reconciliations; the hold gate at every issue; OPT-7L-03 for every operation still open. A cause that persists opens its reason again. |
| ICR-7L-07 [OD-7L-31, "prohibited operations"] | **What a resolution cannot do.** It cannot delete anything, issue or claim an operation, set any operation's outcome, mark any entry or intent `VERIFIED_ABSENT`, release or bypass a hold, change a tenant scope or binding, write evidence, change any deadline, or bypass the version-specific protocol. Its functions hold no storage permission. |
| ICR-7L-08 [OD-7L-31, condition 7] | **Immutable audit.** Request, each approval, each rejection, each `STALE` refusal and the execution write insert-only records and audit rows through `audit.fn_insert_audit_event`: `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_RESOLUTION_REQUESTED`, `_APPROVED`, `_REJECTED`, `_REFUSED_STALE`, `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_RESOLVED`. Each carries the intent, the reasons, the request, the human identities and the proof identifiers, and no key or content. **Extended for FG-7L-R7-02** (proposed action kinds): `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_OPENED` for each opening occurrence; `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_RESOLUTION_WITHDRAWN`, `_STALE` (the terminal transition, with `stale_reason`, the changed components and the triggering record) and `_EXPIRED`; `_REFUSED` with a category for every other refused call (OPA-14), `_REFUSED_STALE` being the category of a call that found its request stale. The closure, IRR and provenance rows are insert-only (IRC-7L-05; RQL-7L-14). |
| ICR-7L-09 | **Denial and deadlines.** A rejected, withdrawn, stale or expired request changes nothing except its own terminal state, which frees the slot for a successor (RQL-7L-12): the reasons stay open; Class 1 containment continues where ICM-7L-03 allows; Class 2 stays halted; the deadline is unchanged; past it, unauthorized retention is reported (ICM-7L-08). |
| ICR-7L-10 [OD-7L-31] | **Status.** The capabilities and functions are a proposal: AP-7L-54 (§35.8), not approved for application, not applied, not implemented in Phase 7L. Until they exist, no intent can leave `INCIDENT`. Class 1 containment still runs, because it needs no resolution. Class 2 intents stay halted, logically denied, with their deadlines reported. |

#### 35.4h Resolution evidence per incident reason (FG-7L-R7-01)

**Root cause.** ICR-7L-02 promised "a closed list of evidence kinds" for each reason, but it listed evidence for only some reasons and groups. ICR-7L-05 then required the execution function to "re-verify the evidence references", which had no definition for the other reasons. The same omission caused three further defects. (1) Most of the evidence listed was human: Security's finding, Privacy's assessment. No rule said which technical condition had to be shown restored. (2) Several closing conditions could never hold, because the rerun of ICR-7L-06 re-reads the same historical evidence. An unmatched CloudTrail event stays unmatched for the whole interval *I* (ACF-7L-05, -06; F (f6); E-17). An out-of-region closure bucket stays in the closure's history (RDQ-7L-24; E-14). Resolution led to `QUIESCING`, then to the same reason, then back to `INCIDENT`, and no rule stated that outcome. (3) The `KEY_OUT_OF_PREFIX` evidence, "the corrected attribution through the governed Voice correction", cites a mechanism that exists nowhere. No frozen 5C, 6D or 7x text and no 7L rule defines a correction of a recording's storage key; AP-7L-45 concerns Voice accounting. The correction below does four things. It defines the evidence for every actionable reason. It separates human work from technical proof. It gives reconciled evidence a governed, immutable record. It prevents the transition wherever the closing condition cannot be proven.

**The six resolution notions, kept apart.**

| # | Notion | What establishes it | Can it close an occurrence by itself? |
|---|---|---|---|
| RES-N1 | Investigation completed | The approver's attestation, bound to the approval proof (IEV-11, IEV-12) | **No** |
| RES-N2 | Root cause established | The Security or Privacy attestation, naming the technical evidence it rests on | **No** |
| RES-N3 | Preventive control restored | A technical record from the authoritative subsystem showing that the control that failed is in force now (IEV-03, -04, -05, -07, -14, -16) | Only with RES-N4 where the matrix requires both |
| RES-N4 | Existing evidence reconciled | Every raising event or observation of the occurrence is either superseded by a fresh technical observation of the restored condition, or attributed by an incident reconciliation record (IRR) of a matching class (IRE-7L-06) | Only with RES-N3 where the matrix requires both |
| RES-N5 | Residual exposure remaining | A statement recorded on the closure: what happened and cannot be undone (a disclosure, an out-of-region period, a breached hold, the audit-completeness limit of RR-7L-R6 (ii)) | Never; it is recorded |
| RES-N6 | Capability still fail-closed | Derived, never attested: after the transition every check of ICR-7L-06 reruns, and every issue needs F (ICM-7L-04) | — |

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| IRE-7L-01 [OD-7L-31, condition 5] | **Technical proof is required; human attestation is never enough.** An occurrence is closed only when the technical evidence of its matrix row (RES-N3, RES-N4, or both, as listed) is referenced, exists and passes revalidation at execution. The following are recorded (RES-N1, RES-N2), and are required where the matrix says so, but **never stand for a technical condition**: an incident ticket, an approval, a Security finding, a Privacy assessment, an audit row, a provider support case, an operator's statement. |
| IRE-7L-02 | **Three closing conditions, fixed per reason by the matrix.** *Restored*: the control that failed is in force again, and the evidence that raised the reason is reconciled. *Contained*: the cause is permanent or historical, but every copy it produced is located inside the admitted closure, and the path that produced it is closed. *Proven safe*: a fresh observation shows that the condition that raised the reason does not hold, and recorded evidence explains why it was raised. A reason whose matrix row offers none of the three for the actual facts is **not resolvable** (IRE-7L-10). |
| IRE-7L-03 [ICR-7L-05] | **Evidence records and references.** An evidence record is an insert-only row in G-15, written by the subsystem that produced it. It holds: identifier; organization and intent; kind (IEV-01 … -16); scope (bucket, account, Region, operation or event); producing principal (`session_user`); provider request identifiers; a result class from the kind's closed list; a digest of the result; the database time of its commit (`clock_timestamp()` after its locks); and the record it supersedes, if any. A request references evidence records, per covered occurrence, by identifier. Nothing is copied. No key and no content is stored in a request (RDQ-7L-21). The Voice requester has the executor produce the records through its ordinary inspection operations, verifier runs and monitor runs, none of which deletes anything. |
| IRE-7L-04 | **Latest of its kind.** A referenced provider-derived record (IEV-01 … -04, -07, -08, -16) must be the latest record of its kind and scope when the request is created. A newer record with the same result class leaves the request valid. A newer record with a different result class is an *evidence change*. The producing function records the change as a finding on the intent, which changes the fingerprint (RQL-7L-02 (4)), and the open request becomes `STALE` (`EVIDENCE_CHANGED`) in the same transaction (RQL-7L-06). For IEV-08, "the same result class" means CRX-7L-02: equal effective unmatched sets, by event identity, and never the class alone (revised for FG-7L-R8-01). |
| IRE-7L-05 | **Confirmation before execution.** Execution is one PostgreSQL transaction with no provider I/O. So after a request becomes `APPROVED`, the executor runs one *confirmation* of each provider-derived kind the request references, through the same subsystem, and commits it as an evidence record. The execution transaction requires, for each, a confirmation committed no more than `T_fresh` before its clock read (RQL-7L-08), with the **same result class** as the referenced record. If a confirmation cannot be produced within `T_conf` ([CAND] 300 s, as `T_insp`), the execution is refused and the request becomes `STALE` (`CONFIRMATION_UNAVAILABLE`). A confirmation with a different result class is an evidence change (IRE-7L-04). For IEV-08, "the same result class" is CRX-7L-02, and the confirmation must also meet CRX-7L-04 (revised for FG-7L-R8-01). Confirmations are reads. Containment is not deferred for them (RQL-7L-11). |
| IRE-7L-06 [ACF-7L-05, -06; TSA-7L-10; OPT-7L-08] | **Incident reconciliation record (IRR).** For a raising *event* (a CloudTrail management or data event, or the creation of an inventory entry), the request may propose an IRR: the event identifier; the principal, session and `SourceIdentity` the event names; the class; and the evidence records supporting the class. The class list is closed. *Surface change events:* `CHANGE_REVERTED_UNUSED`: the change and its reversal are both identified by events; the surface equals G-17 now (IEV-03, -07); and the data-access reconciliation (IEV-08) over the change interval, from the change event to the reversal's `not_after + T_skew + T_cfg`, finds no access to the key by a principal outside its G-17 function and no `CreateJob` outside a change record. `CHANGE_ADOPTED`: a later change record (IEV-05) adopts the resulting state into G-17 from its own effective time, with the RAD admission evidence that state needs, and the interval before adoption meets the same data-access condition. *Data events:* `REFUSED_NO_EFFECT`: the event records an `errorCode` from the T-1 (b) list (unavailable until PV-R3 (e) passes, like T-3). `PLATFORM_OPERATION`: the `SourceIdentity` is a claimed operation of this intent with equal bucket, key and version, and OPT-7L-08's reclassification is recorded. `WRITE_CONTAINED`: a write or copy, every product of which (bucket, key, version) is located by IEV-01 in a closure bucket that is registered (IEV-06) and admitted (IEV-03), and whose writing path is closed (IEV-03, -05, -07). `DELETION_ATTRIBUTED`: a successful deletion by an identified principal whose path is closed (IEV-03, -05), where IEV-08 shows that this principal made no successful read, copy or write on the key over *I*. **Never matching:** `READ_EXPOSURE` (a successful read: content left the provider's interfaces), `CHANGE_UNRESOLVED` and `UNLOCATED`. The investigation may record them; they close nothing. The execution function checks each class against its evidence: an `errorCode` exists; the operation and the event agree; every product is in a registered and admitted bucket; the interval's reconciliation is complete and empty. An IRR is written only by the execution function, in the closing transaction, and is immutable. It matches the event **for this intent only**, in ACF-7L-05 (a), ACF-7L-06, TSA-7L-10, F (f6), E-17 and E-18. Another intent whose interval contains the same event needs its own. **Revised for FG-7L-R8-01:** before the commit, an IRR exists only as a proposal. The execution tests it as a conditional proof only, never as a fact already committed, and reads the data-access conditions above on the conditional projection (§35.4j CRX-7L-05 – -07). After the commit, monitor runs list the IRR against their raw rows and never revise an earlier run (CRX-7L-09). |
| IRE-7L-07 [RDQ-7L-03, -04; G-17] | **Incident registration in G-17.** A rule, destination, lifecycle rule or principal found to have existed without a G-17 row is registered by a change record (ACF-7L-03). The change record appends a G-17 row marked `INCIDENT_REGISTERED`, citing the opening occurrence. Its effective-from is the earliest time the provider evidence proves (for example a `PutBucketReplication` event), or, where no evidence proves a time, the recording's earliest version. No existing G-17 row is edited or ended retroactively. Registration only widens the closure; it never narrows it. A registered destination enters the closure, and is inventoried and deleted there, only if its account passes RAD-7L-10 and its bucket RAD-7L-11. |
| IRE-7L-08 [ICR-7L-03; ICM-7L-02] | **Security approval.** A request needs the Security approver when any covered reason is marked *Sec*, **and also** when it cites an IRR or an `INCIDENT_REGISTERED` row, whatever the reason. Some non-*Sec* rows need such a record (for example `STATUS_UNEXPLAINED` explained by an unregistered rule). Then the reason the record reveals (`CONFIG_UNRECORDED`, `AUTHZ_CHANGED`, `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`) must also be open and covered. If it is not open, the request is refused, and the evidence-producing function that found the fact opens it. No reason's class or *Sec* mark changes. |
| IRE-7L-09 [ICR-7L-06] | **No re-raise from closed evidence; every re-raise from a persisting cause.** After a closure, the reruns in `QUIESCING` raise a reason again only from a new observation. A persisting or recurring condition opens a **new occurrence** (IRC-7L-03). Closed evidence does not raise it again. An event attributed by a matching IRR is matched (IRE-7L-06). A bucket whose `RESIDENCY_VIOLATION` occurrence closed as contained is judged by RDQ-7L-24 as revised. A held entry whose `HOLD_PRESERVATION_BREACH` occurrence closed is reported as a recorded breach (HLC-7L-13 as revised). `UNEXPLAINED_REAPPEARANCE` counts returns from the latest closure (RDQ-7L-16 as revised). A marker attributed by an IRR has origin `INCIDENT_RECONCILED` (OC-7L-04 as revised). Each exception is defined by a closed occurrence, never by a person's statement. |
| IRE-7L-10 [OD-7L-30] | **Unresolvable means prevented, not resolved.** Where the matrix's closing condition cannot be proven for the actual facts, the request is refused at creation (`EVIDENCE_PROFILE_UNSATISFIABLE`) and again at execution. The intent stays `INCIDENT`. A Class 2 reason keeps every issue refused. A Class 1 reason keeps containment under ICM-7L-03. The deadline is unchanged; past it, every listed entry that is not held is unauthorized retention (ICM-7L-08). The recording is never reported as deleted, verified or resolved. This outcome is RR-7L-R7. |
| IRE-7L-11 | **Fail closed on the evidence itself.** The execution is refused, the request becomes `STALE` with the cause, and nothing is closed, when a referenced record: is missing; belongs to another intent or organization; is of the wrong kind or scope; carries a result class the profile does not accept; is superseded by a record with a different class; or has no confirmation within `T_fresh`. A request covers every open occurrence (ICR-7L-05) and closes all of them or none. |
| IRE-7L-12 | **`DEADLINE_MISSED`.** Record-only. It is never an occurrence. It is never covered by a request, never closed, and never part of the fingerprint. A request that names it is refused. |

**Evidence catalogue (IEV).** Each kind is produced by one authoritative subsystem and is immutable once written (IRE-7L-03). "Confirmed" means IRE-7L-05.

| # | Evidence kind | Producing subsystem (authoritative for) | Identity and immutable reference | Result classes | Validity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IEV-01 | Complete exact-key inventory of a closure bucket (OC-7L-01) | Cleanup executor, through an inspection operation and its broker session (S3: what exists) | Inspection-operation identifier; every page's request identifier | `ABSENT`; `PRESENT`, with each entry's class and version identifier | Latest of its kind; confirmed |
| IEV-02 | Entry metadata (OC-7L-02): replication status, storage class, checksum, Object Lock retention and legal hold | Same | Inspection-operation identifier; request identifiers | `QUIESCENT`, `PENDING`, `CONTRADICTS_G17`, `LOCKED`, `UNLOCKED` | Latest; confirmed |
