| IEV-03 | Storage-authority catalogue check (RAD-7L-11; TSA-7L-04 … -07): deletion role, session-policy capability, bucket policy, broker and verifier roles, and no `s3:BypassGovernanceRetention` | Closure verifier (IAM and S3 policy reads) | Verifier-run identifier; policy digests; request identifiers | `EQUAL_G17`, `DIFFERS` | Latest; confirmed |
| IEV-04 | Closure-configuration snapshot (RDQ-7L-07): replication, lifecycle, versioning and Object Lock configuration of each closure bucket | Closure verifier | Verifier-run identifier; digests | `EQUAL_G17`, `DIFFERS` | Latest; confirmed; `T_cfg` respected |
| IEV-05 | Committed change record (ACF-7L-03) | Change broker and G-17 writer | Change-record identifier; its reconciled events | `RECONCILED` (every event matched; `not_after + T_skew + T_cfg` passed), `OPEN` | Committed and not superseded by a later change record on the same component |
| IEV-06 | `INCIDENT_REGISTERED` G-17 row (IRE-7L-07) | G-17 writer, under a change record | G-17 row identifier; its change record; the cited occurrence | `REGISTERED_ADMITTED`, `REGISTERED_NOT_ADMITTED` | Immutable |
| IEV-07 | Account-complete batch evidence and creation-fence digests (BQA-7L-04, -05, -07) | Closure verifier | Verifier-run identifier; every page's request identifier | `NO_COVERING_JOB_FENCE_HOLDS`, `COVERING_JOB`, `INCOMPLETE` | Latest; confirmed |
| IEV-08 | Continuity reconciliation (ACF-7L-05, -06; TSA-7L-10) over a stated interval, with the proven-delivery watermark and digest validation | Continuity monitor (organization trail, digest files, Event history) | Monitor-run identifier; interval; watermark; immutable raw event rows by identity `(eventID, recipientAccountId, awsRegion)`; `matched_by_irr`; the effective unmatched set (revised for FG-7L-R8-01; CRX-7L-01) | `CONTINUOUS_NO_UNMATCHED` (no raw row), `CONTINUOUS_RECONCILED` (every raw row matched by a committed IRR of this intent; new), `UNMATCHED` (with the effective set), `GAP` | Watermark within `T_ct` of the confirmation. "Same result" is CRX-7L-02, never the class alone. RR-7L-R6 (ii) applies to every result |
| IEV-09 | Incident reconciliation record (IRE-7L-06) | The execution function only, from the request's proposal | IRR identifier, written in the closing transaction | The classes of IRE-7L-06 | Immutable |
| IEV-10 | Residency record: the conformance record and the E-14 check (7K REG-7K-17, -18) | Executor; Deployment's conformance record | Conformance-record version; check identifier | `CONFORMS`, `VIOLATES` (with the bucket) | Current version |
| IEV-11 | Security attestation: investigation, root cause, attribution, residual | The Security approver, inside its approval, bound to its proof (RQL-7L-04) | Decision identifier | — (attested; never technical evidence) | The request's lifetime (≤ 24 h) |
| IEV-12 | Privacy attestation: exposure assessed, notification reference, residual | The Privacy approver, inside its approval | Decision identifier | — (attested; never technical evidence) | Same |
| IEV-13 | Operation terminality (OPT-7L-03) | The executor's resolution function | Operation identifier; its T-0 … T-3 evidence | `RESOLVED_DELETED`, `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED`, `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT`, `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN`, open | Immutable once terminal |
| IEV-14 | Adapter admission and provider validation (RAD-7L-01 … -15; PV-R1 … -R3) | Deployment's conformance record | Conformance-record version; PV result identifiers | `ADMITTED`, `NOT_ADMITTED` | Current version |
| IEV-15 | Preservation-check result (HLC-7L-13) | Executor | Check identifier; listing identifiers | `PRESENT`, `ABSENT` (with the entry) | Latest |
| IEV-16 | Binding validation (RDQ-7L-02; TSA-7L-02): the executor's prefix check, and a broker claim of a fresh inspection operation for the intent's own key, which runs the broker's pattern and UUID validation and mints only an inspection session | Executor and storage-authority broker | Inspection-operation identifier; claim outcome; the validator's release identifier | `VALID`, `INVALID` | Latest; confirmed |

**Resolution-evidence matrix, table A: cause, closing condition and evidence.** Columns: (1) reason; (2) class and *Sec*; (6) technical condition that raised it; (7) condition that must be restored, contained or proven safe; (3) – (5) required evidence, by IEV kind and result class (the producing subsystem and the immutable reference of each kind are in the catalogue); (8) whether the cause can stay unresolved, and what happens then. Every row also needs the attestations of table B. None of them substitutes for a technical item.

| (1) Reason | (2) | (6) Technical condition | (7) Closing condition | (3) – (5) Required technical evidence | (8) Cause unresolved? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OBJECT_LOCKED` | 1 / — | A class V version is under Object Lock retention or legal hold, so its version-specific delete is refused (RDQ-7L-19; S-12, S-30). On an admitted stack this is a configuration defect (RAD-7L-05) | *Restored*: no named version is locked (retain-until passed and legal hold off), or it is absent; no default retention on the bucket; no identity holds `s3:BypassGovernanceRetention` | IEV-02 `UNLOCKED` or IEV-01 `ABSENT` for each named version; IEV-04 `EQUAL_G17` (no default retention); IEV-03 `EQUAL_G17`; IEV-05 `RECONCILED` for any change that removed a default retention or a legal hold | Yes, while a retain-until date is in the future: a compliance-mode period cannot be shortened (S-12). Refused until it passes (IRE-7L-10); containment continues for every other entry |
| `DELETE_REFUSED` | 1 / — | A version-specific delete was definitively refused (T-1 (b): `403 AccessDenied`, `400 InvalidArgument`, `404 NoSuchBucket`) and is still refused past `T_q,max` (OC-7L-07) | *Restored*: the provider admits the version-specific delete under the TSA policies, shown by success, not by a policy reading | IEV-13: a later operation on the same entry `RESOLVED_DELETED` with attribution `THIS_OPERATION`, or the entry `ABSENT` (IEV-01) with attribution `THIS_OPERATION` or `OTHER_OPERATION` of this intent; for `403`, IEV-03 `EQUAL_G17` and IEV-05 for the correction. For `404 NoSuchBucket`, `CONFIG_UNRECORDED` is also open and covered (the closure names a bucket that does not exist) | Yes, while refusals continue: refused; containment re-issues under F. An absence attributed `LIFECYCLE` or `UNATTRIBUTED` proves nothing about the cause; the latter opens `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` |
| `OPERATION_UNRESOLVED` | 1 / — | An operation stays `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN` or unresolved past `T_q,max`, with its version listed and no successor able to delete it, or a listing cannot be read (OPT-7L-09; HLC-7L-16) | *Restored*: every named operation has T-0 … T-3 evidence, and exact-key listings of its bucket can be read. The operations are not changed by the resolution (OPT-7L-09) | IEV-13 terminal for each named operation; IEV-01 complete for the bucket | Yes, for as long as the provider gives no T-2 or T-3 evidence (S-37): refused; successors continue under ICM-7L-05; a held version stays `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED` (RR-7L-R4 (b)) |
| `RESIDENCY_VIOLATION` | 1 / — | A registered, admitted closure bucket is in a Region the stack's class does not permit (RDQ-7L-24; E-14) | *Contained*: the key is absent from that bucket, and no rule can write it there again. Or, for a class S bucket in `R_r` without its REG-7K-17 record, that record now exists going forward. The earlier period stays a violation either way | IEV-10 (the violation, and the current conformance version); IEV-01 `ABSENT` in that bucket, with IEV-13 `RESOLVED_DELETED` for the containment deletions; IEV-05 `RECONCILED` removing every rule that could write the key there, and IEV-04 `EQUAL_G17` showing it; or, for `R_r`, IEV-10 `CONFORMS` from the REG-7K-17 record's effective time | The violation is never undone: RES-N5 records the period. Refused while any entry of the key is in the bucket, or any rule can write it there |
| `MARKER_REPLICATION_UNPROVABLE` | 1 / — | A class M entry fails OC-7L-05 (m1) (a rule that could replicate markers covered the key after the marker's `LastModified`) or (m2) (the batch fence was not proven) | *Proven safe*, only when (m1) holds by G-17 and the occurrence rested on (m2) alone: (m2) is then proven over the marker's interval | (m2): IEV-08 `CONTINUOUS_NO_UNMATCHED` over the marker's interval, with every `CreateJob` event of *J* × *R(a)* matched, and IEV-07 `NO_COVERING_JOB_FENCE_HOLDS`; IEV-04 `EQUAL_G17` with RAD-7L-04 holding now | Yes, whenever (m1) failed. A marker has no replication status (S-28), so Q_M can never be proven for it: refused permanently (IRE-7L-10). Class V entries are deleted by containment; the marker stays, logically denied; RR-7L-R7 |
| `KEY_OUT_OF_PREFIX` | 2 / Sec | The intent's immutable key does not begin with `org/{organization_id}/recordings/` for its organization, or the broker refused the binding (RDQ-7L-02; TSA-7L-02) | *Proven safe*, only for a validator defect: the same immutable key and organization now validate. **The intent's key and organization are never changed; no correction path for a recording's storage key exists** | IEV-16 `VALID` from a validator release later than the refusal | Yes, if the key truly lies outside the prefix: refused permanently. Nothing is deleted by this intent, and no session reaches the object (TSA-7L-04, -06). Security investigates the cross-tenant reference; RR-7L-R7 |
| `CONFIG_UNRECORDED` | 2 / Sec | A closure bucket's configuration differs from G-17, or a rule, destination or copy target exists that G-17 does not record (RDQ-7L-04, -07; situation 3) | *Restored*: G-17 records, from the earliest proven time, every rule and destination that could have written the key; each registered destination is admitted, or its rule is removed going forward (copies already written stay in the closure either way); the live configuration equals G-17; the change that caused it is attributed | IEV-06 `REGISTERED_ADMITTED` for each discovered destination or rule; IEV-05 `RECONCILED`; IEV-04 `EQUAL_G17`; IEV-08 identifying the configuration change. If that change was made outside a change record, `AUTHZ_CHANGED` is open and covered, with its IRR | Yes, if a destination cannot be admitted (outside the organization, the management account, no deletion role): the closure stays incomplete, so refused; RR-7L-R7 |
| `STATUS_UNEXPLAINED` | 2 / — | A class V version's replication status contradicts G-17 (RDQ-7L-10) | *Proven safe*: for every named version, a fresh status that RDQ-7L-10 can decide against G-17 | IEV-02 `QUIESCENT` or `PENDING`, not `CONTRADICTS_G17`, for each named version; IEV-04 `EQUAL_G17`. Where only an unregistered rule explains it: IEV-06 and IEV-05, with `CONFIG_UNRECORDED` also open and covered (IRE-7L-08) | Yes, if the provider keeps reporting a status that no recorded configuration explains: refused; Security may open `PROVIDER_CONTRADICTION` |
| `QUIESCENCE_UNPROVABLE` | 2 / — | A status stays `PENDING` past `T_q,max`, or status, job or inventory evidence cannot be read or is incomplete (RDQ-7L-28; BQA-7L-11; OC-7L-02) | *Restored*: complete inventory; every class V entry quiescent under RDQ-7L-10; complete batch evidence. If the occurrence came from an inventory contradiction (a version gone while `PENDING`, T-7L-07 (a′)), the disappearance is attributed as well | IEV-01 complete; IEV-02 `QUIESCENT` for every class V entry; IEV-07 `NO_COVERING_JOB_FENCE_HOLDS`; for a contradiction, `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` also open and covered | Yes: a replication that stays `PENDING` (a destination that never returns) is RR-7L-R2; refused |
| `UNEXPLAINED_REAPPEARANCE` | 2 / Sec | Entries reappeared in `VERIFYING` a third time (RDQ-7L-16): an unknown mechanism recreates versions | *Restored*: every reappeared entry's creating event is attributed to a documented mechanism (S-5 … S-7, or a write), and that mechanism is fenced now | IEV-08 with the creating events; an IRR of a matching class for each (IEV-09); the fence evidence of the mechanism: IEV-06, -05 and -04 for a rule; IEV-07 for a job; IEV-03 for a writer's path. The reason the mechanism reveals is also open and covered | Yes, if no provider evidence identifies the mechanism: refused; RR-7L-R7 |
| `ADAPTER_INCAPABLE` | 2 / — | The intent was created against a bucket set whose adapter is not admitted (RAD-7L-08; T-7L-07 (l)) | *Restored*: the adapter of that bucket set is admitted by a conformance version later than the opening | IEV-14 `ADMITTED`, with every RAD rule and PV-R1 … -R3 recorded | Yes, for an adapter that cannot be admitted: refused; logically denied (DFR-7L-04); RR-7L-R7 |
| `HOLD_PRESERVATION_BREACH` | 2 / Sec | An entry covered by a hold is absent, and no operation issued before the hold shows the deletion by its own data event (HLC-7L-13; OPT-7L-06) | *Contained*, never *restored*: the held entry is gone. The disappearance is attributed, its path is closed, and every other held entry is present | IEV-15 `PRESENT` for every other held entry; an IRR for the disappearance (`PLATFORM_OPERATION` or `DELETION_ATTRIBUTED`), with IEV-03 and IEV-05 showing the path closed. For a lifecycle removal (attribution `LIFECYCLE`), IEV-04 and IEV-05 showing that no lifecycle expiration rule can act on the remaining held entries (RAD-7L-04 as revised) | The breach is permanent (RES-N5). It stays recorded against the hold, and the entry is never reported as preserved. Refused if the disappearance cannot be attributed, or its path cannot be closed; RR-7L-R7 |
| `BATCH_PROOF_INCOMPLETE` | 2 / Sec | The creation fence is not established, an enumeration is incomplete, an account left the organization or lost its discovery role, or a job was created outside a change record (BQA-7L-04, -07, -08, -11) | *Restored*: a complete account-complete enumeration with the creation fence holding, and every `CreateJob` event in the interval matched or reconciled | IEV-07 `NO_COVERING_JOB_FENCE_HOLDS`; IEV-08 with every `CreateJob` event matched to a change record or reconciled. For a job created outside a change record: an IRR `WRITE_CONTAINED` covering every product it wrote | Yes, for an account outside the organization, management-account membership, or a job whose targets cannot be located: refused; RR-7L-R7 |
| `AUTHZ_CHANGED` | 2 / Sec | A successful surface change event is unmatched, or the surface digests differ (BQA-7L-07; ACF-7L-05, -07) | *Restored*: every unmatched change event is reconciled as `CHANGE_REVERTED_UNUSED` or `CHANGE_ADOPTED`, and the surface equals G-17 now | IEV-08 over the change interval; an IRR for each change event (IEV-09); IEV-03 and IEV-07 `EQUAL_G17` / `NO_COVERING_JOB_FENCE_HOLDS`; IEV-05 for an adoption. Any access in the interval outside G-17 functions is `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`, also open and covered | Yes, for a change that is neither reverted nor adoptable: refused. For the management account, RR-7L-R6 (i). The absence of use events rests on CloudTrail completeness: RR-7L-R6 (ii), recorded as RES-N5 |
| `AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE` | 2 / Sec | A trail, digest or delivery gap; Event history disagreeing with the trail; a stale watermark past `T_q,max`; or an ACF component that cannot be established (ACF-7L-05, -10) | *Restored*: continuity over the gap is proven (late delivery arrived, the digest chain is complete, Event history agrees), and the ACF components are in place | IEV-08 `CONTINUOUS_NO_UNMATCHED` over *I*, the gap included; for ACF-7L-10 causes, IEV-03, -05 and -07 | Yes, when logs or digests are permanently missing: continuity over *I* can never be proven, so refused permanently; RR-7L-R7 and RR-7L-R6 (ii) |
| `STORAGE_AUTHORITY_UNNARROWABLE` | 2 / Sec | The provider cannot narrow a bucket's authority as TSA-7L-03 … -07 require, or a catalogue check found it widened (TSA-7L-14) | *Restored*: the narrowing is in force for every closure bucket, and every deletion-role data event of the period is matched | IEV-03 `EQUAL_G17` for every closure bucket; IEV-05 for the restoring change; IEV-08 with every deletion-role data event matched (TSA-7L-10); IEV-14 with PV-R2 recorded for the bucket | Yes, if the provider lacks the capability: the bucket set is NOT ADMITTED; refused; RR-7L-R7 |
| `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` | 2 / Sec | A data event does not map to a principal of *P(b)* in its G-17 function or to a claimed operation; a write after the intent; a copy to an unregistered target; a credential used outside the attempt records (TSA-7L-10; ACF-7L-06; OC-7L-09; OPT-7L-05, -08) | *Contained*: each such event is reconciled with a matching class; every product is in a registered, admitted closure bucket; the path is closed | IEV-08 with the events; an IRR of class `REFUSED_NO_EFFECT`, `PLATFORM_OPERATION`, `WRITE_CONTAINED` or `DELETION_ATTRIBUTED` for each (IEV-09); for a product in an unregistered bucket, IEV-06 `REGISTERED_ADMITTED`; IEV-01 listing each product; IEV-03 and IEV-05 for the closed path | Yes, for a successful read (`READ_EXPOSURE`) or a product that cannot be located or admitted (`UNLOCATED`): refused permanently. The disclosure is a privacy breach (RES-N5); RR-7L-R7 |
| `MARKER_UNEXPLAINED` | 2 / Sec | A delete marker that a G-17 lifecycle rule does not explain: the bucket policy's deny of unversioned deletes (TSA-7L-06) did not hold (OC-7L-04) | *Restored*: the marker's creating event is attributed, and the deny is in force now. Or *proven safe*: the marker is explained as `LIFECYCLE` by a rule registered from provider evidence | IEV-08 with the creating `DeleteObject` event; an IRR `WRITE_CONTAINED` (the marker is the product, located in a closure bucket); IEV-03 `EQUAL_G17` (TSA-7L-06 effective); IEV-05 for its restoration, with `AUTHZ_CHANGED` open and covered where the deny had been changed. Or IEV-06 and IEV-04 for a lifecycle rule, with `CONFIG_UNRECORDED` open and covered | Yes, if the creating event cannot be found: the deny's effectiveness is unproven, so `AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE` opens and the request is refused; RR-7L-R7 |
| `CLASS_CONTRADICTION` | 2 / — | A listing's class and a `HEAD` or delete response disagree: `405` for a `Version`, `200` for a `DeleteMarker`, `204` without `x-amz-delete-marker` for class M (OC-7L-02, -03, -07) | *Proven safe*: fresh reads of each named entry agree with its listed class | IEV-01 complete, and IEV-02 (class V) or a documented `405` with `x-amz-delete-marker: true` (class M), for each named entry | Yes, if the contradiction recurs on fresh reads: refused; Security may open `PROVIDER_CONTRADICTION` |
| `PROVIDER_CONTRADICTION` | 2 / Sec | The provider behaved outside its documentation: a `204` while the version stays listed, or a data event without an error while the version stays listed (OPT-7L-03) | *Restored*: the contradicted operation has reached a documented terminal outcome, and the documented behaviour is reproduced again | IEV-13 `RESOLVED_DELETED` (T-2) or `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED` (T-3) for the operation; IEV-01; IEV-08 with its data events; IEV-14 with PV-R3 (c) and (e) executed again, in the test account, after the occurrence's `opened_at` | Yes, while the operation stays unproven or PV-R3 cannot be reproduced: refused. The cause of the anomaly may stay unexplained; RES-N5 records it |

**Resolution-evidence matrix, table B: responsibilities, validity, revalidation, failure and oracle.** Columns: (1) reason; (9) Voice-owner responsibility; (10) Privacy approval responsibility; (11) Security approval; (12) validity and staleness; (13) revalidation in the execution transaction; (14) fail-closed behaviour; (15) regression oracle (T-7L-15 (m)). **Default for every row**, which a cell adds to and never weakens: (9) the Voice holder of `recording.cleanup.incident.request` has the executor produce the evidence records, cites them, drafts the IRRs, and edits no intent, row or evidence; (10) the Privacy approver checks the profile and attests IEV-12; (11) Security is required for *Sec* reasons and under IRE-7L-08, and attests IEV-11; (12) provider-derived records are the latest of their kind at creation (IRE-7L-04) and confirmed within `T_fresh` (IRE-7L-05), database records are immutable, and attestations live as long as the request (≤ 24 h); (13) RQL-7L-10: fingerprint, hold verdict, proofs, grants, the covered set, the profile, the confirmations and each IRR's class; (14) IRE-7L-10 and -11: refused, request `STALE` or refused at creation, intent still `INCIDENT`, no closure, deadline unchanged.

| (1) Reason | (9) Voice | (10) Privacy | (11) Security | (12) Validity and staleness | (13) Execution revalidation | (14) Fail-closed | (15) Oracle |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OBJECT_LOCKED` | Identifies, from IEV-08, who set the lock | Records whether the lock period runs past the erasure deadline (unauthorized retention, ICM-7L-08) | Not required, unless the lock was set outside a G-17 function (then `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` is open, IRE-7L-08) | Default | Confirmation IEV-02 `UNLOCKED` or IEV-01 `ABSENT` for each named version; IEV-04 confirmation | A version still locked → refused; containment continues outside the locked entries | (m1) |
| `DELETE_REFUSED` | Classifies the refusal code | Default | Not required, unless the `403` came from a change outside a change record (`AUTHZ_CHANGED`) | Default; IEV-13 immutable once terminal | IEV-13 read in the transaction; confirmation IEV-01; IEV-03 | A refusal later than the success → refused | (m2) |
| `OPERATION_UNRESOLVED` | Lists the operations; never asks for an outcome to be set (OPT-7L-09) | For a held version, confirms that the `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED` report reached the hold's owner | Not required | IEV-13 immutable | Every named operation terminal, read in the transaction; confirmation IEV-01 | An operation not terminal → refused | (m3) |
| `RESIDENCY_VIOLATION` | Default | **Required attestation**: the period, the data concerned and the notification handling (LR register) | Not required, unless the bucket was unregistered (situation 3: `CONFIG_UNRECORDED`) | IEV-10 current version | Confirmation IEV-01 `ABSENT` in that bucket; IEV-04 confirmation | Entry present, or a rule still writing → refused | (m4) |
| `MARKER_REPLICATION_UNPROVABLE` | States which of (m1), (m2) failed | Records that only a marker (no content) remains | Not required | Default | Confirmations IEV-07, IEV-04; IEV-08 watermark | (m1) failure → refused permanently | (m5) |
| `KEY_OUT_OF_PREFIX` | Proposes no key, no organization and no row change | Assesses whether another organization's data is referenced | **Required**: attests the validator defect and the release that corrects it | IEV-16 confirmed | Confirmation IEV-16 `VALID`; the intent's key and organization unchanged since creation (immutable columns) | `INVALID` → refused permanently | (m6) |
| `CONFIG_UNRECORDED` | Requests the change record that registers or removes | Default; where the destination is out of region, `RESIDENCY_VIOLATION` too | **Required**: attests attribution of the configuration change | IEV-04 after `T_cfg` from IEV-05 | Confirmation IEV-04 `EQUAL_G17`; IEV-06 rows committed; IEV-05 `RECONCILED` | `REGISTERED_NOT_ADMITTED`, or the snapshot differs → refused | (m7) |
| `STATUS_UNEXPLAINED` | Default | Default | Only under IRE-7L-08 | Default | Confirmation IEV-02 decidable for each named version | `CONTRADICTS_G17` again → refused | (m8) |
| `QUIESCENCE_UNPROVABLE` | Default | Default | Only under IRE-7L-08 | Default | Confirmations IEV-01, -02, -07 | Any `PENDING` → refused (RR-7L-R2) | (m9) |
| `UNEXPLAINED_REAPPEARANCE` | Default | Default | **Required**: attests the mechanism | IEV-08 watermark | Confirmation IEV-08: no unmatched creation event since; IEV-01 | Mechanism unattributed → refused | (m10) |
| `ADAPTER_INCAPABLE` | Default | Default | Not required | IEV-14 current version | IEV-14 current version `ADMITTED` | `NOT_ADMITTED` → refused | (m11) |
| `HOLD_PRESERVATION_BREACH` | Default; writes no hold record (HLC-7L-08) | **Required attestation**: the hold's owner notified; legal handling referenced | **Required**: attests attribution and path closure | IEV-15 latest; IEV-08 watermark | Confirmation IEV-15 for every other held entry; IRR class check | Unattributed, or path open → refused | (m12) |
| `BATCH_PROOF_INCOMPLETE` | Default | Default | **Required** | Default | Confirmation IEV-07; IEV-08 watermark | `INCOMPLETE` or `COVERING_JOB` → refused | (m13) |
| `AUTHZ_CHANGED` | Default | Default | **Required**: attests attribution, root cause, and RR-7L-R6 where the management account acted | IEV-08 watermark; IEV-03, -07 confirmed | Confirmations IEV-03, -07, -08; IRR class check over the change interval | `CHANGE_UNRESOLVED`, or an access found in the interval → refused | (m14) |
| `AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE` | Default | Default | **Required** | IEV-08 over *I* | Confirmation IEV-08 `CONTINUOUS_NO_UNMATCHED` | `GAP` → refused | (m15) |
| `STORAGE_AUTHORITY_UNNARROWABLE` | Default | Default | **Required** | Default | Confirmation IEV-03 for every closure bucket; IEV-08 | `DIFFERS` → refused | (m16) |
| `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` | Default | **Required attestation**: breach assessment for any read | **Required**: attests attribution | IEV-08 watermark; IEV-01 confirmed | IRR class check against each event; confirmations IEV-01, -03, -08 | `READ_EXPOSURE` or `UNLOCATED` → refused permanently | (m17) |
| `MARKER_UNEXPLAINED` | Default | Default | **Required** | Default | Confirmations IEV-03, -08; IRR class check | Creator not found → refused, and `AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE` opens | (m18) |
| `CLASS_CONTRADICTION` | Default | Default | Not required, unless Security opens `PROVIDER_CONTRADICTION` | Default | Confirmations IEV-01, -02 | Contradiction recurs → refused | (m19) |
| `PROVIDER_CONTRADICTION` | Default | Default | **Required**: attests the investigation; a provider support case is recorded but is not evidence | IEV-14 PV results dated after `opened_at` | IEV-13 terminal; confirmation IEV-01 | Operation unproven, or PV not reproduced → refused | (m20) |

**Coverage check.** The matrix has 20 rows: the 20 actionable reasons of ICM-7L-02, each once. `DEADLINE_MISSED` is the 21st code and is record-only (IRE-7L-12). Eleven rows are *Sec* in table A (2), exactly the eleven of the ICM-7L-02 matrix; five are Class 1 and fifteen Class 2, as there. Table B adds Security nowhere except under IRE-7L-08 and as stated; it removes it nowhere.

#### 35.4i Resolution-request lifecycle and immutable reason closure (FG-7L-R7-02)

**Root cause.** (A) ICR-7L-01 allowed one open request per intent through a partial unique index, and ICR-7L-04 refused a stale or expired request. But no rule made a stale or expired request terminal. Its row stayed open, the slot in the index stayed taken, and a valid successor could not be created, unless an implementation freed the slot by an update that no rule stated. (B) ICM-7L-01 called reason rows insert-only, and ICR-7L-05 told the execution function to "mark those reasons resolved", which is an update of those rows. The correction gives the request an explicit state machine, in which each transition is a committed, audited transaction. Each reason is kept as an immutable opening, closed by a separate immutable closure.

**Request states.**

| State | Open or terminal | Entered by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REQUESTED` | Open | Request function (RQL-7L-03) | Bound to fingerprint *F*; no approval yet |
| `PENDING_REQUIRED_APPROVALS` | Open | Approve function, when the request needs Privacy and Security and only one has approved | Some required approvals present, not all |
| `APPROVED` | Open | Approve function, when every required approval is present | Executable by the executor only (RQL-7L-10) |
| `REJECTED` | Terminal | Reject function | A required approver refused |
| `WITHDRAWN` | Terminal | Withdraw function (7I OEA-09 pattern) | Withdrawn by a holder of the request capability |
| `STALE` | Terminal | Any function of RQL-7L-06 or -07 | Superseded: the incident, the hold verdict, an approval's validity or an evidence record changed. `stale_reason` is one of `FINGERPRINT_CHANGED`, `HOLD_VERDICT_CHANGED`, `APPROVAL_INVALIDATED`, `EVIDENCE_CHANGED`, `CONFIRMATION_UNAVAILABLE` |
| `EXPIRED` | Terminal | Any function of RQL-7L-08 | Not executed within 24 hours of creation |
| `EXECUTED` | Terminal | Execution function (RQL-7L-10) | The intent moved `INCIDENT → QUIESCING`, and every covered occurrence is closed |

**Transitions, complete.** `REQUESTED → PENDING_REQUIRED_APPROVALS | APPROVED | REJECTED | WITHDRAWN | STALE | EXPIRED`; `PENDING_REQUIRED_APPROVALS → APPROVED | REJECTED | WITHDRAWN | STALE | EXPIRED`; `APPROVED → EXECUTED | REJECTED | WITHDRAWN | STALE | EXPIRED`. No transition leaves a terminal state, and no other transition exists. Each one locks the intent row, then the request row, and compares the state it expects, so two callers can never both make a transition from the same state.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| RQL-7L-01 [ICR-7L-01] | **One open request per intent, by lock and by index.** The request relation has the partial unique index `UNIQUE (intent_id) WHERE state IN ('REQUESTED', 'PENDING_REQUIRED_APPROVALS', 'APPROVED')`. Its predicate names states only, never times. A request that becomes `REJECTED`, `WITHDRAWN`, `STALE`, `EXPIRED` or `EXECUTED` leaves the predicate in the transaction that makes it terminal, so the slot is free at that commit. Every function that creates or changes a request first locks the intent row `FOR UPDATE` (RQL-7L-09). The lock serializes; the index is a backstop. |
| RQL-7L-02 [ICR-7L-04] | **The incident fingerprint, exactly.** *F* is the SHA-256 of a length-prefixed canonical encoding of six components. (1) Intent identifier, organization identifier and intent state. (2) The open occurrences (IRC-7L-04), sorted by identifier, each with reason code, subject key, occurrence number and `opened_at`. (3) The latest containment-pass number and whether it completed. (4) The identifier of the latest *finding* recorded on the intent. (5) The intent's deletion operations: the total, the number open (the states of HLC-7L-02's index), the number `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN`, and the number in each terminal state. (6) The latest hold-verdict reference recorded on the intent, and the counts of its entry-level hold records (`SKIPPED_HELD`, `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED`, `DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD`, `DELETED_BEFORE_COVERAGE`). Every round-6 component is kept. Two are made exact. "Operations" are deletion operations: an inspection operation changes nothing in the incident, and what it finds is recorded as an occurrence or a finding, which are components (2) and (4). A *finding* is a recorded anomaly (an unmatched event, a denied attempt, a delivery gap, an evidence change under IRE-7L-04), never the advance of a monitor watermark and never a "present" preservation result. The intent row stores the current *F* and a fingerprint sequence number, written only by RQL-7L-06. |
| RQL-7L-03 [ICR-7L-01] | **Creation.** The request function, granted to the tooling principal (PRV-17 (b)), runs one transaction. (1) Locks per RQL-7L-09; reads the clock after the last lock. (2) An open predecessor that is expired or stale (RQL-7L-07, -08) is moved to `EXPIRED` or `STALE` here, with its audit row. (3) If an open, current request remains: refused (`OPEN_REQUEST_EXISTS`). (4) Verifies the requester's proof (OEA-04 form; purpose `RECORDING_INCIDENT_RESOLVE_REQUEST`; it binds the intent's organization, the intent, *F* and the digest of the request content), an `ACTIVE` session, MFA within the OPA-03 bound, and a live grant of `recording.cleanup.incident.request` for the Voice-owner function, in scope. Consumes the proof (OLC-09 pattern). (5) Refreshes the hold verdict (RQL-7L-06). (6) Requires the covered occurrences to equal exactly the open occurrences of *F*. Requires each occurrence's evidence profile to be satisfiable (IRE-7L-10), with references that exist and are the latest of their kind (IRE-7L-04). Runs the preview of CRX-7L-03 (CRX-7L-05 – -07 on the referenced records); the request is not created unless the remaining set is empty (revised for FG-7L-R8-01). (7) Computes `requires_security` (IRE-7L-08). (8) Inserts the request as `REQUESTED`, with `requested_at` = the clock read of (1) and `expires_at` = `requested_at` + 24 h, together with its covered-occurrence rows, evidence-reference rows and IRR proposals, all immutable. `supersedes_request_id` names the intent's latest terminal request, if any. (9) Writes `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_RESOLUTION_REQUESTED`. The organization comes from the intent (PRV-18). A refused call creates nothing and writes a `FAILURE` audit row (OPA-14). |
| RQL-7L-04 [ICR-7L-03] | **Approval and rejection.** The approve and reject functions, granted to the tooling principal. Locks per RQL-7L-09. RQL-7L-07 and -08 are applied first. If the request is terminal, or becomes terminal now, the decision is refused (`REQUEST_NOT_OPEN`, with the state) and audited, and the proof is not consumed. Then the function verifies: the approver's proof (purpose `RECORDING_INCIDENT_RESOLVE_APPROVE` or `_REJECT`, binding the request identifier, *F*, the organization and the function); an `ACTIVE` session; MFA within the bound; and a live grant of `recording.cleanup.incident.approve` naming exactly that function (`PRIVACY` or `SECURITY`), in scope. The approver's human identity must differ from the requester's and from every other decision on the request (OPA-07). For an approval, the function must be required (`SECURITY` only when `requires_security`) and not yet approved, and the current *F* must equal the request's. A Security approval carries IEV-11; a Privacy approval carries IEV-12. The decision is inserted as an immutable row, unique per (request, human) and, for approvals, per (request, function), and the proof is consumed. An approval moves the request to `PENDING_REQUIRED_APPROVALS` or `APPROVED`; a rejection, by an eligible approver who has not approved it, moves it to `REJECTED`. The audit row is `_APPROVED` or `_REJECTED`. A repeated submission with the same proof returns the stored decision (OPA-13; 7I STP-13). |
| RQL-7L-05 [7I OEA-09] | **Withdrawal.** A holder of `recording.cleanup.incident.request`, with a proof (`RECORDING_INCIDENT_RESOLVE_WITHDRAW`), moves an open request to `WITHDRAWN`; audit `_WITHDRAWN`. The occurrences stay open. |
| RQL-7L-06 | **Eager staleness, in the transaction that changes the incident.** Every function that changes a component of *F* already locks the intent row `FOR UPDATE`: the opening of an occurrence (IRC-7L-01), a containment-pass record (ICM-7L-06), a finding record, an issue and an operation resolution (HLC-7L-02, -07, -08, -10), a hold-verdict record, and every intent transition. Each calls one internal routine after its change and before its commit. The routine recomputes *F* from the authoritative rows. If *F* has changed, it stores the new *F* and increments the sequence. If an open request exists, it moves it to `STALE`, recording the `stale_reason` (`HOLD_VERDICT_CHANGED` for component (6), `EVIDENCE_CHANGED` for an evidence-change finding, `FINGERPRINT_CHANGED` otherwise), the components that changed and the identifier of the triggering record, with a provenance row (7I STP-11 pattern) and the audit row `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_RESOLUTION_STALE`, all in the same transaction. If that audit insert fails, the triggering change rolls back with it (AUD-7I-01). So the incident never changes while a request bound to the old *F* stays open. The routine performs no I/O and waits on no lock beyond the intent row its caller holds, so containment is not slowed. A hold is placed by 7I functions that lock no Voice row (HLC-7L-02). It changes *F* when a Voice function next evaluates it: an issue, an operation resolution, a preservation check, or the create, approve and execute functions, each of which takes the gate in share mode first and records a changed verdict through this routine. |
| RQL-7L-07 | **Lazy staleness.** Every request function (create, approve, reject, withdraw, execute) and the executor's sweep, after taking its locks, checks in this order, and the first failure decides. (1) Expiry (RQL-7L-08). (2) *F* recomputed from the authoritative rows differs from the request's *F*, or from the stored *F*: `STALE` (`FINGERPRINT_CHANGED`). A recomputed value that differs from the stored one is also an integrity alarm, because RQL-7L-06 should already have advanced it. (3) For approve and execute: every stored proof re-verifies under the key relation (7I STP-10 overlap applies to a rotated key); every decider's grant is live, unrevoked and in scope; no decider's human identity is disabled. Otherwise `STALE` (`APPROVAL_INVALIDATED`). (4) For execute: each referenced evidence record is still the latest of its kind, or is superseded only by records of the same class, and each confirmation exists (IRE-7L-04, -05). Otherwise `STALE` (`EVIDENCE_CHANGED` or `CONFIRMATION_UNAVAILABLE`). The terminal transition, its provenance row and its audit row commit, while the requested action is refused and that refusal is audited (OPA-14). |
| RQL-7L-08 [OPA-11] | **Expiry at the 24-hour boundary.** `expires_at` = `requested_at` + 24 h, both fixed at creation. A request is expired when `clock_timestamp()`, read by a statement after the transaction's last lock acquisition, is at or after `expires_at`. Neither the decision nor the stored time uses `now()`, which is the transaction's start and precedes its lock waits. No wait occurs after the read; the commit follows within the same transaction's remaining statements. A function that finds an open request expired moves it to `EXPIRED`, writes `_EXPIRED`, and refuses its own action. The executor also sweeps open requests every `T_sweep` ([CAND] 5 min) so that the state is visible, but nothing depends on the sweep. Every approval therefore lives at most 24 hours (OPA-11); the round-6 refusal of a request "older than 24 hours" is kept. No decision is ever carried to another request. |
| RQL-7L-09 [HLC-7L-02; 7I HLD-10, -15] | **Lock order.** Every function of §35.4h, §35.4i and ICR-7L-05 takes its locks in one order, which extends HLC-7L-02's. (1) The organization's hold gate `FOR SHARE`: taken by the create, approve and execute functions, and by issue and resolution as before. (2) The recording row `FOR SHARE`. (3) The intent row `FOR UPDATE`. (4) The request row `FOR UPDATE`. After that, only inserts: decisions, occurrences, closures, IRRs, evidence records, provenance, audit. Opening and closure rows are never locked. They are immutable, and the open set cannot change while (3) is held, because every opening takes (3) too. Reject, withdraw, the sweep and the finding writer start at (3). No function that holds a later lock asks for an earlier one, and 7I placement takes no Voice row (HLD-15), so no cycle exists. The clock read of RQL-7L-08 follows the last of these locks. |
| RQL-7L-10 [ICR-7L-05] | **Execution (revised for FG-7L-R8-01).** The execution function is granted only to the executor principal, which cannot request, approve or reject (7I OEA-05 pattern). Its only argument is the request identifier. It runs one transaction in two phases. **Decision phase.** It reads; its only possible writes are the verdict record of step 2 and, on refusal, the terminal transition. (1) Locks per RQL-7L-09 (gate, recording row, intent row, request row), then the clock read. If the request is `EXECUTED`, returns the stored outcome and changes nothing; if it is in another terminal state, refuses. (2) Expiry (RQL-7L-08). Staleness and the fingerprint (RQL-7L-07 (2)). The effective-hold verdict, evaluated under the gate and recorded through RQL-7L-06, so a changed verdict makes the request `STALE`. Live grants, proofs and human identities (RQL-7L-07 (3)). (3) Requires the intent `INCIDENT`, the request `APPROVED`, and decisions by distinct humans: the Voice requester and the Privacy approver, plus the Security approver when `requires_security` holds (IRE-7L-08; ICR-7L-03; OPA-07). (4) Validates the immutable source evidence: every referenced record and its confirmation (IRE-7L-04, -05; CRX-7L-02, -04), and every proposed IRR (CRX-7L-05). (5) Computes the conditional projection (CRX-7L-06). (6) Requires every technical proof condition: the covered set equals the open set, and every covered occurrence's profile in §35.4h holds, with each IEV-08 condition read on the projection (CRX-7L-07). **Commit phase.** (7) Inserts the committed IRRs (one per valid matching proposal) and the projection record (CRX-7L-08), then one closure per covered occurrence (IRC-7L-05), with the references to `INCIDENT_REGISTERED` rows. (8) Sets the request `EXECUTED`. (9) Moves the intent `INCIDENT → QUIESCING` (§35.5). (10) Writes the provenance rows and `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_RESOLVED` through `audit.fn_insert_audit_event`, naming the request, the decisions, the closures, the IRRs and the projection record. (11) Commits. Steps 7 – 11 commit together or not at all. **Failure.** A decision-phase failure at steps 2 – 6 writes nothing of steps 7 – 10. It commits only the terminal transition it implies (`EXPIRED`, or `STALE` with its reason) and that transition's audit row (RQL-7L-07). An error in steps 7 – 11 (a constraint, the audit insert, a crash) rolls back the whole transaction. Then no IRR exists, no occurrence is closed, the request stays `APPROVED` and the intent `INCIDENT`; the refusal is audited in a subtransaction under OPA-14 (RQL-7L-16). In every failure, no IRR takes effect and the incident stays open. The resolution deletes nothing and never sets `VERIFIED_ABSENT` (ICR-7L-07; ICM-7L-07), and every check of `QUIESCING` reruns after it (ICR-7L-06). |
| RQL-7L-11 | **Executor ordering and confirmations; no suspension.** The commit of `APPROVED` writes a wake record. The executor then runs the confirmations of IRE-7L-05, which are reads, and then the execution transaction. Containment is **not** deferred for this: issues and operation resolutions continue. If one of them commits first, it changes *F*, the request becomes `STALE` (RQL-7L-06), and the requester may create a successor at once. |
| RQL-7L-12 | **Successors under continuing change.** A request that became `STALE`, `EXPIRED`, `REJECTED` or `WITHDRAWN` frees the slot. A successor is a new request: a new proof, the current *F*, the occurrences open then, evidence references checked again as latest, and `supersedes_request_id` set. The tooling shows the approvers which components of *F* changed since the predecessor, and the predecessor's decisions, for information only. **No decision carries over.** Every approval of a successor is a new decision with a new proof. **Why this converges without suspending erasure.** *F* changes only through the components of RQL-7L-02, and the executor writes none of them on a timer. A containment pass starts only on the triggers of ICM-7L-06. Inspection operations, watermark advances and "present" preservation results are not components. Containment changes *F* only while it has an issuable entry. Every entry of a pass is eventually deleted, held, outside the pass's scope, or refused again because its cause persists. Once the cause that a Class 1 reason names stops producing new work, *F* stays constant until a new fact arrives, and a request made then stays current. If *F* keeps changing because a refused delete is retried or an ambiguous operation receives successors (OPT-7L-07), the cause of that reason persists. Its closing condition (§35.4h) then cannot be shown, and the request would be refused on its evidence anyway. Erasure is never paused for a resolution: containment continues throughout, Class 2 stays halted as OD-7L-30 decided, and the deadline does not move. There is no unlimited approval, no carried approval and no manual state edit. |
| RQL-7L-13 | **Tenant isolation.** The organization comes from the intent (PRV-18). Every relation of this family carries `organization_id` and `intent_id`, with composite foreign keys: requests `(intent_id, organization_id)` → the intent; covered-occurrence rows `(opening_id, intent_id, organization_id)` → the opening; decisions `(request_id, organization_id, fingerprint)` → the request; closures `(opening_id, intent_id, organization_id)` → the opening and `(request_id, intent_id, organization_id)` → the request. A request can therefore name only occurrences of its own intent and organization, and a closure can join only an opening and a request of the same intent. A forged identifier from another organization fails the key, after the function's own check has refused it. Each proof binds the organization (OEA-04 form), so a proof for organization A fails on B. Grant scope is checked as OPA-04 and OPA-10 require. |
| RQL-7L-14 [7I PRV-16 … -22, -28] | **Privileges.** No login role holds any table privilege on the request, decision, covered-occurrence, evidence-reference, IRR-proposal, opening, closure, IRR, evidence-record, consumed-proof or provenance relations: `REVOKE ALL … FROM PUBLIC`, and grants only on functions (PRV-20); partitions per PRV-22; complete ACLs per PRV-28. The functions are `SECURITY DEFINER` with a fixed `search_path` (PRV-16) and check `session_user` (PRV-19). Grants: create, approve, reject and withdraw to the tooling principal only; execute and the sweep to the executor principal only; each evidence-record writer to its producing principal only; nothing to `app_platform_admin`, `app_api` or `app_worker`. A second layer of triggers stops the owning role's ordinary statements. `BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE` raises on openings, closures, decisions, covered-occurrence rows, evidence references, IRRs and evidence records, and `BEFORE TRUNCATE` raises on each of them. On requests, `BEFORE UPDATE` allows only the edges of the transition list, only the columns `state`, `stale_reason`, `stale_detail`, `terminal_at` and `terminal_audit_event_id`, and nothing from a terminal state; `BEFORE DELETE` and `BEFORE TRUNCATE` raise. RLS is enabled and forced on each relation with the tenant policy, as defense in depth only: it does not apply inside the definer functions (PRV-17), and no login role reaches the tables. Disabling a trigger needs the owning role, an infrastructure break-glass identity whose use is alerted (OPA-16 pattern); that residual is the one 7I already states. |
| RQL-7L-15 [7I STP-13] | **Crash and retry.** Each function is one transaction: a crash before its commit leaves nothing, and after its commit everything. A tooling retry with the same proof finds the consumed proof and returns the stored outcome. An executor retry of an `EXECUTED` request returns the stored outcome. If an `APPROVED` request's execution crashed before commit, the retry runs again from the locks, with fresh confirmations if the earlier ones are older than `T_fresh`. |
| RQL-7L-16 [AUD-7I-01; OPA-14] | **Audit and rollback.** Each decision and each transition writes its audit row through `audit.fn_insert_audit_event` in its own transaction (ICR-7L-08). If that write fails, the whole transaction rolls back: no decision, no transition, no closure. For a refusal, OPA-14 applies: the function rolls back to its savepoint and writes the refusal's audit row in a subtransaction. If that write also fails, the action stays refused and an alert is raised; a refusal never turns into a permission. A failed execution audit leaves the request `APPROVED` and the intent `INCIDENT`. A later execution succeeds only while the request is still current and unexpired. |

**Persistence model for reasons (chosen: immutable openings, separate immutable closures).** The alternative, a guarded update of the reason rows, was not chosen. It would need a before/after record of each change anyway, and it would leave a column that some role could be granted to write.

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| IRC-7L-01 [ICM-7L-01] | **Opening occurrence (immutable).** Columns: `opening_id` (database-generated; primary key); `organization_id`; `intent_id`; `reason_code`, a foreign key to the constant class table, which holds class and *Sec* and is writable by no runtime principal; `subject_key`, in a closed form per reason (bucket and version for entry reasons, event identifier for event reasons, bucket for bucket reasons, account for account reasons, the intent for intent-wide reasons; never an object key); `occurrence_no`; `prior_closure_id`; the raising evidence references; `opened_in_state`; `opened_at` (`clock_timestamp()` after the intent lock); the audit-event identifier. Unique `(intent_id, reason_code, subject_key, occurrence_no)`. `occurrence_no` is 1 exactly when `prior_closure_id` is null. Otherwise `prior_closure_id` is unique, and it references the closure of occurrence `occurrence_no − 1` of the same (intent, reason code, subject), through a composite foreign key. An opening is written only by the detecting function, in the transaction that detects the cause. That transaction locks the intent row `FOR UPDATE` and calls the opening routine (§35.4k PCI-7L-01). The routine moves the intent into `INCIDENT` only along the edges of §35.5, for the state it reads under the lock: one edge from `FENCED`, `QUIESCING`, `DELETING`, `VERIFYING`, `BLOCKED_HOLD` or `REOPENED`; none in `INCIDENT`; from `VERIFIED_ABSENT`, the ordered pair `VERIFIED_ABSENT → REOPENED → INCIDENT`, with the challenge record and the opening between the two edges (PCI-7L-02); from `PENDING`, only in the step that enters `FENCED`. It never makes a direct `VERIFIED_ABSENT → INCIDENT`. It writes `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_OPENED` (revised for FG-7L-R9-01). A retry with the same raising evidence finds the open occurrence and inserts nothing. |
| IRC-7L-02 | **At most one open occurrence per subject.** Under the intent lock, the opening function inserts no occurrence while one of the same (intent, reason code, subject) is open. A re-detection is recorded as a finding only if it adds evidence that the occurrence lacks. The keys of IRC-7L-01 make two open occurrences of one subject impossible: occurrence *n* + 1 needs the closure of *n*, and a closure can precede only one occurrence. |
| IRC-7L-03 | **Recurrence.** A cause that appears again after its occurrence closed opens occurrence *n* + 1, with `prior_closure_id` set. It brings a new fingerprint and needs a new request. A closure is never reopened, revoked or edited. |
| IRC-7L-04 | **The open set is derived.** The open occurrences of an intent are its openings that have no closure row. An opening has no status column. `DEADLINE_MISSED` has no opening; it is in the record-only relation of ICM-7L-02. Invariant, checked by every function that holds the intent lock, by an integrity assertion, and at every commit by a deferred constraint trigger (PCI-7L-04 (d)): the intent's committed state is `INCIDENT` if and only if its open set is not empty. No transaction commits `REOPENED` or `VERIFIED_ABSENT` with an open occurrence, or `INCIDENT` without one. Inside one transaction, PCI-7L-02 holds `REOPENED` while it inserts the opening and then makes `REOPENED → INCIDENT`; that intermediate is never visible outside it (revised for FG-7L-R9-01). |
| IRC-7L-05 | **Closure (immutable).** Columns: `closure_id` (primary key); `opening_id`, **unique**, so each occurrence is closed at most once; `organization_id`, `intent_id`, `reason_code`, `subject_key`, `occurrence_no`, bound to the opening by the composite foreign key; `request_id` (composite foreign key with intent and organization); the executed *F* and its sequence number; the closing condition (`RESTORED`, `CONTAINED`, `PROVEN_SAFE`); the evidence-reference and confirmation identifiers; the IRR identifiers; the decision identifiers of the requester, the Privacy approver and, where required, the Security approver; the residual statement (RES-N5); `closed_at`; the audit-event identifier. Closures are inserted only by the execution function, in the transaction of RQL-7L-10. |
| IRC-7L-06 | **No operator path to a reason.** No function takes an opening identifier and closes it, deletes it, or changes its code, class, subject or evidence. A request can close only the whole open set of its intent, and only through execution. No function opens a reason on a person's statement: openings are written by the detecting functions, from provider or database evidence. Forging an opening, closing one by a direct write, or hiding one by deletion would each need a table privilege that no login role has (RQL-7L-14). |
| IRC-7L-07 | **Duplicate concurrent resolvers.** Two executions of one request: the second waits on the intent lock, then finds `EXECUTED` and returns the stored outcome. Two requests cannot both be open (RQL-7L-01). A closure insert for an occurrence already closed fails on `unique (opening_id)` and rolls the whole execution back; the locks make this backstop unreachable. |
| IRC-7L-08 | **Crash consistency.** The closures, the IRRs, the request's `EXECUTED`, the intent's `QUIESCING`, the provenance rows and the audit row are one transaction (RQL-7L-10). No state can exist in which some occurrences are closed while the intent is `INCIDENT`, or the intent is `QUIESCING` with an open occurrence. |
| IRC-7L-09 [7I AUD-7I-01; INV-13; STP-11] | **7I audit requirements.** Openings, decisions, terminal transitions and the execution are each audited in their own transactions. The before-and-after evidence is the immutable opening, the immutable closure, the decision rows and the request's provenance rows. The request's state column is a guarded current state, never the record of history. |

#### 35.4j Conditional reconciliation at execution (FG-7L-R8-01)

**Root cause, verified against the text of round 7.** The existing rules were not a complete, atomic conditional-reconciliation rule, for three reasons. (1) IRE-7L-04 and -05 compared a referenced IEV-08 run and its confirmation by *result class* only. A confirmation reporting `UNMATCHED` with a different event list therefore had "the same result class", and a newly unmatched event that no proposal covers could pass the comparison. (2) Several conditions require the events of the request itself to be matched: table A's `CONTINUOUS_NO_UNMATCHED` (`MARKER_REPLICATION_UNPROVABLE` (m2), `AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE`), table B's IEV-08 confirmations, and the data-access conditions inside IRE-7L-06 (`CHANGE_REVERTED_UNUSED`, `CHANGE_ADOPTED`, `DELETION_ATTRIBUTED`). Before the commit those events are matched only by *proposals*, so the monitor correctly reports them `UNMATCHED`. Read literally, the conditions could never pass, and RQL-7L-10 step (8) gave no rule for reading them conditionally. (3) No rule said what a monitor run reports after an IRR commits. An implementation could rewrite an earlier `UNMATCHED` run, or report `CONTINUOUS_NO_UNMATCHED` over events that had been unmatched. The correction below defines five layers of evidence, a deterministic validation of each proposal, an exact set projection, and the commit and post-commit behaviour. It changes no class, no reason, no approval rule and no frozen text.

**Five layers, kept apart.**

| Layer | What it is | Where it lives; who writes it | Mutable? | What it can establish |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 Raw provider evidence | The monitor's IEV-08 runs and their raw event rows, read from the digest-validated organization trail and Event history | G-15 evidence-record relation; continuity monitor only | Never | What happened, and which events match no change record, no G-17 function and no claimed operation |
| L2 Proposed reconciliation | The IRR proposals on a request | G-15 request relations; request function only, at creation | Never | Nothing by itself. A proposal is a claim to be tested |
| L3 Conditionally reconciled projection | The set computation of CRX-7L-06 inside one execution transaction | Transaction-local; stored only as the projection record of a committed execution | — | Whether every condition would hold if the valid proposals were accepted |
| L4 Committed reconciliation | IRRs written by a successful execution | G-15 IRR relation; execution commit phase only | Never | That this intent's evidence treats the named events as matched, for this intent only |
| L5 Post-commit monitor reconciliation | Later IEV-08 runs that list committed IRRs against their raw rows | G-15 evidence-record relation; continuity monitor only | Never | Effective continuity for F (f6), E-17 and E-18. Earlier runs are not revised |

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| CRX-7L-01 [IEV-08; ACF-7L-05, -06] | **Raw provider evidence.** A monitor run is an evidence record (IRE-7L-03) with immutable child rows. Each row is one surface or key event in the run's scope that the monitor could not match to a change record, to a principal acting in its G-17 function, or to a claimed operation. A row holds: the event identity `(eventID, recipientAccountId, awsRegion)`; event source and name; `eventTime`; principal ARN, session and `SourceIdentity`; the resources (bucket, key, and version where present); `errorCode`; the request and response elements that name products (destination bucket and key; the created version identifier [VERIFY, PV-R3 (p)]); and the log file and the digest-validation identifier it was read from. A run also records: its scope (organization, intent); its interval, from the start of *I* to its watermark; the watermark; the digest-validation result per account and Region; and two derived lists over its raw rows, `matched_by_irr` (each raw row matched by a committed IRR of this intent, with that IRR's identifier) and the *effective* unmatched set (raw rows minus `matched_by_irr`). **Result class.** `GAP` if any account or Region of the interval lacks proven delivery or valid digests. Otherwise `CONTINUOUS_NO_UNMATCHED` if there is no raw row; `CONTINUOUS_RECONCILED` if there are raw rows and the effective set is empty; `UNMATCHED` if the effective set is not empty. The monitor principal can insert runs and rows and nothing else. No function updates or deletes them, and nothing committed later rewrites a run's rows, lists or class (RQL-7L-14). |
| CRX-7L-02 [IRE-7L-04, -05] | **"Same result" for IEV-08.** For IEV-08, "same result class" in IRE-7L-04 and -05 means all of these: neither run is `GAP`; both have the same scope; the later run's interval contains the earlier one's; and their *effective unmatched sets are equal as sets of event identities*. A class alone is never compared. An identity in the later effective set that is missing from the earlier one, or the reverse, is an evidence change: a finding on the intent and, through RQL-7L-06, `STALE` (`EVIDENCE_CHANGED`). The reverse case is an event that has since been matched otherwise; a proposal for it would then cover a matched event. A monitor run that finds a new effective event writes, in one transaction under the intent lock: the run, the finding, and the opening of the event's reason (ACF-7L-05, -06). So the open request's `stale_reason` is `EVIDENCE_CHANGED`. |
| CRX-7L-03 [RQL-7L-03] | **Proposed reconciliation.** A proposal is an immutable row of the request, written at creation (RQL-7L-03 (8)). It holds: proposal identifier; request; organization; intent; class; the covered event identities; the referenced raw rows, by composite key (row, run, intent, organization) into the referenced IEV-08 run; and the evidence records that support the class. A proposal covers one event. It covers two for `CHANGE_REVERTED_UNUSED` (the change and its reversal), and for `WRITE_CONTAINED` it lists the write event and its product set. The covered identities have a unique key `(request_id, event identity)` over all proposals of a request, so one event is covered by at most one proposal. A duplicate or conflicting proposal for one event cannot be inserted, and the creation fails as a whole. Until an execution commits it, a proposal has no effect on any monitor run, on *F*, on F (f6), on E-17 or E-18, or on the matching of ACF-7L-05 and -06. At creation, the request function runs CRX-7L-05 – -07 on the referenced records as a **preview**. A request whose preview fails is not created (`EVIDENCE_PROFILE_UNSATISFIABLE`). |
| CRX-7L-04 [IRE-7L-05] | **The confirmation run.** The execution uses the confirmation IEV-08 run of IRE-7L-05. It has the intent's scope, and an interval from the start of *I* to a watermark within `T_ct` of its commit. It was committed no more than `T_fresh` before the execution's clock read. It is not `GAP`. It is the latest IEV-08 run of the scope. It has the same result as the referenced run under CRX-7L-02. Every proposal is re-bound by event identity to the confirmation's raw rows. The proposal's own copy of a row is never used as evidence. |
| CRX-7L-05 | **Validation of each proposal: deterministic, read-only, in this order.** The first failed check makes the proposal *invalid*, and an invalid proposal subtracts nothing. **V1 Existence.** Every covered identity is a raw row of the confirmation run. An identity known only from the referenced run, from the request or from an attestation is never accepted. **V2 Scope and uniqueness.** The row belongs to this intent's and organization's run (composite key). Its resources are on the intent's surface over *I* (a closure bucket, an account of *J*, a principal of *P(b)*, as G-17 history records them) or are the intent's exact key. No committed IRR of this intent covers the identity; if one does, that is a duplicate attribution, and creation is refused. **V3 Class admissibility.** The class is in IRE-7L-06's closed list and fits the event: `CHANGE_REVERTED_UNUSED` and `CHANGE_ADOPTED` only for a successful management write on the surface; `REFUSED_NO_EFFECT` only for a data event with an `errorCode`; `PLATFORM_OPERATION`, `WRITE_CONTAINED` and `DELETION_ATTRIBUTED` only for a successful data event of any, a write or copy, and a delete action respectively. `READ_EXPOSURE`, `CHANGE_UNRESOLVED` and `UNLOCATED` may be recorded, but are never valid matches. **V4 Class-specific technical evidence.** Each item is a raw row or a committed evidence record, never an attestation. *`REFUSED_NO_EFFECT`*: the `errorCode` is in the T-1 (b) list, and IEV-14 shows that PV-R3 (e) passed. *`PLATFORM_OPERATION`*: the `SourceIdentity` is a claimed operation of this intent, with equal bucket, key and version, and OPT-7L-08's reclassification row exists. *`WRITE_CONTAINED`*: the product set is derived only from the row's request and response elements; if it cannot be derived completely from provider evidence, the event is `UNLOCATED`. Each product is listed by a confirmation IEV-01 of its bucket. That bucket has a G-17 row, native or `INCIDENT_REGISTERED`, effective at the event's time, and an IEV-03 confirmation `EQUAL_G17`. The confirmation run covers that bucket from the event's time. The writer's path is closed (IEV-03, -05, -07 confirmations). *`DELETION_ATTRIBUTED`*: the principal is identified (not anonymous); its path is closed (IEV-03, -05 confirmations); and no raw row of the confirmation shows the same principal making a successful read or copy of the key. *`CHANGE_REVERTED_UNUSED`*: the change and the reversal are both raw rows on the same resource; the reversal's request elements restore the configuration that G-17 recorded before the change (equal digest); IEV-03 and IEV-07 confirmations are `EQUAL_G17`. *`CHANGE_ADOPTED`*: an IEV-05 `RECONCILED` change record adopts the resulting state from its effective time, with its RAD evidence (IEV-03, -07, -14). **V5 Current controls.** The confirmations that each covered occurrence's profile names are present (tables A and B). **V6 Interval.** The confirmation is not `GAP`, and its watermark is within `T_ct` of its commit. **Two phases.** Phase 1 validates the data-event proposals (`REFUSED_NO_EFFECT`, `PLATFORM_OPERATION`, `WRITE_CONTAINED`, `DELETION_ATTRIBUTED`); none of their checks depends on another proposal. Phase 2 validates the change-event proposals and then applies their window condition. Let *R1* be the raw identities minus those covered by valid phase-1 proposals and minus those covered by committed IRRs. A change proposal is valid only if no member of *R1* inside its window is a data event on the key or a `CreateJob`. The window runs from the change's `eventTime` to `eventTime + T_skew + T_cfg` of the reversal, or of the adoption's effective time. Phase 2 cannot change phase 1, so the outcome does not depend on the order of evaluation. |
| CRX-7L-06 | **The projection.** Let *U* be the identities of the confirmation's raw rows; *P* the identities covered by valid proposals of matching classes (phases 1 and 2); and *M* the identities covered by committed IRRs of this intent, recomputed from the IRR relation, not copied from the run's `matched_by_irr`. Then **`remaining_unmatched = U − P − M`**, a set difference over exact identity tuples, never over event names, principals or time ranges. All three sets are confined to one intent, one organization and one interval. *U* is the run's rows. *P* and *M* join raw rows only through composite keys with intent and organization, so no identity from another tenant, intent or interval can enter or be removed. The projection exists only inside the execution transaction. It is stored only as the projection record of a committed execution (CRX-7L-08), and a failed execution leaves no trace of it. |
| CRX-7L-07 [§35.4h; IRE-7L-06] | **What must pass.** (a) `remaining_unmatched` is empty. Any remaining event refuses the execution: an invalid proposal, a non-matching class, or an event no proposal covers. Creation previewed the same computation on the referenced run, and CRX-7L-02 makes the confirmation's effective set equal to it. So a non-empty remaining set at execution means the evidence changed: `STALE` (`EVIDENCE_CHANGED`). (b) Every IEV-08 condition of §35.4h is read on the projection. These are: table A's `CONTINUOUS_NO_UNMATCHED` (`MARKER_REPLICATION_UNPROVABLE` (m2), `AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE`); table A's "every … matched" (`MARKER_REPLICATION_UNPROVABLE`, `BATCH_PROOF_INCOMPLETE`, `STORAGE_AUTHORITY_UNNARROWABLE`); the IEV-08 confirmations and watermarks of table B (`MARKER_REPLICATION_UNPROVABLE`, `UNEXPLAINED_REAPPEARANCE`, `HOLD_PRESERVATION_BREACH`, `BATCH_PROOF_INCOMPLETE`, `AUTHZ_CHANGED`, `AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE`, `STORAGE_AUTHORITY_UNNARROWABLE`, `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`, `MARKER_UNEXPLAINED`); and the data-access conditions inside IRE-7L-06. Each holds only if the confirmation is not `GAP` and the remaining set, restricted to the condition's interval and event kind, is empty. (c) Every other confirmation (IEV-01 … -07, -16) and every database condition of each profile holds. (d) The projection never stands in for continuity. A `GAP` is never reconciled: the execution is refused, and the incident stays open under `AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE`. An event classed `READ_EXPOSURE`, `UNLOCATED` or `CHANGE_UNRESOLVED` always stays in the remaining set. An unknown copy, or a copy in an unregistered destination, stays there unless `WRITE_CONTAINED` validated the product's registration and admission. |
| CRX-7L-08 [IEV-09; IRC-7L-05] | **Committed reconciliation.** In the commit phase, the execution inserts one IRR row for each valid proposal of a matching class. The row holds: IRR identifier; organization; intent; request; proposal; class; the covered identities; the confirmation run and its raw-row identifiers; the evidence records that V4 used; and the closure it belongs to. The IRR's covered identities have the unique key `(intent_id, event identity)`, so one event has at most one committed attribution per intent; a second insert fails and rolls back the execution. The execution also inserts the **projection record**: *U*, *P* by proposal, *M*, the empty remaining set, the confirmation run and the clock read. Invalid or non-matching proposals stay on the request as recorded proposals, and nothing treats them as reconciled. No other function inserts IRRs or projection records. No login role holds a privilege on them, and triggers forbid update, delete and truncate (RQL-7L-14). |
| CRX-7L-09 [F (f6); E-17; E-18; ACF-7L-05, -06; TSA-7L-10] | **Post-commit monitor reconciliation.** After the commit, the next monitor run computes its raw rows exactly as before. An event reconciled by an IRR still matches no change record and no G-17 function, so it is still a raw row; the run lists it in `matched_by_irr`, with the IRR's identifier. If nothing else is unmatched, its class is `CONTINUOUS_RECONCILED`. Earlier runs keep their `UNMATCHED` class, raw rows, watermark and provenance unchanged, including the referenced run and the confirmation. **No run ever reports `CONTINUOUS_NO_UNMATCHED` over an interval that contains a raw unmatched event.** F (f6), ACF-7L-05 and -06, TSA-7L-10, E-17 and E-18 read the effective set of the latest run, and they list the IRRs that it used. |
| CRX-7L-10 [RR-7L-R6 (ii)] | **Events that arrive late.** An event delivered after the confirmation's watermark is not in *U*. If the finding it produces commits before the execution takes the intent lock, *F* changes and the request is `STALE` (RQL-7L-06). If it arrives after the commit, the next run reports it as raw and effective. The monitor opens its reason, a new occurrence (IRC-7L-03), through the opening routine (PCI-7L-01), for whatever state the intent has reached by then: one edge into `INCIDENT` from `QUIESCING`, `DELETING`, `VERIFYING` or `BLOCKED_HOLD`; none in `INCIDENT`; and, if the intent has reached `VERIFIED_ABSENT`, `VERIFIED_ABSENT → REOPENED → INCIDENT` in one transaction, with the verification recorded as falsified (PCI-7L-02, -05, -06; revised for FG-7L-R9-01). The committed IRRs are unaffected. Meanwhile the resolution authorized no deletion: `QUIESCING` has no issue action, and every later issue needs F (f6), with a watermark within `T_ct` (ICM-7L-04). This is the delivery lag that RR-7L-R6 (ii) states; it is not closed here. |
| CRX-7L-11 [ICR-7L-07; ICM-7L-09] | **No other path.** No person, role or function can insert an IRR or a projection record, mark an event matched, close an occurrence, edit or delete a raw row or a monitor run, or set `VERIFIED_ABSENT`, except as stated here. IRRs and closures are written only by the commit phase of RQL-7L-10, raw rows only by the monitor's insert, and `VERIFIED_ABSENT` only from `VERIFYING` with E-1 … E-18. The CloudTrail logs themselves are protected by the log archive (M-4) and by digest validation (M-5). A run that cannot validate them is `GAP`. |
| CRX-7L-12 | **Determinism.** An execution's result is a function of: the immutable request (proposals and references); the immutable decisions; the immutable confirmation runs and evidence records; the committed IRRs of the intent; and the rows locked by RQL-7L-09. Validation (phase 1, then phase 2) and the set difference do not depend on order. The only time-dependent steps are the clock read of RQL-7L-08 and the `T_fresh` and `T_ct` comparisons made against it. |

**Before and after, two examples.**

| Step | Example A: a reverted bucket-policy change, no use | Example B: a successful read by an unattributed principal |
|---|---|---|
| Raw evidence (L1) | Run *R0*: raw rows *e1* (`PutBucketPolicy`) and *e2* (its reversal); class `UNMATCHED`; occurrence `AUTHZ_CHANGED` open | Run *R0*: raw row *e3* (`GetObject` on the key by a principal outside *P(b)*); `UNMATCHED`; occurrence `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` open |
| Proposal (L2) | One `CHANGE_REVERTED_UNUSED` proposal covering *e1* and *e2* | `READ_EXPOSURE` recorded for *e3*. It is not a matching class |
| Preview at creation | V1 – V6 pass; phase 2 window: no data event on the key and no `CreateJob` in *R1*; *U* = {*e1*, *e2*}, *P* = {*e1*, *e2*}, *M* = ∅, remaining = ∅. Request created | remaining = {*e3*}. Creation refused (`EVIDENCE_PROFILE_UNSATISFIABLE`); no request; a `FAILURE` audit row |
| Execution (L3) | Confirmation *R1c*: same effective set {*e1*, *e2*}. Projection repeated; remaining = ∅; every other confirmation holds | — |
| Commit (L4) | One IRR covering *e1* and *e2*, the projection record, the closure; request `EXECUTED`; intent `QUIESCING`; `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_RESOLVED` | No IRR. The intent stays `INCIDENT`, Class 2, no deletion; RR-7L-R7 |
| Later monitor (L5) | *R2*: raw rows {*e1*, *e2*}, `matched_by_irr` = {*e1*, *e2*}, class `CONTINUOUS_RECONCILED`. *R0* and *R1c* stay `UNMATCHED`, byte-for-byte | Every run keeps *e3* in its effective set. No `VERIFIED_ABSENT` is possible for this intent |

#### 35.4k Opening an incident after completion (FG-7L-R9-01)

**Root cause, verified against the text of round 8.** IRC-7L-01 told the function that detects a cause to lock the intent and "move the intent to `INCIDENT` if it is not there". That instruction named no source state. §35.5 lists `VERIFIED_ABSENT → REOPENED` and `REOPENED → QUIESCING | INCIDENT` and says "No other transition exists", so `VERIFIED_ABSENT → INCIDENT` is forbidden. Three detectors run after `VERIFIED_ABSENT`: the sentinel (RDQ-7L-27), the audit reconciliation (BQA-7L-09; TSA-7L-10) and the continuity monitor's post-commit runs (CRX-7L-09). CRX-7L-10 described a late event only as a return to `INCIDENT` "from `QUIESCING`". BQA-7L-09 said that a write after `VERIFIED_ABSENT` "means `REOPENED`", but not whether its reason opens, while IRC-7L-04 allows an open occurrence only in `INCIDENT`. No rule said how the two edges, the opening and the record of the falsified verification commit together. An implementation had three choices, and each was wrong: write the forbidden edge; refuse the opening and leave the verification unchallenged while its contradiction is known; or commit `REOPENED` and the opening separately, which leaves a committed `REOPENED` with an open occurrence, or, after a crash between them, a committed finding with no reason. The same gap existed before `FENCED` (FND-7L-14, §35.1). The correction adds no edge. It defines one opening routine, a post-completion procedure that uses the two existing edges in a fixed order inside one transaction, the records that keep the earlier verification, and the classification of late evidence.

**The opening routine: what it does in each state (PCI-7L-01).** "Opening" is the insert of an occurrence under IRC-7L-01 … -04. The state is the one the routine reads after it holds the intent lock.

| State read under the lock | Opening | Transitions, in this order, in the detecting transaction | Audit rows, in the same transaction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PENDING` | Only by the step that enters `FENCED`, for a cause that its own checks find (RDQ-7L-02, -04; FND-7L-14) | `PENDING → FENCED`, with that step's lock records and closure record; then the opening; then `FENCED → INCIDENT`. Any other caller is refused with an integrity alarm and rolls back | The step's own row; `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_OPENED` |
| `FENCED`, `QUIESCING`, `DELETING`, `VERIFYING`, `BLOCKED_HOLD` | Inserted | The opening; then the existing edge into `INCIDENT` | `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_OPENED` |
| `INCIDENT` | Inserted, or not inserted under IRC-7L-02 (an occurrence of the same subject is open; a finding only if it adds evidence) | None | `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_OPENED` for an insert |
| `REOPENED` | Inserted | The opening; then `REOPENED → INCIDENT` | `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_OPENED` |
| `VERIFIED_ABSENT` | Inserted, only through PCI-7L-02 | `VERIFIED_ABSENT → REOPENED`; then the opening; then `REOPENED → INCIDENT`. Never one edge | `RECORDING_CLEANUP_VERIFICATION_REOPENED`, then `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_OPENED` |

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| PCI-7L-01 [IRC-7L-01; §35.5] | **One opening routine, dispatched on the locked state.** Every detecting function opens a reason only by calling one internal routine inside its own transaction, after it holds the intent row `FOR UPDATE` (RQL-7L-09 (3)). The routine reads the intent's state after the lock and applies the row of the table above for that state. It never uses a state read before the lock, and it takes no expected state from its caller. So a detector that computed its evidence while the intent was `VERIFIED_ABSENT`, and gets the lock after another detector has reopened it, applies the `INCIDENT` row. The routine is `SECURITY DEFINER`, has no grant, and is called only by the detecting functions (RQL-7L-14). It writes no IRR, no closure and no deletion operation. Every rule of §35 that says a cause "is `INCIDENT`", "goes to `INCIDENT`" or "opens" a reason means: opens it through this routine. |
| PCI-7L-02 [§35.5; IRC-7L-01, -04; RDQ-7L-27; BQA-7L-09; TSA-7L-10; CRX-7L-10] | **The post-completion opening, in this exact order, in one transaction.** It applies when the routine finds `VERIFIED_ABSENT` and the evidence names at least one actionable reason (table below). (1) Lock the intent row `FOR UPDATE`; read the clock after the lock (`clock_timestamp()`, as RQL-7L-08). (2) Validate: the caller is the producing principal of its evidence kind (`session_user`; IRE-7L-03); every evidence row belongs to this intent and organization through its composite key (RQL-7L-13), and the organization is taken from the intent (PRV-18); a monitor run passes the sequence check of PCI-7L-07; and each event identity or entry is new, that is, not matched in the verification's own run, not covered by a committed IRR of this intent (*M* of CRX-7L-06), and not the subject of an open occurrence. If nothing new remains, the transaction writes only the run (row L7 below) and changes no state. (3) Insert the evidence: the monitor run and its raw rows, the sentinel result, or the inspection record. (4) Insert the finding. (5) Insert the challenge record (PCI-7L-05). It names the verification it concerns, each affected E-item as `FALSIFIED` or `CHALLENGED`, the absence effect (PCI-7L-06) and the evidence of (3). (6) `VERIFIED_ABSENT → REOPENED`, with its provenance row (7I STP-11 pattern) and `RECORDING_CLEANUP_VERIFICATION_REOPENED`, naming the challenge. (7) Insert one opening per reason (IRC-7L-01), with `opened_in_state` = `REOPENED` and the challenge among its raising evidence, and write the privacy-incident record that RDQ-7L-27 requires. (8) `REOPENED → INCIDENT`, with its provenance row and `RECORDING_CLEANUP_INCIDENT_OPENED`, naming each opening. (9) The fingerprint routine of RQL-7L-06. (10) Advance the detector's progress marker for this evidence (PCI-7L-07). (11) Commit. Steps 3 – 10 commit together or not at all. Each audit row is written through `audit.fn_insert_audit_event` inside the transaction (7I AUD-7I-01). The original verification record, its E-1 … E-18 and its monitor runs stay unchanged. |
| PCI-7L-03 [RDQ-7L-27; ACF-7L-05 (d); §35.5] | **A reopening with no reason yet.** Two kinds of evidence challenge a verification without naming a reason: an S3 Inventory entry for the key that no exact-key listing has confirmed (RDQ-7L-27), and a `GAP` run over part of *I* (ACF-7L-05 (d)). For them the transaction makes steps 1 – 6, 9 and 10 of PCI-7L-02 and commits `REOPENED` with no open occurrence. In `REOPENED` the executor re-fences (PCI-7L-10) and inspects: exact-key listings of every closure bucket (OC-7L-01) through inspection sessions (TSA-7L-02), and further monitor runs. The outcome is decided by evidence only. (a) A reason is found, for example OC-7L-09's write after the commit, or `AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE` when the gap persists past `T_q,max` from the first `GAP` run, as ACF-7L-05 (d) applies it in `VERIFYING`.
