### 35.9 Regression T-7L-07 — recording deletion with replication (replaces §34.7 T-7L-07)

Specified; **not executed**. Owners: Voice; Storage; Platform. Gates: AG-7L-09; CON-08; AG-7L-06 for LS-D-VOX. Each case asserts the intent's state, the three conditions of RDQ-7L-01 and the recorded evidence. Cases (a), (b), (e), (g) and (j) need a stalled or controllable replication. On AWS S3 that cannot be induced on demand, so they run against a **synthetic adapter** that implements S-1 … S-13 as documented, including a controllable `PENDING` that later completes. **Their results are test-only evidence about the protocol, not provider evidence.** The other cases also run against the real provider under PV-R1.

| Case | Setup and action | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| (a) **Mandatory counterexample** | (1) Upload v1 to the primary bucket with one destination. (2) Stall v1's replication: status `PENDING`. (3) Commit the deletion intent. (4) The executor attempts to delete every observable copy. (5) The destination's listing is empty. (6) Resume the stalled replication. (7) Observe the destination. (8) Check the intent | At (4) the executor deletes **nothing**: v1 is `PENDING`, so the intent stays `QUIESCING` (RDQ-7L-11). At (6) v1 appears as `REPLICA` in the destination and the source turns `COMPLETED`. Only then does the intent reach `DELETING`, delete v1 in both buckets by version ID, and pass `VERIFYING`. **At no point before E-1 … E-18 is the intent `VERIFIED_ABSENT`.** Logically denied throughout |
| (a′) Adversarial variant (synthetic only) | As (a), but the source v1 is deleted by a test-only fault injection while `PENDING`, bypassing the executor; then replication resumes | The executor cannot read v1's status any more and finds the inventory contradicting the recorded one. The intent goes to `INCIDENT` (`QUIESCENCE_UNPROVABLE`). `QUIESCENCE_UNPROVABLE` is Class 2: nothing is deleted while the intent is `INCIDENT`. If the synthetic provider then creates v1 in the destination, it stays until a resolution (ICR-7L-05) returns the intent to `QUIESCING`, which inventories and deletes it; the intent never reaches `VERIFIED_ABSENT` from `INCIDENT` |
| (b) | A replica appears in a destination after a deletion pass (synthetic: delayed replica write) | `VERIFYING` finds it; back to `QUIESCING`; new inventory; deleted; after the third time, `INCIDENT` (`UNEXPLAINED_REAPPEARANCE`) |
| (c) | Status `PENDING` beyond `T_q,max` | `INCIDENT` (`QUIESCENCE_UNPROVABLE`); escalated; nothing deleted; deadline unchanged; past the deadline, `DEADLINE_MISSED` and an unauthorized-retention report |
| (d) | Status `FAILED` (real provider: replication role permission withdrawn, which AWS documents as producing `FAILED`) | Quiescent only with the batch fence held; deletion proceeds in every closure bucket; E-8 recorded |
| (e) | A replication rule is changed between `QUIESCING` and `VERIFYING` | Through the governed path: refused, because the configuration lock is held. Out of band (synthetic, or a test-only policy exception): snapshot 2 differs, so the intent goes to `INCIDENT` (`CONFIG_UNRECORDED`) |
| (f) | A destination bucket was added after the recording was stored, and a Batch Replication copied the key there | The closure includes it from G-17; its versions are inventoried and deleted; absence verified there too |
| (g) | A Batch Replication job is scheduled covering the prefix | Governed path: refused while the intent holds the lock. A job found by `ListJobs` / `DescribeJob`: the intent waits in `QUIESCING`; a job whose scope cannot be determined counts as covering |
| (h) | A source version is deleted before its replication completes (by the executor) | Impossible by RDQ-7L-11; a build that allowed it fails this test |
| (i) | A replica under Object Lock retention | `INCIDENT` (`OBJECT_LOCKED`, Class 1); the other versions are deleted only by containment issues under ICM-7L-03 and F; never closed |
| (j) | Executor crash after the deletes and before the final verification; and crash between a delete and its record | Restart in `DELETING` / `VERIFYING`; re-list; no duplicate harm; `VERIFIED_ABSENT` only after the full verification |
| (k) | An intent already `VERIFIED_ABSENT`; the key appears in a later inventory report | `REOPENED`; privacy incident; protocol re-run; the earlier verification recorded as falsified |
| (l) | Adapter without version listing, replication status or job listing | Not admitted (RAD-7L-08); no recording stored through it; an intent created against it by fault goes to `INCIDENT` (`ADAPTER_INCAPABLE`) |
| (m) | Plain delete only (unversioned) | Never issued by the executor; a test-only plain delete leaves versions; listings show them; no completion |
| (n) | `recording.deleted` delivered while replication is `PENDING` for hours | CON-08 acknowledges once the intent exists (RDQ-7L-30); LS-D-VOX is not pinned; the intent continues independently |
| (o) | ACC-08 accounting for CON-08 | Satisfied by row `DELETED` plus an existing intent; a missing intent is ACC-05 |
| (p) | Legal hold and deletion interleavings | **Replaced by T-7L-09.** The batch authorization it tested is withdrawn (RDQ-7L-13) |
| (q) | Key outside the organization's prefix | `INCIDENT` (`KEY_OUT_OF_PREFIX`); nothing deleted |
| (r) | Class E stack whose closure contains an out-of-region bucket | `INCIDENT` (`RESIDENCY_VIOLATION`, Class 1); deletion there continues only as containment issues under ICM-7L-03 and F; never `VERIFIED_ABSENT` from `INCIDENT`; see T-7L-15 (c) |
| (s) | URL issued 1 minute before the intent; download started at minute 14 | No new URL after the intent; the old URL's GET after its version's deletion fails; `VERIFIED_ABSENT` not before the horizon (minute 16); the in-flight transfer is the stated residual |
| (t) | CDN caching recordings without completed invalidation | Not admitted; or, if invalidation is used, `VERIFIED_ABSENT` waits for its recorded completion |
| (u) | Database restored to a point before the intent | Quarantine; journal reconciliation re-creates the intent; the recording stays `DELETED`; nothing served |
| (v) | Lifecycle transition of a `COMPLETED` version to an archive class during `QUIESCING` | Inventoried with its class; deleted by version ID; verified absent |

**T-7L-09 — legal hold versus external deletion (FG-7L-R4-01; owners Voice, Privacy; gates AG-7L-09; requires AP-7L-53 for the frozen wording).** Specified; **not executed**. Database interleavings are made deterministic with two sessions and the gate's own lock waits. Each fixture states who holds the gate when the other asks. Provider timing (delay, drop, loss of a response) uses the synthetic adapter, **labelled test-only**. Real-provider refusals are PV-R2. **Universal oracle O-H (revised for FG-7L-R5-02).** For every hold *H*, and every entry *v* of either class that *H* covers at its commit: at every observation after *H*'s commit, *v* is present in its closure bucket, unless *v*'s issue record precedes *H* in journal order. In that case: the request was *admitted* no later than `not_after + T_skew` (by the data event's `eventTime`, PV-R3 (e)); *when it took effect* is not asserted; and either `DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD` (or `_COVERAGE`) exists for (*v*, *H*), marked late effect where it disappeared after *H*, or, while the operation has no terminality evidence, `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED` exists and *v* is never reported as preserved. An entry recorded `SKIPPED_HELD` whose operations are all T-0, T-1 (b) or T-3 must be present at every later observation. The order evidence is the journal and the gate's commit order. Test-recorded timings are synthetic.

| Case | Interleaving | Authoritative state | Permitted deletion | Privacy acceptance oracle |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Hold before authorization | *H* commits. Then the issue transaction runs | Registry: *H* applies; verdict held | None | No operation; `SKIPPED_HELD`; `BLOCKED_HOLD`; no claim; no data event; *v* present |
| (b1) Hold placement waits on an issue | Session 1 holds the share gate (paused after step 4). Session 2 asks for the exclusive gate and waits. Session 1 commits; session 2 commits | Operation `ISSUED` before *H* | *v* only | `DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD` (*v*, *H*); every other version issued afterwards is `SKIPPED_HELD`; O-H |
| (b2) Issue waits on a placement | Session 2 holds the exclusive gate. Session 1 waits for share; session 2 commits; session 1 reads | Verdict held | None | As (a); the verdict lists *H* |
| (c) Hold immediately after authorization | Issue commits; *H* commits before the broker claim | Operation `ISSUED` before *H* | *v*, within *W* | The deletion data event is no later than `not_after + T_skew`; `DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD`; the next version is held; O-H |
| (d) Hold after authorization, before the S3 request | Claim; the worker pauses; *H* commits; the worker resumes. (d1) before `not_after`; (d2) after it | (d1) issued before *H*; (d2) the provider refuses | (d1) *v*; (d2) none | (d1) as (c). (d2) `REFUSED` → `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED` → held (`SKIPPED_HELD`); *v* present at every later observation |
| (e) Hold during an in-flight deletion | The synthetic adapter delays its response; *H* commits while the request is open | Issued before *H* | *v* | Nothing resolved before `not_after + T_skew`, and nothing by elapsed time. While no evidence exists: `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED`. Then: (e1) a `204` and a listing without *v* → `DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD`; (e2) the synthetic adapter applies the deletion one hour after *H*, response lost → T-2 with `THIS_OPERATION` → `DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD`, marked late effect; (e3) the adapter never applies it and never answers → `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN` for as long as the test runs, *v* never reported as preserved |
| (f) Authorization expires before the request | The worker sends after `not_after` | Provider refusal (`aws:CurrentTime`) | None | `REFUSED`; *v* present; a new attempt needs a new issue, which sees any hold |
| (g) Ambiguous provider result | The connection drops after send: (g1) the synthetic provider executed; (g2) it did not | `AMBIGUOUS` | (g1) *v*; (g2) none | No resolution before `not_after + T_skew`. (g1) The listing lacks *v*: T-2 → `RESOLVED_DELETED`; with a hold present, `DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD`. (g2) The listing shows *v*: `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN`, **not** `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED`; with a hold present, `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED`, **not** `SKIPPED_HELD`. Only a refusal data event (T-3, after PV-R3 (e)) turns (g2) into `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED` and then `SKIPPED_HELD`. Without a hold, a successor is issued (OPT-7L-07). A build that maps (g2) to `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED` on a listing fails |
| (h) Worker crash before deletion | Crash after the claim, before `SEND_STARTED`; restart | Operation `CLAIMED`, open | None | A second claim is refused; no send after `not_after`; `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT` (T-0 (ii)); new issue under the gate. Variant (h′): crash after `SEND_STARTED` → as (g) |
| (i) Worker crash after provider success | Delete succeeds; crash before the record; *H* commits during the outage | Issued before *H* | *v* | `RESOLVED_DELETED` by listing; `DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD`; no second delete; O-H |
| (j) Hold release and retry | `BLOCKED_HOLD`; release under the exclusive gate | Registry: *H* released; no other hold | Remaining versions, through new issues | `QUIESCING` with a new inventory; every new deletion has its own issue after the release in journal order; the earlier `SKIPPED_HELD` records are kept |
| (k) Concurrent deletion workers | Two workers on one intent and one version | Intent row `FOR UPDATE`; partial unique index | One operation only | Exactly one open operation and one claim per version; at most one deletion data event per operation |
| (l) Newly attributed subject | *H* (phone P) exists and does not reach the recording. (l1) An edge linking the recording to P commits before the issue. (l2) The issue holds the head share lock; the edge writer waits | (l1) verdict held. (l2) issued before coverage | (l1) none. (l2) *v* | (l1) as (a). (l2) `DELETED_BEFORE_COVERAGE` with the edge's provenance; later versions held |
| (m) Index or key unavailable | A relation is `UNVERIFIED` (HLD-19 b) | No usable verdict | None | No issue; a decision record with `INDEX_UNVERIFIED`; *v* present |
| (n) Journal unavailable | The append fails inside the issue transaction | Rolled back | None | No operation; no claim possible; *v* present |
| (o) A held version disappears | A test-only out-of-band delete of a held version, with no operation | Registry: *H* applies | None permitted | Preservation check: `HOLD_PRESERVATION_BREACH`; reconciliation: `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`; never closed by time |

**T-7L-10 — account-complete batch quiescence (FG-7L-R4-02; owners Storage, Platform; gate AG-7L-09).** Specified; **not executed**. Each case asserts *J*, *R(a)*, the pass result and E-8, E-16, E-17. Cases needing a fence breach are synthetic and labelled test-only. Cases (b) – (f), (j) and (n) also run on the real provider under PV-R2.

| Case | Setup | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Two buckets in one account | Primary and destination in account A | *J* = {A}; one enumeration per Region of *R(A)* covers both; a covering job on the destination keeps `QUIESCING` |
| (b) Primary and destination in separate accounts | Primary in A, destination in D | *J* = {A, D}; both enumerated; E-16 lists both |
| (c) Batch job in the source account | Copy job in A over the prefix | Found in A; `QUIESCING` until terminal |
| (d) Batch job in the destination account | Copy or replication job created in D over D's bucket | Found **only** by D's enumeration. An implementation that enumerates A alone fails this case |
| (e) Job created after the first inventory | After pass 1: (e1) the governed principal attempts it; (e2) another principal of a member account; (e3) a synthetic fence breach | (e1) refused by the per-bucket lock; (e2) refused by the SCP (`CreateJob` denied); (e3) found at pass 2 → `INCIDENT` (`BATCH_PROOF_INCOMPLETE`) |
| (f) `ListJobs` returns several pages | More jobs than `maxResults` (synthetic 2,500; real: `maxResults` 1); covering job on the last page | Every `NextToken` followed; the covering job found; page count and request identifiers recorded |
| (g) Missing `NextToken` page | Page 2 fails (`InvalidNextTokenException`, 5xx or a dropped page) | Enumeration incomplete; restarted from page 1; partial pages never merged; persistent failure past `T_q,max` → `INCIDENT` |
| (h) `DescribeJob` access denied | Job listed, description refused | Scope unknown → covering → `QUIESCING`; past `T_q,max` → `INCIDENT` (`QUIESCENCE_UNPROVABLE`) |
| (i) Manifest scope unknown | Manifest outside the governed manifest bucket, or under a key the verifier cannot use | Covering |
| (j) Copy job through a different principal | (j1) Created in a member account by a non-governed principal; (j2) created in an account outside the organization with a role outside *P(b)* | (j1) SCP refusal; (j2) the job's tasks are refused by the bucket policy; no version is created; the closure listings are unchanged; CloudTrail shows `AccessDenied` |
| (k) Account or bucket removed from the configuration | A former destination account has effective-to set; the recording predates it | The account stays in *J*; it is still enumerated; if its discovery role is gone → `INCIDENT` (`BATCH_PROOF_INCOMPLETE`) |
| (l) Incomplete cross-account permissions | D's discovery role works in one Region of *R(D)* and is refused in another | Incomplete → `INCIDENT`; never `VERIFIED_ABSENT` |
| (m) A delayed copy after an empty listing | Synthetic: a copy into a closure bucket appears after the final listing | Detected by the sentinel (→ `REOPENED`, then the listing decides; §35.4k PCI-7L-03) or by the reconciliation of the write data event (→ `VERIFIED_ABSENT → REOPENED → INCIDENT` in one transaction; PCI-7L-02); the earlier verification recorded as challenged or falsified by an immutable challenge record (PCI-7L-05) |
| (n) The authorization surface changes between passes | Account D moved to an organizational unit without the SCP; or a role's trust widened. (n′) The same change, **reverted** before pass 2 | (n) Digest differs, and the change event is unmatched → `INCIDENT` (`AUTHZ_CHANGED`). (n′) Digests equal; the unmatched change events still give `AUTHZ_CHANGED` (ACF-7L-05). An implementation that relies on the digests alone fails (n′); see T-7L-14 |
| (o) Management account | A closure bucket owned by the management account | Not admitted (RAD-7L-10) |

**T-7L-11 — tenant-scoped storage authority (FG-7L-R4-03; owners Storage, Security, Voice; gate AG-7L-09).** Specified; **not executed**. Every refusal is observed **at the provider**: the test calls S3 directly with the credential, bypassing the executor and the broker's own checks. The oracle is the provider's `AccessDenied`, with the CloudTrail event, and an unchanged exact-key listing. Cases (b) – (k) run on the real provider under PV-R2.

| Case | Action | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Valid deletion in tenant A | A deletion operation for A's version; broker session; delete | Allowed; data event with `SourceIdentity` = the operation; reconciled |
| (b) Tenant A's session on tenant B's key | Same session, B's key and version | Refused by the role policy (resource mismatch) and by the bucket policy (explicit deny); B's listing unchanged |
| (c) Forged organization identifier | (c1) An envelope or a caller supplies B's organization for A's recording; (c2) a non-broker principal calls `AssumeRole` with tag B; (c3) the tag value is `*`, contains `?` or `/` | (c1) The binding comes from the intent; nothing of B is reachable. (c2) Refused by the trust policy. (c3) Refused at `TagSession` |
| (d) Cross-account destination, wrong tenant scope | A session for D's bucket tagged A, used on B's key in D | Refused in D |
| (e) Credential theft without code execution | A stolen deletion session used on another version, another key, or after `not_after`; a stolen broker credential used off its boundary | All refused; off-boundary `AssumeRole` refused [VERIFY] |
| (f) `PutObject` or `CopyObject` | With a deletion session and with an inspection session | Refused (explicit deny); no version created |
| (g) Replication-configuration change | `PutReplicationConfiguration` with any cleanup session or the closure verifier | Refused |
| (h) Expired session | After `not_after`; after STS expiry | Refused by `aws:CurrentTime`; `ExpiredToken` |
| (i) Missing tenant-specific authorization | A test-only role variant without the trust condition, assumed without the tag | The empty variable matches no resource; the bucket `NotResource` deny applies; refused |
| (j) Unversioned delete | `DeleteObject` without a version ID, with a deletion session | Refused; no delete marker created |
| (k) Verifier reads content | Closure verifier calls `GetObjectVersion` on a recording | Refused |

**T-7L-12 — delete markers and object classes (FG-7L-R5-01; owners Voice, Storage; gate AG-7L-09).** Specified; **not executed**. Each case asserts the class of every entry, E-5, E-6, E-10 and E-12, the deletion order (OC-7L-06) and the intent's state. On an admitted stack no principal can create a marker on the prefix (TSA-7L-04, -06), so markers are made in a **test account** with the deny relaxed, or by the synthetic adapter, each **labelled test-only**. Cases (a) – (e), (h), (j) and (l) also run on the real provider under PV-R3. The expected responses are the documented ones (S-25 … S-31).

| Case | Setup and action | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| (a) One data-bearing version, no marker | Key with v1 only | Listing: one `Version`; `HeadObject` `200` with its status; delete `204` without `x-amz-delete-marker`; final listing empty |
| (b) One version and one marker | v1, then an unversioned delete in the test account: marker m1, `IsLatest` true; v1 `IsLatest` false | Two entries, V and M. `HeadObject` on v1 `200`; none required on m1. v1 deleted first, then m1 (`204` with `x-amz-delete-marker: true`). Between them the key still reads as deleted by key. Variant (b1): the test configures a G-17 lifecycle rule that explains m1 (`LIFECYCLE`), and the deletions above follow. Variant (b2): m1 is `UNEXPLAINED` → `INCIDENT` (`MARKER_UNEXPLAINED`, Class 2) at inventory, **before** any issue: nothing is deleted until a resolution; see T-7L-15 (a) |
| (c) Several versions and several markers | v1, m1, v2, m2, v3 (test account); `max-keys` 1 | Every page followed to `IsTruncated` false; five entries classified; five issue records; all V before any M; final listing empty. A build that stops at the first page fails |
| (d) `HeadObject` `405` for an explicit marker | Diagnostic HEAD on m1's version ID. (d′) Synthetic: `405` **without** `x-amz-delete-marker`. (d″) Synthetic: `405` for an entry listed as `Version` | (d) `405` with `x-amz-delete-marker: true` and `Last-Modified`: consistent with the listing; no metadata is required. (d′) Not marker evidence; re-listed; the listing decides. (d″) Re-listed; still a `Version` → `INCIDENT` (`CLASS_CONTRADICTION`) |
| (e) A marker on an otherwise empty key | Only m1 exists (its version deleted earlier in the test account) | Q_V vacuously true; m1 quiescent under (m1), (m2); deleted by version ID; final listing empty |
| (f) An eligible replicated marker, if the policy supports it | The admitted configuration does not support it (RAD-7L-04). (f1) Admission check against a rule with `DeleteMarkerReplication` `Enabled`, or a V1 rule. (f2) Test account with such a rule: marker in the source, replicated asynchronously | (f1) **NOT ADMITTED**. (f2) No status exists for the marker (S-28): Q(m1) not provable → `INCIDENT` (`MARKER_REPLICATION_UNPROVABLE`); class V entries are deleted only by containment issues (Class 1; Q_V holds; ICM-7L-03); no marker deletion is issued; never `VERIFIED_ABSENT` |
| (g) A marker from a disallowed unversioned delete | (g1) Real provider: unversioned `DeleteObject` by a cleanup session and by another principal. (g2) Test account, deny relaxed | (g1) `403`; no marker; listing unchanged. (g2) A marker with a new version ID; `MARKER_UNEXPLAINED`; and the relaxation is a bucket-policy change event → `AUTHZ_CHANGED` (T-7L-14) |
| (h) A marker in a destination bucket | m1 exists only in destination D (test account) | Classified in D; deleted with D's deletion role (TSA-7L-07); the version-specific deletion is not replicated back (S-4); final listings of both buckets empty |
| (i) A marker appears during verification | Synthetic: after every delete, a marker with `LastModified` after the commit appears; no class V entry is current | Back to `QUIESCING`; new inventory; `INCIDENT` (`UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`, Class 2); nothing is deleted while `INCIDENT`; after a resolution, `QUIESCING` inventories and deletes the marker; no `VERIFIED_ABSENT` from `INCIDENT` |
| (j) Provider denial while deleting a specific marker | A session bound to marker m1, used on marker m2 (PV-R2, S-22); and a synthetic transient `403` on m1 | Cross-use refused; m2 listed. For m1: `REFUSED` → `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED` (T-1 (b)) → a new issue under the gate; persistent past `T_q,max` → `INCIDENT` (`DELETE_REFUSED`) |
| (k) A legal hold while versions or markers remain | *H* commits after v1 is deleted and before m1 is issued | m1's issue finds the hold: `SKIPPED_HELD`; `BLOCKED_HOLD`; the preservation check confirms m1 present; on release, a new inventory and a new issue |
| (l) Crash after a marker's deletion, before its outcome is recorded | m1's delete succeeds; the worker crashes before the response is stored; restart | The attempt is `AMBIGUOUS`; the listing lacks m1 → T-2 → `RESOLVED_DELETED`, attribution `THIS_OPERATION` from the data event; no second delete; with a hold committed meanwhile, `DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD` |

**T-7L-13 — ambiguous provider outcomes and terminality (FG-7L-R5-02; owners Voice, Storage, Privacy; gate AG-7L-09).** Specified; **not executed**. One case per fault sequence of §35.4e. Timing, lost responses and late effects use the synthetic adapter, **labelled test-only**; its late effects can be scheduled hours after the deadline. Refusals and the data-event record of a refusal run on the real provider under PV-R3 (e). The universal oracle: **no operation is ever `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED` without T-1 (b) or T-3 evidence; no entry is `SKIPPED_HELD` while any of its operations lacks terminality evidence; no state changes by elapsed time.**

| Case | Sequence (§35.4e) | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| (a) | 1, rejected before admission: (a1) claim after `not_after`; (a2) `403` from the session policy | (a1) Claim refused → `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT`. (a2) `REFUSED` → `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED`; the version listed; a new issue under the gate |
| (b) | 2, definitive success | `204`; listing without the version → `RESOLVED_DELETED`, `THIS_OPERATION`. Variant (b′), synthetic: `204` but the version still listed → `PROVIDER_CONTRADICTION` |
| (c) | 3, timeout before reaching AWS | Synthetic TCP-connect failure: `NOT_DELIVERED`; one more attempt allowed before `not_after`; none made → `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT`. Variant (c′): a read timeout *after* the connection → `AMBIGUOUS`, not `NOT_DELIVERED` |
| (d) | 4, reaches AWS, response lost | (d1) Synthetic provider applied it: T-2 → `RESOLVED_DELETED`. (d2) It refused it: no response, version listed → `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN`; after PV-R3 (e), the refusal event → `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED` (T-3). (d3) It holds the request: `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN`; a successor is issued and deletes; both operations `RESOLVED_DELETED`, attributions `OTHER_OPERATION` and `THIS_OPERATION` |
| (e) | 5, accepted, then a hold commits | (e1) `204` before *H*'s resolution transaction → `DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD`. (e2) No evidence → `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED`, audit row written, Privacy notified; then the synthetic late effect → `DELETED_BEFORE_HOLD`, late effect. (e3) Refusal event → `SKIPPED_HELD`, present at every later observation |
| (f) | 6, ambiguous, the version keeps being listed | 1,000 listings over 48 synthetic hours: `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN` throughout; alert after `T_unp,warn`; a successor without a hold; with a hold, re-reported at each `T_pres`; past `T_q,max` without a deletable successor, `OPERATION_UNRESOLVED` |
| (g) | 7, ambiguous, the version disappears later | (g1) Data event under this operation → `RESOLVED_DELETED`, `THIS_OPERATION`, late effect. (g2) No data event after delivery is proven → `UNATTRIBUTED` → `INCIDENT` (`UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`). (g3) A G-17 lifecycle rule could remove it and no event exists → `LIFECYCLE` |
| (h) | 8, authorization expires before a request is issued | The worker reaches `not_after` before `SEND_STARTED` → `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT`; a forced send afterwards → `403` (S-20) → `RESOLVED_NOT_DELETED` |
| (i) | 9, crashes at each point | (i1) After the issue: `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT`. (i2) After the claim: second claim refused; `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT`. (i3) After `SEND_STARTED`: `AMBIGUOUS`, as (d). (i4) After a `403` was received but not stored: `AMBIGUOUS`; the refusal event (T-3) or the successor decides |
| (j) | 10, an operator tries to resolve manually | Every direct write to the operation table and every call of the resolution function without OPT-7L-03 evidence is refused; nothing changes; the attempt is logged |
| (k) | 11, beyond the privacy deadline | The deadline passes with the version listed and the operation `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN`: `DEADLINE_MISSED`; reported as unauthorized retention (no hold) or `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED` (hold); the deadline is unchanged; the report never says "deleted", "bounded" or "resolved" |
| (l) | OPT-7L-08 | A second deletion data event under one `SourceIdentity`; or a data event under an operation recorded `RESOLVED_NOT_SENT` → `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`; the operation reclassified from the event |

**T-7L-14 — authorization-fence continuity (FG-7L-R5-03; owners Security, Platform, Storage; gate AG-7L-09).** Specified; **not executed**. Each case asserts E-8 and E-17 and the intent's state. Management-account actions and missing events are run in a **test organization** or synthetically, **labelled test-only**. Member-account refusals run on the real provider under PV-R3 (g), (h). The universal oracle: **no `VERIFIED_ABSENT` for an intent whose interval *I* contains an unmatched successful surface change, an unmatched access to the key, or an unproven trail-continuity period, whatever the two snapshots say.**

| Case | Action | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| (a) The mandatory adversarial example | Steps 1 – 6 of §35.4f, with the change made by the management account | `AUTHZ_CHANGED` at step 2; `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` and `BATCH_PROOF_INCOMPLETE` at step 3; equal snapshots at step 5 recorded; never `VERIFIED_ABSENT`. A build that passes on the snapshots fails |
| (b) SCP detach and reattach | The management account detaches the member SCP and reattaches it 10 minutes later, during `DELETING` | `DetachPolicy` and `AttachPolicy` unmatched → `AUTHZ_CHANGED`; it persists after the reattachment; snapshots equal |
| (c) Bucket-policy relaxation and restoration | (c1) A member principal, and the member root, call `PutBucketPolicy` | (c1) Refused by the SCP; denied events reported to Security; the intent continues. (c2) Test-only exemption: success, then restoration → `AUTHZ_CHANGED` |
| (d) Role trust widening and restoration | `UpdateAssumeRolePolicy` on a role of *P(b)*, then back | Member principal: refused. Test-only exemption: `AUTHZ_CHANGED`, recorded from the `us-east-1` events |
| (e) Organization membership changes | (e1) `MoveAccount` of D to an OU without the SCP, and back. (e2) D calls `LeaveOrganization` | (e1) `AUTHZ_CHANGED` and `BATCH_PROOF_INCOMPLETE` (BQA-7L-08). (e2) Refused by the SCP |
| (f) Batch-job creation in the window | While the SCP is detached (test organization), a member principal creates a copy job with the governed batch role | `CreateJob` unmatched; the source reads are unmatched data events; `BATCH_PROOF_INCOMPLETE`, `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` |
| (g) A job that completes before the final enumeration | The job of (f) reaches `Complete` before pass 2 | Found by pass 2's terminal-status listing and by its `CreateJob` event. A build that lists non-terminal statuses only fails |
| (h) A copy to an unregistered target | The job of (f) writes to a bucket in an account outside *J* | The closure listings are unchanged, and the test asserts that they are not used as the oracle; the source-key data events give `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`; never `VERIFIED_ABSENT` |
| (i) Audit delivery delay or missing events | (i1) Synthetic delivery delay beyond `T_ct`. (i2) A missing hour of digest files. (i3) A single dropped change event for a change that is **not** reverted. (i4) A dropped change event for a reverted change whose use left a data event. (i5) All events of (a) dropped | (i1) Held in `VERIFYING`; past `T_q,max` `AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE`. (i2) `AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE`. (i3) The snapshot differs → `AUTHZ_CHANGED`. (i4) `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`. (i5) Not detectable; the test asserts that the report names RR-7L-R6 (ii) as the condition of the verification and does not claim more |
| (j) A policy change by a privileged principal | (j1) The member root calls `PutBucketPolicy`. (j2) The management account uses `AssumeRoot` with `S3UnlockBucketPolicy` (test organization) | (j1) Refused by the SCP (S-32, S-34). (j2) Whether an SCP restrains it is PV-R3 (k); in either case the `AssumeRoot` and `DeleteBucketPolicy` events → `AUTHZ_CHANGED` |
| (k) A failed fence installation | (k1) The SCP fails to attach. (k2) The exemption is not tag-bound. (k3) The trail lacks data events or integrity validation. (k4) An MRAP contains a closure bucket | NOT ADMITTED (RAD-7L-14, ACF-7L-10); an existing intent → `AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE` |
| (l) A governed change during cleanup | The provisioning pipeline asks for a change record on a bucket that an open intent holds | The change record cannot commit (lock conflict); the change broker mints nothing; no event |

**T-7L-15 — incident-state authorization (FG-7L-R6-01; OD-7L-30, -31; owners Voice, Privacy, Security; gate AG-7L-09; the resolution cases need AP-7L-54).** Specified; **not executed**. Database interleavings use two sessions and the row locks' own waits. Provider conditions use the synthetic adapter or a test account, **labelled test-only**. **Universal oracle O-I**, checked after every step of every case: (1) every deletion data event maps to an issue record whose intent was `DELETING`, or `INCIDENT` with every open reason Class 1, and whose F evidence (ICM-7L-04) and hold verdict are stored on it; (2) no issue exists while any Class 2 reason is open; (3) no `VERIFIED_ABSENT` follows `INCIDENT` without an intervening `QUIESCING` reached through ICR-7L-05; (4) the intent's deadline equals its value at creation; (5) the erasure step stays open, and every entry still listed past the deadline without a hold is reported as unauthorized retention; (6) every state change has its audit row.

| Case | Setup and action | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| (a) An unexplained marker found before any deletion | Inventory in `QUIESCING` finds marker m1 with no lifecycle explanation; v1 and v2 present | `INCIDENT` (`MARKER_UNEXPLAINED`, Class 2) in the inventory transaction. No issue for v1, v2 or m1, attempted repeatedly; each attempt refused by the issue function. Inspection and preservation checks continue. The deadline is unchanged |
| (b) An unexplained marker found after some legitimate deletions | `DELETING`; v1 already `RESOLVED_DELETED`; a fresh listing (F (f1)) for v2's issue finds m1 | v2's issue refused; `INCIDENT` (`MARKER_UNEXPLAINED`). v1's deletion stays recorded as lawful (its F and verdict are on its issue record). v2 and m1 stay. An operation already in flight for another entry resolves only by OPT-7L-03 |
| (c) A class E recording in an unauthorized Region | A registered, admitted closure bucket of a class E stack is in another Region | `INCIDENT` (`RESIDENCY_VIOLATION`, Class 1); a residency incident record. A containment pass, then issues under F in every closure bucket, including the out-of-region one; no copy is made; never `VERIFIED_ABSENT` from `INCIDENT` |
| (c′) The same copy in an unregistered bucket | The copy is found by ACF-7L-06 in a bucket not in G-17 | `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` (Class 2), plus `RESIDENCY_VIOLATION` where its Region is known; **no** deletion anywhere until a resolution registers and admits the bucket |
| (d) A class S recording in an unauthorized third Region | Class S stack; a registered closure bucket in a Region other than `R_o` and `R_r` | As (c): Class 1, containment under F. Variant: a bucket in `R_r` without REG-7K-17's authorization record is the same incident |
| (e) A new hold covering the recording | (e1) Hold placed while `INCIDENT` (all Class 1), during containment. (e2) Hold placed while `INCIDENT` (Class 2) | (e1) The next issue takes the gate and finds the hold: `SKIPPED_HELD`; the intent stays `INCIDENT` (ICM-7L-10); preservation checks run. An issue already committed before the hold follows HLC-7L-08 and OPT-7L-06. (e2) Nothing to refuse; preservation checks run. In both, on release, nothing is issued until ICM-7L-03 and F hold again |
| (f) Incident owner approval granted | `INCIDENT` (`AUTHZ_CHANGED`); the fence is restored (change records reconciled); request by a Voice holder; approvals by a Privacy holder and a Security holder, three different humans | ICR-7L-05 → `QUIESCING`; audit rows; then a full rerun: snapshot, inventory, quiescence, both job passes, catalogue checks, ACF reconciliation. If a check fails again, `INCIDENT` again. No entry is deleted by the resolution itself |
| (f′) Approval defects | (f′1) The requester approves their own request (two sessions). (f′2) Only Privacy approves a *Sec* reason. (f′3) A new reason opens between approval and execution. (f′4) The approval is 25 hours old. (f′5) An approver's grant is revoked before execution | Each is refused: (f′1) same human; (f′2) Security missing; (f′3) the request becomes `STALE`; (f′4) the request becomes `EXPIRED` (RQL-7L-08; revised for FG-7L-R7-02); (f′5) the request becomes `STALE` (`APPROVAL_INVALIDATED`). The intent's state is unchanged, and each refusal and transition is audited |
| (g) Incident owner approval denied | The Privacy holder rejects | The request ends `REJECTED`; the reasons stay open; a Class 1 incident keeps containing, a Class 2 incident stays halted; the deadline is unchanged; past it, unauthorized retention is reported |
| (h) Missing tenant attribution | The intent's key fails the prefix check, or the broker refuses the binding (`KEY_OUT_OF_PREFIX`) | Class 2; no issue, no session, no data event; resolution needs Security, and its evidence is the corrected attribution through the governed Voice path, never an edit of the intent |
| (i) Storage authorization or replication proof unavailable | (i1) The RAD-7L-11 catalogue check fails in a containment pass. (i2) A version turns `PENDING` in the fresh `HeadObject` of F (f4). (i3) The monitor watermark is older than `T_ct` | (i1) `STORAGE_AUTHORITY_UNNARROWABLE` (Class 2): containment stops. (i2) That issue is refused; past `T_q,max`, `QUIESCENCE_UNPROVABLE` (Class 2). (i3) The issue is refused until the watermark is current; past `T_q,max`, `AUTHZ_CONTINUITY_UNPROVABLE` |
| (j) Worker crash immediately after `INCIDENT` is committed | Crash after the transaction that commits `INCIDENT` and its first reason | Restart in `INCIDENT`. Class 2: nothing issued. Class 1: no issue until a new containment pass completes after the reason. Operations open at the crash resolve only by OPT-7L-03 |
| (k) Two workers racing to resume an incident | (k1) Two executors start a containment pass. (k2) Two calls execute the same approved request. (k3) One worker executes the resolution while another commits an issue | (k1) The pass number's compare-and-swap lets one pass record; the other is discarded. (k2) One `INCIDENT → QUIESCING`; the second finds the request `EXECUTED`, returns its stored outcome and changes nothing (RQL-7L-10). (k3) Both lock the intent row `FOR UPDATE`. Whichever commits first decides: either the issue commits under `INCIDENT` (the fingerprint changes, so the resolution is refused `STALE`), or the resolution commits first (the issue then finds `QUIESCING` and is refused) |
| (l) Privacy deadline exceeded during incident resolution | `INCIDENT` (Class 2) with a request pending; the deadline passes | `DEADLINE_MISSED` record-only (ICM-7L-02); the intent state is unchanged; unauthorized retention reported for every listed, unheld entry; the pending request is not invalidated by the record itself, but the fingerprint does not change either. No issue becomes admissible because of the deadline (ICM-7L-05) |

**T-7L-15 extended for the seventh review (FG-7L-R7-01, -02).** Specified; **not executed**. The same owners, gate and labelling apply. **Universal oracle O-R**, checked after every step of every case below, together with O-I: (1) at most one request of the intent is in `REQUESTED`, `PENDING_REQUIRED_APPROVALS` or `APPROVED`; (2) no request has left a terminal state; (3) every `EXECUTED` request has the required decisions by distinct humans, other than the requester, each bound to its *F*, and its execution's clock read precedes its `expires_at`; (4) every closure joins an opening and an `EXECUTED` request of the same intent and organization, and no opening has two closures; (5) the intent is `INCIDENT` if and only if it has an open occurrence; (6) no opening, closure, decision, IRR or evidence row has changed since its insert (the test compares a full snapshot of those rows); (7) every decision, transition, opening and closure has its audit and provenance rows; (8) no occurrence is closed without the technical evidence of its table A row: a build whose only evidence is attestation fails.

| Case | Setup and action | Authoritative state | Pass / fail oracle |
|---|---|---|---|
| (m1) `OBJECT_LOCKED` | (m1a) Retain-until in the future; a request with complete attestations. (m1b) Retention passed, legal hold off, no default retention | (m1a) Occurrence open. (m1b) IEV-02 `UNLOCKED` | (m1a) Creation refused (`EVIDENCE_PROFILE_UNSATISFIABLE`); containment continues outside the locked entry. (m1b) `EXECUTED`; `QUIESCING` inventories and deletes. Fail: any closure in (m1a) |
| (m2) `DELETE_REFUSED` | (m2a) The policy is corrected (IEV-05) but no later operation has succeeded. (m2b) A later operation `RESOLVED_DELETED`, `THIS_OPERATION`. (m2c) The entry disappears, attributed `UNATTRIBUTED` | (m2b) IEV-13 terminal | (m2a) Refused. (m2b) `EXECUTED`. (m2c) Refused; `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS` opens |
| (m3) `OPERATION_UNRESOLVED` | (m3a) The operation is still `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN`. (m3b) A later listing gives T-2 | Operation records unchanged by any request | (m3a) Refused; successors continue. (m3b) `EXECUTED`. Fail: any operation outcome written by a request function |
| (m4) `RESIDENCY_VIOLATION` | (m4a) An entry is still in the out-of-region bucket. (m4b) Absent, the rule removed, Privacy attestation present. (m4c) After (m4b), a new entry appears there | (m4b) Closure `CONTAINED` | (m4a) Refused. (m4b) `EXECUTED`; the later `QUIESCING` does not raise the reason for that bucket; E-14 lists the closed violation. (m4c) Occurrence 2 opens, with `prior_closure_id` |
| (m5) `MARKER_REPLICATION_UNPROVABLE` | (m5a) A rule with `DeleteMarkerReplication` `Enabled` covered the key after the marker. (m5b) Only (m2) failed, and IEV-08 proves the interval | (m5a) Occurrence open, permanently | (m5a) Refused at every attempt; class V entries deleted by containment; the marker stays; RR-7L-R7 reported. (m5b) `EXECUTED` |

**T-7L-15 extended for the eighth review (FG-7L-R8-01).** Specified; **not executed**. The same owners, gate and labelling apply. Monitor runs are produced from a test organization trail, or synthetically, **labelled test-only**. PV-R3 (e) and (p) are taken as passed only in the cases that say so. **Universal oracle O-C**, checked after every case together with O-I and O-R: (1) no IEV-08 run, raw row, `matched_by_irr` list or class differs from its value at insert (compared byte for byte with a snapshot); (2) no run reports `CONTINUOUS_NO_UNMATCHED` over an interval containing a raw row; (3) every committed IRR has a projection record whose remaining set is empty and whose *U*, *P* and *M* come from one run of the same intent and organization; (4) no IRR exists without an `EXECUTED` request and closures in the same transaction; (5) no event identity has two committed IRRs in one intent.

**T-7L-15 extended for the ninth review (FG-7L-R9-01).** Specified; **not executed**. The same owners, gate and labelling apply. Late provider evidence comes from a test organization trail, a test S3 Inventory configuration, or is synthetic, **labelled test-only**. Unless a case says otherwise, each case starts from intent *X* in `VERIFIED_ABSENT` with verification 1 (E-1 … E-18; latest run *R_k*, class `CONTINUOUS_NO_UNMATCHED`), its share locks released and no request. A *reader* session polls *X*'s state, without locks, throughout every transaction. **Universal oracle O-P**, checked after every case together with O-I, O-R and O-C: (1) no provenance row records `VERIFIED_ABSENT → INCIDENT` or `PENDING → INCIDENT`, and every edge out of `VERIFIED_ABSENT` goes to `REOPENED` and has a challenge record in its transaction; (2) at every commit, the state is `INCIDENT` if and only if the open set is not empty, and the reader never observes `REOPENED` with an open occurrence, nor `REOPENED` at all from a transaction that went on to `INCIDENT`; (3) no verification record, E-item, monitor run, raw row, `matched_by_irr` list, class, sentinel result, challenge record, opening, closure or IRR differs from its value at insert (a snapshot compared byte for byte); (4) every committed finding about verification 1 has its challenge record in its own transaction and, when it names a reason, its opening, with the intent in `INCIDENT`; (5) no deletion data event and no issue record exists for *X* while it is `REOPENED`, and none in `INCIDENT` except under ICM-7L-03; (6) every transition, opening and challenge has its provenance and audit rows in its own transaction; (7) the runs of *X* have consecutive sequence numbers and non-decreasing watermarks.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Approval sequence (OD-7L-32).** (1) Document the mitigations (this table). (2) Implement the controls in the authorized implementation phase. (3) Execute the required provider validations. (4) Record the actual evidence and the unresolved exposure. (5) Obtain the Security owner's sign-off. (6) Complete the applicable legal review. (7) Present the residual risk to the owner for an individual final decision. Only step 1 is done. If verification fails, or the owner finds the remaining exposure unacceptable, recording storage stays disabled. RAD-7L-14 and AG-7L-09 stay `CLOSED` until step 7 records an acceptance. OD-7L-32 does not approve RR-7L-R4, RR-7L-R5, AP-7L-53, AP-7L-54 or any other packet.

### 35.11 Adversarial checks added to §34.13

| # | Attack | Outcome under §35 |
|---:|---|---|
| 21 | Delete while replication is `PENDING`, then let it resume | No deletion before quiescence (RDQ-7L-11); counterexample T-7L-07 (a) |
| 22 | Add a destination and run Batch Replication during cleanup | Configuration and batch fences (RDQ-7L-06, -08); evidence E-4, E-8 |
| 23 | Copy the object in place to recreate it | Write fence; Batch Copy fenced; no copy right for any runtime identity (RDQ-7L-05, -08, -23) |
| 24 | Declare completion on empty listings | Never sufficient (RDQ-7L-01, -16; E-1 … E-18) |
| 25 | Issue an unversioned delete and call it deletion | Never issued; a delete marker hides nothing (RDQ-7L-14) |
| 26 | Hold the stream entry until replication settles | CON-08 follows EXT-02 (RDQ-7L-30); no pin |
| 27 | Close a long-`PENDING` intent to meet a deadline | Forbidden; a missed deadline is an incident and unauthorized retention (RDQ-7L-28) |
| 28 | A class E recording replicated out of region | Residency incident (Class 1); deletion there continues only as containment issues under ICM-7L-03 and F (RDQ-7L-24, revised) |
| 29 | A reappearance after completion is overwritten by a new success | Recorded as falsified; `REOPENED` (RDQ-7L-27) |
| 30 | Place a hold just after a deletion is authorized and expect it to be honoured | A hold committed before the issue prevents it. After the issue, only that one version, decided under the gate, is in *W*; recorded; AP-7L-53 states it (HLC-7L-03, -05, -08). There is no lease to exploit |
| 31 | Pause the worker after authorization and delete long after a hold | The provider refuses after `not_after` (HLC-7L-04; S-20); the version is then held |
| 32 | Treat a timeout as "not deleted" and re-issue under the old authorization | No resolution before `not_after + T_skew`, and none by elapsed time; only OPT-7L-03 evidence decides, and a still-listed version leaves the operation `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN`; a new attempt needs a new issue under the gate (HLC-7L-07, revised for FG-7L-R5-02) |
| 33 | Two workers race to delete one version | One open operation and one claim per version (HLC-7L-10) |
| 34 | Make the hold function wait, or fail, while deletions are in flight | It inspects and waits for nothing; HLD-12 is untouched (HLC-7L-06) |
| 35 | Run a copy job in an account the source listing cannot see | *J* includes every account that can hold a closure bucket or principal; an account outside *J* is denied by the bucket policy (BQA-7L-02, -04 (iii)) |
| 36 | Hide a covering job on a later `ListJobs` page | Pagination to the end; incomplete enumeration is never a pass (BQA-7L-05) |
| 37 | Detach the SCP between the two job checks | Digest change → `AUTHZ_CHANGED` (BQA-7L-07) |
| 38 | Use a tenant-A credential on tenant B's object | Refused by the role policy and by the bucket policy independently (TSA-7L-04, -06); T-7L-11 (b) |
| 39 | Set the session tag to `*` to widen the substituted pattern | Refused at `TagSession` (TSA-7L-05) |
| 40 | Steal the cleanup worker's credential and delete directly | It has no object permission; it can claim only already-issued operations (TSA-7L-01, -13) |
| 41 | Delete with an unversioned `DeleteObject` to leave a marker | Refused by the provider (TSA-7L-04, -06) |
| 42 | Compromise the broker | Not prevented; detected by reconciliation; stated as RR-7L-R5 (a) |
| 43 | Leave a delete marker so that the inventory cannot complete, and the intent stalls | Class M needs no `HeadObject`; its evidence is the listing (OC-7L-03); quiescence is defined (OC-7L-05) |
| 44 | Answer a HEAD on a data version with `405` to have it skipped as a "marker" | The class comes from the listing only; a `405` for a `Version` is `CLASS_CONTRADICTION` (OC-7L-01, -02) |
| 45 | Hide an entry beyond the first page of `ListObjectVersions` | Pagination to `IsTruncated` false; incomplete runs never pass (OC-7L-01) |
| 46 | Delete the current marker first, so that an old by-key URL serves the content again | Every class V entry of a bucket is deleted before any class M entry (OC-7L-06) |
| 47 | Replicate a marker after its source copy is deleted, to defeat final verification | Marker replication excluded at admission; otherwise not provable → incident (OC-7L-05; RAD-7L-04) |
| 48 | Drop the response of an accepted delete, then place a hold, and expect the version reported preserved | `OUTCOME_UNPROVEN`; `HELD_PRESERVATION_UNASSURED`; never `SKIPPED_HELD` without T-1 (b) or T-3 (OPT-7L-04, -06) |
| 49 | Wait long enough and declare a still-listed version "not deleted" | Elapsed time and listings that show the version are not evidence (OPT-7L-03) |
| 50 | Rely on the IAM deadline to cancel an accepted request | The deadline bounds admission only; no cancellation is claimed (OPT-7L-01) |
| 51 | Have an operator mark an ambiguous operation resolved | No function, role or grant writes an outcome (OPT-7L-09) |
| 52 | Detach the SCP, copy, reattach, and pass on equal snapshots | Unmatched change events and source-key data events; snapshots are necessary only (ACF-7L-05 … -07); T-7L-14 (a) |
| 53 | Create and finish a copy job between the two job passes | Pass 2 lists terminal statuses; `CreateJob` events are reconciled (BQA-7L-07) |
| 54 | Change the bucket policy as the member account's root user | Refused by the SCP, which binds the member root (S-32, S-34) |
| 55 | Act from the management account | Not prevented; detected; RR-7L-R6 (i); recordings stay NOT ADMITTED until it is dispositioned (RAD-7L-14) |
| 56 | Read "deletion reduces exposure" in prose as permission to delete in any incident | The issue function admits an `INCIDENT` issue only under ICM-7L-03; Class 2 refuses every issue; the §35.5 action table is authoritative |
| 57 | Let the deadline pass so that "the obligation" forces a deletion | `DEADLINE_MISSED` is record-only and grants nothing (ICM-7L-02, -05) |
| 58 | Treat an unexplained marker as harmless and keep deleting | Class 2; TSA-7L-14; resolution needs Security (OC-7L-04; ICR-7L-03) |
| 59 | Approve one's own resolution, or approve with only Privacy for a *Sec* reason | Refused by human-identity comparison and the per-reason approval rule (ICR-7L-03) |
| 60 | Approve, then change the incident, then execute the old approval | Fingerprint mismatch → `STALE` (ICR-7L-04) |
| 61 | Use a resolution to reach `VERIFIED_ABSENT` or to release a hold | The only effect is `INCIDENT → QUIESCING`; everything reruns (ICR-7L-06, -07; ICM-7L-07) |
| 62 | Delete an out-of-region copy in a bucket that G-17 does not know | Class 2 (`CONFIG_UNRECORDED` / `UNATTRIBUTED_STORAGE_ACCESS`); no deletion role exists there; registration first (§35.4g situation 3) |
| 63 | Reuse the approvals of a stale request for its successor | Decisions belong to one request by key; none carries over (RQL-7L-12, -13) |
| 64 | Leave a stale request open so that no successor can be made | The slot is freed in the transaction that makes the request terminal; creation terminates a stale predecessor itself (RQL-7L-01, -03, -06) |
| 65 | Close a reason with a ticket and three signatures | Attestation never stands for a technical condition (IRE-7L-01); T-7L-15 (m22) |
| 66 | Edit or delete a reason row to hide it | No table privilege; triggers; the open set is derived from immutable rows (IRC-7L-04, -06; RQL-7L-14) |
| 67 | Reconcile an unattributed read so that `VERIFIED_ABSENT` passes | `READ_EXPOSURE` never matches (IRE-7L-06); RR-7L-R7 |
| 68 | Register an unregistered destination "from now on", so that its old copies fall outside the closure | `INCIDENT_REGISTERED` takes effect from the earliest proven time, or from the earliest version; registration only widens (IRE-7L-07) |
| 69 | Change the incident just before execution | Eager staleness in the changing transaction; recomputation in the execution (RQL-7L-06, -07) |
| 70 | Execute exactly at the 24-hour mark after a lock wait | The clock is read after the last lock; `now()` is not used (RQL-7L-08); T-7L-15 (p3) |
| 71 | Name another organization's reason in a request | Composite keys and the organization-bound proof (RQL-7L-13); T-7L-15 (ab) |
| 72 | Resolve `KEY_OUT_OF_PREFIX` by "correcting" the key | No correction path exists; the key is immutable; the request is refused (§35.4h; ICR-7L-02 as replaced) |
| 73 | Let a confirmation with a longer `UNMATCHED` list pass as "the same class" | IEV-08 runs are compared by effective set, never by class (CRX-7L-02) |
| 74 | Cite an event that the monitor never recorded, so that a proposal "reconciles" it | V1 accepts only raw rows of the confirmation run (CRX-7L-05) |
| 75 | Cover one event twice, with two classes, to slip one through | Unique `(request_id, event identity)`; unique `(intent_id, event identity)` on committed IRRs (CRX-7L-03, -08) |
| 76 | Subtract another tenant's or another interval's event | Composite keys to the raw row's run, intent and organization; *U* is one run (CRX-7L-06) |
| 77 | Rewrite the earlier `UNMATCHED` run after the commit, so that history shows `CONTINUOUS_NO_UNMATCHED` | Runs are insert-only; later runs use `CONTINUOUS_RECONCILED` (CRX-7L-01, -09); T-7L-15 (au) |
| 78 | Treat a CloudTrail gap as reconciled because every known event has a proposal | `GAP` is never reconciled (CRX-7L-07 (d)); T-7L-15 (al) |
| 79 | Make a late finding "simple" by writing `VERIFIED_ABSENT → INCIDENT` | No such edge; the transition trigger refuses it (PCI-7L-04 (a)); T-7L-15 (bh) |
| 80 | Commit `REOPENED` first and the opening later, so that a crash leaves a known finding without a reason | The finding, the challenge, both edges and the opening are one transaction; the deferred invariant refuses `REOPENED` with an occurrence (PCI-7L-02, -04); T-7L-15 (bc), (bd) |
| 81 | Overwrite verification 1, or rewrite its monitor run, once a late event shows it wrong | Insert-only; the challenge record states `FALSIFIED` or `CHALLENGED` (PCI-7L-05); T-7L-15 O-P (3) |
| 82 | Treat an S3 Inventory hit as proof and delete the copy from `VERIFIED_ABSENT` or `REOPENED` | No object session in `VERIFIED_ABSENT`; no deletion in `REOPENED`; deletion only through `QUIESCING → DELETING`, under F and the gate (PCI-7L-03; §35.5) |
| 83 | Treat every late event as a reappearance, or none as one | Two separate effects: one per E-item, one on absence (PCI-7L-06). A read before the deletion falsifies E-17 and leaves absence `NOT_CONTRADICTED` |
| 84 | Cover a late event with an earlier IRR because its name, principal and time look the same | Identity tuples only (CRX-7L-06); no IRR is written from late evidence (PCI-7L-09); T-7L-15 (ay′) |
| 85 | Race two monitors so that one reopens while the other "re-verifies" or overwrites the run | The state is read only under the lock; the run sequence is compare-and-swap; `REOPENED` never returns to `VERIFIED_ABSENT` (PCI-7L-01, -07); T-7L-15 (ba), (bb) |
| 86 | Advance the detector's position in one transaction, record the finding in another, then crash | The position advances only with the finding (PCI-7L-07); T-7L-15 (bc) |
| 87 | Re-verify a reopened intent without its fence | Re-fencing before any `QUIESCING` work; E-7 runs from the re-acquisition (PCI-7L-10); T-7L-15 (bi′) |

Both failed closed (no deletion without fresh evidence), which is why they are rated Minor; the reviewer is asked to confirm the rating. **FND-7L-11:** AWS documents the permission for a version-specific `DeleteObject` inconsistently (S-27). TSA-7L-04 and -06 deny `s3:DeleteObject` explicitly. If PV-R3 (f) shows that a version-specific delete also needs `s3:DeleteObject`, those denies would refuse every deletion. **RR-7L-R2 is recorded as an unbounded privacy residual, not as a closed item.** Like RR-7K-10, it awaits an owner disposition at go-live under OD-7L-12. It blocks no design freeze, because the design fails closed: logical denial, no false completion, and an incident. **RR-7L-R4, RR-7L-R5, RR-7L-R6 and RR-7L-R7 are recorded the same way.** R7 (seventh review) is the consequence of preventing every resolution whose closing condition cannot be proven: the recording stays undeleted and logically denied, and past its deadline it is unauthorized retention. No disposition is proposed. None is proposed as safe. R4 exists only if AP-7L-53 is approved, and its part (b) is detected, not prevented. R5 (a) is a compromised authorized workload, detected and not prevented. R6 is the management account and the completeness of the audit trail: detected, not prevented. Its treatment path is chosen (OD-7L-32: mitigate, verify, then decide), but **the risk is not accepted**, and until step 7 of that sequence records an individual acceptance no stack can be admitted for recordings (RAD-7L-14). Closed production gates relevant to recordings: AG-7L-09 (and, through it, AG-7L-06 for LS-D-VOX and the admission of CON-08); RAD-7L-14; AB-7I-14 for every data-subject erasure; AG-7L-01 for logical denial. All nine AG-7L gates are `CLOSED`.
